
- Of this module's packages, the root imports only `protocol` and `protocol/bridge`, std-and-protobuf packages, as connect's root imports `connect/protocol` (Q-REPO-3). `protocol` imports `protocol/bridge`, never the reverse, so a type both use is declared only in `protocol/bridge` (4.9). The root never imports `device/`: `cli/` (`ur tun`, `ur bridge`) and sdk's `DeviceLocal` wire `device.Bridge` to the root's `BridgeState`, so the iOS extension links neither the root nor `protocol` (D-SDK-20).
- **Build tags.** Desktop-only code (the OS tun, §17.10; installers; the macOS keychain, §5.10) lives in `cli/` or carries `!ios && !android && !sdk_mobile_bind`. Package connect links gVisor into every importer through its untagged tun.go (connect/tun.go:38-47), so root files that use package connect (client generations and `SidecarEnv`, `Subprotocol` and streams, sockets dial and listen, the bridge, tls and smtp listeners) carry `!sidecar_http`, as do the engine host interfaces (`host_*.go`), since no engine runs in the page Worker. The rest, §5.4's events, actions, binding and `Sign` included, uses the root's own `Id` ([16]byte), `Logger`, `MonitorValue` and `CallbackList`, and reaches api through the net/http `SidecarApi` (bearer plus DPoP signer), in both legs; connect-facing files convert at that boundary, and §4.7 fails the `sidecar_http` leg on any connect or gVisor package (§18.10).

```go
// host_service.go: supplied by the hosting process; engines never import server, so go-redis,
// minio-go and prometheus stay out of sidecar.
type ServiceHost struct {
	Authenticator Authenticator       // jwt -> Principal (server/session)
	Quota         Quota               // reserve, commit, release (§20)
	Metrics       Metrics             // prometheus in server
	Tasks         Tasks               // once-keyed jobs (taskworker)
	Redis         Redis               // cas, incr, scripts, TTLs, hash-tagged keys; evs and gkm keep only soft state
	                                  // they rebuild there (owner decision 136); keyspace events only via the shared
	                                  // subscriber, never per client, the pattern that melted the cluster on
	                                  // 2026-07-15 (server/model/peer_model.go:32-37)
	Blobs         BlobStore           // the segment bucket and each metadata cluster's bucket, by cluster id, the
	                                  // first holding place/ (owner decision 145): If-Match and If-None-Match
	                                  // puts, streamed put, ranged get, prefix list, delete (X13)
	Push          Push                // server to client (X8)
	ServiceClient ServiceClientSource // jwt and urls for the engine's connect client
}

// Each engine that a server/cli/<svc> hosts; server wraps it with readiness, /status, stats and
// PROXY-unwrapped listeners. pushservice's types run inside existing services instead.
type Engine interface {
	Handler() http.Handler // or Serve(net.Listener) for stream engines
	Ready() bool
	Drain()
	Close()
}
```

evs and gkm keep durable state only in `Blobs` (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [19](#od-19), [21](#od-21)): a repo's metadata objects and its gkm group's live on the metadata cluster that the repo's create-only `place/<repo_id>` on the first cluster names, which the engines resolve and cache ([owner decision 145](#od-145); §11.8). Other engines take a store (`SmtpEdgeStore`, …) that server/model implements beside the migrations.


```text
development (every sidecar branch and main)
  sidecar/go.mod            module github.com/urnetwork/sidecar        root: core, protocol/, mcp/,
                                                                       device/, <svc>service/, sidecartest/
  sidecar/cli/go.mod        module github.com/urnetwork/sidecar/cli    ur and git-remote-ur; requires the root

  sidecar/smtpproof/go.mod  module github.com/urnetwork/sidecar/smtpproof   provers and the verifier, which
```

- **Imports:** besides this repository's modules, connect and its replaced forks are the only first-party modules a sidecar module requires, never proxy or the userwireguard it requires (proxy/go.mod:9-10), so `ur proxy add` (cli/UI.md:39-41) runs in `cli/` on §17's userspace `connect.Tun`.
- **Third-party:** `dependencies.yml` lists each module with SPDX id, reason and leg (client, engine, cli, test). Allowed: MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, MPL-2.0; refused: GPL family, SSPL, BUSL, custom, unlicensed. Initial: protobuf v1.36.11, x/crypto, docopt-go, pires/go-proxyproto, go-sdk v1.7.0 for mcp/ and go-winio v0.6.2 for §5.8's pipe (server/go.mod:30, 67), purego v0.11.2 for the macOS Keychain (Apache-2.0), wireguard's tun (MIT) for `cli/`'s OS tun (§17.10); in the test leg, `mlsinterop/`'s peers [R:ext-storage-crypto](design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md).
- **Versions:** shared modules match connect, sdk and server, because an uncoordinated bump fails server's `-mod=readonly` build (server/README.md:12); protobuf follows §18.10.

```text

  deps      server, sdk, sn or an unlisted module in a leg's go list -deps; the root module requiring any module

  layering  the root importing a package of this module other than protocol and protocol/bridge; protocol
            importing beyond std, protobuf and protocol/bridge, or protocol/bridge beyond std and protobuf; a
            client package importing a <svc>service
  legs      the ios_extension leg's deps including the root package or protocol; the sidecar_http js leg's deps

  cgo       CgoFiles, except keychain_darwin.go in §5.10's darwin fallback leg
  hygiene   replaces other than 4.7's; registry conflicts; stale generated code; a release leg built with
```

- **Consumers:** server, sn (sn/go.mod:207) and four sdk modules add the require and replace above, server also for `smtpproof`; lock.yml, a pinned entry (source_graph_test.go:145-151) and `./cli/<svc>` (service_compile_test.go:13); build/.gitmodules, a `sidecar` submodule; run.sh, 4.9's release step after connect's and before sdk's, and `warpctl build` per service (:3398-3477); deploy-rollout.zsh, a class per service (:23-40).

### 4.8 Branches and cross-repo pinning

- **Branches.** Each repo a milestone touches (§23.4) gets a `sidecar` branch on its normal remote, public where the repo is ([owner decision 118](#od-118)); the extension and apps only if the owner opts in. `main` stays production-ready (build/README.md:5).
- **Pins.** server@sidecar's lock and build@sidecar's submodules pin the same `sidecar` commits, which server's source-graph tests confirm.
- **Merge, never rebase.** A rebase orphans pinned commits and skips the commit-msg hook (connect/.githooks/commit-msg:17-18). Merge `main` in weekly and before each gate, in the order connect, sidecar, sdk, sn, server, warp/config/vault/xops/mmm, build, re-pinning each time.
- **To `main`** at each milestone's Gn-out (§23.8): every touched repo, server and sdk included, in that order, once the pinned set passes its checks, migrations are additive and release-compatible (connect/CODESTYLE.md:85-89), connect's default-off changes lead and the code is dark (D-OPS-10). Branch migrations stay pending until their own Gn-out registers them (D-OPS-6), so one track's merge never applies the other track's group, and M3's pilot runs on production ([owner decision 118](#od-118); §23.9).

### 4.9 Generation, targets, versions, license, style

- **Protobuf:** `protocol/Makefile` runs `protoc -I=. --go_out=. --go_opt=paths=source_relative protocol/*.proto protocol/bridge/*.proto` from the repo root, so files register as `protocol/<name>.proto` and `protocol/bridge/<name>.proto` in package `urnetwork.sidecar`; sdk and server link connect's and sidecar's packages, and a duplicate path or name panics at init (protobuf@v1.36.11/reflect/protoregistry/registry.go:42, 128, 152), so `config.proto` and `acl.proto` import the types 4.4 lists for `protocol/bridge`, never redeclare them. `tool` pins protoc-gen-go v1.36.11, and output is committed.
- **Mobile, wasm, C ABI:** gomobile binds only sdk (§18.3). `make size` gates from v0: the `ios_extension` leg (`device/` and `protocol/bridge` only; D-SDK-20) fails if sidecar adds over §18.10's 1 MiB, and the `sidecar_http` js leg is measured unstripped from M2 against §18.10's 41,943,040 B goal and miss rule (D-SDK-19). No C ABI: desktop apps use the `ur` daemon (§5) or sdk's generated ABI (sdk/cgo/gen/gen.go).
- **Versions.** Development paths stay unversioned, as connect's and sdk's do; the release runs their steps (build/all/run.sh), which §22.4's release fixture checks:

```text
branch     v<version> in each repo (:1302)
root       go mod edit -module .../sidecar/v2026 (:1540-1543); quoted import paths in Go files and Makefiles
           rewritten (:1560-1566); the tree moved into v2026/, nested modules left in place (go_mod_fork,
           :1639-1683); tag v2026.M.D-<code> (:1781-1786)
smtpproof  the same as its own module: .../sidecar/smtpproof/v2026, tag smtpproof/v2026.M.D-<code>; in every
           repo its paths are rewritten before the root's subpackage pass, which skips lines already carrying
           /vN (:1564-1566)
cli        requires both tags, builds ur, never tagged as a module
version    the release sed fills Version, as for sdk (sdk/sdk.go:737; :1964)
generated  .pb.go files are committed, never regenerated on the release branch; descriptors keep
           protocol/<name>.proto and protocol/bridge/<name>.proto, so one module identity registers each
           descriptor once
fixture    the tags served through GOPROXY=file:// with GOWORK=off, an empty module cache and no replaces:
           root, protocol and an engine package import at the tag, ur builds from cli/, go list -m all shows
           one sidecar path, each descriptor registers once, and sdk's go mod graph holds no smtpproof or
           prover dependency
```

- **License and style.** The full MPL-2.0 text, copyright 2026 BringYour, Inc., is the first `sidecar` commit and reaches `main` at M0's Gn-out; GitHub reads connect's abbreviated notice (connect/LICENSE:1-3) as "Other". CODESTYLE.md adopts connect's plus the leaf, host and dependency rules; `.githooks/commit-msg` is copied byte for byte into sidecar, config and vault before their first `sidecar` commit.

| macOS | `.pkg` and `.tar.gz` of a Developer ID `ur` bundle with a provisioning profile and hardened runtime (D-CORE-12), notarized and stapled (run.sh:2644-2673) | `/usr/local/bin/ur`, linked into the bundle |
| Linux | `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.pkg.tar.zst` (nfpm) and `.tar.gz` | `/usr/bin/ur`; the script uses `/usr/local/bin/ur` |
| Windows | `.zip`, winget later; signtool SHA-256 with a timestamp (windows/app/SIGNING.md:17) | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\URnetwork\ur.exe` |

- **`git-remote-ur`** ships beside `ur` in every package as a link to the same binary, which dispatches on argv[0] (a copy in the Windows zip); git runs it for `ur://` URLs from PATH (gitremote-helpers(7); §11.11), so Windows users add the zip's directory to PATH.
- **Build.** `CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath` from `cli/`'s module, archive times from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (server/cli/api/Makefile:1, 4); macOS's keychain goes through purego (D-CORE-12).
- **Release integrity.** Signing is the gate ([owner decision 77](#od-77)): a VirusTotal scan (run.sh:2257-2298), then a `SHA256SUMS` SSH-signed by an offline two-person Ed25519 key (§2.6), whose public key the repo and ur.io publish. `install.sh` on ur.io (mmm's branch from M1, §23.4; owner decisions [15](#od-15), [16](#od-16)) pins the key, verifies signature and checksum (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`, OpenSSH 8.1+) and refuses on any failure.
- **Harness configs (§16)** use `ur`'s absolute path, since GUI-launched hosts lack the shell PATH ([MCP debugging](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2025-03-26/tools/debugging.md)). v0 has no self-updater.

### 4.11 The documents in the sidecar checkout

The one commit mixes engineering inputs (PLAN.md, FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md, product.md, mocks/, the Tailscale and agent-work-record reports) with business material (pitches, market notes, cold5/'s outreach drafts, market research), and all of it goes public as it is, history included (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118)). DESIGN.md joins it on the `sidecar` branch with design-research/, which its research links need, so its citations of pitch5.html and market2.md resolve publicly.

### 4.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scrub, then publish a filtered clone (D-REPO-8 as drafted) | Business material stays private | A second repository, a rewrite and a path allowlist | Rejected ([owner decision 117](#od-117)) |
| `/v2026` in development paths | One identity in every build | Breaks connect's and sdk's convention and consumers' v0.0.0 requires; the rewrite already publishes `/v2026` | Rejected (D-REPO-1) |
| `cli/` in the root module | One module | The root requires `smtpproof`, whose requirements then enter every consumer's graph, sdk's legs included | Rejected (D-REPO-2; [owner decision 104](#od-104)) |

§23.10 rejects D-REPO-9's private mirrors ([owner decision 118](#od-118)).

### 4.13 Decisions proposed

**D-REPO-1 (proposed).** Use §4.7's go.mod, §4.9's proto naming, an unversioned development path, and the release rewrite to `/v2026` that connect and sdk use (§4.9). *Why:* §4.3's replace and lock rules, protobuf's init-time panic, and the release convention; Go accepts a v2026 tag only on a `/v2026` path, which only the release tree has.

**D-REPO-2 (proposed).** Use §4.4's tree: MLS in root `mls_*` files ([owner decision 43](#od-43)), server-only engines in `<svc>service` packages ([owner decision 104](#od-104)), the device role in the leaf `device/` over `protocol/bridge`, which alone declares the types it parses (D-SDK-20), connect-facing and engine-host root files under `!sidecar_http` (D-SDK-19), test peers only in `mlsinterop/`; `cli/` and `smtpproof/` are nested modules the root never requires. *Why:* CODESTYLE groups files by prefix (connect/CODESTYLE.md:49-62); owner rule 1; a message declared twice panics at init, and importing connect links gVisor; test peers must not raise consumers' versions, and a root requirement reaches every consumer's module graph.

**D-REPO-3 (proposed).** Engines live in sidecar behind §4.5's `ServiceHost` and stores, and server hosts each one (Q-REPO-1). *Why:* logic stays in sidecar, persistence beside the migrations, and URnetwork-only infrastructure behind interfaces ([owner decision 48](#od-48)).

**D-REPO-4 (proposed).** Enforce §4.7 with `make check` and §4.9's v0 `make size` gate; ship no binding or C ABI. *Why:* no hosted CI exists, sidecar must be checked as the bindings build it, and a cgo file would enter gomobile's macOS slice.

**D-REPO-5 (proposed).** X9 changes are generic, additive, off by default and wire-compatible, tested in connect and merged to connect `main` first. *Why:* connect serves every client.

**D-REPO-6 (proposed).** Consumers wire sidecar as §4.7 lists, and branches follow §4.8. *Why:* the gates fail closed, pins must stay reachable (owner rule 4), and migration versions are positions.

**D-REPO-7 (proposed).** License, style, hook and distribution per §4.9 and §4.10, with offline-signed sums. *Why:* the open-source promise, the owner's commit rule, and no single origin may ship a client.

**D-REPO-8 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 117](#od-117): no scrub, archive, filtered clone or path allowlist; the repo keeps its documents and history.

**D-REPO-9 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): no private mirrors; every `sidecar` branch uses its repo's normal remote and merges to `main` at each Gn-out.

### 4.14 Open questions

**Q-REPO-1.** How do PLAN.md:5-7's repos split a service? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 19](#od-19)):** (a), a sidecar engine that server hosts and backs with its stores (D-REPO-3). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-2.** [X9] Which connect changes may land on connect's `sidecar` branch? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 22](#od-22)):** (b), §4.6's dispositions, as owner decisions [85](#od-85) and [86](#od-86) amend them. *Residual:* C17, for the extension's streaming Worker only, after §18's spike.

**Q-REPO-3.** May `protocol/` be an exception to connect/CODESTYLE.md:26? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 52](#od-52)):** (a), with a `make check` test that `protocol/` and `protocol/bridge` import nothing else from sidecar (§4.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-4.** When does sidecar go public, and with which documents? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118)):** now, as it is (§4.11), superseding the scrub and later publication of owner decisions [51](#od-51) and [107](#od-107); nothing waits for publication (§4.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-5.** Should server-only engines live in the root (PLAN.md:13)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 104](#od-104)):** (b), child packages, and (d), a nested module for the X7 prover (§4.4); `cli/` is a nested module too, so the root never requires the prover (§4.7). *Residual:* none.

### 4.15 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:13** ("all service code goes in the root"): engines live in `<svc>service` child packages and the X7 prover in a nested module, so no mobile or wasm build links them ([owner decision 104](#od-104); Q-REPO-5), and the device role in the leaf `device/`, so the iOS extension links no root package (Q-SDK-5, closed by peer review; D-SDK-20).
- **PLAN.md:9-21** (the tree) stands; `cli/` carries its own go.mod so the prover's requirements stay out of consumers' module graphs ([owner decision 104](#od-104)).

### 4.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the tree and modules, `ServiceHost`, the X9 rows, the checks, §4.8's and §4.11's rules, §4.9's release rewrite, and §4.10's install paths (§11, §16).
- **Consumes:** §6 (X8), §10 (X12), §11 (X19; placement), §13 (X1), §17 (X18; C5's dial fence and per-flow idle, `WindowDelegation`, C18's alias map), §18 (X14; `sidecar_http`, `device/`), §19's gates and pending migrations (D-OPS-6), §22.4's `sidecar_testhooks` and release fixture, §23's milestones.
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, tables:** none (routes: C11).
- **Services and config:** §4.5's server column; lock.yml; build/.gitmodules; run.sh; deploy-rollout.zsh; dependencies.yml.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §6 adds no protobuf `service` blocks; §6, §9-§15 and §19 follow §4.5's placement; §6.9, §7.9, §8.8 and §17 declare what the device role parses only in `protocol/bridge`'s `signed.proto`, `auth.proto` (§8.8's `GrantRevoke`, `Suspend` and `Unsuspend` included) and `bridge.proto`, which `config.proto` and `acl.proto` import (4.4); §5.4 and §18.10 keep connect types out of the `sidecar_http` leg's files, and §18.10 excludes `host_*.go` (4.4); §10, §11 and §19 keep each repo's metadata on the cluster its `place/` object names ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); §5.8 and §11.11 define `git-remote-ur`'s daemon mode; §17, §2.10 and §22 cover C18; §23.9 merges every touched repo at each Gn-out.

### 4.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engine or root code bloats the iOS extension | Low | High | `<svc>service` packages; the leaf `device/` and the `ios_extension` import rule; `make size` |
| Branches drift from mains that release almost daily | High | Medium | Weekly and per-milestone merges; pending migration groups (D-OPS-6) |
| A secret or AI-attributed message on a public branch stays served by hash (https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/removing-sensitive-data-from-a-repository, read 2026-11-03) | Low | Medium | The hook in every clone (connect/.githooks/commit-msg:23-27); `--scan` before each push and at each Gn-out (§23.8); secrets only in vault |
| A Go release breaks purego, leaving macOS pass-only | Low | High | Pinned version; a Keychain round trip in `make check`; cgo fallback |
| A tagged consumer resolves two sidecar module paths or registers a descriptor twice | Low | High | 4.9's rewrite; §22.4's release fixture |

### 4.18 Phasing

- **v0, before code (M0):** after [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip, LICENSE, the hook, DESIGN.md, the root's and `cli/`'s go.mod, dependencies.yml and `make check` on sidecar's `sidecar` branch, merged at M0's Gn-out; M0's branches; the lock entry, the release step and its fixture.
- **v0, first usable:** §4.6's M1, M4 and M5 rows; the first hosted engine; signed `ur` packages; the `make size` gate; `sidecar_http`'s import rule (M1) and size measure (M2); `device/` and its `ios_extension` rule (M4).
- **v1:** C18 (M6); Homebrew, winget, apt/yum. **Later:** C4 with §18's worker, and C17 for that streaming Worker if its spike needs it.
- **Blocking:** M0's `make check` blocks the first consumer pin; C13 blocks C18.

## 5. The Sidecar core: identity, keys, lifecycle, local state

### 5.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns `sidecar.Sidecar` (lifecycle, components, events, the outward-action gate); the client identity (X10); the client side of login, enrollment, pairing, admission, owner consent, refresh, revocation and AUTHZ1; and the daemon, local IPC, local state, keys, recovery and platform variants. §6 owns the subprotocol; §7 enrollment routes, auth keys, OAuth, the AUTHZ1 server fix and config records; §8 policy; §10 MLS; §11 evs; §16 MCP and approvals; §18 hosting; §20 counting.

### 5.2 Requirements

| R-CORE-2 | Hold "an authenticated jwt, connect client, api, and encryption key" | PLAN.md:14 |
| R-CORE-3 | The CLI speaks stdio MCP by default | PLAN.md:19-20 |

| R-CORE-5 | The git identity is the sidecar client id | PLAN.md:59 |

### 5.3 What exists today

**connect**
- `BringYourApi` has `AuthNetworkClient(Sync)`, `RemoveNetworkClient` and `GetClientKey`, but no refresh (connect/api.go:20-62, :256-330, :548-570). `NewClient` (connect/transfer.go:2267) takes a `ClientKeySeed` (:1657-1663) and `ClientAuth` (connect/transport.go:348-364).
- `ClientKeyManager.Sign` signs without a label (connect/transfer_key.go:221-229), and the key history does not stop an operator malicious from first contact (connect/transfer_key_history.go:22-26). The ClientKey is plain Ed25519 from a 32-byte seed (connect/transfer_key.go:127-129).
- Package connect's untagged tun.go imports gVisor (connect/tun.go:38-50), so a file using any connect type, even `Id` (connect/id.go:15), `Logger` (connect/log.go:41), `MonitorValue` or `CallbackList` (connect/util.go:74, :220), links the IP stack.

**server**
- A client token creates only its own children (`source_client_id`, server/model/network_client_model.go:191, :359-379). A child is exempt from the client caps (:502, :649-671), never becomes a peer (connect/transfer.go:17611-17617) and ends with its parent (server/session/by_jwt.go:679-700).
- The reaper deactivates a top-level client after 30 idle days and deletes it 30 days later, and deletes a child after 30 days unseen (server/model/network_client_model.go:3905, :3925, :4193). One resident serves each client id and instance (server/model/network_client_resident_model.go:62-68).
- `/auth/code-create` escalates a client token (server/api/route_authz.go:122), and expiry is not enforced (server/session/AUTH.md:229; §7.3); a removed client's tokens stop at once (server/session/AUTH.md:197). `GET /auth/refresh` takes a bare Client token (route_authz.go:114), and `POST /network/auth-client` (OwnClient) mints and reissues client tokens (:131), neither with a proof of possession.

**Missing:** everything below.

### 5.4 Sidecar: fields, settings, lifecycle, components

```go
// Every leg: sidecar.go, settings.go and the root's id, log and monitor files use no connect type, so
// §18.10's sidecar_http leg links them (§4.4). Sidecar is safe for concurrent use.
type Id [16]byte // connect.Id's layout (connect/id.go:15); connect-facing files convert: connect.Id(id)

type Logger interface { // connect.Logger's methods (connect/log.go:41); connect-facing files adapt it
	Info(args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warningf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
	V(level int32) Verbose // Verbose: Enabled(), Info, Infof
}

// MonitorValue[T comparable] and CallbackList[T any]: the root's copies of connect/util.go:74, :220.

type SidecarApi struct { // net/http: bind, refresh, the exchange and the sidecar routes (§7-§20)
	stateLock  sync.Mutex
	byJwt      string                                        // the authenticated jwt
	dpopSigner func(method, url, ath string) (string, error) // the ClientKey's proof (§7.4), by crypto/ed25519
	transport  http.RoundTripper // connect leg: dials by its ClientStrategy's ConnectSettings().DialContext
	                             // (connect/net_http.go:777, connect/net.go:232), egress-bound as
	                             // connect/net_http.go:3663-3668 requires; sidecar_http: net/http's fetch
}

type Sidecar struct {
	host           SidecarHost // Store(); KeyStore() (nil: pass only); TokenSource() (nil: D-CORE-8's refresher)
	settings       *SidecarSettings
	sidecarApi     *SidecarApi
	state          *MonitorValue[SidecarState] // Locked → Unenrolled ⇄ Offline ⇄ Online (5.6); a locked
	                                           // store → Locked (5.9); only a verified SidecarRevoke → Revoked
	eventCallbacks *CallbackList[SidecarEventFunction]

	stateLock sync.Mutex
	keychain  *keychain        // nil while locked; holds this network's root key R_n (5.9)
	identity  *SidecarIdentity // ids and identity public key
	leg       *sidecarLeg      // declared per leg: !sidecar_http, a BringYourApi on the same jwt, the components
	                           // and one connect.Client per client generation; sidecar_http, the long-poll (§6.8)
}

type SidecarAction struct { // every outward action (I-8)
	Kind      SidecarActionKind // tls/ or smtp/ publish or listen; forward; expose; egress change; invite or share;
	                            // alias create or delete; agent-config write or delete in a shared repo (§16.5);
	                            // DNS user record set or delete; mail to a non-member not yet approved, or to
	                            // any non-member in a tainted run; payment
	Canonical []byte            // built by the daemon; payload_sha256 = SHA-256(Canonical)
	Risk      SidecarRisk       // max(policy, daemon classifier); an agent may only raise it
	RunId     *Id               // a decision binds (approval_id, run_id, agent_id) and authorizes at most
	AgentId   *Id               // `uses` distinct actions, each once (§16 D-MCP-11)
}

type SidecarEvent struct { // AddEventCallback, `ur status`, the sdk listener (§18.5), ur://acl/grants
	Kind       SidecarEventKind // state, approval_pending, member_added, member_removed, key_changed, refused,
	                            // admission_alarm, recovery_rebind, recovery_window, recovery_unseen (5.6),
	                            // head_alarm (§6.4)
	State      SidecarState
	Reason     SidecarStateReason // Unenrolled: expired, refused, parent_lost, session_ended, keystore_lost;
	                              // Revoked: signed (§18.5's GetStateReason)
	GroupId    *Id // membership kinds: the §10 group
	SidecarId  *Id // membership kinds: the leaf or wrapped reader; admission_alarm: the admitted sidecar;
	               // recovery_rebind: its signer; recovery_unseen: the recovered device; head_alarm: the peer
	ApprovalId *Id
	HeadAlarm  SidecarHeadAlarm // head_alarm: fork, withheld (PROOF OF WITHHOLDING), unverified, or unwitnessed
	                            // (24 h without a consistent witness; 1 h for a revocation it signed)
	Evidence   [2][]byte        // head_alarm: my pin and the peer's or api's, as §6.5 encodes them (AuthPin,
	                            // GroupHead, GenHead or RefHead); recovery_rebind at a void: the AuthPins
	                            // at which keychain.wrap was sealed to the voided binding and re-sealed (5.9)
}

type SidecarStatus struct { // Status(): `ur status`, §18.5's GetState and GetStateReason
	State       SidecarState
	Reason      SidecarStateReason
	Generation  int64     // the bound client generation (5.5)
	WitnessedAt time.Time // the newest consistent HeadCheck witness (§6.4); zero: none yet
	Unverified  [][]byte  // the open UNVERIFIED auth pins (§6.4), as AuthPin bytes; empty: none
}

type SidecarIdentityBinding struct { // 5.5; signed by the ClientKey and the identity key
	NetworkId, SidecarId, ClientId Id
	Generation                     int64 // n+1 for every new client: re-enrollment, pairing, fallback (5.8)
	ClientPublicKey                []byte
	IdentityPublicKey              []byte
	IssuedAt                       time.Time
}

type SidecarSettings struct {
	Instance, ApiUrl, PlatformUrl, AuthUrl, AppVersion string
	EvsUrl, GkmUrl, SocketsUrl, DnsUrl                 string // defaults from §19.4
	Connect               *SidecarConnectSettings      // client generations (below)
	ProtocolSettings      *SidecarProtocolSettings     // §6.6
	TokenRefreshSettings  *SidecarTokenRefreshSettings // sdk's schedule (sdk/device_token_manager.go:20-27, :266-275): jti-drawn 0.4-0.5 window, 5 min floor, 15 min retry
	KeychainSettings      *SidecarKeychainSettings     // Argon2id parameters, auto-lock, pass attempts (5 per 10 min)
	LocalSettings         *SidecarLocalSettings        // sockets, idle exit, request bound
	Mcp                   *SidecarMcpSettings          // §16
	Ingest                *SidecarIngestSettings       // §16.7
	Record                *SidecarRecordSettings       // §16.8
	ComponentQueueMessageCount, ComponentQueueByteCount int
	MemoryBudgetByteCount int64 // contains §6's process-wide reassembly, idempotency and credit caps
	StreamChunkByteCount  int
	Log                   Logger // nil: connect.DefaultLogger() (glog), adapted; sidecar_http: none unless set
}

func DefaultSidecarSettings() *SidecarSettings
func (self *Sidecar) Unlock(passphrase []byte) error // nil: the key store's wrap of U (5.9)
func (self *Sidecar) Enroll(ctx context.Context, credential *SidecarEnrollCredential) error
func (self *Sidecar) Authorize(ctx context.Context, action *SidecarAction, decision *bridge.Signed) error // nil, or *ApprovalPendingError
func (self *Sidecar) Sign(purpose string, signedType bridge.SignedType, body []byte, agentId *Id) (*bridge.Signed, error) // §6.9
func (self *Sidecar) ServiceToken(ctx context.Context, resource string, scopes []string) (string, error)
func (self *Sidecar) Status() SidecarStatus
func (self *Sidecar) AddEventCallback(callback SidecarEventFunction) func()
func (self *Sidecar) Close()
func (self *Sidecar) CloseAndWait(ctx context.Context) error

// !sidecar_http files only, with the client generations, streams, sockets, bridge, tls and smtp listeners and
// the engine host interfaces (host_*.go), since no engine runs in the page Worker (§4.4); the sidecar_http leg
// declares SidecarConnectSettings empty and NewSidecar without components.
type SidecarConnectSettings struct {
	ClientStrategySettings    *connect.ClientStrategySettings
	ClientSettings            *connect.ClientSettings // Required, no P2P; provides Network, plus Service while on tls/ or smtp/ (§13.6) and FriendsAndFamily while sharing (§8.11); never Public (§6)
	PlatformTransportSettings *connect.PlatformTransportSettings
}

type SidecarComponent interface {
	Name() string                 // "evs", "sockets", "mail", "bridge", "tls"
	Attach(env *SidecarEnv) error // per client generation; returns promptly
	Close()
}

type SidecarEnv struct { // immutable; Ctx ends with the generation
	Ctx         context.Context
	Client      *connect.Client
	Api         *connect.BringYourApi
	SidecarApi  *SidecarApi
	Identity    *SidecarIdentity
	Secrets     SidecarSecrets // keychain namespace
	Store       SidecarStore   // component directory, streaming I/O
	Subprotocol *Subprotocol   // §6: inline, zero-wait handlers; streams
	Authorize   func(ctx context.Context, action *SidecarAction, decision *bridge.Signed) error // the gate
	Log         Logger
}

func NewSidecar(ctx context.Context, host SidecarHost, components []SidecarComponent, settings *SidecarSettings) (*Sidecar, error)
func (self *Sidecar) Pair(ctx context.Context, childJwt string) error // 5.8: same network, new ClientKey, generation n+1
func (self *Sidecar) AddComponent(component SidecarComponent) (func(), error)
```

**Lifecycle.** Per client generation, `run()` builds the client, registers §6's id 21842, handles §6's `core` push, and calls `Attach` outside `stateLock`; in the `sidecar_http` leg a generation is its long-poll (§6.8), which carries `core`, and no component attaches: §18.10's kept files run on `SidecarApi` and the keychain. Complete envelopes go to their component's bounded, zero-wait queue, which drops and counts when full (connect/CODESTYLE.md:119). `StreamData` fills per-stream buffers bounded by §6.7's credit instead, since stream bytes cannot be dropped (:123); an overrun resets the stream with PROTOCOL. Callbacks never block or call `CloseAndWait` (:171).

**Outward-action gate (I-8).** Every outward method calls `Authorize`, which passes under an active approved grant (§8) or a §16.6 decision that passes its spend check ([owner decision 75](#od-75)), reserving the use durably before the effect (§16 D-MCP-11); otherwise it writes an `ApprovalRequest`, emits `approval_pending` and returns pending. In a tainted run (I-9) each outward action needs a fresh decision: the daemon spends no further use of a decision whose request was untainted (§16.6's TS1), and harness evidence counts only if the matching `requests` rule names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)). MCP, control mode, the CLI, local SMTP submission and the sdk remote backend all pass it; server-visible actions carry the decision to §8.10's gate.

### 5.5 Identity (X10)

| Level | Id | Durable | Key | Admitted by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Network | `network_id` | yes | — | platform |
| Member | `user_id` (§7) | yes | recovery keys (5.9) | login; an admin's config-repo record |
| Sidecar (a device instance in one network) | `sidecar_id` | until revoked | Ed25519 identity key ([owner decision 44](#od-44)); X-Wing ReaderKey (§10.5) | `SidecarAdmit` in the config repo (5.6) |
| Client (transport) | `client_id` | until reaped | connect ClientKey | operator-signed history |
| Agent | `agent_id` in the sidecar | per registration | Ed25519 subkey, `not_after` ≤30 d (v1) | an attribution label |

- **Binding.** `POST /sidecar/bind` appends each `SidecarIdentityBinding` (5.4) to a never-reaped log, which §6's `Hello` checks (D-PROTO-13). Each new client (5.8) binds generation n+1 under the same `sidecar_id` and identity key, keeping admissions and grants. The binding names the client id as well as its key, so a peer resolves a client to its sidecar from signed bytes (§17.9). The `sidecar_id` names MLS leaves, ReaderKeys, statements, admissions, client names and bridge addresses; the client id stays the transport, contract and policy subject. Git committers ([owner decision 81](#od-81)) and §8's `sidecar:<id>` and `client:<id>` resolve through the log, and a sidecar reads a repo iff a subject it hosts does.
- **Agents.** A device or `--instance` is one sidecar per network. Agents are attribution labels on its client (`source = agent_asserted`) holding no credential or group key; the daemon signs, decrypts and enforces per-agent reads for them. Own reach (grants, an overlay address, an ssh key) needs the agent's own sidecar under its own OS user, container or VM ([owner decision 4](#od-4)); otherwise grants attach to the sidecar, usable by any local process ([owner decision 47](#od-47)).
- **Signatures.** §6's typed `Signed` (a purpose and §6.11's `SignedType`), Ed25519 in v0: the identity key signs every statement the server stores or verifies, and approvals unless a presence key does (§16.6); agent subkeys only sealed provenance, revoked by `AgentRevoke`; the ClientKey only the binding and §7.4's DPoP proofs. A compromised identity key means a `SidecarRevoke` for compromise and a new `sidecar_id`.

### 5.6 Login, enrollment, admission, refresh, revocation

| Path | Credential (used once, then erased) | Client |
|---|---|---|
| `ur login [--invite <link>]` | §7.8's `ur-cli` (PKCE; the device grant in v1) mints a single-use, user-owned auth key (≤5 min) for the daemon, then drops the OAuth token, and offers to register a platform presence key (§16.6) | top-level (§20.8); a child after pairing (5.8, M8) |
| `ur connect --token ur-authkey-…` | A §7 auth key (expiry, uses, tags, ephemeral), whose server part alone enrollment sends (§7.8); from a pre-approved key's client-only `#<bundle>` the daemon signs its own `SidecarAdmit` with the Delegation's key and keeps only its reader key (§10.5); `urn_` keys are refused | top-level; tagged or user-owned |
| sdk host | The device's token mints the child (`admin_refused: true`); the host's `TokenSource` refreshes it (§18.7), with the core's DPoP signer installed (`Api.SetDpopSigner`) | child |

- **Enrollment.** The daemon generates the ClientKey seed, identity key, ReaderKey and `sidecar_id`, calls `POST /network/enroll` (§7) or `/network/auth-client`, declaring no provider egress unless `ur proxy` or a public exit is set (§20.8), then `POST /sidecar/bind`, and persists the keychain only if the reply confirms `admin_refused`. Until §7.4's stage 2 is live, `ur` refuses to enroll, and an enrolled daemon alarms, where an sdk `.auth_state` (sdk/local_state_auth.go:31-35) or the URnetwork extension's `chrome.storage.local` in a browser profile (extension/src/background/index.ts:134) holds a readable network `by_jwt` (D-TRUST-3). An `--ephemeral` keychain stays in memory; reaping revokes it (§7.10).
- **Admission (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112)-[114](#od-114), [126](#od-126)-[128](#od-128), [144](#od-144), [149](#od-149)).** Until a config-repo `SidecarAdmit` (§7.9) names it, a sidecar gets no peer, MLS group, wrap or grant. The rules:

```text
genesis  before the owner's first untagged device signs it (§7.9), tagged and ephemeral enrollments
         get no_genesis; a ur login device without an invite's or auth key's anchor shows a safety
         number over the genesis and its identity key for the admitter to compare (§2.8 EX5); a
         code-only recovered device, which has no admitter, passes §7.9's recovery anchor in this
         order before any commit, wrap, sealed write or further statement:
           1 it takes the config group's RK_g from its config RecoveryWrap once admitted (signers)
             or, under a restored binding, which takes no wrap, by §7.9's restored order: pending,
             it signs only its AuthorityProposal; activated, it uploads its ReaderKey but no
             KeyPackage, so no Add precedes 3, and fetches the late ReaderWrap of the current
             generation a config writer gives it (KF2), or one a later rotation stages (§10.5)
           2 that RK_g matches gen/<g>'s C_g and opens, down the ladder, the config head its newest
             verified base names
           3 the head's records chain to a genesis whose SHA-256 its own binding's genesis_sig there
             signs under the Ed25519 key its code derives
         a failed check raises head_alarm (fork, with that base's AuthPin) and it acts no further
         (§2.8 EX5)
signers  one admin: a device of a member outside the AdminSet
         alone, the member's consented device (§8.5): its own untagged devices, unless the network
           turns self_admit off; its recovery key: the same, with one admin's cosign while
           self_admit is off
         k of n: an AdminSet member's device; its existing device counts as one, and a counted
           member's recovery key may stand for that member under §7.9's recovery window and veto
           (recovery_window), so a personal network (k = 1) recovers alone after it
         restored: a binding a cascade void restored (§7.9), until a signer outside P signs it
           again, admits only through that window: its scoped admission activates 72 h after it
           is filed, with no counted cosign, unless an AdminSet device vetoes (owner decision 149)
         a tag owner's device, or an auth key's Delegation: sidecars with its tags (§7.8)
         never a read_only device (§7.9)
consent  member M's owner-bound repos (vault, mailbox, secret) take a device d only if
         consented(d, M) (§8.5): M's consented device or recovery key signed its admission, d is M's
         first device and enrolled from an invite to M, d signed the Genesis, or M's consented device
         signed OwnerConfirm{d}; never an ephemeral d; others, such as one an admin alone admitted,
         stay parked there
alarm    M's devices raise admission_alarm for every admission under M that none of them signed,
         recovery-key ones included, and approval_pending for an unconsented one (D-CORE-13); each
         raises recovery_rebind for every RecoveryRebind of M it did not itself sign, including one
         another device of M signed, offering to revoke that signer for compromise, and for every
         binding of M that §7.9's cascade voids, naming any span its keychain.wrap was sealed to
         it (5.9); every member device shows recovery_window while an authority statement with a
         recovery-key signature, or a restored binding's admission (signers), is pending, from
         §7.9's window start p, and raises recovery_unseen if it activates less than 72 h minus
         10 min after the device applied p, or if the device first verifies a valid veto only after
         applying the activation; each device that may revoke the recovered device then offers its
         revocation (§7.9); every admitted sidecar raises head_alarm for each of §6.4's alarms:
         FORK, PROOF OF WITHHOLDING, an UNVERIFIED pin, and no consistent witness (5.4)
reads    every admitted sidecar, ephemeral ones included, reads the config repo (owner decision 6;
           §8.6's ceiling excepts it)
         member devices: MLS leaves of each repo they read, at most 1,000 per group (D-KEYS-2); in
           the config group by §7.9's leaves rule (owner decision 144): live member devices rank by
           (live_since, sidecar_id), the first 1,000 are leaf-entitled and the rest read by
           per-generation wraps as agents do, moving between the two by §7.9's move rule; members
           accept a config Add or external join only of an entitled device
         config-group commits: the signer of an admission or revocation commits what it requires (an
           entitled device's Add, a leaf's Remove and its rotation, or a wrapped reader's first wrap
           or rotation), so a self-admitted device reads with no admin online; a wrapped signer
           commits no Add or Remove, only wraps and rotations, and the next leaf commit removes a
           leaf target (§7.9, §10.9); a recovery-admitted device, once anchored (genesis), self-joins
           by external commit if entitled, else reads by its RecoveryWrap, or under a restored
           binding by the ReaderWrap it anchored on, then by wraps (§7.9's commit and wrapped)
         tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars: per-generation ReaderWraps (§10.5), with no
           commit or leaf, a Delegation-admitted one at once through its Delegation's reader key;
           on data repos they default to deposit (§8.5)
revoke   any writer leaf commits the Removes a signed revocation requires, never a wrapped device;
         revoking a wrapped sidecar is a new generation not wrapped to it; a SidecarRevoke for
         compromise parks §7.9's cascade closure P from its since_n, a log position, each record
         counted from its carrying entry, never its signer's at, each parked device until a signer
         outside P confirms it; it voids the Delegations a sidecar in P signed, and those sidecars'
         recovery bindings, KeyRegisters and EvsShares until a signer outside P signs them again
         (§7.9, D-TEAM-26)
```

- **Refresh.** `sidecarTokenManager`, a root file in both legs, runs the sdk schedule on `GET /auth/refresh` through `SidecarApi` with a DPoP proof that crypto/ed25519 signs by the ClientKey (§7.4), and on a refused credential (connect's `AuthorizationClosed`, connect/transport.go:528, or a 401), against §7's 7-day, no-grace expiry (D-TEAM-14); it installs tokens in `SidecarApi` and the keychain and, where connect links, by `api.SetByJwt` and `transport.SetAuth` (:1924). A refused refresh returns the sidecar to `Unenrolled` with its identity and admission; only a `SidecarRevoke` that verifies against the config, announced by the `core` push or a refused bind, means `Revoked`; an unverifiable claim leaves it Unenrolled and alarms (`refused`). Events of an older client generation are dropped. After a Postgres restore, a refresh whose identity, binding or registration api lacks answers `restore_required`, and the daemon re-registers its identity and newest binding (`POST /sidecar/bind`, taken once the re-published projection admits the key), then its mail host keys, TLS endpoints and push token (§19.10).
- **Revocation.** `ur logout` signs a `SidecarRevoke` (`removed`) for its own `sidecar_id`, removes its client (`POST /network/remove-client`) and wipes state. A signer allowed above revokes a lost device the same way, as `lost`, or as `compromise` with `since_n` (above): the daemon proposes the first entry timed at or after the loss time the person gives, which the person may move earlier, and lists what P parks and voids before the person confirms on `/dev/tty` or in an app's UI; it signs none whose P holds its own sidecar. The server removes the revoked client (§7.10), closing its connections within about 90 s (server/session/AUTH.md:197).

### 5.7 AUTHZ1: a sidecar token must not administer the network

**Threat.** A same-user agent, inside the trust boundary ([owner decision 47](#od-47)), reads the client token and posts `/auth/code-create` for a network login. §7.4's P0 (D-TEAM-1) refuses child and admin-refused tokens on all 37 gated routes and confines `strict_exp` bearers to its sidecar-route allowlist, and D-TEAM-14 expires sidecar-held ones after 7 days, renewable only with the ClientKey's DPoP proof, all before any sidecar ships (owner decisions [45](#od-45), [103](#od-103), [131](#od-131)).

| Mitigation | Residual |
|---|---|
| Only the daemon holds the token: never in env, argv, logs, MCP, replies, or any file but the keychain (I-7) | a same-user process reading the keychain; a token copied alone renews, exchanges and mints nothing, but authenticates a transport until `exp` (Q-CORE-4 (c)) |
| Service tokens (§7.8): one audience, ClientKey-proved, never leaving the daemon; harness git uses the local git server and `git-remote-ur` (§11) | scoped, 15 min |
| No admin path in the daemon or MCP: `ur admin` and `ur login` run §7.8's `ur-cli` in the CLI process, with one-command, DPoP-bound admin tokens whose `cmd` digest binds method, path and body, used once (D-TEAM-7) | the person must check the consent code |

### 5.8 The daemon and local IPC

```text
harness --stdio-- ur (relay) ---+                                  ur daemon --instance X
git --- git-remote-ur ----------+-- unix socket / named pipe -->   local API | MCP sessions | git
ur status, ur login, app -------+   peer-credential check          a Sidecar per network --> platform

hello   {"ur_local":1,"mode":"mcp"|"control"|"hook","version","harness","agent","cwd","pid"}
        {"ur_local":1,"mode":"git","version","repo":"<net>/<repo>","service":"git-upload-pack"|"git-receive-pack"}
.ur     network = "k7q2m9"        # TOML at a project root: a label or alias
        agent = "api-refactor"    # optional default for --agent

pair    app (device client D, same network) --control socket--> daemon
        app: POST /network/auth-client {source_client_id: D, admin_refused: true} -> child C's jwt
        app --Pair(C's jwt)--> daemon: new ClientKey; POST /sidecar/bind generation n+1; remove any
                                       top-level client; the SidecarAdmit stands (it names sidecar_id)
lost    D removed or reaped -> C ends (5.3) -> daemon Unenrolled (parent_lost), identity kept -> ur login
        or re-pair
unpair  ur login -> top-level client as the next generation -> remove C
```

- **One daemon per instance.** `ur mcp`, and bare `ur` when stdin is not a terminal ([owner decision 57](#od-57)), relay to the daemon, where MCP runs (§16), never logging to stdout. If none answers, `ur` spawns `ur daemon` detached; a flock on `<state>/lock` keeps one, and an auto-spawned daemon exits when idle unless mail, sockets or bridge is on. It hosts a `Sidecar` per network, sharing the unlock key U (5.9) and MCP endpoint but no client, root key or identity key (Q-CORE-6).
- **Protocol.** After the hello, the socket carries newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 or, after a `git` hello, raw pkt-line bytes for one repo of that `<net>`'s `Sidecar` (§11.11). The mode selects a protocol, never a privilege: authority statements, admissions, `OwnerConfirm` and `KeyRegister`, and acl and bridge statements other than §16.6's own-resource filings, are signed only for a `ur` command confirmed on /dev/tty or in an app's UI. The own-resource filings (a `GrantActivate` of this sidecar's own approved request, §8.8; a `GrantRevoke` of a grant whose subject it is; its own `BridgeAddress` for its first map as a host, §17.4; the `BridgeRoute`, `BridgeMap` and `BridgeWithdraw` of its own rules, §17.8) are signed from any mode, one for an outward action only through 5.4's gate. Version skew is refused; replies never carry tokens, keys, the pass or the recovery code.
- **Authentication.** The peer uid must equal the daemon's (SO_PEERCRED; LOCAL_PEERCRED in a 0700 directory; a go-winio pipe with a user-SID DACL); same-user agents may call it ([owner decision 47](#od-47)), and outward actions still pass the gate. Control uses nothing else ([owner decision 84](#od-84)): `--port` (cli/UI.md:17-18) sets the first port of the local services (git, submission, IMAP; §11, §15), which bind `0.0.0.0/::` unless `--listen` narrows them (cli/UI.md:11), authenticate every caller and, off loopback, serve only TLS, or ssh for git ([owner decision 130](#od-130)).
- **Project file ([owner decision 23](#od-23)).** `.ur` names a label or alias, never a legacy network_name (D-DNS-2), holds no secret and may be committed. The daemon finds it from the hello's `cwd` up to the git top level or `$HOME`. A network-scoped call uses its `network` argument, else `.ur`, else the only network; otherwise it fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION naming the networks.
- **Pairing (owner decisions [4](#od-4), [87](#od-87)).** A desktop app in remote mode (§18.4) pairs over the control socket, a sandboxed app (apple/app/app.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:1129, :1762) through its app-group socket (5.9); the daemon never holds the device's token.
- **Units.** The daemon runs as the user (Q-CORE-3). `install-daemon` writes a LaunchAgent `network.ur.ur.<instance>` (macOS), `systemctl --user enable --now ur@<instance>` plus linger when headless (Linux), or a Task Scheduler logon task (Windows); `uninstall-daemon` removes it (`--purge` also revokes the client and `sidecar_id` and deletes the state).

### 5.9 Local state, keychain, OS key stores, recovery

```text
<state>  macOS ~/Library/Application Support/ur/<i>; Linux $XDG_STATE_HOME/ur/<i>;
         Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\URnetwork\ur\<i>
  sidecar.json      non-secret: urls, network/client/sidecar ids, instance id, machine-id hash
  unlock.wrap       the instance unlock key U (32 B), wrapped by the OS keystore and the pass (Argon2id
                    params, salt)
  net/<network_id>/
    keychain.wrap   R_n wrapped by U and, by HPKE, to its member's current recovery X-Wing key in n only,
                    re-sealed as the device applies each change to that member's current binding (a
                    RecoveryBind or RecoveryRebind, §7.9's cascade voiding one, or a signer outside P
                    signing a restored one again), with no HPKE copy while none is current
    keychain.ur     AEAD(R_n): n's client jwt, ClientKey seed, identity and agent keys, ReaderKey
                    (a fresh X-Wing pair every 7 days and before its 30-day not_after, never re-signed;
                    a replaced private key kept only until its not_after, for wraps staged to it,
                    §10.5), a Delegation's reader key (§7.8), a pending recovery proposal's or
                    admission's id (§7.9), §10's key cache
    authlog/        §7.9's retained log: A_k digests; the newest entries' bytes, up to HeadCheckProof's
                    64 KiB (bases as headers), and while it sends proven the proof it verified (§6.4);
                    on a member device, every entry from api's retention point on, for a site loss (§19.10)
    approvals/ runs/ restore/ <component>/   §16's approval ledger, run taint and restore points, and
                    each component's state, under keys derived from R_n
  lock, log/ (size-bounded glog)
socket   $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ur/<i>.sock; macOS DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR (104-byte sun_path), plus, for a
         sandboxed desktop app, a short-named socket in its app-group container, a group the ur
         bundle also claims (§4.10): ~/Library/Group Containers/6BGU69Q742.group.network.ur/
         (apple/app/network/network-macOS.entitlements:35-38; the direct build's group differs);
         Windows \\.\pipe\urnetwork-ur-<sid>-<i>
```

- **Instances.** Names match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}` (default `default`, or `UR_INSTANCE`). Each instance has its own state, daemon, sockets and U, and per network its own client, `sidecar_id`, R_n and persisted connect `InstanceId`, so restarts keep the resident.
- **At rest.** Each network's 32-byte random root key R_n derives an HKDF-SHA256 key per file class (`urnetwork-sidecar-v1/local/<class>`). Files are sealed in streamed chunks with XChaCha20-Poly1305 (wasm's AES is table-based), path in the AAD, via temp file, fsync, rename. A locked or failing store never resets identity (§18.5).
- **Pass (cli/UI.md:82-85).** Argon2id at 64 MiB, t=3, p=4 (RFC 9106 §4), or 19 MiB, t=2, p=1 on mobile and wasm (OWASP). The pass or the OS keystore yields U, which opens every R_n ([owner decision 23](#od-23)'s shared unlock); a pass change rewraps U, and `ur keychain rotate` rotates U and every R_n. The CLI reads the pass only from `/dev/tty` with echo off, and the pass approves nothing (owner decisions [47](#od-47), [75](#od-75)).
- **Recovery code (owner decisions [62](#od-62), [127](#od-127), [149](#od-149)).** 128 bits as 12 BIP-39 words, shown once per membership, so no recovery key links a person's networks ([owner decision 23](#od-23)) and no device keeps a master secret. It derives X-Wing and Ed25519 recovery keys, which a `RecoveryBind` config record binds to the member (§7.9); devices wrap that network's R_n and the member's repo key generations to the X-Wing key (§10.8). With the code alone, a new device restores, reading before admission only the authorization log and its member's recovery wraps (§7.9), admits itself under 5.6's signers, passes §7.9's recovery anchor in 5.6's order (genesis), then joins its groups (above 16 leaves, once one leaf is online to write the current GroupInfo) and revokes the lost devices, rotating their groups (§10.8). `ur keychain recovery-rotate` signs a `RecoveryRebind` (§7.9): the old code then admits nothing and gets no new wrap, and if §7.9's cascade voids the rebind, admits only through the recovery window and gets none until a signer outside P signs its restored binding again (5.6); it opens at once what was wrapped to it before, whatever the window or a veto, and reads the current generation until the next rotation, which `--compromise` makes a remove rotation with a path epoch at once (§10.8). A device a restored binding admits anchors on a config ReaderWrap (5.6's genesis), whose RK_g opens only the config group's sealed GroupInfo to it: it self-joins that group if entitled, KF2 adds it to its other groups once it uploads KeyPackages, and a group whose leaves are all in P opens to it only through that binding's surviving wraps; it then offers `recovery-rotate`, whose rebind gives its member a current binding again (§7.9's after).
- **Backup.** OS-keystore wraps are device-bound, so a backup restores only with the pass (U) or a network's code (its R_n); new hardware keeps the `sidecar_id` only via `--replace`, which revokes the old client. No re-seal reaches a backup sealed before it, whose `keychain.wrap` the code it was sealed to still opens, and with it the identity key, ClientKey seed, ReaderKeys and key cache. So each device whose backups may hold a sealing to a code retired for compromise, or to a binding §7.9's cascade voids (the span its `recovery_rebind` names, 5.6), is revoked for compromise and enrolled anew, never moved by `--replace`, which keeps its identity key (§7.9, §10.8); for a void, each device that may revoke it offers that revocation from a since_n at the voided binding's entry, since no keychain was sealed to that binding earlier.
- **Store states (D-CORE-15).** The OS key stores and the sdk's `SidecarKeyStore` (§18.5) answer reads with one of four statuses and writes with Ok, Locked or Failed:

```text
Present  a value that fails decoding or AEAD counts as Failed, never Absent
Locked   the sidecar enters Locked; once the store unlocks, the host calls Unlock(nil)
Failed   as Locked, and alarms; neither Locked nor Failed creates, overwrites or deletes anything
Absent   no sidecar_id recorded in sidecar.json: create U; R_n is created only at network n's first
         enrollment, with no sidecar_id recorded for n
         one recorded: the item is lost; open U by the pass, or R_n by n's recovery code, else
         Unenrolled (keystore_lost), creating nothing until the person confirms re-enrollment as a
         new device; a lost net/<network_id>/keychain.wrap is the same loss for network n
```

| Platform | Wrap of U |
|---|---|
| macOS CLI | The data protection keychain (`AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, group `<team>.network.ur.cli`) via purego, from a Developer ID `ur` bundle (§4.10; D-CORE-12) |
| Apps, extension | The host's `SidecarKeyStore` (§18.5, §18.7) |
| Windows | DPAPI |
| Linux desktop | Secret Service |
| Linux headless | The pass, else a 0600 key file with a warning |

### 5.10 Platform variants, build tags, logging, metrics, memory

| Variant | Build | Host | IPC |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI darwin | `CGO_ENABLED=0`; keychain file `darwin && !ios && !sdk_mobile_bind` (purego; GOOS=ios satisfies `darwin`; 5.11's fallbacks) | `ur daemon` | socket |
| CLI linux | `CGO_ENABLED=0`; files `linux && !android` (GOOS=android satisfies `linux`) | `ur daemon` | socket |
| CLI windows | `CGO_ENABLED=0` | `ur daemon` | pipe |
| gomobile | sdk's `sdk_mobile_bind`; the `ios_extension` leg links only §18's device role (D-SDK-1) | app process (§18) | none |
| wasm | `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm`, `_js.go` files; the page Worker builds `-tags sidecar_http`, linking no connect package: 5.4's every-leg types and `SidecarApi` carry its identity, keychain, token path (bind, DPoP refresh, exchange) and approval views (§18.10) | extension worker, ur.io pages (owner decisions [26](#od-26), [76](#od-76)) | none |

- **Settings, logs, memory.** `DefaultSidecarSettings()` is the only source of defaults (connect/CODESTYLE.md:144, :151). Logs go through `settings.Log` behind `V(n).Enabled()`, never with secrets, content or peer IPs; `SidecarStats` feeds `ur status --stats`, with no telemetry. The host sets the process limit (`sdk.SetMemoryLimit`; 32 MiB in the iOS app) and the sidecar keeps to `MemoryBudgetByteCount`.

### 5.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Each MCP process embeds a Sidecar | no daemon | N child clients or a fight over the resident; an admission and a leaf or wrap per process | rejected |
| The ClientKey signs everything | already attested | reaped with its client; unlabeled | rejected |
| Connect's types in every root file | one `Id`, `Logger` and api client | the page Worker links gVisor: a connect-only js/wasm main is 55.0 MB (§18.10) | rejected (5.4; D-SDK-19) |
| Network credential beside the client token, as in sdk's `.auth_state` (sdk/local_state_auth.go:28-37) | admin from the CLI | an admin credential agents can read | rejected |
| Share the device's client in process (X10 option (c)) | no second client | Opportunistic (sdk/device_local_provider.go:258); escapes the admin-refused mark (I-6); no sidecar role in the iOS tunnel (D-SDK-1) | ruled out ([owner decision 4](#od-4); owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| One root key per instance, wrapped to each membership's recovery key | one key | one network's recovery code opens every network's keys ([owner decision 23](#od-23)) | rejected (D-CORE-14) |
| macOS: the file-based login keychain, or a cgo leg | no bundle; Apple's C API | deprecating (D-CORE-12); cgo breaks §4.7 | fallbacks if the bundle or purego fails §22.5 |

### 5.12 Decisions proposed

**D-CORE-1 (proposed).** PLAN.md:14's jwt, client, api and encryption key are the sidecar's own `by_client_jwt`, one `connect.Client` per generation (none in the `sidecar_http` leg), the root's net/http `SidecarApi` plus, where connect links, `BringYourApi`, and its network's keychain root key R_n; files outside `!sidecar_http` use only the root's `Id`, `Logger`, `MonitorValue` and `CallbackList` (5.4). *Why:* PLAN.md:7; an agent-readable network credential is an admin credential; importing connect links gVisor (5.3).

**D-CORE-2 (proposed).** `NewSidecar` returns a running Sidecar with its components attached; there is no `Start`. *Why:* connect/CODESTYLE.md:169.

**D-CORE-3 (proposed).** Envelopes go to bounded zero-wait component queues and stream bytes to credit-bounded buffers (5.4). *Why:* handlers must not block (connect/subprotocol.go:77-85); stream bytes cannot be dropped (connect/CODESTYLE.md:123).

**D-CORE-4 (proposed).** One client per sidecar, a child of the device client where an sdk host or pairing provides one, else top-level; agents are labels on it unless they run their own sidecar. *Why:* [owner decision 4](#od-4).

**D-CORE-5 (proposed).** Durable identity is the `sidecar_id` and identity key, admitted by a config-repo `SidecarAdmit` and bound to each client generation, its id and key, by a never-reaped, dual-signed binding. *Why:* clients are reaped and re-parented; operator attestation could add readers.

**D-CORE-6 (proposed).** The identity key signs every statement; agent subkeys sign only sealed provenance. *Why:* domain separation; survival across client generations; no agent id on the server (§11.5).

**D-CORE-7 (proposed).** Enrollment uses only one-time or scoped credentials, never a network credential or `urn_` key; the daemon declares no provider egress by default and fails closed without the admin-refused mark. *Why:* AUTHZ1, D-TEAM-6, §20.8.

**D-CORE-8 (proposed).** The core reimplements the sdk refresh schedule, and a refused refresh ends the client generation, not the sidecar; only a verified `SidecarRevoke` revokes. *Why:* connect has no refresh, sdk is not importable (§4.6), and a lost client is no revocation.

**D-CORE-9 (proposed).** One daemon per instance hosts a `Sidecar` per network behind uid-checked sockets or a pipe that return no secrets and grant nothing by mode. *Why:* one owner of the clients and keychain; owner decisions [23](#od-23), [84](#od-84).

**D-CORE-10 (proposed).** A random root key seals local files with XChaCha20-Poly1305, one per network, each wrapped by the instance unlock key, which the OS keystore and the pass wrap, and by only that network's recovery key (D-CORE-14). *Why:* cli/UI.md:82-85; unattended start; owner decisions [23](#od-23), [62](#od-62).

**D-CORE-11 (proposed).** Every outward action passes `Sidecar.Authorize` from every entry point, under an approved grant or a §16.6 decision labeled by its evidence, each use reserved before its effect (§16 D-MCP-11). *Why:* any same-user process can drive the CLI or control mode ([owner decision 75](#od-75)).

**D-CORE-12 (proposed).** macOS wraps the unlock key in the data protection keychain via purego, from a bundled `ur`. *Why:* §4 forbids cgo; a bare CLI cannot use access groups; TN3137 puts the file-based keychain "on the road to deprecation" (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3137-on-mac-keychains).

**D-CORE-13 (proposed).** Members' devices alarm as 5.6 states and sign `OwnerConfirm` only through `ur approve` on `/dev/tty` or the app after the safety-number check, never MCP. *Why:* [owner decision 126](#od-126); no rogue admin or stolen recovery code adds a reader, and no stolen device rebinds its member's code, unseen.

**D-CORE-14 (proposed).** Local roots are per network under one instance unlock key. *Why:* [owner decision 23](#od-23)'s shared unlock must not let one network's recovery code open another's keys.

**D-CORE-15 (proposed).** No store state but `Absent`, with no recorded `sidecar_id`, creates a root key; a lost item asks the person before a new identity. *Why:* a lock or a store fault must never reset identity.

### 5.13 Open questions

**Q-CORE-1.** [X10] What client identity does a sidecar run under? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 4](#od-4)):** its own Required client (D-CORE-4, 5.8), never the device's own client (5.11). *Residual:* none.

**Q-CORE-2.** Cross-cutting. How do standalone and cloud-VM sidecars count? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 4](#od-4)):** one declaring no egress is exempt from `concurrent_clients` and the 100-client cap and counts against `sidecar_clients` (§20.8, Q-QUOTA-4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-CORE-3.** Does the daemon run as the user or a service account? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** the user, everywhere, since agents are inside the device trust boundary ([owner decision 47](#od-47)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-CORE-4.** Cross-cutting (§6, §7). Must a sidecar prove possession of its ClientKey? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (b) in v0: a `strict_exp` bearer adds a DPoP proof (RFC 9449) by its ClientKey on refresh, the token exchange and `POST /network/auth-client` (§7.4), the jti single-use and the key the newest bound one; sdk hosts carry it through `Api.SetDpopSigner`, installed by sdk/sidecar.go, before D-CORE-8's refresher is switched off on any host; (c), proof on transport auth, later, with its residual stated in §7.4. *Residual:* none.

**Q-CORE-5.** Is the recovery code also an MLS recovery member? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 62](#od-62)):** no; it derives keys for §10.8's recovery wraps (5.9), and an admin re-add restores team repos, not owner-bound ones ([owner decision 126](#od-126)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-CORE-6.** Cross-cutting. How does one device join several networks? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 23](#od-23)):** one daemon hosts a `Sidecar` per network (5.8), sharing the keychain unlock and MCP endpoint but no client, root key or identity key; a team sidecar is top-level there (§20.8). *Residual:* none.

### 5.14 Departures from PLAN.md

None: PLAN.md:14 and :59's git identity hold, and D-CORE-1 reads "encryption key". Bare `ur` on a terminal is §16's departure from PLAN.md:20 ([owner decision 57](#od-57)).

### 5.15 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the 5.4 API, its alarms, state reasons and `Status()` with `witnessed_at` and open UNVERIFIED pins; its every-leg root types and `SidecarApi`; the identity key, ReaderKey and binding; the client side of admission, owner consent, pairing and recovery; the per-network keychain and its store states; 5.8's local JSON-RPC, `git` mode and `.ur` rules.
- **Consumes:** §6 (id 21842, typed `Signed` and §6.11's `SignedType`, both in `protocol/bridge`, `Hello`, `core` push, `SidecarProtocolSettings`, HeadCheck's `witnessed_at` and alarms); §7 (enrollment, auth keys and their client-only bundle, Delegations, `ur-cli`, token exchange, P0 with its route allowlist and DPoP proof, D-TEAM-14, config records, the leaves rule); §8 (`autogroup:sidecar`, `sidecar:<id>`, consent); §10 (ReaderWraps, recovery wraps, external commits, the config group's leaves and wraps); §11.11; §16 (`ur approve`, D-MCP-11's ledger, presence keys, the `Mcp`, `Ingest` and `Record` settings); §18 (`TokenSource`, `SidecarKeyStore`, remote mode, `sidecar_http`); §19.10; §20.8; §4 (purego, the bundle, §4.4's build tags).
- **Subprotocol messages:** `core` push (server → sidecar: a revocation hint, verified against the config (5.6); forced resync; §6).
- **API routes:** existing `POST /network/auth-client` (also the pairing child) and `POST /network/remove-client` (OwnClient), `GET /auth/refresh` (Client), auth-client and refresh taking a `strict_exp` bearer's DPoP proof (§7.4); refresh gains one error, `restore_required` (5.6, §19.10). New, classified by §7:
  - `POST /sidecar/bind` (Client; also re-registration after a restore);
  - `GET /sidecar/identity/<sidecar_id>` (Client, for the caller's own network or one with an active §8.11 share): `identity_public_key`, `identity_alg`, `status` and the current binding, never `user_id`.
- **Tables:** owned by api; migration ≥926; never reaped, but deleted with their network.
  - `sidecar_identity(sidecar_id, network_id, identity_public_key, identity_alg, status, create_time, revoke_time)`;
  - `sidecar_identity_binding(sidecar_id, generation, client_id, client_public_key, signatures, create_time)`, append-only.
- **Services and config:** no new server service; 5.8's client units, the `.ur` file and the macOS bundle.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §7.9 and §8.8 define the signers, `self_admit`, the recovery window and its start p, how a restored binding's scoped admission enters it ([owner decision 149](#od-149)), its veto, a late veto's precedence and `recovery_unseen`, the rebind alarm, the config group's leaves rule ([owner decision 144](#od-144)), `RecoveryBind`, `OwnerConfirm`, `SidecarRevoke`'s reasons and compromise cascade from `since_n`, the voids at which 5.6 alarms and 5.9 re-seals, `no_genesis` and the recovery `anchor` with its `restored` order, by which a device a restored binding admitted, which no RecoveryWrap reaches until that binding is signed again, anchors on the late config ReaderWrap a config writer gives it (KF2) or a later rotation stages (§10.5) before it uploads a KeyPackage or self-joins; §7.4 the DPoP rule and stage 2's wait for the app and extension releases; §10 makes member devices the leaves (in the config group the first 1,000 by §7.9's rank, the rest wrapped), agents wrapped readers and the signing leaf the config group's committer (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128)), and parks unconsented devices; §6.6 and §16 define `SidecarProtocolSettings` and the `Mcp`, `Ingest` and `Record` settings, and §16.6 the own-resource filings 5.8 admits from any mode and TS1's refusal (5.4); §7.9's retain row and fold cadence bound the log 5.9 retains, and §18.4 applies them per host; §6.4 and §7.9's anchor define `head_alarm`'s alarms; §18.5 relays 5.4's alarms, `recovery_rebind` (at a void too) and `head_alarm` included, offers admins the veto of a restored binding's admission, and maps its state reasons; §18.10's leg links only 5.4's every-leg files; §11.11 serves the `git` mode.

### 5.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A same-user agent uses the sidecar's token or keys ([owner decision 47](#od-47)) | High | High | the P0, D-TEAM-14, ClientKey proofs, the gate |
| A same-uid process, such as a prompt-injected agent's shell, forges a PermissionRequest hook event (owner decisions [47](#od-47), [75](#od-75)) | Medium | High | §16.6's presence prompt and the presence key `ur login` offers; harness evidence never signs key, consent or authority statements, and in a tainted run counts only where a `requests` rule names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)); records mark `source = hook` |
| The app's `.auth_state` or the extension's `chrome.storage.local` on the same host holds a network `by_jwt` | Medium | Critical | §7.4's stage 2, before the first desktop sidecar, waits for the app (§18.7) and extension releases that stop persisting it ([owner decision 45](#od-45)); until then, preview networks only and 5.6's enrollment refusal (D-TRUST-3) |
| A sidecar ships before the P0 | Medium | Critical | fail closed (D-CORE-7) |
| A store loses its item, or a host reports a lock as absence | Medium | High | D-CORE-15: `keystore_lost` and the person's confirmation, never a silent new identity; the pass's wrap of U |
| An approver skips the safety-number comparison | Medium | High | invites and auth keys carry the genesis; every device sees admissions; HeadCheck (§6) |
| A paired daemon's parent client is removed or reaped (5.3), ending its child | Medium | Medium | identity and admission survive; `ur login` re-binds (5.8) |
| Losing every device and the code loses data | Low | High | recovery wraps; admin re-add ([owner decision 62](#od-62)) |
| A rogue or compromised admin admits a device under a member | Medium | High | owner-bound repos refuse it without consent; the member's devices alarm ([owner decision 126](#od-126)) |
| A stolen recovery code, or the code a stolen device rebinds its member to, with that member's login or the operator's help, reads its wraps at once, whatever the window or a veto, until a compromise rebind or §7.9's cascade voids its binding, and opens keychain backups sealed to it; with `self_admit` on, for a member outside the AdminSet, it also admits a device at once, which reads the member's repos until revoked (owner decisions [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126), [127](#od-127), [149](#od-149)) | Low | High | the member's devices alarm (`recovery_rebind` at the rebind and at its void) and revoke it; `ur keychain recovery-rotate --compromise`, then revoking for compromise and enrolling anew each device whose backups may hold a sealing to it (5.9); no device stores the code |

### 5.17 Phasing

- **v0 (§23 M1-M3)**, after §7's P0 and D-TEAM-14: M1, the daemon on darwin, linux and windows, top-level enrollment (`ur connect --token`, `ur login`), `/sidecar/bind`, refresh with DPoP proofs and `restore_required`, fail-closed, the per-network keychain under U with D-CORE-15's store states, the local API, and 5.4's every-leg root types and `SidecarApi`, which §4.7's `sidecar_http` check holds from M1; M2, config-repo admission and revocation with the key authority, owner consent, alarms, the config group's leaves and wraps, and ReaderKeys (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [112](#od-112), [114](#od-114), [126](#od-126), [127](#od-127), [144](#od-144)), the recovery code, its wraps of R_n and its rotation, and the `git` mode (§11); M3, the gate with D-MCP-11's reserved uses and [owner decision 142](#od-142)'s tainted-run rule, and `.ur`, with §16.
- **v0, app hosts (§23 M8):** sdk hosts and desktop pairing (§18.17).
- **Browser (§18.17):** the HTTPS-only wasm page Worker, built `-tags sidecar_http`, for ur.io/recurd at M4 and the team console at M6 (owner decisions [26](#od-26), [76](#od-76)).
- **v1 (§23 M6):** several networks per daemon, with team networks (owner decisions [23](#od-23), [55](#od-55)); the RFC 8628 device grant; agent subkeys.
- **Later:** the extension's Worker and wasm streams (C4); transport proof of possession (Q-CORE-4 (c)).

## 6. The sidecar subprotocol: envelope, RPC, streams, server push

### 6.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns the sidecar's wire protocol on connect's subprotocol layer: id, envelope, chunking, RPC, streams, push (X8), peer authentication, `HeadCheck` and its control contracts, typed `Signed`, encryption and contract modes, and the message, signed-type, code and topic registries. Sockets go to §9, policy and the config repo to §7 and §8, the witness rule to §2, evs notifications to §11, keys to §5 and §10, payer and escrow to §20 (X11), wakes to §18 and §19, connect changes to §4 (X9).

### 6.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-PROTO-1 | Sidecar traffic rides connect; the sidecar depends only on connect | PLAN.md:7 |
| R-PROTO-2 | The subprotocol protobufs live in `sidecar/protocol` | PLAN.md:15-16 |
| R-PROTO-3 | Changes to a subscribed dir or subpath are notified "via a subprotocol message" | PLAN.md:55 |
| R-PROTO-4 | tlsedge reaches one listener over the subprotocol after find-listener and accept | PLAN.md:82 |
| R-PROTO-5 | Rules affecting a client are "sent in real time" | PLAN.md:119 |
| R-PROTO-6 | Every frame, with overheads, fits one 16 KiB transport message; connect does not fragment | connect/transfer.go:1700-1724 |
| R-PROTO-7 | Handlers never block and copy what they keep | connect/subprotocol.go:77-85 |
| R-PROTO-8 | Residents and relays cannot read peer traffic; pushes are hints, never content | CONVENTIONS §0; [owner decision 17](#od-17) |
| R-PROTO-9 | Memory is bounded per peer and per process, within §18.4's mobile budgets | [R:sdk-clients](design-research/sdk-clients.md) |
| R-PROTO-10 | Every ack has stated semantics; a transfer ack is not delivery | connect/transfer.go:17309-17335 |
| R-PROTO-11 | Sidecar connect traffic runs e2e Required, never Opportunistic or Off | CONVENTIONS §0 |
| R-PROTO-12 | Any admitted reader sidecar, agents included, can witness a writer's pins, whatever the network's policy | [owner decision 129](#od-129); derived |

### 6.3 What exists today

- **Registration.** Ids below 1024 are refused, the reserved variants are unexported, and each id has one typed codec (connect/subprotocol.go:46-50, :512-535).
- **Dispatch.** Inline, with no source check; ControlId refuses sends and has no contract or e2e session (connect/subprotocol.go:590-651, :902-905; connect/transfer_encrypt.go:3684-3686).
- **Size and order.** A 16 KiB floor and pool classes up to 8 KiB (connect/transfer.go:1700-1724; connect/message_pool.go:423-431); order holds within a send sequence, which 60 s without an ack ends (connect/transfer.go:5781-5796, :904).
- **Encryption.** Off by default, Opportunistic in the sdk provider (sdk/device_local_provider.go:258). Required holds sends and discards received plaintext after acking it (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:470-497). `Peer` exposes no session key (connect/transfer.go:608-620).

Missing: peer RPC, streams, flow control, application acks, sidecar push (residents send only listener-produced control frames, with no ack callback, server/connect/resident.go:4901-4908, though `Client.Send` takes one per frame, connect/transfer.go:4228-4235), and a source check on ControlId frames over P2P.

### 6.4 Id allocation, versioning, negotiation, peer identity

- **Id.** One public id, `sidecar.SubprotocolId = 0x5552` (21842, "UR"), registered per client with `connect.RegisterSubprotocol`; 21843-21851 are held, and sdk refuses 21842-21851 for apps (§18). An inner `type` (§6.11) puts all services behind one dispatcher.
- **Versioning.** `version` is the wire major (1). An unknown major gets `Error{VERSION}` with the receiver's range, an unknown type UNIMPLEMENTED; unknown fields are skipped, and an unknown code fails its call or stream without retry.
- **Hello.** `Hello`/`HelloResult` carry versions, features, limits and the sender's `SidecarIdentityBinding` (§5.5).
