| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service pushes to the listener first (X8) | Early refusal | A non-e2e ControlId push per connection (§6.8) | Rejected |
| Per-listener MAC ticket (contract pattern) | Cheap verify | Server holds the keys; no receipt | Rejected |
| 4-tuple hash (SO_REUSEPORT) | Stateless, sticky | Load-blind; aborts a closing socket's queue without `tcp_migrate_req` ([R:ext-edge](design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.10) | Opt-in affinity |
| Presence-only liveness | No heartbeats | Residents outlive disconnects ~5 min (`server/CLIENTCLOSE.md`); no load data | Rejected |
| Edge-delegated ticket keys | Edges survive a sockets outage | Keys on edge hosts; C9 still needs Redis | Later |
| Plaintext application names | Server-side globs | URnetwork reads every internal name | Rejected ([owner decision 67](#od-67)) |
| One HMAC per whole name | Hides depth | No server-side prefix grants | Rejected |
| `ur share` as an evs object sealed under a link-fragment key | Works while the sharer is offline | Changes format 1, which freezes at M2 | Rejected (D-SOCK-16) |

### 9.12 Decisions proposed

**D-SOCK-1 (proposed).** Key sockets on `(network_id, name)`, resolving `<net>` per call. *Why:* names are mutable and reclaimable.

**D-SOCK-2 (proposed).** Use 9.4's namespaces and host forms, refusing deeper names. *Why:* one rule for §13-§15; a wildcard covers one label, and [owner decision 40](#od-40)'s scopes add one.

**D-SOCK-3 (proposed).** Registrations are 45 s leases renewed every 15 s by the full set, in pages of at most 1,024 entries (9.5), carrying load. *Why:* one idempotent path; Redis loss heals in one interval.

**D-SOCK-4 (proposed).** Find returns single-use 30 s Ed25519 tickets (primary, backup) carrying the grant expiry; the service never contacts listeners. *Why:* push stays off the connection path; tickets are reach evidence.

**D-SOCK-5 (proposed).** Schedule by weighted P2C on `(est + 1) / weight` with listener caps, opt-in affinity, a per-dialer share cap and 64-listener samples. *Why:* load-aware, stale-tolerant and bounded.

**D-SOCK-6 (proposed).** Dial with a 5 s accept timeout, the backup ticket, then ≤3 Finds carrying failed tickets; ejection needs reporters from 2 networks. *Why:* bounded latency; a lying reporter harms only itself.

**D-SOCK-7 (proposed).** Keep state in Redis Cluster with per-group hash tags and field TTLs. *Why:* warp has no key routing; per-network tags create hot nodes.

**D-SOCK-8 (proposed).** Adopt 9.9's `net.Listener`/`net.Conn` API with syscall-compatible errors. *Why:* existing Go code and retry logic work unchanged.

**D-SOCK-9 (proposed).** Delete registrations on `{X}c_removed`; keep no per-dial record beyond §2.8's sock-2 fields (≤300 s) and sock-3 pairs (≤24 h). *Why:* reuses the removal signal; minimal metadata.

**D-SOCK-10 (proposed).** Host the engine as `server/cli/sockets` with Client-class routes, sidecar-classified (§7.4). *Why:* registration load stays off `api`.

**D-SOCK-11 (proposed).** Platform services listen as `ur/<service>` in `urnetwork-edge`, authorized by the service. *Why:* sidecars reach smtpedge through the same Find and Service path.

**D-SOCK-12 (proposed).** Edge tickets bind one of the caller's K clients, and edge Finds write the `{svc_}` pair authorizing C9 until the grant ends; source equality holds for edge tickets too, and only the Hello check is waived (9.6). *Why:* step 3 stays exact; contracts outlive the ticket, not the grant.

**D-SOCK-13 (proposed).** Send names outside `tls/`, `smtp/` and `ur/` only as 9.4's HMAC token paths, sealed for listings, under the config repo's `K_sock`, rotated on §11.6's triggers. *Why:* [owner decision 67](#od-67), built like evs paths ([owner decision 2](#od-2)); prefix grants still work.

**D-SOCK-14 (proposed).** Gate registrations and Finds on the signed id-only projection (§7.9, §8); listener and dialer each re-derive the grant from the config repo. *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [6](#od-6) and [72](#od-72): a breached server can only deny or delay.

**D-SOCK-15 (proposed).** System protection bounds registration and Find work, never the number of names or established use: a per-client token bucket charges each Find and each registration page of at most 1,024 entries, larger sets going as pages (9.5), and a spend check precedes signing (9.6, 9.10). *Why:* [owner decision 66](#od-66) allows system-protection bounds but no count caps; an authenticated byte-free client otherwise pins Redis and the signing key.

**D-SOCK-16 (proposed).** `ur share` is a live sharer: a blinded `share/<token>` socket, a fragment-borne 256-bit secret, a durable use count and an expiry (24 h by default, at most 30 days), on the transfer balance, available while the sharing sidecar runs (9.9). *Why:* R-CTX-31; no link outlives its expiry, even with unlimited uses; an evs object under a link key would change format 1, which freezes at M2.

### 9.13 Open questions

**Q-SOCK-1.** Is load-aware weighted P2C, with opt-in affinity, an acceptable reading of PLAN.md:69's "similar to socket reuse on linux"? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 65](#od-65)):** yes, as 9.7 designs, with drain and retry. *Residual:* none.

**Q-SOCK-2.** Do abuse caps contradict "IP and port forward [unlimited]" (PLAN.md:359)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 66](#od-66)):** yes, so none apply; the transfer balance alone limits use, and 9.10 keeps overload protection. *Residual:* none.

**Q-SOCK-3.** Which relationship carries cross-network streams (X11, §20)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** Q-PROTO-3 (b), accepted with [owner decision 11](#od-11): Service (C9) for edges, authorized by 9.6's pair; shares ride §17's IP path as FriendsAndFamily ([owner decision 86](#od-86)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SOCK-4.** Should application names be blinded from the server? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 67](#od-67)):** yes, as 9.4's token paths under the config repo's `K_sock` (D-SOCK-13); public edge names stay plaintext, and clients resolve names locally. *Residual:* none.

### 9.14 Departures from PLAN.md

- The scheduler is load-aware, not a 4-tuple hash (Q-SOCK-1, [owner decision 65](#od-65)).
- Internal names reach the server blinded (Q-SOCK-4, [owner decision 67](#od-67)).
- PLAN.md:74: other networks reach a listener by IP through a §17 share, not a §9 dial (§8.16; Q-BRIDGE-6, [owner decision 86](#od-86)).
- PLAN.md:82's tls edge "opens a client on a network": edges are `urnetwork-edge` platform clients in Service mode (§13.14, Q-TLS-5; owner decisions [11](#od-11), [59](#od-59)).

### 9.15 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the grammar, namespaces and token paths; registry, scheduler, tickets, admission; the control-plane bounds; `{svc_}` pairs; hooks; `SocketHint`; the Go API, `ur socket` and `ur share`.
- **Consumes:** §6 streams, `StreamRejectCode`, `Signed`, the Hello check, topic `sock`, Required mode; §4 C9; §5 identity keys, `Authorize`, local file classes; §7.9's authorization log and projection (§8's rows and audiences, statements, revocations); the config repo's `K_sock` and policy; §12 resolution; §13-§15 edge dialers, hooks; §16's reserve-before-effect ledger (D-MCP-11); §19, §20 limits and `OverLimit`; §21 suspensions.
- **Subprotocol messages:** `SocketHint` (0x1001, ControlId→client, topic `sock`; revocation, forced drain); `SignedSocketTicket` in `StreamOpen.ticket`; `StreamRejectCode` `retry|busy|denied|invalid|quota` (1-5; 0 unspecified) in `StreamReject.code`; on `share/` streams, 9.9's fixed-width share header.
- **API routes** (`/socket/*` is sidecar-classified, on §7.4's `strict_exp` allowlist): `POST /socket/registrations` (Client; 9.5, pages of ≤1,024 entries; statuses, `server_time`, keys); `POST /socket/find` (Client; 9.6, errors 9.9; platform callers add K client ids); `GET /socket/list` (Client, same network; token paths, edge and sealed names); `GET /socket/keys` (Public).
- **Tables:** none (9.8's Redis keys, behind `SocketStore`).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/sockets`; vault ticket keys; pro.yml `tls_endpoints`; `sockets_control_qps` and `urnetwork_edge` (the `urnetwork-edge` network id) in `config/<env>/sidecar.yml` (§6.10.1, §19.11).
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §4.5's engine stores include `SocketStore`, with field TTLs and an atomic pick-and-increment.
  - §7.9's projection lists Team scopes (9.4); §11.6 keeps the path-epoch triggers 9.4 cites, authorization expiries batched with shrinks.
  - §13.7 dispatches on `AppMode` (D-TLS-13) and defines a raw endpoint's `link` check; §20.7's `OverLimit` lists spent networks within 5 s.
  - §22.5 tests 9.5's pages (a 3,000-name set as three pages, range-scoped unlisten, out-of-range and stale pages refused, one interval rebuilding the set after Redis loss); fixed vectors for 9.4's `K_tok` and `K_seal`, tokens and 152 B seals, a moved or mismatched seal dropped; and 9.9's share: no get or resume at or past `expire_millis`, a live stream reset there, a sharer restarted past it serving nothing, `--expires` over 30 days refused, and uses never exceeded across a crash after a Reserve.

### 9.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A dead listener costs 5 s until skipped | Medium | Medium | Backup ticket; exclusion; 45 s lease |
| A leaked signing key forges tickets until rotation | Low | High | Vault; rotation; both ends' checks refuse unauthorized streams |
| Reconnect storms, uncapped groups or byte-free clients load the service | Medium | Medium | Jitter; `retry_after_ms`; sampling; the per-client bucket and pre-sign spend check (D-SOCK-15); fair queuing; shedding |
| The bucket delays a legitimate client making over 50 calls a second: opening that many streams, or renewing over about 768,000 names (750 pages per 15 s) | Low | Low | Burst 500; `retry_after_ms`; 45 s leases outlast a late page; `find_total` and `registration_calls_total{result}` show it; sidecar.yml tunes the bound |
| Edge names are public; token paths show structure; a dropped or expired reader, with server help, tests guessed names until `K_sock` rotates | High | Low | §2.8 rows; rotation and its alarm (9.4) |
| A blanket `listen` grant (§8.5's grant 1) lets any member's untagged device join an application group and take dials | Medium | Medium | `exclusive`; narrower `listen` rules |
| A sockets or Redis outage fails Finds (`unavailable`) and new edge connections; streams stay up | Low | High | Every lb host; failover; §19.10; SLO burn pages the out-of-hours rota ([owner decision 143](#od-143)) |
| Dialers inflate `est` or report falsely | Medium | Medium | 9.7's per-dialer share cap, decay, two-network ejection |
| A leaked share link lets any sidecar of the network redeem its remaining uses until it expires | Medium | Medium | `--count`; `--expires` (24 h default); `ur share rm`; each Reserve names the getter |

### 9.17 Phasing

- **v0 (§23 M5):** the `sockets` service with 9.10's bounds; blinded application names; `tls/` with §13, `AppMode` included; tickets, P2C and 9.7's per-dialer cap; `SocketHint`; the Go API; `ur socket` and `ur share`; MCP tools. Blocked by §6 streams, §5 identity, the config repo and projection (X3, M2) and §4's C9.
- **v0, mail track:** `smtp/` with §15 (M7); `ur/` once §14 passes D-SMTP-16's gate, DATA mode included (M9; owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99), [125](#od-125)).
- **v1 (M6):** affinity, with §13; Team scope hosts (owner decisions [40](#od-40), [55](#od-55), [58](#od-58)), the `smtp/` ones with §15.
- **Later:** region-aware selection (one lb site today, [R:ext-edge](design-research/ext-edge.md) §5 R8), slow start, edge-delegated ticket keys, registration over push.

## 10. Group keys for evs: MLS and the GKM service

### 10.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns X12: the in-house MLS subset, ciphersuite, credentials and groups; GKM, stateless over metadata-cluster objects (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [145](#od-145)); the key hierarchy, generations, key holders and their wraps, the write-gate predicate, membership flows and committers, revocation, erasure, recovery, re-seeding, key domains and sizes. §5 owns the identity key and recovery code, §6 push and `HeadCheck`, §7.9 the config repo, the authorization log and the config group's `leaves` rule, §8 readers and consent, §11 the object format, placement and the gate's enforcement, and §19 the file cluster.

### 10.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-KEYS-1 | MLS (RFC 9420) secures evs from v0 | PLAN.md:44; [owner decision 1](#od-1) |
| R-KEYS-2 | One directory = one git repo, under "one session key stored in GKM" | PLAN.md:53 |
| R-KEYS-3 | Lazy rewrap: a client that detects a needed rewrap sends a checkpoint | PLAN.md:47-50, :338 |
| R-KEYS-4 | Forward-only revocation: a removed or expired holder reads nothing new | PLAN.md:149, :167-168; I-15 |
| R-KEYS-5 | One accepted Commit per epoch | PLAN.md:157-161; RFC 9420 §14 |
| R-KEYS-6 | No server holds a group secret, epoch key or file key; gkm sees ciphertext and 10.6's headers | CONVENTIONS §0; PLAN.md:221; I-1; [owner decision 115](#od-115) |
| R-KEYS-7 | MLS built in house in the sidecar repo, pure Go, no cgo | owner rule 1; [owner decision 43](#od-43); sdk/js/Makefile:69 |
| R-KEYS-8 | A breached server yields only ciphertext and listed metadata and adds no reader | P5:745 |
| R-KEYS-9 | Two key domains: sessions for their author, others reading only by consent or as the audit reader; actions and approvals for admins | P5:579, :640; MK2:482-486; [owner decision 126](#od-126) |
| R-KEYS-10 | Per-entry keys for records from the first release | REC:217-223; [owner decision 61](#od-61) |
| R-KEYS-11 | MLS membership follows the signed readers, which clients verify; agents, and config readers past a network's first 1,000 member devices, hold wraps, so no member-device cap applies | owner decisions [3](#od-3), [6](#od-6), [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144); §8.12 |
| R-KEYS-12 | Ciphertext resists harvest-now-decrypt-later by a passive adversary | [R:ext-storage-crypto](design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.5, §2.12; [owner decision 44](#od-44) |
| R-KEYS-13 | Signed grants, admissions and revocations decide membership, waiting for no admin; members update their own leaves | owner decisions [7](#od-7), [8](#od-8), [113](#od-113), [128](#od-128) |
| R-KEYS-14 | gkm's durable state is objects on its repo's metadata cluster, never Postgres or Redis, written within §11.13's NVMe write budget; acks are Redis soft state | owner decisions [2](#od-2), [136](#od-136), [140](#od-140), [145](#od-145) |

### 10.3 What exists today

- **GKM** appears only at PLAN.md:53; no repo has code for it [R:ext-storage-crypto](design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md).
- **Go 1.27.3** (connect/go.mod:3). `crypto/hpke` implements X-Wing as `MLKEM768X25519()`, KEM 0x647a, from draft-ietf-hpke-pq (GOROOT/src/crypto/hpke/pq.go:21, :39-41); `crypto/mldsa` arrived in Go 1.27 (GOROOT/api/go1.27.txt:4).
- **Constraints.** The browser build is `CGO_ENABLED=0` (sdk/js/Makefile:69). server's `BlobStore` has `PutIfAbsent` but no Delete, If-Match or ranged read (server/blob.go:160-192); `ServiceHost.Blobs` adds them, per metadata cluster (§4.5, §19).
- **Test material** (2026-11-03). The mlswg's 16 vector files carry only RFC 9420's classical suites (https://github.com/mlswg/mls-implementations/tree/main/test-vectors). MIT differential peers: thomas-vilte/mls-go v1.6.0 (0x0001-0x0003; [R:ext-storage-crypto](design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.4); tmc/mls, whose provisional 0x004F has exactly 0x0010's algorithms (wire.go:33-50); OpenMLS, whose unregistered 0x004D pairs X-Wing with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (https://cryspen.com/post/pq-openmls/).

### 10.4 Implementation, ciphersuite, credentials

**Subset (D-KEYS-12).** Only what evs uses; anything else is refused when parsed.

| RFC 9420 feature | v0 |
|---|---|
| Tree math; codec, mls10 only (§6, App. C) | yes |
| Labeled crypto, key schedule, exporter (§5, §8) | yes |
| Secret tree, PrivateMessage, transcript hashes (§6.3, §8.2, §9) | handshakes only |
| TreeKEM, parent and tree hashes, validation (§7) | yes |
| Add, Remove, GroupContextExtensions, inline (§12.1); path-only commits for self-update (§12.4) | yes |
| Welcome, `ratchet_tree`, ExternalInit (§12.4.3) | external commits only to resync or recover |
| KeyPackages, last resort; credential 0xF552 (§10, §16.8, §17.5) | yes |
| PSK, ReInit, branching, application messages, external senders, standalone and Update proposals | refused |

**Conformance.** No vectors exist for 0x0010, so every mlswg vector file covering a v0 feature runs under 0x0001; 0x0010 adds X-Wing known-answer tests (KATs) and [owner decision 43](#od-43)'s differential runs: mls-go under 0x0001, tmc/mls under 0x004F mapped to 0x0010, and OpenMLS's 0x004D once an M0 KAT matches its X-Wing to Go's. **The 0x0010 gate (D-KEYS-10)** adds what those cannot show:

```text
specified  the MLS wire (credential 0xF552, GkmCommitHeader, GenRotate, ur_group) and suite 0x0010, at M2's
           entry review; no field is removed after it
frozen     at M2's exit review (D-PHASE-7), on §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact:
  kem      X-Wing KATs: tmc/mls's encapsulation and decapsulation equal Go's crypto/hpke MLKEM768X25519() on
           fixed seeds
  stacks   one scripted lifecycle in both directions between mls_* and tmc/mls (0x004F mapped to 0x0010): at
           least 10 epochs with a Welcome, path commits, a Remove, an external commit with ExternalInit and a
           PrivateMessage decrypted per epoch, both sides computing equal epoch_authenticator and "UR evs 1.0
           kek" exporter outputs
  ladder   GenWrap's, LeafWrap's and GenLink's AAD (10.5), reproduced by mlsinterop/'s own code
  gaps     no stacks step may be a gap: one tmc/mls lacks holds the freeze unless a second peer runs it in
           both directions (OpenMLS's 0x004D, once its M0 KAT matches); mlswg vectors under 0x0001 count toward
           no part of it
```

**Ciphersuite ([owner decision 44](#od-44); D-KEYS-12).** 0x0010, MLS_128_MLKEM768X25519_AES128GCM_SHA256_Ed25519, in groups and credentials from v0 (draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-07, Publication Requested 2026-11-01; [R:ext-storage-crypto](design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.1). Each MLS AEAD key is used once, so wasm's table-based AES (GOROOT/src/crypto/internal/fips140/aes/aes_generic.go:58-74) is no practical timing target.

**Framing (D-KEYS-3).** Member commits are PrivateMessage (RFC 9420 §6.3), whose clear header shows group_id, epoch and content type; only external commits (resync, recovery self-join) are PublicMessage, as RFC 9420 §6 requires for non-members. `authenticated_data`, clear but bound into the AEAD and signature, adds only what the gate needs and no roster delta ([owner decision 59](#od-59)):

```proto
message GkmCommitHeader {   // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto, in authenticated_data of every commit
  uint64  generation = 1;   // the generation of this epoch's GenWrap: the newest gen/ the committer holds;
                            //   0 only for a recovery self-join that carries no GenWrap (10.6's epoch PUT, 10.8)
  AuthPin auth = 2;         // the state (§7.9) the new roster was checked against
}
```

**Leaves and readers (D-KEYS-2).** Member devices that read a repo are its group's leaves, at most 1,000 (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [7](#od-7), [60](#od-60)); in a data repo, those past the 1,000 seats wait keyless (§8.12). Agents read by 10.5's wraps, outside that cap ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). Readers are §8's `RepoReaders`, which every device evaluates ([owner decision 6](#od-6)) and the projection carries as ids. In the config group, which every admitted sidecar reads, §7.9's `leaves` rule alone ranks member devices, whose admissions carry no not_after, and moves them between leaf and wrap, as a function of the log ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the rest, and an entitled device not yet added, read by ReaderWraps (wrapped) and stay leaves of their data repos. §10 adds:

```text
adds      members accept a config-group Add or external join only of a leaf-entitled device (§7.9); one
          without a KeyPackage reads by ReaderWrap until it uploads one, and no other device takes its place
wrapped   a wrapped member device commits no config-group Add or Remove, only first wraps and rotations (10.9)
```

**Credential.** Private-use type `ur_sidecar = 0xF552` (RFC 9420 §17.5), required through `required_capabilities`; KeyPackages are public, so it names no member, tag or client:

```proto
message UrMlsCredential {                         // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto
  bytes sidecar_id = 1;                           // durable leaf identity (§5)
  bytes identity_public_key = 2; string identity_alg = 3;  // §5; ed25519 in v0
  bytes mls_signature_public_key = 4;             // rotated by self-update
  uint32 cipher_suite = 5; int64 not_after = 6;   // 0x0010 (owner decision 44)
  bytes admission_sha256 = 7;                     // its §7.9 SidecarAdmit; Genesis for the first device
  bytes identity_signature = 8;                   // §6 signing, purpose mls-credential, fields 1-7
}
```

- **Admission (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [127](#od-127)).** Members accept a credential only if an unrevoked, unparked `SidecarAdmit`, verified through the authorization log back to the genesis and signed as §7.9 allows (one admin, the member's own device unless `self_admit` is off, or k of n for AdminSet members), names its sidecar_id and identity key. Only a network's first device is trusted on first use, against its safety number (§2.8 EX5). Clients pin that key, refuse a second and share pins through §6's `Hello` (D-PROTO-13). After a `SidecarRevoke`, GKM deletes the sidecar's KeyPackages.
- **Self-updates and forks.** A leaf that commits no path for 7 days (30 in groups above 50 leaves) commits a path-only commit (D-KEYS-14). Clients pin each push's sealed (group_id, epoch, epoch_authenticator) (§11.6) and each generation's C_g, refuse a lower or conflicting pin with an alarm and compare pins by §6's `HeadCheck`, whose generation heads serve holders that are not leaves (I-16, D-PROTO-14, D-TRUST-10; [owner decision 129](#od-129)).

### 10.5 The key hierarchy: what "one session key stored in GKM" means

The MLS exporter changes every epoch, is not forward-secure (draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11 §4.4), and gives a new member nothing earlier, so the evs keys sit above MLS:

```text
MLS epoch e --MLS-Exporter("UR evs 1.0 kek", repo_id, 32)--> KEK_e (key-encryption key)
RK_g: repo key generation g, 32 random bytes = PLAN's "session key"; cause_g ∈ {remove, request, schedule}
GKM stores only:
  GenRotate_g = the Signed record in gen/<g> (below): C_g, parent C_{g-1}, cause, auth pin, time, holders
                hash, GenLink_g, an optional LeafWrap, the drop key
  GenLink_g   = XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_link_g, RK_{g-1}; aad repo_id||g||cause_g)         the ladder
  GenWrap_e   = XChaCha20-Poly1305(KEK_e, RK_g; aad group_id||e||g)    in epoch object e, g its newest
  LeafWrap    = XChaCha20-Poly1305(KEK_e, RK_g; aad group_id||e||g)    in GenRotate_g, for every leaf of e
  GroupInfo_e = XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_groupinfo, GroupInfo incl. ratchet_tree; aad group_id||e)
                inside each epoch object at <= 16 leaves; on demand above (10.6)
  RecoveryWrap_{m,g}   = HPKE-XWing(recovery_pub_m, RK_g)                                    (10.8)
  ReaderWrap_{g,s}     = §6 Signed, purpose reader-wrap, {group_id, g, s, HPKE-XWing(ReaderKey_s, RK_g)}
  DelegationWrap_{g,d} = §6 Signed, purpose reader-wrap, {group_id, g, d, HPKE-XWing(reader key of d, RK_g)},
                         d = delegation_id = SHA-256(Signed Delegation)
RK_g --HKDF-SHA256(salt repo_id, info "UR evs 1.0 "||purpose||u64be(g) [||group_id||u64be(e)])-->
     link|fek|manifest|path|ref|drop|groupinfo
ReaderKey_s = §6 Signed, purpose reader-key, {sidecar_id, xwing_public_key, not_after <= 30 days}; every reader
              holds one, a fresh X-Wing pair every 7 days (readerkey, below)
ur_group    = GroupContext extension {network_id, repo_id, kind, owner_member_id}, fixed at creation
```

- **PLAN.md:53, precisely.** One current key, RK_g, encrypts every new object, and GKM stores it only wrapped (I-1). It rotates when a key holder drops or its authorization expires (`remove`), on `ur keys rotate` (`request`) and after 30 days (`schedule`); Adds and self-updates keep it, so in-flight writes stay valid.
- **Ladder.** RK_g opens every earlier generation, so a joiner gets the whole history; to withhold history, use a new repo (§11). A removed reader gets no later KEK, RK or wrap, but keeps every generation it held and opens files untouched since its removal until they are rewritten or `ur evs rekey` re-checkpoints them. MLS updates heal the tree and its KEKs, but a copied keychain derives every KEK until the device's own next path commit (10.4) and opens every ReaderWrap to its ReaderKey until the weekly replacement (readerkey, below), so content heals only at the first generation sealed after both: while the device runs, a thief reads what is sealed up to about 37 days after the copy, 60 above 50 leaves (both within 7 days, the path commit within 30 above 50 leaves, then up to 30 days to the next generation), and every earlier generation through the ladder; a Delegation's reader key in it reads as the Residual below says. X-Wing protects ciphertext against harvest-now-decrypt-later by a passive adversary ([owner decision 44](#od-44)); signatures are Ed25519, so an adversary that can forge them (a future quantum computer, say) and that the operator serves could forge admissions and, through the ladder, read all retained history. External resync needs RK_g, under which the GroupInfo is sealed, never a published identity key alone.
- **Authentication.** The key schedule and every GroupInfo signature bind `ur_group`; clients accept RK_g only if it matches `gen/<g>`'s signed C_g; the newer, verified generation authenticates each GenLink, whose AAD covers the cause §11's rewrap rule reads; a missing key is refused, never defaulted (ePrint 2024/546).

**Generations (D-KEYS-15).** C_g = SHA-256("UR evs 1.0 commit" ‖ repo_id ‖ u64be(g) ‖ RK_g), and every evs head carries the generation pin {group_id, g, C_g} (§11.8). `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match, is the only place a generation exists: MLS commits change the tree and give joiners the newest generation's key in GenWrap_e, and the rotation a Remove requires is a separate gen/ claim, by any writer.

```proto
message GenRotate {              // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto; §6 Signed, purpose gen-rotate, by the rotator's identity key
  bytes   group_id = 1; bytes repo_id = 2;
  uint64  generation = 3;        // g; generation 1 is written with epoch 0 (KF1) and has no parent
  bytes   parent_commitment = 4; // C_{g-1}
  bytes   commitment = 5;        // C_g
  uint32  cause = 6;             // 1 REMOVE, 2 REQUEST, 3 SCHEDULE; REMOVE iff it covers a shrink, an
                                 //   authorization expiry or a compromise retirement since the parent (10.9)
  AuthPin auth = 7;              // the state KeyHolders was computed at (§7.9); never below the previous
                                 //   base or the parent's auth
  int64   time_ms = 8;           // the evaluation time for expiries; within 10 min of gkm's clock
  bytes   holders_sha256 = 9;    // SHA-256 over the sorted KeyHolders(R, auth, time) identities (below)
  uint32  wrap_count = 10;       // staged wraps and recovery wraps, for completeness checks
  bytes   genlink = 11;          // GenLink_g
  LeafWrap leaf_wrap = 12;       // optional: one wrap for every leaf of that epoch, 72 B
  bytes   drop_public_key = 13;  // only for kinds that take deposits (D-KEYS-17)
  int64   drop_not_after_ms = 14;
}
message LeafWrap { uint64 epoch = 1; bytes ciphertext = 2; }  // RK_g under KEK_epoch, aad group_id||epoch||g
```

```text
Rotate: one algorithm for every cause and every rotator
1  S = my newest verified state (n, A_n); t = now; H = KeyHolders(R, S, t); require me in H or covered by a
   Delegation in H, and me ∈ writers(R, S) or, in the config group, me = the signer of an admission or
   revocation this rotation answers (owner decision 128) or, after api's reap of an uncovered ephemeral
   agent, of its admission (§7.10)
2  g = the newest generation (GET gen/<g+1> answers 404); RK' = 32 random bytes; persist RK' and the
   GenRotate draft in my keychain
3  stage deliveries for g+1 under c8 = hex(C_{g+1}[0:8]), up to 16 PUTs at once:
     leaves        if I am a leaf at the current epoch e and e's tree holds no leaf outside H, one leaf_wrap
                   under KEK_e inside GenRotate; else a ReaderWrap to each leaf's ReaderKey
     config        member devices in H that e's tree lacks, wrapped or not yet added, a device a restored binding
                   admitted among them once activated (10.8): a ReaderWrap each (owner decision 144); in other
                   groups they join by Add (KF2)
     agents        not covered by a live Delegation: a ReaderWrap each
     Delegations   live ones in H: a DelegationWrap each
     recovery      members reading R with a current RecoveryBind: a RecoveryWrap each
4  PUT gen/<g+1> If-None-Match                                          <- the linearization point
     201      done; hint (D-KEYS-19); the generation is complete, since every delivery already exists
     412      GET it and check it (10.9); if it covers every shrink and expiry I rotate for, adopt it and fetch
              my wrap; else go to 1, rotating at g+2
     unknown  GET gen/<g+1>: my commitment = done; another = 412; 404 = repeat 4 with the same bytes
5  seal content to g+1; delete my keychain draft
retry      the GenRotate bytes, named by their commitment; every delivery precedes the claim, so a crash before
           4 leaves only staged objects, which GC removes after 24 h, and one after it a complete generation;
           a recipient whose ReaderKey appears later gets a late wrap from any holder (wrap-pending)
remove X   a writer leaf commits Remove(X) at epoch e+1 (the revoking device first, 10.9); then any writer
           rotates, a leaf by leaf_wrap under KEK_{e+1}, which X cannot derive; until a leaf commits the
           Remove, a wrapped writer (an agent, or in the config group a wrapped member device, 10.4)
           may rotate by ReaderWraps to every remaining leaf, no leaf_wrap uses an epoch whose tree holds X,
           and the next leaf commit must remove X; wrapped writers never commit Removes (owner decisions 114,
           144), yet no repo stays gated while every leaf is offline
```

**Key holders (D-KEYS-16).** For repo R at state S and time t:

```text
KeyHolders(R, S, t) = leaf(s)        member devices reading R (§8.12), MLS leaves of R's group; in the config
                                     group wrapped ones (10.4) hold wraps and keep this identity
                    ∪ agent(s)       other admitted sidecars reading R, unless covered
                    ∪ delegation(d)  live Delegations whose tags read R and whose key is not dropped
                    ∪ recovery(m)    members reading R with a current RecoveryBind
covered(s, R)  = s was admitted under a Delegation d with delegation(d) ∈ KeyHolders(R, S, t)

identity bytes = kind byte (1 leaf, 2 agent, 3 delegation, 4 recovery) || sidecar_id | delegation_id | member_id
readerkey  every reader, leaves included, keeps a current ReaderKey at gkm/rk/<sidecar_id>, replacing it with a
           fresh X-Wing pair every 7 days, never re-signing an old pair, and keeping a replaced private key only
           until its not_after, for wraps staged to it; a wrap to s uses the ReaderKey gkm serves, current at the

covered    a covered agent reads R through its Delegation's wrap and holds no ReaderWrap there; it holds a key

                                          until revoked                       revoked agent (owner decision 114)
SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise}         delegation(d) leaves there          shrink: a REMOVE rotation excludes d
```

**Residual ([owner decision 114](#od-114)).** Every holder of a Delegation's reader key, each agent it admitted and each copy of its auth key included, reads every later generation of the config repo and the Delegation's tag repos until `DelegationRevoke`, `not_after`, a non-reap revocation of one of its agents or a compromise revocation whose closure voids it (§7.9's cascade); reaping an agent does not revoke the key. Bounds: `not_after` is required, at most 90 days (§7.8); the console gives CI and cloud Delegations 30 days and replaces them (a new Delegation, then `DelegationRevoke` of the old) at each CI secret rotation; the last two causes drop the key at once.

| Content key | Use (all with XChaCha20-Poly1305) |
|---|---|
| `fek` | Wraps each object's random 256-bit key (PLAN.md:148) in a sealed segment header (general repos) or a deletable slot (record-class repos, group inboxes; 10.8) |
| `manifest` | Names, entry fields, push metadata and ref names (§11) |
| `path` | Token keys per path epoch (§11.6, [owner decision 2](#od-2)) |
| `ref` | Ref ids, from RK_1 for the repo's life, since they name every `head/`, `log/` and `idx/` key (§11.6) |
| `drop` | An X-Wing key pair for deposits that depositors cannot read back, published in its generation's GenRotate under the depositor rule below |
| `groupinfo` | Seals GroupInfo and its tree per (group_id, epoch) |

```text
depositor (D-KEYS-17)  before sealing to generation g's drop key, a depositor, which reads the config,
           requires: GenRotate_g verifies; g is the newest generation gkm serves (10.14's drop-key route); g
           covers R's holders_shrunk_at and every holder expiry up to now in its own state (§7.9); now <
           drop_not_after_ms; g is not below its pin for R, which it then raises; else it waits for a newer
           rotation, which the gate makes writers write
```

Clients cache every RK_g in the §5 keychain, keep MLS state, trees included, on disk under §5's AEAD, load one group's tree at a time (§18.4's budgets) and delete other epoch secrets (RFC 9420 §9.2). Every derivation and unwrap calls §22's `testHookSecret`.

### 10.6 GKM: the Delivery Service and wrapped-key store

GKM is a strongly consistent Delivery Service (DS; RFC 9750 §5.2.1) with no state of its own: its records are metadata-cluster objects ordered by conditional writes (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [21](#od-21), [145](#od-145)). It verifies 15-minute capability tokens offline (aud `gkm`; scopes `repo:<id>:r|rw|admin`, `deposit` on the drop-key route only, and an unadmitted client's `recovery:<member_id>` for that member's own recovery wraps), honors an `r`, `rw` or `admin` scope only while its subject reads or writes the repo, as the scope says, in gkm's newest verified state (§8.12), and honors §7.8's `rev/` objects.

```text
on the repo's cluster

                                                                            (for owner-bound kinds, only the owner's
                                                                            consented device) or by a network admin's
                                                                            outside owner-bound kinds

                                                exists                      uploader, time, GenWrap_n of the newest
```


**Write gate (D-KEYS-6; D-EVS-18).** The predicate below, over §7.9's causal identities, decides which writes a key-holder change blocks; §11.8 enforces it at each ref's head CAS. Target: p99 close-to-reopen ≤5 min with a writer online; alarm at 1 h.

```text
pass      a push or deposit to R declaring generation g passes only if g covers R's holders_shrunk_at in evs's
          newest verified state and no holder of R expired in (t_g, now] (§7.9's coverage)
shrinks   SidecarRevoke, MemberRevoke and parks (§7.9's compromise cascade); api's reap of an ephemeral
          sidecar no live Delegation covers; Suspend; GrantRevoke and RepoRevoke of a grant that reads;
          DelegationRevoke and a Delegation's key drop (10.5); a compromise retirement (SidecarRevoke or
          RecoveryRebind with reason compromise), a shrink by §7.9's test though a rebind keeps recovery(m)'s
          identity; an authority statement's completion that drops a holder; any base whose rows drop one
expiries  RepoGrant and requested grants' expires; an agent's SidecarAdmit and a Delegation's not_after (a
          member device's admission carries none, §7.9); a ReaderKey's lapse is none (10.5)
never     admissions, grants, OwnerConfirm, Unsuspend, routine RecoveryRebinds, reaps of covered agents, and a
          config member device's move between leaf and wrap (owner decision 144)
window    heads' auth pins never fall (§11.8); a push validated before a shrink commits ordered before it,
          within §11.8's bound: about 10 s, 5 min if api's notification is lost, plus §19.6's 10 s store
          request deadline, since §11.8 issues and reissues a head PUT only within 5 s of its validation
```

**Sizes (D-KEYS-14)**, from RFC 9420's structures, which §22.8 measures at M2:

```text
inputs: X-Wing key 1,216 B, ciphertext 1,120 B (GOROOT/src/crypto/mlkem/mlkem.go:27, :30;
```

**What GKM sees.** §2.8 adopts these rows verbatim; [owner decision 115](#od-115) confirmed them (Q-KEYS-12).

```yaml
gkm-1:
  sees: GroupForm chain (repo_id, group_id, previous group, generation, signer); epoch 0 (network_id, cipher suite 0x0010 (owner decision 44), creator)
  why: one accepted commit per epoch; re-forming
  ttl: life of the repo
gkm-2:
  sees: epoch objects; group_id, epoch, content type, generation, auth pin, size, time, uploader sidecar_id; the commit as PrivateMessage ciphertext; GenWrap
  why: ordering; the write gate
  ttl: 30 d, then until every leaf acking in the last 30 d has applied it; never the newest epoch
gkm-3:
  withdrawn: no roster delta in the clear (owner decision 59); membership shows only as sidecar ids in gkm-4, gkm-5, gkm-7 and gkm-10, as in api-7
gkm-4:
  sees: KeyPackages (init and leaf HPKE keys, signature key, credential: sidecar_id, identity key, suite, not_after, admission hash, signature); claims (group, claimer, target); ReaderKeys (owner decision 114)
  why: asynchronous adds; wrapped readers
  ttl: KeyPackages until claimed, or 90 d; claims 90 d; ReaderKeys until replaced, at most 30 d
gkm-5:
  sees: Welcome objects and pointers; recipient sidecar_ids and KeyPackageRefs in the clear; secrets and GroupInfo encrypted
  why: deliver joins
  ttl: until every recipient has acked, at most 90 d
gkm-6:
  sees: external commits, for resync and recovery only (PublicMessage); the joiner's leaf and credential, its removed old leaf, their ExternalInit and Remove proposals and their UpdatePath's public keys and encrypted path secrets
  why: offline catch-up and recovery
  ttl: as gkm-2
gkm-7:
  sees: key ladder; GenRotates (group, generation, parent and own commitments, cause, auth pin, time, holders hash, signer; GenLink and leaf-wrap ciphertexts; the drop public key where the kind takes deposits); GroupInfo pointers and, above 16 leaves, sealed GroupInfo; staged and late wraps (group, generation, commitment prefix, recipient sidecar_id or delegation_id, ciphertext, signer; owner decisions 114, 144)
  why: ladder, resync, deposits; wrapped readers
  ttl: life of the repo; GroupInfo until superseded; wraps until the next generation's exist, staged wraps of a lost claim 24 h
gkm-8:
  sees: recovery wraps (member_id, group_id, generation, HPKE ciphertext); the bindings are §7.9's RecoveryBind config records, not gkm objects
  why: recovery after losing every device
  ttl: until a RecoveryRebind replaces them or the repo is deleted; staged ones of a lost claim 24 h
gkm-9:
  sees: request log; client, route, group, time, bytes (GroupInfo requests included)
  why: rate limits, abuse
  ttl: 7 d
gkm-10:
  sees: acks in Redis {gka_<group_id>}; group_id, sidecar_id, newest applied epoch, time; written at most daily
  why: retention
  ttl: overwritten by the leaf's next ack; 31 d after its last write; deleted with its group's gkm objects at a shred (§11.12); soft state outside the rdb bundles, lost with Redis, after which gkm deletes no epoch for 30 d; a hold's copy excepted (api-14)
```

### 10.7 Flows

**KF1. Create a repo.** A member's device C files §8.8's `RepoCreate`, creates the repo in evs as `keying` (§11.12), placing it ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), and becomes its admin ([owner decision 8](#od-8)); a config repo follows §7.9's bootstrap. `POST /gkm/groups` writes `epoch/0` (a random 16-byte group_id, GenWrap_0 and the sealed GroupInfo), `gen/1` (the GenRotate of a new RK_1, without a parent) and C's GroupForm. C writes generation 1's deliveries (10.5's step 3: ReaderWraps, DelegationWraps, RecoveryWraps) while the repo is still keying, resuming from its keychain after a crash, and only then has evs activate it, so no content predates its recovery wraps. C then adds the other leaves in one Add-only commit with its Welcome and GroupInfo.

**KF2. Add a device D.** D enrolls, its `SidecarAdmit` enters the authorization log (§5.6, §7.9), and it uploads a ReaderKey and, as a member device, KeyPackages (a device a restored binding admitted, only once anchored, 10.8). Once the state lists D where its subject reads, and again at D's first KeyPackage upload (10.6), GKM hints `pending` to the writers, and a committer per 10.9 claims a KeyPackage and commits the Add with other pending changes, the Welcome, the sealed GroupInfo and GenWrap; an agent, or a config member device that is wrapped or has no KeyPackage (10.4; [owner decision 144](#od-144)), gets a late ReaderWrap of the current generation instead, and a covered agent reads at once through its Delegation's wrap. D checks RK_g against `gen/<g>`'s C_g and walks the ladder (10.5). Owner-bound repos park a D without its owner's consent (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)), whose devices raise `approval_pending` until an `OwnerConfirm`.

**KF3. Add a member N.** A repo or network admin signs N's grant into the repo's access log (§8.8; owner decisions [7](#od-7), [8](#od-8)), or in an owner-bound repo the owner's device an `EvsShare` ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), and KF2 runs for N's devices: the granting device at once, other writer leaves after 15 s plus jitter; while none is online, N waits and nothing leaks.

**KF4. Remove a member or device X** (§7.10). The revocation's log entry n' drops X from the key holders of every repo it read, so evs refuses writes whose generation does not cover n' (10.6, §11.8), and evs and gkm refuse X's tokens (§7.8). A committer per 10.9, the revoking device first, commits the Remove with a path; any writer then rotates (10.5), staging its wraps before it claims `gen/<g+1>`, at the latest through `EnsureWritable` before its next write, so reaps batch. A wrapped X needs only the rotation, and a wrapped revoker in the config group rotates first, leaving a leaf X's Remove to the next leaf commit (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144)). D-TRUST-10's witness stop never holds a Remove, rotation or revocation ([owner decision 129](#od-129)).

```text
   api (§7.10)       evs               gkm               writers
1  |--entry n'------>|                 |                 |   holders_shrunk_at = n': 412 below; receivers 451
2  |                 |                 |--hint pending-->|   per-client gkm topic, the revoking device first
3  |                 |                 |<--epoch/<e+1>---|   a writer leaf: Remove + path; header (g, (n', A'))
4  |                 |                 |<--gen/<g+1>-----|   any writer: staged wraps, then the claim at (n', A')
5  |                 |<--write at g+1, auth >= n'---------|   the gate passes it
```

**KF5. Offline catch-up.** Up to 100 epochs behind, the device replays each later commit in order (each epoch derives from the previous `init_secret`). Further behind, or if commits were pruned, processing fails or its leaf was removed as stale, it opens the current sealed GroupInfo (10.6) with the key of the generation it names, from its wrap (a device whose ReaderKey lapsed publishes a new one and waits for a late wrap), and resyncs by external commit (ExternalInit, a Remove of its old leaf, GenWrap_{e+1}); else it awaits a re-add or uses its recovery code (10.8). Nothing is lost.

**KF6. Concurrent commits.** The 409 loser, having stored no Welcome, processes the winner and retries what remains. Rotations race only on `gen/<g+1>` (10.5).

**KF7. gkm unavailable.** Cached keys serve reads and deposits; evs checks the gate itself from the authorization log, so writes continue while every shrink is covered, and a removal still stops them until gkm returns and a writer rotates. Joins, catch-up and membership changes wait.

### 10.8 Revocation, erasure, recovery, re-seeding, key domains

**Removed or expired holder X ([owner decision 64](#od-64)).** X keeps what it held up to generation g and loses everything after: the generation that covers its drop is cause REMOVE (10.9), so content rewraps lazily, each file's next write a full checkpoint under a fresh object key (§11.7; Q-KEYS-10), and path tokens re-key through §11.6's path epoch, at once for a member's device or a compromise, within 24 h for other drops and for expiries ([owner decision 2](#od-2)); §11.6 reconciles the two.

**Erasure ([owner decision 61](#od-61)).** An entry's key lives only in a deletable slot (§11.12), so an ERASE push deleting it, cached copies and mirrors' slot copies (§11.12) shred the entry even if ciphertext survives; no operator copy holds slots or wraps ([owner decision 90](#od-90)), and owner devices' mirrors hold slot copies and apply each erasure (§11.13). gkm, like evs, refuses a `deleted` repo but for a re-seed's GroupForm (below; [owner decision 82](#od-82)); its shred (§11.12) deletes the repo's gkm objects and `{gka_}` acks, and again after 10 min for writes in flight (10.6's checks), even under a preservation hold, subject to counsel ([owner decision 133](#od-133)), and members drop its keys.

**Recovery when M loses every device (owner decisions [62](#od-62), [127](#od-127), [128](#od-128), [149](#od-149)).** §5.9's recovery code derives X-Wing and Ed25519 keys that §7.9's `RecoveryBind` binds to M; every rotator, agents included, wraps RK_g to every reading member's current X-Wing recovery key, a public key every config reader holds, and the ladder opens older generations.
- With the code, a new device is admitted by the recovery key under §7.9's window and veto, meanwhile reading only the authorization log and M's own recovery wraps (10.14). The window and veto bound admission, not those wraps, which the code opens at once: a code holder with M's login holds every generation wrapped to M's recovery key and, through the ladder, each earlier one, and with the operator's ciphertext reads them, whatever a veto does, until `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}`; revoking the device it admitted does not retire the code (§2.10). It fetches its recovery wraps (the newest per group) and, once admitted, first passes §7.9's `anchor` on its config-group RecoveryWrap, raising §5.4's `head_alarm` (fork) and acting no further otherwise; only then does it open each group's sealed GroupInfo, self-join by external commit the config group and every group M writes ([owner decision 128](#od-128)), join the others through KF2, sign `SidecarRevoke` for M's lost devices (k of n for an AdminSet member's devices, its own signature counting as one), remove their leaves and rotate (10.5), in any order: a self-join may leave revoked leaves if it carries no GenWrap (generation 0) and its next commit removes them, so no generation reaches a thief's leaves. Above 16 leaves, a self-join waits for one leaf online to write the current GroupInfo; past the config group's first 1,000, the device reads the config by its RecoveryWrap, then by wraps (§7.9; [owner decision 144](#od-144)).
- A binding a void restored takes no RecoveryWrap until a signer outside P signs it again (§7.9's cascade), so the device it admits, once its proposal activates, keeps §7.9's `restored` order, anchoring on a ReaderWrap, never an Add: it uploads its ReaderKey but no KeyPackage, fetches the late ReaderWrap of the config group's current generation that a config writer gives it (KF2), or one a later rotation stages while e's tree lacks it (10.5), and passes the anchor on that wrap's RK_g, with the same alarm and stop on a failure. Only then does it self-join the config group if leaf-entitled, by the one sealed GroupInfo that RK_g opens (else reading the config by those wraps), upload KeyPackages, so that KF2 adds it to its other groups, revoke, remove and rotate as above, and offer `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9), whose binding takes RecoveryWraps again; a group whose leaves are all in P opens to it only through that binding's surviving RecoveryWraps.
- `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9) signs a `RecoveryRebind` (§7.9), re-wraps, deletes M's old wraps and requests a `request` rotation in M's groups, or, for a code retired as compromised (`RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}`), a `remove` one, which starts an immediate path epoch and full checkpoints (§11.6, §11.7). No rebind or void reaches a keychain backup sealed before it, whose `keychain.wrap` the retired or voided code still opens (§5.9), yielding that device's identity key, ClientKey seed, ReaderKeys and key cache, so after a compromise rebind or a void each device whose backups may hold such a sealing is revoked as compromised (§7.9) and enrolled anew, since `--replace` keeps its identity key (§5.5).
- Without the code, admins revoke the lost devices and admit a new one (§7.9), moving every team repo M read to a new generation; M's owner-bound repos, which need M's consent ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), and single-member repos are lost.

**Site loss (D-KEYS-13; order in §19.10).** gkm objects have no off-site copy (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)), but devices keep each group's MLS state and every RK_g: a device 10.6's GroupForm rules allow, a repo admin's and for owner-bound kinds the owner's consented device, re-forms each group under a GroupForm linked to the cached RK_g, re-uploads the ladder and re-adds readers and RecoveryWraps, and members check the signer and their cached C_g. A repo re-seeded as deleted (§11.13) takes only that GroupForm, with its epoch 0 and ladder, while deleted ([owner decision 82](#od-82)): devices open its files from their cached RK_g once it is restored, its readers rejoin by KF2 and late wraps, and a shred deletes the group. Slots return from owner devices' mirrors (§11.13). Repos no device holds are lost (§2.18).

**Key domains ([R:product](design-research/product.md) S4)**, each its own repo and group, take §8.5's kind defaults as readers, which policy narrows (owner-bound kinds: [owner decision 126](#od-126)).

| Domain | Readers (agents by wrap) | Deposits by drop key |
|---|---|---|
| Author vault ([R:product](design-research/product.md) S1, S2) | the author's consented devices; `EvsShare` recipients | the author's other devices, tagged and headless sidecars |
| Team record ([R:product](design-research/product.md) S3; X20) | admins' and auditors' devices | members' and tagged sidecars; authors keep copies |
| Shared team repos | every reading sidecar (§8) | — |
| Config (§7.9) | every admitted sidecar; member devices past the first 1,000 by wrap ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) | — |
| Burner vault and mailbox (§15) | the user's consented devices | `tag:mail` receivers, which cannot read the archive |

**Escrow ([owner decision 63](#od-63)).** None by default, and never silent: Team's v1 opt-in `tag:audit` reader on a customer device (sidecar/improve.md:106-108; §8.5's `audit` block under a k-of-n `AuditOptIn`) gets ReaderWraps only once every member's config holds the block and each affected reader list shows it.

### 10.9 Authorization of MLS operations

GKM sees no proposal ([owner decision 59](#od-59)), so members verify each decrypted commit and each wrap against its header, the authorization state at its auth pin (§7.9) and the repo's access log (§8.8). On a mismatch a member alarms and never adopts or encrypts to the epoch or generation; a bad commit can stall a group until an admin revokes its committer and the group re-forms through the ladder. GKM originates nothing; no group has external senders (I-4).

**Committers (owner decisions [113](#od-113), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144)).** The signed input, not the committer, carries the authority, so no membership change waits for an admin, and members reject a commit without it. Wrapped writers (agents, and the config group's wrapped member devices, 10.4) rotate by re-wrapping but never commit an Add or Remove.

```text
Add            committer  a writer leaf, the granting device first; for a first wrap (an agent's, a
                          Delegation's or a wrapped member device's), any writer; in the config group also the
                          admission's signer, by an Add from its leaf, or by the first wrap if it or the
                          device is wrapped, and from its leaf the signer of a revocation that made the device
                          leaf-entitled (§7.9's move)
               check      a signed grant in the access log, admission or EvsShare, or owner decision 63's audit
                          assignment; in an owner-bound repo only the owner's consented devices (§8.5) and their
                          EvsShares (owner decision 126); in the config group a leaf only for a leaf-entitled
                          device (§7.9); admitted, unrevoked, unparked, outside URnetwork platform networks, key
                          pinned, KeyPackage claimed for this group
Remove         committer  a writer leaf, the revoking device first; in the config group also the revocation's
                          signer from its leaf, a wrapped signer rotating instead; never the target (RFC 9420
                          §12.2)
               check      its signed input: a SidecarRevoke or MemberRevoke (which a server deactivation
                          follows), a park (§7.9), a Suspend, a revoked or expired grant, in the config group
                          the target's loss of leaf entitlement at the auth pin under §7.9's rank (it reads on
                          by wraps), or staleness, whose input is §7.9's stale_leaf_days (90) past the target
                          leaf's last change epoch, which members check against their own record and the epochs'
                          times; a stale-removed device returns by resync (KF5)
Rotation       committer  any writer that holds the key, as a holder or covered by a Delegation, at a pin
  alone                   covering what it rotates for, wrapped ones included (owner decision 114); in the config
                          group also the signer of the admission or revocation (owner decision 128) or, after
                          the reap of an uncovered ephemeral agent, of its admission (§7.10), each while a holder
               check      the rotation checks below; deliveries only to key holders (10.5)
Self-update    committer  the leaf itself, by a path-only commit
               check      sidecar_id and identity key unchanged
External       committer  the sidecar itself
  commit       check      resync (same sidecar_id and key, removing at most its old leaf), or a recovery-admitted
                          device's self-join in the config group, if leaf-entitled, or in a group its member
                          writes, under the Add row's checks; it may leave revoked leaves, carrying no GenWrap
                          (generation 0), if its next commit removes them
GroupContext   committer  a repo admin's leaf (required_capabilities); rotations need none
  Extensions   check      kind and owner never change
ReInit, PSK, external or standalone proposals: refused

rotation checks: every member, for each GenRotate
signer    in KeyHolders(R, auth, time) or covered by a Delegation in it, and a writer at auth or, in the config
          group, the signer of the statement it answers (owner decision 128) or, after the reap of an
          uncovered ephemeral agent, of its admission (§7.10)
chain     parent_commitment chains; auth is on my chain and not before my previous base

          epoch tree holds no non-holder leaf

          retirement since the parent, or its parent is poisoned (below)

          REMOVE), and admins revoke the signer

          generation-0 epoch has no GenWrap; the next leaf commit after a leaf's drop, or its loss of config
```
