
### 10.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| PublicMessage handshakes or a clear roster delta | GKM checks proposals or rosters | GKM reads credentials, proposals, the tree (RFC 9420 §16.4) or the roster | Ruled out (owner directive; [owner decision 59](#od-59)) |
| Every admitted sidecar a leaf | One key path; read is membership | A commit per CI join and reap; agents share the 1,000 leaves | Rejected ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) |
| Generations raised both by MLS commits and by wrapped writers | No separate claim object | Two paths mint g+1 and fork the ladder | Rejected (D-KEYS-15) |
| A rotation at every reap of a Delegation-covered agent | Each reap looks like a removal | Excludes nothing the Delegation's key still reads | Rejected (D-KEYS-16) |
| 1,000 member devices per network, or a larger config tree | No member wraps | The cap refuses Teams past ~330 members; 5,000 leaves make a 7.9-14 MB tree and path commits to ~6 MB, past §18.4's budgets | Rejected ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) |
| Proxy re-encryption (PLAN.md:223, :284-327) | The server re-wraps headers blind | Semi-honest (PLAN.md:323), against D-TRUST-1; no supported Go pairings (golang.org/x/crypto/bn256 is deprecated: bn256.go:22-23) | Rejected |

### 10.11 Decisions proposed

**D-KEYS-1 (proposed).** MLS, built in house, distributes key-encryption keys under 10.5's hierarchy from v0 (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [43](#od-43)). *Why:* tree post-compromise security for KEKs; content keys heal only at the first generation after a device's next path commit and ReaderKey replacement (10.5); the ladder keeps §11's format distributor-independent.

**D-KEYS-2 (proposed).** One MLS group per evs repo, with a leaf per reading member device, at most 1,000; other readers hold ReaderWraps, and in the config group so do member devices past §7.9's first 1,000, which commit there only wraps and rotations. *Why:* owner decisions [1](#od-1), [7](#od-7), [60](#od-60), [114](#od-114) and [144](#od-144).

**D-KEYS-3 (proposed).** Member commits are PrivateMessage whose clear header adds only the generation and the auth pin; only external commits are PublicMessage. *Why:* [owner decision 59](#od-59); the gate needs both.

**D-KEYS-4 (proposed).** Credential 0xF552 binds the MLS key to `sidecar_id` and the identity key under a config-repo `SidecarAdmit`; only the genesis rests on trust on first use, and owner-bound repos add only consented readers (10.9). *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126); R-KEYS-8, R-KEYS-9.

**D-KEYS-5 (proposed).** GKM keeps no state of its own and orders, claims, delivers and retains through conditional object writes on its repo's metadata cluster, with acks as Redis soft state (10.6). *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [136](#od-136), [145](#od-145); RFC 9420 §14.

**D-KEYS-6 (proposed).** Commit before write: an authorization-log entry that shrinks a repo's key holders, or a holder's expiry, closes evs's gate (D-EVS-18) until a generation covering it is claimed (§7.9, 10.5), which is cause REMOVE (10.9); generations also rotate on request and every 30 days. *Why:* no server transaction changes readers ([owner decision 5](#od-5)), and an expired holder must lose new content as a removed one does (R-KEYS-4).

**D-KEYS-7 (withdrawn).** Superseded by owner decisions [113](#od-113) and [128](#od-128): the signed statement, not an admin committer, authorizes each membership change (10.9).

**D-KEYS-8 (proposed).** Drop keys in each generation's signed GenRotate give write-only deposits, which depositors accept only if the generation covers every shrink they know (10.5); each key domain is its own repo. *Why:* agents deposit sessions they cannot read (R-KEYS-9).

**D-KEYS-9 (proposed).** Rotating devices wrap each generation to every reading member's current `RecoveryBind` key; Team's only escrow is a visible audit reader. *Why:* owner decisions [62](#od-62), [63](#od-63), with no server-guessable secret.

**D-KEYS-10 (proposed).** M2's entry fixes the MLS wire's fields; its exit freezes them and suite 0x0010 on §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact (10.4), with 10.4's conformance plan, fuzz targets run as Go tests and 10.6's sizes measured (§22.8); the security page says this MLS on draft suite 0x0010 is not independently audited. *Why:* owner decisions [99](#od-99), [101](#od-101), [119](#od-119) (§2.18).

**D-KEYS-11 (proposed).** Tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars read and write through ReaderWraps, and live Delegations get DelegationWraps that cover their agents (10.5). *Why:* [owner decision 114](#od-114): no commits, and reads with no member online.

**D-KEYS-12 (proposed).** MLS is 10.4's subset on ciphersuite 0x0010 from v0, migrating through GroupForm and the ladder if IANA assigns this suite another value. *Why:* [owner decision 44](#od-44).

**D-KEYS-13 (proposed).** After a site loss, repo admins' devices, and for owner-bound kinds the owner's consented devices, re-seed each group from their keychains under a GroupForm linked through the ladder (10.8). *Why:* gkm has no off-site copy (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)).

**D-KEYS-14 (proposed).** Groups scale by 10.6's sizes: 10.4's self-update interval, KF5's resync, GroupInfo on demand above 16 leaves, daily acks, trees on disk. *Why:* a full 1,000-leaf tree is 2.8 MB, which a per-epoch GroupInfo would rewrite about 143 times a day.

**D-KEYS-15 (proposed).** `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match by the rotating writer, is the only place a generation exists; MLS commits never raise the generation, and a removal is a Remove commit followed by an independent rotation (10.5). *Why:* two paths minting g+1 fork the ladder; one claim object serializes every rotator (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128)).

**D-KEYS-16 (proposed).** KeyHolders are leaves (in the config group, member devices past its first 1,000 by wrap), uncovered agents, live Delegations and recovery keys; live Delegations get DelegationWraps keyed by delegation_id; a covered agent's reap is no shrink, and a Delegation's key drops at `DelegationRevoke`, `not_after`, any non-reap revocation of one of its agents or §7.9's cascade voiding it (10.5). *Why:* [owner decision 114](#od-114)'s read-at-once, bounded, with no dropped party signing the rotation that excludes it.

**D-KEYS-17 (proposed).** Drop keys ride each generation's signed GenRotate, only for kinds that take deposits; a depositor seals only to a generation that covers every shrink and expiry it knows and is not below its pin; the deposit scope reaches only the drop-key route (10.6, 10.14). *Why:* a stale but unexpired drop key would reach a removed reader.

**D-KEYS-18 (proposed).** At most 16 leaves, the epoch object carries the sealed GroupInfo and `group-info` is a pointer rewritten at each Add and by gkm with any epoch 16 or more past it, resync probing to a 404; KF1 writes its first wraps, recovery wraps included, before evs activates the repo; above 16, recovery and resync need one leaf online (10.6-10.8). *Why:* a crash between two PUTs must not break code-only recovery.

**D-KEYS-19 (proposed).** `gkm:<group_id>` is versioned epoch × 2^24 + generation, and work hints go on the per-client `gkm` topic of the sidecars that must act (10.14). *Why:* same-epoch work hints and commit-less rotations must not be dropped as stale.

**D-KEYS-20 (proposed).** Retention never deletes a group's newest epoch, moves the `group-info` pointer before deleting the epoch it names, and keeps every GenRotate for the repo's life, as a gen/ object or in a gen pack (10.6, 10.16). *Why:* the next commit needs its predecessor, and code-only recovery needs no epoch history.

**D-KEYS-21 (proposed).** gkm acks are Redis soft state, and the epoch reconciler deletes only while the ack family is 30 days old; a GroupInfo above 16 leaves is written at most once per epoch, on request. *Why:* acks are rebuildable ([owner decision 136](#od-136)), and a 1,000-leaf GroupInfo costs ~0.7 MB on each drive.

### 10.12 Open questions

**Q-KEYS-1.** [X12] Build MLS or fork it? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 43](#od-43)):** build 10.4's subset in house (~5-8k lines); its audit is deferred ([owner decision 99](#od-99)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-2.** [X12] Which ciphersuite? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 44](#od-44)):** 0x0010 (X-Wing, Ed25519) from v0; groups migrate through the ladder if IANA assigns another value. *Residual:* post-quantum confidentiality against a passive adversary only; a future Ed25519 forgery is retroactive through the ladder (10.5, §2.18) until 10.16's hybrid signatures.

**Q-KEYS-3.** [X12] At what granularity are groups formed? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 60](#od-60)):** per repo, grants mapping onto membership; agents hold wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-4.** [X12] What do "GKM" and "one session key stored in GKM" mean? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** a DS plus wrapped, laddered generations (10.5) in the file cluster. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-5.** What admission evidence must a credential carry? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110)):** a config-repo `SidecarAdmit` chained to the genesis, subsuming DeviceAdmit; a member's own device may sign it ([owner decision 112](#od-112)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-6.** Is per-entry crypto-shredding required? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 61](#od-61)):** for record-class repos and mail, through format 1's key slots. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-7.** How does a member recover after losing every device? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 62](#od-62)):** a recovery code receiving wraps under a signed, rotatable binding, plus admin re-add of team repos (10.8); its key counts as one of k after a 72 h veto window ([owner decision 127](#od-127)); a binding the cascade restored admits only through that window, its device anchoring on a config ReaderWrap ([owner decision 149](#od-149)). *Residual:* §2.10's row for an operator colluding with a recovery-code thief: the code opens its wraps at once, whatever the window or a veto, until `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` (revoking the device it admitted does not retire it), and keychain backups sealed before a rebind stay open to the old code (10.8).

**Q-KEYS-8.** Should teams get escrow? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 63](#od-63)):** a visible audit reader on a customer-operated device, a Team opt-in in v1, never silent (10.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-9.** [X12] Does v0 ship MLS, or per-device wraps with MLS in v1? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 1](#od-1)):** MLS in v0 (PLAN.md:44); agents' wraps carry its generations ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-10.** Is 10.8 the right reading of PLAN.md:50 and :338? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 64](#od-64)):** lazy rewrap, a full checkpoint at the first write after a `remove` generation, plus `ur evs rekey`. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-11.** How long does GKM keep epoch objects? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), 30 days, then until every leaf that acked in the last 30 days has applied them, on four conditions (10.6): the newest epoch is never deleted, and the `group-info` pointer moves before the epoch it names goes; nothing the ladder, resync or recovery needs lives in an epoch (generations are `gen/` objects, GroupInfo rides in the newest epoch at 16 leaves or fewer or in `group-info` above, and recovery wraps are their own objects), so a device past retention resyncs from GroupInfo; a preservation hold pauses the sweep ([owner decision 133](#od-133)); and §19.9 sizes the family at M2's benchmark: a 10-leaf group keeps about 42 commits of 11-17 KB plus inline GroupInfo (1.2-1.9 MB), a 1,000-leaf group about 26 MB. *Residual:* §19.9's measured size.

**Q-KEYS-12.** [X12; directive residual] Which header values does gkm see? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 115](#od-115)):** 10.6's rows: ciphertext, group id, epoch, sizes and sidecar ids (membership, as api-7 shows it; [owner decision 72](#od-72)), never, in a member commit, a proposal, credential change, tree or key; external commits show gkm-6's values. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-13.** Does [owner decision 7](#od-7)'s "only from keys allowed to grant" bind the committer or the change? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 113](#od-113)):** (b) the change (10.9), withdrawing D-KEYS-7. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-14.** Who commits the config group's membership changes, when only admins write config records (§8.8)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 128](#od-128)):** (a) also the leaf that signed the admission or revocation; recovery-admitted devices self-join by external commit (10.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-15.** How many member devices may one network hold, given the config group's 1,000-leaf cap? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)):** (b), with no member-device cap: from the start, member devices past the first 1,000 read the config group by per-generation wraps, as agents do, and stay leaves of their data repos, each still at most 1,000 leaves, amending [owner decision 114](#od-114) for the config group only; §20.4 keeps 5,000 Team admissions. §7.9's `leaves` rule ranks and promotes (10.4); wrapped devices commit no config-group Add or Remove, so a wrapped signer writes an admission's first wrap or a revocation's rotation, and the next leaf commit removes a leaf (10.9). Cost: ~1.3 KB of wrap per wrapped device per config rotation. *Residual:* none.

### 10.13 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:147** ("participants are leaves"). Member devices are leaves ([owner decision 60](#od-60)); agents hold wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114) on Q-ACL-9; D-KEYS-11), as do member devices past the config group's first 1,000 there ([owner decision 144](#od-144) on Q-KEYS-15).
- **PLAN.md:148.** Per-object keys are wrapped under RK_g, which the epoch KEK or a holder's wrap delivers (Q-KEYS-4).
- **PLAN.md:221.** Narrowed by the owner directive: gkm holds ciphertext plus 10.6's header values (Q-KEYS-12).
- **PLAN.md:223, :284-327.** Proxy re-encryption is rejected (10.10).

### 10.14 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `GkmClient` (`CurrentRepoKey`, `RepoKey(repoId, generation)`, `EnsureWritable`, which first commits the pending changes its device may, `DropKey`); `EvsRepoKey.DeriveKey(purpose, context)`; credential validation and pins (also for §6's `Hello`); GenRotates and drop keys, ReaderWraps, DelegationWraps and recovery wraps; 10.5's KeyHolders and 10.6's gate predicate (§7.9, §11.8, §11.12).
- **Consumes:** keys, bindings, keychain, recovery code, `SidecarEvent` (§5); topics, `Signed`, `HeadCheck` (§6); tokens, `rev/` (§7.8); the authorization log, `AuthPin`, causal identities, recovery, the `leaves` rule and removals (§7.9, §7.10); `RepoReaders`, seats, kind defaults, consent, `OwnerConfirm`, access logs, `audit`, `EvsShare` (§8); kinds, `repo/` state, `place/`, slots, manifests, path epochs, the head-CAS gate and the write budget (§11); `ServiceHost.Blobs` per cluster and Redis (§4.5, §19).
- **Subprotocol messages:** `GkmHint{group_id, epoch, kind}` in `PushHint` (§6.11, 0x1301): commit on `gkm:<group_id>` (version = epoch × 2^24 + generation); pending, welcome, key-packages-low and wrap-pending (a GenWrap, wrap or sealed GroupInfo is missing) on the per-client `gkm` topic (§6.8).
- **API routes:** Client class, under 10.6's tokens, specified in connect/api/bringyour.yml.

  ```text
  POST /gkm/key-packages, /gkm/key-packages/claim, /gkm/reader-key
  POST /gkm/groups;  GET /gkm/groups/<id>;  POST /gkm/repos/<id>/forms    (GroupForm: create, re-form)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/epochs?after=          epoch objects, in order, with their sizes
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/epochs/<n>             200, 409 (with the winner), 403, 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/gen/<g>                the claim: 201, 412 (with the winner), 403, 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/wraps/<g>/<c8>         staged or late ReaderWraps and DelegationWraps
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/welcome/<n>, /group-info, /ack (Redis)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/gen?since=, /wraps/<g>;  GET /gkm/welcomes
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/drop-key?since=<g>     deposit, r, rw, admin: the newest GenRotate, up to 64 after since
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/group-info?want=<epoch>  sealed; an older one also hints wrap-pending (KF5)
  GET|POST|DELETE /gkm/recovery/<member_id>/wraps  GET also under an unadmitted client's recovery:<member_id>,
                                                   for that member's own wraps only (§7.8, §7.9)
  ```
- **Tables:** none; gkm's durable state is 10.6's objects (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [21](#od-21), [145](#od-145)), and Redis `{gka_<group_id>}` holds acks as soft state ([owner decision 136](#od-136)).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/gkm` hosts `gkmservice` from v0; root `mls_*` and `gkm_*` files and the nested `mlsinterop/` test module (D-REPO-2, D-REPO-3, D-OPS-2); the reconciler (retention, hints, staged-wrap GC) in taskworker; limits in config/all/pro.yml.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §7.9 defines the authorization log, `AuthPin`, the causal identities (a compromise retirement shrinks though a rebind keeps the holder's identity; ReaderKey lapses are no expiry, 10.5) and `holders_shrunk_at`, `RecoveryBind` and its reasons, `stale_leaf_days`, Delegations, the recovery window, `anchor` and `restored` order, the compromise cascade, the Delegations it voids and the bindings it restores, which take no wrap until re-signed, and the `leaves` rule, refusing a not_after on a member device's admission; §7.8 gives member devices other than read_only ones gkm `rw` in the config group and issues the `deposit` and `recovery:<member_id>` scopes; §7.10 and §8.12 name 10.9's committers, §7.10 also the reaped agent's admission signer, §8.12 the data repos' seats and §8.5 consent, and §8.6's ceiling passes the config kind default's read row, so ephemeral sidecars read the config as 10.5's depositor rule needs; §5.4 alarms on admissions a member's devices did not sign and raises `head_alarm` (fork) on a failed recovery anchor, and §5.9 has each device re-seal `keychain.wrap` at every change to its member's current binding, a void included, with no HPKE copy while none is current.
  - §11.8 enforces 10.6's predicate at each ref's head CAS, reissuing a timed-out head PUT only within 5 s of its validation, owns `place/` and lists the first cluster's families, gkm's per-sidecar objects included; §11 owns path epochs (authorization expiries batched within 24 h), §11.7's checkpoint after a REMOVE generation, deletion (its shred deleting the group's gkm objects and `{gka_}`, again after 10 min; a re-seed's GroupForm the only gkm route it admits while deleted), mirrors, re-seeding and §11.13's write budget, whose inputs count expiry rotations and path epochs; §19.6 sets the 10 s store request deadline; §19.9 sizes gkm's objects, gen/ unpacked until 10.16's packs start, expiry rotations and the first cluster's per-sidecar ones included.
  - §22.7 covers 10.5-10.9's cases, the gate's 412 (a compromise rebind's at the old generation included), an expired RepoGrant's REMOVE rotation, checkpoint and path epoch (FS-18), gkm accepting a generation-0 recovery self-join, a reap's config rotation by the admission's signer, an admin-only admission never reading its member's vault or mailbox, a recovery self-join with no leaf online, FS-20 also killing KF1's creator before activation and gkm between an epoch 16 past the pointer and the pointer's rewrite, a 1,001st member device reading the config by wrap, and a Team member whose only device was stolen recovering by the restored code, its device anchoring after the window on its config ReaderWrap (a forged one raising `head_alarm`), then self-joining, KF2 adding it elsewhere; FS-6 holds a gkm commit at a barrier across a --now shred and restores a repo re-seeded as deleted; §22.8's M2 benchmark measures 10.6's sizes and drive costs, a 1,000-leaf group on the iOS surrogate cell and 1 h requested grants on large repos included; its schedules lose the ack family and race a repo's placement, its group landing on the repo's cluster.

### 10.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| The unreviewed in-house MLS misreads RFC 9420 or skips a check ([owner decision 99](#od-99)) | Medium | Critical | 10.4's subset, conformance plan and 0x0010 gate; disclosure (§2.18, [owner decision 119](#od-119)) |
| IANA assigns this suite another value, or X-Wing changes | Medium | Medium | Migration through GroupForm and the ladder ([owner decision 44](#od-44)) |
| An operator substitutes a network's first device at trust on first use | Low | High | Safety numbers; genesis in invites and auth keys |
| A member stalls a group with a commit the others refuse | Low | Medium | Alarms; revocation; re-forming (10.9) |
| A rogue or compromised admin admits a device under a member | Medium | Medium | Consent gates owner-bound repos ([owner decision 126](#od-126); 10.9); the member's devices alarm (§5.4); team repos stay readable until revocation |
| A removed leaf stays in a repo's MLS tree until a writer leaf commits its Remove (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144)) | Medium | Low | Wrapped writers' rotations reopen the gate meanwhile, and no leaf wrap uses an epoch that holds it (10.5); hints wake writer leaves |
| A reaped Delegation-admitted agent, or a leaked auth key, reads later config and tag-repo generations ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) | Medium | High | `not_after` ≤ 90 d (30 d for CI), replaced at each CI secret rotation; any non-reap revocation of its agents, or a compromise cascade voiding it, drops the key (10.5) |
| Large groups strain phones (10.6's sizes) | Medium | Medium | D-KEYS-14; §22.8's benchmark |
| Short grants (1 h requested grants) expire often, and each covering generation is REMOVE, so files re-checkpoint at their next write and a repo's batched path epoch recurs daily, ~17 h of copying for a 1M-file ref (§11.6) | Medium | Medium | One rotation covers every expiry up to its time_ms, and writers batch them at a pending hint or their next write (KF4); 16-diff chains checkpoint anyway; at most one batched path epoch per repo a day (§11.6); §11.13's inputs and §19.9's gen/ row count these rotations and epochs, and §22.8's fixture of 1 h requested grants on large repos reports rotations, full checkpoints and path-epoch copy operations a day |
| A wrapped config rotator past 1,000 member devices writes a ReaderWrap per member device | Low | Low | A leaf rotator's one LeafWrap covers every leaf; §11.13's budget never refuses REMOVE rotations |
| With no witness, shared writes stop at `witness_bound_hours` (default 72 h), a lone cloud agent's included (§2.8's bound, which a split defeats) | Medium | Medium | Agents witness ([owner decision 129](#od-129)); 24 h alarm; up to 168 h; Removes, rotations and revocations never stop |
| After a void leaves M no current binding, M, its network's only config writer, loses every device: no config writer remains to give the device M's restored code admits its ReaderWrap (KF2), so it never anchors ([owner decision 149](#od-149)) | Low | High | M's devices raise `recovery_rebind` at the void (§5.4), and any of them can run `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9) to bind a code that takes wraps; meanwhile only surviving RecoveryWraps open (10.8) |
| Site loss erases every gkm object ([owner decision 94](#od-94)) | Low | Critical | Device re-seed (D-KEYS-13); owner-device mirrors |

### 10.16 Phasing

- **v0 (M2):** all of 10.4-10.9 but v1's items, with D-KEYS-10's gates, D-KEYS-14's scaling and `ur evs rekey`, a client job that re-checkpoints every file of a repo under the current generation in multi-part pushes of at most 1,024 entry writes, at most 50 files/s per repo, resumable from its last committed push.
- **v1:** the Team audit reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63)), and with Team at M6 the config group's wraps for member devices past the first 1,000 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)).
- **Later:** 0x0020 by migration, with hybrid Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 authority signatures; SafeExportSecret (draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11); key transparency; moving a group with its repo once a move tool exists ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); gen packs, once §19.9's projection from §22.8's M2 count needs them: taskworker writes `gkm/<group_id>/genpack/<k>`, holding gen/<256k+1>..<256k+256> verbatim, If-None-Match with repo/ rechecked as for every gkm write, once 64 newer generations exist, then deletes those objects, a retry that finds the pack verifying it and resuming the deletes; a read falls back from gen/<g>'s 404 to genpack/<⌊(g-1)/256⌋>, and a claim still needs gen/<g-1> as an object, so none lands at or below a pack; packs count as gen/ for every other rule (gkm-7's life of the repo, shreds and their 10-minute repeat, re-seeds) and hold no slot, so erasure is unchanged.
- **Dependencies:** §7.9's authorization log and config repo, §8.5's consent, §11's format 1 and §19's conditional writes block v0; §22.8's M2 benchmark sets §19.9's epoch-retention size (Q-KEYS-11's residual).

## 11. Encrypted versioned storage: format, git service, head API, subscriptions

### 11.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns evs repos and kinds, `config` included; the format and what the server sees (X2, [owner decision 2](#od-2)); the file-cluster objects, their placement and the push, commit and read protocols; refs and their modes, record streams and deposits; git compatibility and the local tier (X19, [owner decision 24](#od-24)); subscriptions; GC and evacuation, the metadata write budget and fair share, quotas, durability, deletion and export.

Keys come from §10, identity from §5, push from §6, tokens, the projection and grants from §7 and §8, hardware from §19 (X13), quotas from §20 and layouts from §15 and §16. The metadata clusters also store, and 11.13 budgets, §7's `proj/`, `projrows/` and `rev/`, §10's `gkm/` and §21's `hold/` objects.

### 11.2 Requirements

### 11.3 What exists today

- **No code** exists for evs or a git server [R:server-platform](design-research/server-platform.md) §5.10.
- **BlobStore** has an overwriting Put (server/blob.go:674-679), PutIfAbsent as one If-None-Match request (:683-697), whole-object Get, List and SetLifecycle, but "deliberately no Delete", no ranged read and no streamed put (:155-183).
- **MinIO.** The deployed build (§19.3) checks If-Match and If-None-Match under its namespace lock but proceeds when that read loses quorum (minio@v0.0.0-20251015172955-9e49d5e7a648 cmd/erasure-object.go:1261-1279); PR #21653, merged 2025-10-24, fixes it, and [owner decision 18](#od-18)'s clusters build from the final upstream source (§19.6). MinIO verifies `x-amz-checksum-sha256` before an object exists (cmd/object-handlers.go:1993-2006) and inlines shards of up to 128 KiB in xl.meta (internal/config/storageclass/storage-class.go:278-294). It stores an object as a directory and lists that directory as one object without descending (cmd/metacache-walk.go:239-264). Names are at most 1,024 B (cmd/object-api-utils.go:197-203). xl.meta up to 4 KiB is written O_DSYNC, and larger ones with O_DIRECT and fdatasync (cmd/xl-storage.go:2247-2285). An overwrite also writes the previous xl.meta, inline data included, as a backup until quorum (:2784-2800, :2874-2887). With several pools, a PUT picks its pool by free space even when its key lives in another pool, and checks its precondition only there (cmd/erasure-server-pool.go:637-656; cmd/erasure-object.go:1261-1285). A DELETE evaluates no precondition (cmd/object-handlers.go:2563-2671; cmd/object-api-options.go:273-318), so an If-Match sent with it is ignored.
- **lb.** `client_max_body_size 16m` is global (warp/warpctl/config.go:1301); `streamable_paths` (warp/services/services.go:694-701) get 60 s timeouts and no request buffering (warp/warpctl/config.go:2311-2319).
- **Crypto and clients.** x/crypto v0.54.0 (connect/go.mod:30) has XChaCha20-Poly1305 (chacha20poly1305/xchacha20poly1305.go:24) and no AES-SIV. Clients are reaped after 30+30 idle days (server/model/network_client_model.go:3905, :3925), so the durable signer is §5's `sidecar_id`.

### 11.4 Architecture

```text
git, harnesses        sidecar daemon                                  evs (stateless)             file cluster (§19.6)
 push/fetch ------->  local git server (http, ssh), git-remote-ur     tokens verified offline     metadata clusters (NVMe); a
                      bare repo; sealed mirror of evs objects         head CAS: tip on git refs,  repo lives on the one its
 MCP tools -------->  sync engine --segments, signed pushes, HTTPS--> path-level on file refs --> place/ names: repo/ head/
 apps (head mode) ->  EvsClient  <--PushHint evs:<repo_id> (§6)-----  batches; lazy index folds   log/ pb/ idx/ slot/ hp/ pmap/
                      keys: §10 RK_g -> path, ref, manifest, fek      hints via §6's Redis        pidx/ gkm/; the first also
                                                                      Redis: hints, leases, push  place/ proj/ projrows/ rev/
                                                                      sequence, head cache        hold/, per-sidecar gkm/
                                                                      usage events -> §20         segment cluster (HDD):
                                                                      write budget, fair share    seg/ pack/
```

evs never parses git, holds no key (I-1) and keeps no Postgres or durable Redis state; Redis carries §6's hints and rebuildable soft state: leases, the push sequence, a verified head cache (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [17](#od-17), [136](#od-136)).

### 11.5 X2: what the server sees

[Owner decision 2](#od-2) settles X2's residual (Q-EVS-1): the server sees exactly §2.8's evs rows, one per 11.8 family: each ref's token tree, push DAG, pins and per-file changes (token, time, uploader, Padmé-padded size), each client's reads and subscribed prefixes, and which pushes one evs process batched. It never sees names, contents, messages, authors, branch or display names, agent ids or entry sequence numbers, nor links equal content across or within repos (per-repo keys, random nonces, records reused only for renames and merges).

**Token leak bound.** A token alone shows only its place in the tree. With the server's help, a key holder can test guessed names created before the path epoch that drops it (11.6), which a member device's removal or a compromise makes due at once, new names in general, config and mailcfg repos waiting for it, and other drops and authorization expiries within 24 h, each landing when a mapper commits (writers alarm an hour past due), and guessed branch names for the repo's life, since ref ids stay keyed from RK_1. A Delegation's reader key counts as dropped only at its DelegationRevoke, its `not_after` or a non-reap revocation of one of its agents (§10.5). Holders follow files they knew through the map.

### 11.6 Format: keys, tokens, records, segments

**Keys** are §10.5's `fek`, `manifest`, `drop`, `path` (tokens of path epoch p, from RK_p) and `ref` (ref ids, from RK_1, since they name every `head/` and `log/` key).

**Tokens:**

```text
names    name_i is the path component's raw bytes as git stores them, never normalized, so NFC and NFD names are
         distinct paths, as in git
tokens   t_i = HMAC-SHA256(K_path_p, t_{i-1} || name_i)[:16], t_0 = 16 zero bytes, K_path_p = HKDF-SHA256(RK_p, salt
         repo_id, info "UR evs 1.0 path" || u64be(p)); 26 base32 characters in keys; at most 32 components, keeping
         keys within MinIO's 1,024 B; deposits, whose writers hold no path key, use random ids
ref ids  ref_id = HMAC-SHA256(K_ref, "ref" || ref name bytes)[:16], K_ref = HKDF-SHA256(RK_1, salt repo_id, info
         "UR evs 1.0 ref" || u64be(1)), so any reader derives head/<repo>/<ref> for `main`; deposit refs: the first
         16 B of SHA-256(repo_id || sidecar_id)
leaks    K_path is per repo, so one path has one token on every ref of a repo in one epoch (overlays need this);
         ref ids stay keyed from RK_1, so a removed holder can test guessed branch names for the repo's life
         (11.5, §2.8's evs-2)
```

**Path epochs ([owner decision 2](#od-2) item 9)** are named by the generation p that derives K_path, 1 at creation:

```text
due      the first commit whose generation pin crosses a REMOVE generation (§10.5: it covers a shrink, an
         authorization expiry or a compromise retirement, §7.9) records it in head.path_epoch.due; evs classifies
         it by what it covers and sets due_by_ms; writers alarm 1 h past due_by_ms:
         immediate: a member's or a member device's removal, or a compromise retirement (a SidecarRevoke or
           RecoveryRebind with reason compromise, agents included; §10.6), due_by_ms that commit's time; in
           general, config and mailcfg repos, whose names carry meaning, a push creating a path (a change with
           base_entry_version 0, or a directory add) then gets 412 PATH_EPOCH_DUE until the epoch lands; vault,
           mailbox, record and team_record name entries only by random id or sequence (§15.7, §16.8) and keep
           creating
         batched: other key-holder shrinks (§7.9; a reap of an agent its live Delegation covers is none) and
           authorization expiries (a RepoGrant's or requested grant's expires, a SidecarAdmit's or Delegation's
           not_after); no block; due_by_ms 24 h after the first
map      the writer that rotates, or any writer holding every name of the ref (a full-sync device, or a mobile
         mirror of under 100,000 names), wrapped agents included (owner decision 114), uploads Signed EvsPathMap
         parts for the newest generation p_new to pmap/<repo>/<ref>/<p_new>/<path_map_sha256>/<k>/_: per live
         path, its token path in p_new, in the current epoch and in every source the head lists, and its name
         re-sealed for the new parent and child tokens; the map binds its source head (map_source_version,
         map_source_chain); keys name the map, so a mapper whose source left the window, or that finds another's
         map abandoned, uploads a fresh one; once p or a newer epoch commits, taskworker deletes p's uncommitted
         maps, and the nightly pass deletes a map uncommitted 25 h after its upload by 11.13's orphan rule
tail     paths that window versions after the map's source create get moves like the map's, which the mapper
         builds from those pushes: the PATH_EPOCH push carries them in its payload under path_tail_sha256, and evs
         checks every token path those versions create (base_entry_version 0) against them, else 409 naming the
         paths, so a creation costs the mapper a longer tail, never a fresh map
block    10 min past due_by_ms, a mapper may stop creation for at most 2 min, at most once each 10 min: POST
         .../path-epoch/block {ref_id, ms <= 120,000} sets head.path_epoch.block_until_ms by one head CAS that
         raises only the fence (11.8); until it passes, a push creating a path gets 412 PATH_EPOCH_DUE after a
         fence (11.8's refuse row), so the mapper's tail stops growing and its epoch commits
commit   a PATH_EPOCH push (file and git mode alike; it carries no git commit, and in git mode it takes TIP like
         every push, its mapper re-signing on a newer head or, on a busy ref, first taking the seal lease) commits
         if its map's parts exist, each under 24 h old, path_map_sha256 matches, its source version is in the
         window with a matching chain, its tail covers every creation after that version, and its own process's
         fold left nothing unfolded (11.7 (4)); the head then makes p_new current, lists the old current epoch
         first among the sources (at most 3: a fourth waits, 412 EPOCH_SOURCES_FULL, while creation stays
         blocked), clears due and the block; pushes declaring an older epoch get 412 PATH_EPOCH, part and seal
         checks included, and re-tokenize
copy     one taskworker job per ref, for the newest map and its tail only, as P2 work (11.13), running the moves in
         descending token-path order, so a directory moves after its children: each move reads the entry from the
         newest source holding it, keeps its folded versions, rewrites a directory's name table from its children's
         moves, matching each row in that row's own epoch, PUTs the new entry (If-None-Match, carried) and deletes
         every source copy; on 412 a file, or a removed or fresh entry (11.7), is done, its source copies deleted
         unmoved, and a carried directory's carried rows are translated and the entry PUT If-Match, read again on
         412; after each PUT it HEADs the path's prefixes in the current epoch and, finding one removed or fresh,
         turns what it put into a marker (If-Match on that PUT's ETag, 11.7; on 412 the newer entry stands); at most
         50 operations a second per repo, 150 while two or more sources stand, 250 in all; it rereads the head at
         least every 5 s (11.7's stale rule) and stops when a newer map supersedes its own; at the end it LISTs
         idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p_i>/ for each source, deletes the markers there unmoved, alarms on any other entry or
         carried row the map missed and keeps that source listed; when every source is empty, a fence write drops the
         sources (11.8), and 11.7 collects the current epoch's markers; one a fold left racing a move reads as absent
read     clients send each path's token path in the current epoch and in each listed source that may hold it:
         where they knew its name before the cut-over, or their listing showed it in that epoch (a carried row, or
         a row of an entry that source served); a name they hold no row for they look up through its parent, and
         an untagged row's child is in the current epoch (copy, above); while sources stand, evs also HEADs in the
         same round a path's prefixes' current entries, whose state (11.7) rides in object metadata, each settled
         by 11.7's rule: under a removed prefix the path is absent, and under a fresh one too unless its own
         current entry is fresh; else evs uses the current entry, else the newest source's, and if every GET of the
         path returned 404 it GETs the current one again, since the copy PUTs it before deleting a source copy;
         changes name their source paths by the same rule (the payload's source paths) and a delta removing a
         child lists its token in each epoch that may hold it, so a fold drops a carried row too, and the server
         sees no source-epoch token of a name created since the cut-over; readers check a carried row under its
         epoch's tokens and AAD
leases   the PATH_EPOCH hint reaches every lease holder of the ref, which re-creates its leases in p_new; a
         holder that missed it does so at its next resync (11.10)
costs    a 1M-file ref moves in about 17 h at 50 operations a second (3 per entry), about 6 h at 150; while sources
         stand, a read takes a HEAD per prefix and, for an unmoved path, a GET per listed source, in the same round
```

**Removal: tokens now, content later (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [64](#od-64)).** Tokens re-key at once, server-side: the server sees them, a removed key holder could keep testing them, and the copy moves no content. New names in general, config and mailcfg repos wait for the map, so none is tokenized under a removed key. Content rewraps lazily: the removed reader already holds every version it could decrypt, so a file's first write checkpoints it under the new generation (11.7 (4)), or `ur evs rekey` does; moved entries keep their bodies under their old generation, which the ladder opens for current readers.

**Nonces.** Every AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 with random 192-bit nonces, so writers share no counter, wasm needs no lookup tables (§10.4), and nothing is encrypted deterministically.

```text
record          header sealed under manifest (160 B): record id, kind, key ref, body length, base record id,
                result git oid, nonce prefix. Body: 64 KiB STREAM frames under its object key, nonce = 19 B
                prefix || 32-bit counter || final flag, as in age (https://github.com/C2SP/C2SP/blob/main/age.md).
                AAD = repo_id || file_id || record id || generation || frame index. evs checks nothing.
segment         immutable, <= 8 MiB: 32 B public header {URvs, format 1, flags, repo_id, generation}, records,
                random padding to Padme(length); id = SHA-256 of all bytes. evs checks id, size, repo, generation.
object key      random 32 B, wrapped under fek_g. General repos: one per segment or inline chain, in its sealed
                header, which is owner decision 61's slot per segment, erased with the repo. Group inboxes: one
                per message, in a deletable slot/ object (§15.7). Record-class repos: one per entry or chain, in
                a deletable slot/ object. Deposits: one per deposit, HPKE to the drop key, in a slot/ object
                CONSUME deletes. Slot ids are 16 random bytes drawn per statement: a push rebuilt after a refusal
                draws new ones, and a retry of the same statement keeps them (11.8)
statements      §6 Signed by the §5 identity key only: EvsPush (purpose evs-push), EvsPathMap (evs-path-epoch,
                by a writer), EvsImport (evs-import, by a repo admin; 11.11), EvsReseed (evs-reseed, by a repo
                admin; 11.13)
kinds           EvsLocator.kind 1 (segment) and 2 (inline) ship in format 1; 3 (push-payload range) and 4 (pack
                range) are reserved, and format-1 readers refuse them, so either can ship with a format version
                that readers learn before writers use it
```

**Records** are `checkpoint`, `diff` (a git pack delta against the file's previous version, https://git-scm.com/docs/gitformat-pack) or `chunk`. Trees are not stored: directory names and each child's sealed {mode, oid} rebuild them exactly. Commits travel sealed in push records with provenance (§5.5's `agent_id`; agent-subkey signatures from v1) and §10's `epoch_authenticator`. A file's random 16-B `file_id`, sealed in its entry, lets a rename keep its chain and stops evs swapping chains between files.

```proto
message EvsPush {                       // sidecar/protocol/evs.proto, inside §6 Signed, purpose evs-push; <= 1 KiB signed
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; uint32 ref_kind = 3; bytes owner_sidecar_id = 4;
  bytes push_id = 5;                    // 16 random bytes; names this statement only (11.8)
  uint64 base_version = 6; bytes base_chain = 7;        // the head it read: v and C_v
  repeated EvsChange changes = 8;       // every change, while the signed statement stays <= 1 KiB
  bytes sealed_metadata_sha256 = 9;     // commits, messages, provenance, epoch_authenticator, EvsImport
  uint64 generation = 10; uint64 path_epoch = 11;
  AuthPin auth = 12;                    // the authorization pin (n, A_n), §7.9
  bytes signer_sidecar_id = 13; bytes client_id = 14; int64 time_ms = 15;
  uint32 flags = 16;                    // 1 FORCE, 2 DELETE, 4 BASE, 8 IMMUTABLE, 16 CONSUME, 32 PATH_EPOCH,
                                        // 64 ERASE, 128 CLOSURE (an erasure's re-checkpoint, 11.12)
  bytes path_map_sha256 = 17;           // PATH_EPOCH: SHA-256 over the epoch's EvsPathMap parts, in order
  uint32 part_count = 18;               // 0 for a one-part push, else 2 to 1,024
  bytes parts_sha256 = 19;              // SHA-256 over the parts' SHA-256s in part order (the list is in the payload)
  uint32 ref_mode = 20;                 // 1 git, 2 file (11.7)
  reserved 21;                          // the pin's chain lives in auth (12)
  bytes group_id = 22; bytes generation_commitment = 23;     // the generation pin with generation: {group, g, C_g}
  bytes changes_root = 24; uint32 change_count = 25;         // when changes are not inline: the root over all of them
  repeated EvsTokenPath changed_prefixes = 26;               // then: token paths, <= 512 B in all, covering every change
  bytes new_objects_sha256 = 27;        // segments (id, padded size, upload day) and slots (id) it introduces
  uint64 map_source_version = 28; bytes map_source_chain = 29;  // PATH_EPOCH: the head the map covers (11.6)
  bytes erased_sha256 = 30;             // ERASE, CLOSURE: SHA-256 of its payload's (slot id, key index) list (11.12)
  bytes path_tail_sha256 = 31;          // PATH_EPOCH: SHA-256 of the tail's moves in its payload (11.6), or empty
  bytes source_paths_sha256 = 32;       // while sources stand: SHA-256 of the payload's source paths (11.6), or empty
}
message EvsTokenPath { repeated bytes token = 1; }            // 16 B per component
message EvsChange {
  repeated bytes token_path = 1;        // 16 B per component, in the push's path epoch
  uint32 base_entry_version = 2;        // 0 creates; the path-level CAS condition (directories merge, 11.7)
  bytes entry_sha256 = 3;               // SHA-256 of the new EvsEntryVersion; empty deletes
}
message EvsPushPart {                   // unsigned; parts_sha256 binds it
  bytes push_id = 1; uint32 part = 2;
  repeated EvsChange changes = 3;       // at most 1,024 entry writes; a path appears in one part only
  repeated bytes entry_versions = 4;    // EvsEntryVersion bytes, as each change's entry_sha256 names
  repeated bytes inline_records = 5;    // those that fit in 1 MiB; the rest go into segments
  bytes sealed_metadata = 6;            // a slice; sealed_metadata_sha256 covers the slices in order
  bytes changes_root = 7;               // root over this part's changes; the statement's root is over these roots
}
message EvsEntryVersion {               // what entry_sha256 hashes; in the push record, and folded into idx/
  uint32 version = 1;                   // base_entry_version + 1; a creation's above a standing removal's (11.7)
  bytes push_id = 2; uint64 base_version = 3;            // the push that wrote it and the head it read
  bytes prev_push_id = 4; uint64 prev_commit_version = 5; // the version it replaces, for history walks
  int64 time_ms = 6; uint32 kind = 7; uint64 padded_size = 8;
  bytes sealed_fields = 9;              // file: {file_id, mode, git oid, size}; directory: none
  repeated EvsLocator chain = 10;       // file: at most N+1 records
  repeated bytes slot_ids = 11;
  EvsNameTable names = 12;              // directory: a push's delta; in idx/, a fold's table (11.7)
  uint32 layout = 13;                   // directory: 0 single; other values reserved and refused
}
message EvsNameTable { repeated EvsName names = 1; repeated bytes removed_tokens = 2; }  // a fold's table removes none
message EvsName {                       // sealed as 11.7's name row
  bytes token = 1; uint32 kind = 2; bytes sealed_name = 3;
  uint64 epoch = 4;                     // 0, or the source epoch whose token and AAD a carried row keeps (11.6)
}
message EvsLocator {
  uint32 kind = 1;                      // 1 segment, 2 inline; 3 (push-payload range) and 4 (pack range) reserved
  bytes id = 2;                         // kind 1: segment_id, at seg/<repo>/<id> or through spidx/ (11.13)
  uint32 offset = 3; uint32 length = 4; bytes inline = 5;
}
message EvsPathMap {                    // purpose evs-path-epoch; at most 8 MiB per part
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; uint64 path_epoch = 3; uint32 part = 4; uint32 parts = 5;
  repeated EvsPathMove moves = 6;
  uint64 source_version = 7; bytes source_chain = 8;    // the head whose paths the map covers
}
message EvsPathMove {
  repeated bytes new_token_path = 1;
  repeated EvsSourcePath sources = 2;   // the path in the current epoch and in each listed source
  bytes sealed_name = 3;                // re-sealed under AAD with the new parent and child tokens
}
message EvsSourcePath { uint64 epoch = 1; repeated bytes token_path = 2; }
message EvsImport {                     // purpose evs-import; carried in the push's sealed metadata
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; bytes tip_oid = 3; bytes oid_list_sha256 = 4; uint32 count = 5;
}
message EvsReseed {                     // §6 Signed, purpose evs-reseed, by a repo admin (§8.8); §19.10
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2;
  uint64 version = 3; bytes chain = 4;  // the re-seeded head: v and C_v
  bytes incident_id = 5;                // the recovery's identity (§19.10)
}
message EvsUploadReceipt {              // unsigned; evs MACs it (11.13), the push carries it back
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes segment_id = 2; uint64 padded_size = 3; int64 upload_ms = 4;
  bytes uploader_sidecar_id = 5; uint32 key_id = 6; bytes mac = 7;  // HMAC-SHA256 over fields 1-6, first 16 B
}
message EvsPlace {                      // where a batch record's bytes are (11.8); assigned by evs, 20 B packed
  uint32 minute = 1; uint32 instance = 2; uint32 seq = 3; uint32 offset = 4; uint32 length = 5;
}
```

```text
size     a signed statement is at most 1 KiB, so log pages hold statements; big change lists move to the payload
         under changes_root
payload  in the push's batch record for a one-part push, else spread over its parts and its seal: entry versions,
         sealed metadata, inline records, the change list when not inline, the part hashes, the new-objects list
         (segment id, padded size and the UTC day of its upload, from its receipt; slot ids), new slot bodies, the
         erased list, a PATH_EPOCH's tail moves, the source paths (per change, an EvsSourcePath for each listed
         source that may hold it, 11.6's read rule, in change order), the reuse list of committed versions whose
         segments a new version cites ((ref, token path, entry version), 11.8) and, per entry version, its Merkle
         proof to changes_root (empty when inline)
checks   at push time evs checks that each entry version hashes to its change's entry_sha256, that the change list
         matches changes_root, is sorted (merkle, below) and changed_prefixes cover it, and that the payload lists
         match new_objects_sha256, parts_sha256, erased_sha256, path_tail_sha256 and source_paths_sha256; a
         statement over 1 KiB is refused
merkle   RFC 9162 hashing: leaf SHA-256(0x00 || bytes), node SHA-256(0x01 || left || right); changes sort by
         their token paths' bytes, each part a contiguous run in part order, so inclusion proofs of two adjacent
         leaves show that no path between them changed (11.9)
```

### 11.7 Diffs, checkpoints, index entries, reconstruction

**Mapping to git.** Each ref has a mode: git-mode refs, which the local tier writes, commit only on their tip; file-mode refs land by path ([owner decision 141](#od-141)). One evs push carries one git ref update, in parts when large (11.8); its cleartext changes are the net change per path, and its sealed metadata holds every commit with each intermediate commit's sealed changes, so export rebuilds every original oid.

```text
mode  written by                commit condition                       on a lost race                  export
git   the local tier: ur mount, TIP: base_version = v, a whole-ref     409; git reports a stock        the original commits
      git-remote-ur, ur evs     CAS for every push, FORCE and          non-fast-forward; the client    and oids
      import, and evs_write     PATH_EPOCH included                    fetches, merges or rebases
      through it (§16.2)                                               (new commits) and pushes again
file  evs_write on file-mode    path-level CAS: each changed file      evs lands a disjoint push at    one deterministic commit
      refs, head mode, record   path's newest committed entry version  the next version itself; a      per version: tree = the
      streams, deposits, mail,  equals its base_entry_version, and     shared path answers 409 with    state, parent = the previous
      config, mailcfg           base_version >= v - 63                 the paths                       version's, committer
                                                                                                       <client_id>@ur.invalid of the
                                                                                                       signer, time time_ms, message
                                                                                                       "ur push <push_id hex>"
set       the ref's first push sets ref_mode in its statement and the head; another mode is refused (409 REF_MODE);
          only git-mode refs take overlays (below), which are git mode
replay    replaying readers of a git-mode ref check TIP; that the first new commit's parent is the previous tip, and
          descent, except on a FORCE push the refs table allows or the first push after a DELETE; oids; and that
          every new commit's committer is the signer's <client_id>@ur.invalid (owner decision 81) except the oids
          an EvsImport lists, so the forced identity is a property of the stored history, not only of the hook;
          PATH_EPOCH pushes carry no commit and are skipped in descent
head mode mobile and wasm read both modes and write only file-mode refs; the SDK's Write on a git-mode ref returns
          EVS_GIT_REF, since a head-mode client cannot build a git tree, which needs every sibling's oid
scope     tags are git-mode refs pushed IMMUTABLE; LFS, replace refs, notes other than export's refs/notes/ur,
          partial-clone filters and atomic multi-ref pushes are outside v0 (11.11)
why tip   a path-disjoint landing gives a git ref a tree no git commit has, so export could not keep the original
          oids, and a server-made merge would merge shared branches automatically, which sidecar/market2.md:519-520
          forbids; tip CAS costs a client retry only when two merges meet (about 2% in the twenty-agent test)
```

**Checkpoints (PLAN.md:63)** are written when (1) the chain has N = 16 diffs; (2) its diffs exceed 50% of the file's size (Mercurial's revlog rule, [R:ext-storage-crypto](design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.10); (3) the file is new, or the delta outgrows it; or (4) a REMOVE generation (§10.5's GenRotate `cause`: it covers a shrink, an authorization expiry or a compromise retirement) is newer than the chain's key, which is PLAN.md:50's rewrap rule ([owner decision 64](#od-64)); every checkpoint draws a fresh object key.

**Large files** over 8 MiB are 4 MiB `chunk` records, rewritten only where touched; fixed sizes avoid content-defined chunking, whose chunk sizes leak and whose keyed variants were broken in 2025 (ePrint 2025/558). The v0 file cap is 2 GiB.

**Index entries** cache each path's committed versions, folded from committed pushes; push records hold every one:

```text
version   an EvsEntryVersion (11.6): a file's sealed fields, its chain (at most N+1 locators, inline when it pads to
          <= 16 KiB) and slot ids; a directory's names
holds     only committed versions, written by folds: per file up to four folded EvsEntryVersions with their push id
          and commit version u, the newest with its inline records and older ones with inline records elided (evs
          restores them from the push record before serving the signed bytes); per directory one name table, as of
          the newest delta applied; per removed path its marker (removal, below); a fold never drops the newest
          folded version, and drops older ones only for newer
newest    a path's newest committed version at a head H is the newer of its entry's newest folded version, a marker's
          removal included, and the newest version after h that changes the path or a prefix holding it (the digest
          first, then the statement's change list), h being the folded_through of a head evs read before the entry: a
          fold's PUTs precede the commit that raises folded_through over them, so the entry holds every version
          through h; H's window must hold every version after h, else evs reads the entry again after H, and a folded
          version committed after H's v sends evs to a newer head; head reads, listings and 11.8's path-level CAS,
          reruns included, all use this rule
versions  a removal is one of the path's versions, one past its last, which its marker keeps (owner decision 148);
          base_entry_version 0 names the path absent, never written or removed, and a creation's entry version must
          exceed that of a removal its marker or the window holds, so a re-created path continues its versions and a
          push based on one from before the removal fails 5g; a client refused creating (409) reads the removal
          (11.9) and retries; replaying readers require this of a creation committed within 64 versions of the
          removal, after which a collected marker lets the path restart at 1, as no push based before the removal can
          then commit
fold      for a ref's window versions (f, u]: read their statements and entry versions (the process's cache, else
          batch ranges); per changed file path, its newest version or removal (its own or a prefix's) in (f, u],
          skipped when a window version after u changes that file again; per changed directory, every delta in (f, u]
          past the version its entry holds, applied in version order, since a newer delta never replaces an older
          one; GET each entry (404: create it, once a cluster read of the ref's head in this fold succeeds, 11.13's
          skip rule), merge (a file's folded versions, the newest four kept; a creation replaces what the entry held,
          carrying nothing), PUT If-Match (If-None-Match to create), on 412 read again and merge; an entry that
          already holds a version is not written, and a marker takes only a newer one (collect, below); folds are
          idempotent, and any evs process may run one
stale     each fold and copy write is cancelled 15 s after it issued the cluster read of the ref's head it relies on
          (§19.6: it applies by then or never), a page-out's fold reading the head from the cluster when step 4's came
          from the cache; a fold relies only on a read whose folded_through is at most its f, stopping at one above it
          (another folded its range), and a copy only on one still listing its sources, so no write planned before
          the horizon rose or the sources dropped lands 15 s later
when      (1) after a commit that leaves 96 or more versions unfolded, the committing process folds the oldest 64,
          off the reply path, at most once per ref per 10 s; (2) 10 min after a ref's last commit, the process that
          made it folds the rest; (3) a commit that pages versions out of the window first folds any of them still
          unfolded (11.8 step 6); (4) a PATH_EPOCH push's process first folds every unfolded version, as step 6
          does for a page-out (on a busy git-mode ref under the seal lease), and its step-7 head sets
          folded_through = v, so an idle ref whose folded_through trails v still commits its epoch
horizon   folded_through: every file change at or below it, a removal as its marker, is in its path's entry or
          replaced by a newer window version of that file, and every directory delta at or below it is applied to its
          name table; it rises only with a commit by the process that folded, so folds add no head write, and a stale
          value costs readers only statement reads
lag       if a page-out's fold cannot finish within 11.8's 5 s rule, the commit proceeds without paging, the window
          growing to at most 255 versions; past that, pushes to the ref get 429 FOLD_BEHIND with retry_after_ms
epochs    a fold writes the current path epoch's entries, each, while the head lists sources, with its state in its
          object metadata: carried, as the copy writes, when the change's source paths (its push record) name a
          source still holding the path, keeping that source's folded versions and tagging its untagged rows with its
          epoch, rows already carried keeping theirs until the copy translates them (11.6); fresh when the path is
          new to the current epoch, a re-creation replacing a marker and carrying nothing; or removed:
removal   a fold never deletes an entry (owner decision 148): a removal at r gives the path and, for a directory,
          every current-epoch entry below it (LIST) a marker {removing push id, r, the path's version (versions,
          above)}, in version order with the versions below it, by PUT If-Match on the entry it read (If-None-Match
          on a 404) only while that entry holds a version older than r, a marker staying as it is; on 412 it reads
          again; the path's own marker precedes that LIST, so while sources stand no read or copy falls back to a
          source at or below it (11.6), and no repeated, queued or late removal fold writes over an entry a later
          fold wrote, which holds a newer version
collect   markers whose removal r the horizon has passed by a base range (folded_through >= r + 64, so no push based
          before it can commit, 11.8) are collected while the head lists no source, by taskworker's nightly pass from
          the removals the ref's statements name after head.collect.done (a removed directory's markers by LIST), in
          windows: one head CAS raising only the fence sets collect {through: the window's newest r, until_ms: 30 s
          on}, opening only 100 ms after the last window lapsed; 15.1 s later, every fold write planned on an older
          head having applied or been cancelled (stale, above), it GETs each marker of a removal at or below through
          and DELETEs it once, unconditionally (11.3), cancelled at until_ms (§19.6: by then or never), and once all
          have answered sets done to through by another such CAS; a fold that read a head whose until_ms is ahead
          writes over no such marker until 100 ms past it, nor does one on a process whose clock is unsure (11.8's
          fence row), and a 404 needs no wait, a window deleting a key once
directory a push's directory change is a delta {names added, child tokens removed} that merges without a path-level
          CAS, since each child's own path is checked, except that a child directory D is checked both ways: a push
          removing D gets 409 with D's path if a delta to D committed after its base, and a push changing D gets
          that 409 if D's removal committed after its base; a fold applies committed deltas to the name table {child
          token, kind, sealed name}; at most 4,096 children and 448 KiB of name table (its EvsName rows: tokens,
          kinds, sealed names with nonce and tag; a carried row counted at its untagged size, so the bound holds
          through a copy, its epoch adding 3-5 B, under 466 KiB at the bound, within idx/'s 512 KiB), checked in
          step 5g against the folded table plus the deltas after h (newest, above; 409 DIRECTORY_FULL), which is
          v0's git limit; the bytes bind first, at 3,584 children whose names are under 64 B; `layout` reserves
          paging; §15 and §16 shard by sequence and size directories by these bytes
name      sealed alone: the name, then 0x80 and zeros to the next multiple of 64 B, under a random 24 B nonce with
          a 16 B tag; AAD repo_id || path epoch || parent and child tokens; with its token, kind and framing, an
          untagged row takes 128 B for a name under 64 B, 194 B under 128 B, and 64 B more per further 64 B
repair    an entry that lacks its path's newest committed version older than the window is refolded from that push's
          record; a version a newer one replaced is reached by the history walk; push records, log pages, packs and
          parcels are the record, idx/ the cache
keys      idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/<t1>/.../<tn>.e: the entry of path t1..tn sits beside the directory t1/.../tn/ that
          holds its children's keys, so no key prefixes another (11.3), and a file entry takes one directory and one
          file on each drive instead of two directories and a file; LIST by prefix still lists a subtree
```

Readers check each name against its token, so evs folds committed directory deltas itself, and pushes adding different files to one directory never conflict on a file-mode ref.

**Overlays.** Only git-mode refs take overlays: a ref created from one (an agent branch) records its base (ref, version) and writes only the paths it changes. A path it has not changed has the base ref's version at that base version, which its writers (the local tier) and its readers settle and check by replaying both refs; head mode reads no overlay (§18.5's `ReadHead` names no ref). So 5g checks an overlay only on paths its own entries or window hold, TIP settling the rest, a chain citing the base's segments names that base version as a `reuse` source (5h), and 11.9 answers `base` {ref, version} for any other path; §22 covers overlays by FS rows, not the model.

**Reconstruction:** check the entry version against its statement (11.9), read the chain, unwrap its keys, apply the deltas and check the blob oid. Delta bases over 1 MiB spill to the sealed local store.

### 11.8 The evs service: objects, push, commit, reads

**Objects.** `ServiceHost.Blobs` (§4) gives stateless evs an unversioned bucket on each cluster, so a DELETE or overwrite keeps no prior version ([owner decision 90](#od-90)):

```text
metadata cluster (NVMe)                    holds                                            written             size       lifetime
place/<repo_id>                            the repo's metadata cluster (placement, below);  If-None-Match       <= 256 B   the repo and its
                                           first cluster only                                                              tombstone
repo/<repo>                                kind, owner_member_id, state and deletion_id     If-Match            <= 4 KiB   the repo; a shredded
                                           (11.12), object format, sealed name                                           tombstone stays
head/<repo>/<ref>                          the commit point: fields, 64-byte window         If-Match; created   <= 9 KiB   the ref; DELETE leaves
                                           entries                                          If-None-Match       (17 while  a tombstone head
                                                                                                                folds lag)
log/<repo>/<ref>/<n>                       versions 64n..64n+63: their window entries and   If-None-Match;      <= 70 KiB  history; packed after
                                           Signed EvsPush, C_{64n-1} and C_{64n+63}          equal bytes on 412             24 h (11.13)
pb/<yyyymmddhh>/<mm>/<instance>-<seq>      a batch: push, part, seal and reseed records     If-None-Match and   <= 256 KiB 25-26 h, then evacuated
                                           of one evs process (below)                       its checksum        (one record: 1 MiB) whole (11.13)
idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/<t1>/.../<tn>.e       index entry in path epoch p: folded committed    If-Match; created   <= 512 KiB the path; a
                                           versions, or a removal's marker, its state in    If-None-Match                  marker until
                                           object metadata (11.7)                                                          collected (11.7)
slot/<repo>/<slot_id>                      up to 64 sealed object keys: under fek_g, or     If-None-Match;      <= 8 KiB   until erased, consumed
                                           HPKE to the drop key for deposits                rewritten If-Match             or shredded; a dead
                                                                                                                           push's, <= ~26 h
hp/<repo>/<parcel_id>                      a small repo's records older than 24 h (11.13)   If-None-Match       <= 256 KiB until packed, <= 7 d
pmap/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/<map>/<part>/_       a Signed EvsPathMap part (11.6); <map> is its    If-None-Match       <= 8 MiB   the committed map:
                                           map's path_map_sha256                                                           the ref's history;
                                                                                                                           others go (11.6)
pidx/<repo>/<ref>/<v_first>-<id>           a pack's or parcel's records and log pages, and  If-None-Match       <= 1 MiB   as its pack or parcel
                                           the segments they introduce; <id> is that
                                           container's (11.13)
spidx/<repo>/<n>/_                         reserved (11.13): offsets of segments in a pack  If-None-Match       <= 1 MiB   as its pack
hold/<network_id>/<case_id>/_              §21.9's preservation hold, written by api;       api                 <= 1 KiB   its kind's (§21.9):
                                           first cluster only                                                              90 d, renewable
                                                                                                                           once, or 1 year for
                                                                                                                           report_2258a
segment cluster (HDD)
seg/<repo>/<segment_id>                    one segment; segment_id = SHA-256 of its bytes   If-None-Match and   <= 8 MiB   while a retained
                                                                                            its checksum                   version names it
pack/<repo>/<pack_id>                      records and log pages older than 24 h, >= 256    If-None-Match and   >= 256 KiB history
                                           KiB or 7 d old (owner decision 136); reserved:   its checksum        or 7 d
                                           segments
Redis (soft state, owner decision 136)     {evsq_} push sequence, {evsl_} leases, {evsh_} head cache (11.9, 11.10)
C_0 = SHA-256("UR evs 1.0 ref" || repo_id || ref_id);  C_v = SHA-256(C_{v-1} || push_id_v || SHA-256(Signed EvsPush_v))
```

```text
decides   head/ alone: a ref's state changes only by a head If-Match (If-None-Match to create)
immutable place/ log/ pb/ hp/ pmap/ pidx/ spidx/ seg/ pack/: created once; a 412 on equal bytes is success; never
          overwritten; deleted only whole, by evacuation, packing, orphan GC, consumption, retention or shred, and
          place/ never in v0
cache     idx/: If-Match (owner decision 2), written only by folds of committed versions and removals (markers), each
          also in its push record, and deleted only by a copy (its sources), 11.7's collection or a shred; none
          decides an outcome
fences    repo/ (lifecycle CAS, 11.12), slot/ (created If-None-Match, equal bytes on 412 success; rewritten only to
          drop erased keys)
keys      no key prefixes another (11.3): entries end in .e beside their children's directory; map, spidx and hold
          keys end in /_, and pidx/ keys under a ref have one fixed length
```

**Placement ([owner decision 145](#od-145)).** The metadata tier grows only by whole clusters, never MinIO pools, whose PUTs can pass a precondition in a pool the key is not in (11.3):

```text
place     PUT /evs/v1/repos/<id> first creates place/<repo_id> {cluster id, creator sidecar_id} on the first
          metadata cluster (If-None-Match), naming the cluster that takes new repos (§19.9); on 412 it reads the
          object: the same creator continues on the cluster it names, any other gets 409; only then does it write
          repo/<id> there, so of two racing creates exactly one places the repo, and a retry never moves it
resolve   evs and gkm read a repo's place/ once and cache it for the process's life, since it never changes (a 404
          for 5 s); every metadata object of the repo and its gkm group, batch records included, lives on that
          cluster, so each ref keeps one commit point
first     the first cluster also holds §7's proj/, projrows/ and rev/, §10.6's per-sidecar gkm/ objects (KeyPackages
          and their claims, ReaderKeys, Welcome pointers) and §21's hold/
form      each cluster is one homogeneous 8-drive set at EC:4 in one pool (owner decisions 116, 139); a repo's
          cluster changes only with a later move tool that keeps one commit point
```

**Authorization.** The daemon's §7 service token (aud `evs`, scope `repo:<id>:deposit|r|rw|admin`, 15 min) never leaves it (I-7). evs verifies it offline, checks §7.8's `rev/` objects for its three subjects, honors a scope only while its newest verified state agrees (D-ACL-21), read from §7.9's verified `{acl_}e` cache, which only api writes, else from `proj/`, and matches `ur_sidecar_id` to §5's binding; `admin` covers FORCE, DELETE, BASE, ERASE, CLOSURE and its uploads, re-seeding, deletion and restore, and in §19.10's re-seed mode only `/reseed` (§7.8). evs-7 is evs's 7-day service log (§19.8).

**The head** (D-EVS-29) is server-internal, never a client wire format:

```proto
message EvsHead {                       // head/<repo>/<ref>; written only by If-Match (create: If-None-Match)
  uint64 version = 1; bytes chain = 2;  // v, C_v
  bytes push_id = 3;                    // the push committed at v
  uint32 ref_kind = 4; uint32 ref_mode = 5; bytes owner_sidecar_id = 6; bytes sealed_ref_name = 7;
  EvsOverlay base = 8;                  // an overlay's (ref_id, version)
  AuthPin auth = 9; reserved 10;        // authorization pin (n, A_n), §7.9: never falls (below)
  bytes group_id = 11; uint64 generation = 12; bytes generation_commitment = 13;  // generation pin: never falls
  EvsPathEpoch path_epoch = 14;         // 11.6
  bytes window = 15;                    // 64-byte EvsWindowEntry records, versions v-w+1..v, oldest first;
                                        // w in 64..127, at most 255 while folds lag (11.7)
  uint32 fence = 16;                    // raised by every write that changes no version (below, 11.13)
  EvsSealLease lease = 17;              // git mode: {push_id, until_ms}, or empty
  bool deleted = 18;                    // DELETE committed; a later push to the name continues the versions
  bytes window_base_chain = 19;         // C at version v-w, so the window's chain is computable forward
  uint64 folded_through = 20;           // 11.7's horizon: file changes folded or replaced, directory deltas applied
  int64 written_ms = 21;                // evs's clock at this head's write (11.13's orphan rule)
  int64 fence_ms = 22;                  // its writer's clock at the newest refusal, evacuation or GC fence (outcomes)
  EvsCollect collect = 23;              // 11.7's marker collection: done, through and a window's until_ms
}
message EvsOverlay { bytes ref_id = 1; uint64 version = 2; }
message EvsSealLease { bytes push_id = 1; int64 until_ms = 2; }
message EvsPathEpoch {
  uint64 current = 1;                   // p: the generation whose RK derives K_path
  repeated EvsEpochSource sources = 2;  // at most 3 older epochs still holding entries, newest first
  uint64 due_generation = 3;            // a generation that requires a new epoch, or 0
  bool due_blocks_creation = 4; int64 due_by_ms = 5;
  int64 block_until_ms = 6;             // a mapper's creation block (11.6), or 0
}
message EvsEpochSource { uint64 epoch = 1; bytes map_sha256 = 2; }
message EvsCollect { uint64 done = 1; uint64 through = 2; int64 until_ms = 3; }
```

```text
entry     EvsWindowEntry, 64 B, fixed layout: push_id (16) | statement_sha256[0:16] (16) | place (20) | paths_digest
          (8) | flags (4: bit 0 the push creates a path; bit 1 its change list is in the payload under changes_root;
          bit 2 PATH_EPOCH; bit 3 FORCE, DELETE, BASE or ERASE; bits 16-31 its change count, saturating)
digest    a 64-bit Bloom filter, k = 2, over each changed token path and, when the change list is not inline, each
          covering prefix: indexes from SHA-256("UR evs digest" || token path)[0:4] mod 64 and [4:8] mod 64; evs
          queries a path and each of its prefixes: a match only sends it to the statement's change list, and a miss on
          all of them proves the push changed neither the path nor a prefix holding it
size      at most ~0.85 KiB of fields plus 127 entries: ~8.8 KiB, typically ~7 KiB, so its xl.meta is one 4 KiB block
          (or three 1 KiB blocks) on each drive; a log page holds its 64 versions' entries and Signed EvsPush
          statements and C at both ends, at most ~70 KiB
fill      at step 7 evs appends P's entry from the statement it checked and the place its batch write returned;
          readers never parse the head object (they get 11.9's head summary)
etag      every head write raises the version or, for a write that commits nothing (a fence, a seal lease, a creation
          block, dropping drained path-epoch sources, a collection window), the fence, so an ETag never repeats; only
          refusal, evacuation and GC fences also set fence_ms (the outcome rule below)
trust     a wrong place, hash or digest can only produce a missing or mismatched statement, which breaks the chain
          and alarms; the digest cannot hide a change, because readers check every returned statement's change list
```

**Batches (D-EVS-30):**

```text
key       pb/<yyyymmddhh>/<mm>/<instance>-<seq>: the UTC hour and minute the batch was opened, the evs process's
          random 32-bit id (8 hex) and its counter within that minute (8 hex)
bytes     header {"URpb", format 1, instance, minute, seq, created_ms, record count} | records | index | trailer
          {index offset, SHA-256 of all bytes before it}; at most 256 KiB, or one record of up to 1 MiB
record    {type, repo_id, ref_id, push_id, signer_sidecar_id, time_ms, length, body}; push: the Signed EvsPush and its
          payload (11.6); part: the Signed EvsPush, EvsPushPart k, its receipts and the head version evs checked it
          at; seal: the Signed EvsPush, its parts' places and each part's changes_root and first token path;
          reseed: a re-seeded push (11.13)
place     an EvsPlace (11.6), 20 B: where a record's bytes are
open      each evs process holds one open batch per metadata cluster, for repos placed there; a request's record
          joins it at step 6 (a part or seal at its own step), and the request waits for that batch's write
flush     a process writes an open batch when it reaches 256 KiB, when its oldest record has waited 20 ms, or at once
          when it has no batch write in flight there and took fewer than 50 records in the last second; at most two
          batch writes in flight per process and cluster; a record over 256 KiB is a batch alone
write     PUT If-None-Match, the SHA-256 as x-amz-checksum-sha256; a 412 reads the key back: equal bytes are success,
          others a fault that alarms; an unknown outcome GETs the key: equal bytes written, 404 written again with the
          same bytes; with the store unreachable, every waiting request gets 503, retryable, since nothing it carried
          reached a head
```
