[Owner decision 140](#od-140)'s binding limits are the drive budget: at most 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS at the design load, met at ~27-43 KiB a push before [owner decision 148](#od-148)'s markers, which add ~12.5-14 KiB a removed entry (§22.8's fold row counts them); the head's If-Match overwrite alone (~14 KiB, [owner decision 2](#od-2)) sets the floor (Q-EVS-9). §22.8's M2 exit runs this mix at 2× year one with the write budget on, refilled at 0.8 DWPD for the run, a restart included: p99 ≤ 25 ms per operation, at most 43 KiB per push per drive ([owner decision 140](#od-140)), no push refused by the budget, no ref at FOLD_BEHIND and no batch past 26 h. Batches are per process and cluster (11.8), so at ~8 evs processes a set near its capacity sees ~1-1.6 records a batch and sustains ~400-450 pushes/s (~530-600 on 1 KiB blocks), not the ~490-650 [owner decision 145](#od-145) records, which assumed batches shared across the whole load; year two needs five to six sets, sized from §22.8's records per batch per cluster. Each next cluster starts at §19.9's triggers, the second at about 1.25× year one, and takes new repos ([owner decision 145](#od-145)).

**Fair share and the write budget ([owner decision 140](#od-140)).** No network can wear or take a metadata cluster from the others, and no count cap applies ([owner decision 66](#od-66)):

```text
budget   every metadata write spends its cluster's one budget: 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS on the busiest
         drive not under heal (§19.6), a bucket only measured drive bytes drain (§19.6's counters), refilled at
         0.768 DWPD (0.8 x 24/25) with 1 h of depth, so no 24 h window passes 0.8 DWPD; IOs are bounded, not
         metered: each drive write moves at least one 512 B sector, so the refill caps a drive's sustained writes
         at ~33,000 a second, 39% of 85,000
price    each write is priced before it is issued in drive bytes: the cost row above (§22.8's measurement) times k,
         the measured over the priced bytes of the last 10 min
classes  P0, never queued or refused, bounded by its classes' own rate limits (§10.6's 60 commits an hour per
         uploader and group; §7.9's per-network append limits; 11.12's ERASE rate): rev/, proj/, repo/ lifecycle
         (deletion, restore), shred steps, ERASE and CLOSURE pushes within that rate and every slot rewrite, gkm
         Removes and REMOVE rotations; P1, queued per network: pushes, parts, gkm commits, Adds, Welcomes,
         KeyPackages, GroupInfo, path maps; P2: folds, evacuation, packing, GC, copies, retention, fences
accounts every 5 s {nvb_<set>} publishes the allowance T: the next 5 s of refill, times 1 while the bucket is at
         least half full and falling linearly to 0.2 when it is empty, less P0's measured writes of the last 5 s;
         T splits as A1 for P1 and A2 for P2; a P1 admission debits A1 at full price, its own writes plus the P2
         work it causes (fold share, batch delete, evacuation, parcel and pidx/ writes), and credits that deferred
         part to P2, so shedding a push sheds its P2 work; P2 writes debit only A2, which is P2's credit up to its
         backlog and the bucket's level; while the backlog exceeds the credit, A2 is topped up to 40% of T (above P2's steady ~37%
         until §22.8's fold and trash rows measure it) and A1 shrinks by the top-up; every evs, gkm and taskworker
         process reports in {nvb_<set>} every 5 s its queued P1 priced bytes, its P2 backlog and the credit it
         admitted, and §19.6's publishing loop splits A1 by the first and A2 by the second
order    P2 runs by deadline: evacuation, oldest minute directory first; the folds a page-out needs; other folds,
         path-epoch copies, packing, retention and GC; a fence goes with the work that raises it, a refusal's with
         its request
queue    each evs, gkm and taskworker process queues P1 work per network (the token's) and serves the queues by
         weighted fair queuing on priced bytes, with tier weights in pro.yml (<tier>.sidecar: store_weight; 1, 4 and
         16), within its A1 share
shed     past 100 ms of queueing delay it refuses first the network with the most queued priced bytes per weight:
         429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with retry_after_ms (§6.5's codes)
fallback a process without a fresh allowance for 60 s runs at half its last shares, and one that never had an
         allowance, at start, at the refill over twice the process count
bound    no request does more than a part's ~2,060 operations, so an import interleaves with other networks
outside  §19.5's W2 zones still count per address
```

**GC and evacuation ([owner decision 136](#od-136))**, all P2 work under the write budget:

```text
gc        folds keep up to four folded versions a path, and markers go in 11.7's collection windows; history stays
          forever by default, and record-class repos follow §16's retention through an admin BASE that re-lists the
          live set and keeps every push statement; deposits go after CONSUME, and segments no retained push names
          after 7 d; taskworker works from the log, the hourly evacuation and one LIST of each repo's prefixes a
          night, and skips held networks' in-scope objects (§21.9)
when      hourly (so each day everything older than 24 h leaves the batches; owner decision 136), taskworker
          evacuates each minute directory pb/<h>/<m>/ of each metadata cluster once that minute is over 25 h old:
          batches leave NVMe within 26 h, and a small repo's history leaves its parcels within 7 d (move, below)
resolve   per batch, GET it whole; per record, Resolve its push id on its ref (11.8): committed at this place ->
          keep; committed at another place -> drop; dead -> drop, deleting the new slots its record lists, the only
          cleanup (11.8); pending -> raise the ref's fence (one head CAS), then Resolve again; parts follow their
          seal; reseed records count as committed
move      per repo, the kept records plus its log pages older than 24 h, one pack or parcel per repo a run across all
          the minute directories it evacuates: once its aged material (these, its parcels and unpacked log pages)
          reaches 256 KiB, one pack/<repo>/<pack_id> on the segment cluster (If-None-Match, its SHA-256 as checksum)
          holds all of it, then a pidx/ entry per ref, then its parcels and those log pages are deleted; below
          256 KiB, one parcel hp/<repo>/<parcel_id> (If-None-Match) and its pidx/ entries; a repo's aged material
          also packs once its oldest (parcel content or unpacked log page) is 7 d old: in the run that evacuates
          the repo, or, for an idle repo, in the nightly pass, which packs any whose oldest would pass 7 d before
          the next pass
delete    once every repo of a minute directory is moved, DELETE each of its batches, whole (I-EVS-7)
skip      every P2 write for a repo (folds, moves, packing, copies) rereads repo/ when issued, not when queued (cached
          at most 5 s), and proceeds only while it shows active or deleted, or, for moves and packing, shredding
          while a hold/ has the repo in scope (§21.9); so an unheld repo in shredding or shredded loses its batched
          records here, and no write re-creates its objects after its shred; a deleted, restorable repo keeps them;
          a held network's records, a shredding repo's included, are moved as usual and nothing deletes them while
          the hold stands; phases 5-6 remove a shredding repo's once it ends (11.12)
index     pidx/<repo>/<ref>/<v_first>-<id> (v_first zero-padded to 20 digits, <id> the container's pack_id or
          parcel_id, the first 16 B of SHA-256 over its bytes; nothing extends it, and containers never share a
          key): {container kind, versions v_first..v_last with each record's kind, offset and length, the log pages
          it holds, the segment ids its records introduce}; a push whose parts and seal evacuate in different runs
          has an entry in each container; a parcel is replaced by its pack's entries first, then the parcel and its
          entries are deleted
readers   a record whose batch is gone is found by LIST pidx/<repo>/<ref>/ (cached; entries never change), a pack's
          entry taken over a parcel's for a record both name, and a range read
negative  a reader whose cached pidx/ or spidx/ lookup misses or names a deleted container, and so gets a 404, drops
          the cache and lists again; a container precedes its index entries, and both precede the deletion of what
          they replace, so one retry finds the object
resume    a run first lists the repo's pidx/ entries and moves only what no container holds (from a parcel, what no
          pack holds); a container with equal bytes on 412 is reused, entries are create-only, and a batch is
          deleted only after its minute's moves finished, so a killed run restarts the minute; the nightly pass
          deletes a pack or parcel with its entries once newer containers' entries name its every record, and one
          no entry names after 25 h
cost      at year two ~6 HDD PUTs a second (busy repos' packs); on the metadata cluster ~3 parcel and pidx/ writes a
          second in year one and ~30 in year two at 10 records a parcel (§22.8 measures records per parcel), and one
          DELETE per batch; NVMe residency 25-26 h for batches, and for a small repo's history at most 7 d after its
          commit plus an hour
```

**Uploads (D-EVS-34):**

```text
receipt   a segment PUT (?push=P) that stores the segment (If-None-Match, its id as x-amz-checksum-sha256) answers
          200 {EvsUploadReceipt} (11.6), MAC'd under evs's receipt key key_id; nothing is written to the metadata
          cluster
existing  if the segment exists (412), evs HEADs it (one HDD operation, only on re-uploads) and answers a receipt
          with its LastModified as upload_ms, or 409 SEGMENT_STALE when that is over 23 h old: the client re-seals
          the chain under a new key and nonce, so a new segment id
push      the push request (step 3) and each part carry one receipt per new segment, unsigned and outside the
          statement; check h: each receipt's mac is valid, for this repo, its uploader is the push's signer, and
          upload_ms is under 24 h old by evs's clock; parts are checked at part time, and their records keep their
          receipts, whose age the seal checks again
keys      receipt keys are evs configuration, rotated monthly with the previous key kept 48 h (§19.4); losing a key
          only makes pending uploads re-upload
orphans   the nightly pass LISTs each repo's seg/ prefix on the segment cluster, as it does for stored bytes; a
          segment that no committed push of the repo introduced (pidx/ entries record what evacuated records
          introduce; records still in batches are read in place) and whose LastModified is over 25 h old is an
          orphan: taskworker raises the fence of each ref of the repo whose head was written before that
          LastModified + 24 h (one head CAS each, at most one a day), waits the store's request deadline, checks the
          repo's commits since its first check again, then deletes the segment; an uncommitted path map over 25 h
          old goes the same way, fencing only its ref (11.6)
why       a push, or a seal for its parts, adopts a segment only with a receipt under 24 h old at its last check and
          commits within 5 s of it, so every adoption commits within 24 h of the upload, plus 5 s and the store's
          request deadline; one stalled on an idle ref fails its head CAS after the fence and ends 503 unknown, and
          the client's retry finds its receipt too old (409 SEGMENT_GONE after its own fence; re-upload); one on a
          ref written after the 24 h mark was fenced by that write; one that committed is found by the second check
```

**Quotas (§20.6, §20.7):**

```text
bytes     a repo's stored bytes are the sizes of its seg/, pack/ and hp/ objects as LIST returns them, plus the
          record lengths its head windows and log pages give for versions still in batches, minus what only a hold
          keeps (owner decision 133) and any pack or parcel whose every record a newer container's pidx/ entry
          names (the nightly pass deletes it unless held; §20.7); usage batches move the count between passes
cost      by inference, one LIST per repo prefix a night (~6 LIST/s on the metadata clusters at year two's ~555,000
          repos, the rest on the HDDs) and one head GET per ref written in the last 26 h
limit     at the storage limit, and while the network is spent, evs refuses from its cached over-limit list
          (overshooting by up to a minute), with §20.7's QuotaRefusal, segment uploads and any push that names a new
          segment or inline record; it accepts maintenance pushes, which add no payload (CONSUME, BASE, ERASE,
          PATH_EPOCH and its maps, DELETE, deletion and restore, EvsReseed), and re-seed uploads, an erasure's
          CLOSURE push with its payload and ?closure=1 uploads within 11.12's rekey bounds and its eraser's own
          allowance, and config and mailcfg pushes within §7.9's limits, so a full network can still change policy
          and erase, at the floor within the wait below, a record entry's `erasure` note waiting until the network is
          under the limit and not spent (11.12); their bytes count as usual, and in v0 an erasure frees no stored
          bytes, its ciphertext staying until v1's compaction (11.12)
wait      an eraser's allowance (§20.4's evs_closure_bytes_per_day: 64 MiB a UTC day, never under
          evs_closure_bytes_floor's 4 MiB whatever §21 sets) re-keys 60 full i/ segments a day, 3 at the floor; an
          eraser runs a larger erasure as CLOSURE and ERASE pairs sized to what remains, since a push adopts only
          uploads under 24 h old (uploads, above), so at the floor one entry's erasure waits at most until the next
          00:00 UTC and a backlog of n full re-keys under ⌈n/3⌉ days (§20.7), each pair's entries keeping their keys
          and index fields openable until its ERASE commits; below the limit and not spent, none waits
transfer  evs reports transfer and payload deltas in 60 s usage batches whose batch id is their retry identity
          (§20.6), so a crash loses at most one window of one process's bytes: under-billing, never double-billing
```

**Durability (owner decisions [89](#od-89), [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94), [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[139](#od-139)).** Erasure coding survives two of four hosts for objects whose every shard exists (§19.6), on 8 × PM9A3 1.92 TB at EC:4 (~7.7 TB usable); with two down, writes get 503 until the cold spare returns one. A site loss loses server-held data (§19.10), so owner devices keep full mirrors of every record-class repo and the config, slots included, as the customer's own copies (no operator copy holds slots or wraps; [owner decision 90](#od-90)): the owner's always-on device for vaults and mailboxes, an admin's for team records and the config. An iOS-only user has none ([owner decision 12](#od-12)), so the app mirrors `mailcfg` and the mailbox's `vault/` and `i/` and head-reads `m/` bodies, which a site loss erases (§2.18, §15.16). Unconsumed deposits and unmirrored repos are lost.

```text
contents  a full mirror holds every record and object a committed push names (statements, payloads, parts, segments,
          packs' contents), the repo's slot objects as their wrapped bytes (fek-wrapped or drop-HPKE), the RK ladder
          in its keychain (§10.5) and the ERASE pushes; the device that signs an ERASE keeps it for §19.10's 30-day
          re-seed window
status    `ur status` reports each repo's coverage: full when every ref is mirrored within 1 h of its head, objects
          and slots are complete, erasures are applied and a hash check ran within 7 days; otherwise partial, naming
          what is missing; an unmirrored record-class repo is named
erasure   immediate on the server; on each mirror, which applies each ERASE push before its next sync (11.12)
re-seed   by §19.10's runbook (POST .../reseed): config first, then groups, then per repo, placed afresh (11.8), the
          ERASE pushes devices hold first, then statements, payloads, parts, segments and pack contents past the
          current head in version order, as reseed records, and last, after every ref's history, the slots; evs
          applies every ERASE before it serves a slot, accepts a slot only if a re-seeded version names it and no
          ERASE covers its key, and takes re-seeds only for repos the projection lists live or restorable (a repo
          whose access log ends in RepoDelete past 7 d or with now is refused; one whose log ends in an unrestored
          RepoDelete without now, under 7 d old, is placed with repo/ deleted{deletion_id, its entry's time} first,
          then takes its history, group and slots (11.12's re-seed exception), so access stays refused and restore
          and the timer resume); where every surviving copy ends below a reader's pin, a repo admin's
          EvsReseed{repo, ref, version, C_v, incident} (11.6) lets that reader accept the shorter history, shown as
          a loss
```

### 11.14 Performance and concurrency (verified in §22)

| Path | Target |
|---|---|
| Commit → hint at an online subscriber | p50 ≤ 300 ms, p99 ≤ 2 s |
| Local push (≤ 64 KiB) → remote commit, desktop | p50 ≤ 1 s |
| Agent commit on device A → visible on device B | p50 ≤ 2 s, p99 ≤ 5 s |
| Head read, file ≤ 1 MiB | p50 ≤ 250 ms on desktop, ≤ 600 ms on mobile |
| Head read 100 versions behind its pin | statements ≤ 100 KiB, verify ≤ 20 ms on mobile |
| Head read of a path a later 100,000-change push left alone | adjacent-leaf proofs of ~1.4 KiB a path level, never its change list |
| Throughput per repo | ≥ 50 MB/s on desktop, ≥ 5 MB/s on mobile |
| evs working set | ≤ 4 MiB in the iOS app process (§18.4); never a whole file, segment or delta base over 1 MiB in RAM |
| Drive writes per push on the metadata set | ≤ 43 KiB per drive at 2× year one's mix; ≤ 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS at any load (11.13) |

**Concurrency.** Pushes to one ref meet only at its head's If-Match: a file-mode loser with disjoint paths retries inside evs, so one ref sustains roughly 20-50 pushes/s; a git-mode loser gets a stock non-fast-forward and merges. Distinct refs never contend. In the twenty-agent test (§22), agents write their own refs in real time, and a merge into main every 60 s meets another in its ~60 ms window about 2% of the time, then merges again.

### 11.15 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plaintext paths (PLAN.md:59), or a sealed client index ordered in Postgres (the drafted Q-EVS-1 (c)) | Server-side paths; or only repos and refs visible | Names, shape and sizes in the clear; or 3-RTT cold reads, client-side GC, Postgres on the storage path | Ruled out (owner directive; [owner decision 2](#od-2)) |
| A per-ref lock with a fencing token | No retries | One more round trip; a stalled holder still writes, since no store condition spans two objects | Rejected; the git-mode seal lease lives in the head |
| Disjoint git landing, then a merge push by any writer | No client retry | No defined tip until the merge; two pushes per landing; automatic merges | Rejected ([owner decision 141](#od-141)) |
| A server-made deterministic merge commit | No client work | Merges shared branches automatically (sidecar/market2.md:519) | Used only for file-mode export |
| Folds every ~10 s or 32 versions | Fresher entries | Agents pushing every ~10 s fold each push alone: ~3 index writes, ~54 KiB a drive | Rejected |
| One head PUT for several pushes, or batches per repo | Fewer writes | Gains only past ~50 pushes/s a ref; most repos see under one a second | Rejected |
| A head per version, created If-None-Match | ~5 KiB less a push | [Owner decision 2](#od-2) fixes the head If-Match as the commit point | Rejected |
| MinIO pools for the metadata tier | One namespace | A multi-pool PUT checks its precondition only in the pool it picks (11.3) | Rejected ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) |
| go-git as the local server | No git binary | v6 is a beta (https://github.com/go-git/go-git) | Rejected |

### 11.16 Decisions proposed

**D-EVS-1 (proposed).** Plaintext git lives only on reading sidecars; evs holds segments, index entries and signed pushes and never parses git. *Why:* server plaintext is a design error (CONVENTIONS §0).

**D-EVS-2 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): the token tree replaced the sealed client index (D-EVS-12).

**D-EVS-3 (proposed).** Blobs are git-delta chains under 11.7's checkpoint rules. *Why:* PLAN.md:50 and :63; a reconstruction reads at most 17 records and 1.5× the file size.

**D-EVS-4 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): ref CAS lives in `head/` objects (D-EVS-13).

**D-EVS-5 (proposed).** Only the §5 identity key signs pushes, which name `sidecar_id` and `client_id` and are pinned as (ref, version, C_v); agent attribution is sealed. *Why:* I-4, I-16 and PLAN.md:59.

**D-EVS-6 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): the server keeps a path index of objects (D-EVS-12).

**D-EVS-7 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 24](#od-24): the local git tier ships with `git-remote-ur` (D-EVS-15).

**D-EVS-8 (proposed).** Owned refs sync in real time; shared git-mode refs serialize by tip CAS, with explicit client merges, and file-mode refs land disjoint pushes by path-level CAS; no conflict is resolved automatically. *Why:* sidecar/market2.md:513-531; owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24), [141](#od-141).

**D-EVS-9 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): usage flows as events (D-EVS-16).

**D-EVS-10 (proposed).** Record-class owned refs are append-only streams, and deposits end in a reader's CONSUME. *Why:* §16's chains need streams a stolen writer cannot rewrite (Q-ARCH-9 (a)).

**D-EVS-11 (proposed).** Kinds are fixed at creation; `vault`, `mailbox` and `secret` (any number a member, such as §13.8's ACME account keys) bind `owner_member_id` and are read only by the owner's consented devices (§8.5), their `EvsShare`s' subjects and [owner decision 63](#od-63)'s audit reader. *Why:* [owner decision 126](#od-126); sessions and mail stay with their owner unless shared (R-ACL-11, R-KEYS-9, R-TRUST-7).

**D-EVS-12 (proposed).** Paths are 11.6-11.7's token tree, re-keyed by a signed map bound to its source head and keyed by its hash, plus a tail for paths created since: due at once on a member device's removal or a compromise, new names in name-bearing repos waiting for it, else (other shrinks, authorization expiries) due within 24 h; re-keyed when a mapper commits, which a creation block of at most 2 min, 10 min past due, assures; up to three source epochs overlap, the copy translating directory rows a fold carried and removals during it leaving removed entries, so no read falls back to a stale source, and no name created after cut-over gets a source-epoch token. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2) and [64](#od-64), with no index rewrite per CI reap and no epoch starved by steady creation.

**D-EVS-13 (proposed).** evs is stateless over 11.8's objects, each repo's on the cluster its `place/` names: only the head If-Match decides; all else a push writes is immutable or an index cache that committed records rebuild; readers use only versions the head history names. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [20](#od-20), [145](#od-145); no lost response or cleanup removes committed data.

**D-EVS-14 (proposed).** Subscriptions are token-prefix leases per path epoch, Redis soft state that holders re-create after a loss, answered once the lease exists; hints carry only server-held fields, versioned by the push sequence, a Redis counter seeded from the master's clock, so it restarts above every earlier value. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [17](#od-17), [136](#od-136).

**D-EVS-15 (proposed).** The local tier is the system git behind the daemon's authenticating fronts plus `git-remote-ur`, with plaintext only on loopback, TLS or ssh beyond it, and [owner decision 81](#od-81)'s committer hook. *Why:* owner decisions [24](#od-24), [81](#od-81), [84](#od-84) and [130](#od-130), without a go-git server.

**D-EVS-16 (proposed).** Stored bytes are each repo's `seg/`, `pack/` and `hp/` object sizes plus its batch-resident record lengths, less held-only objects and superseded containers, counted nightly and moved by usage batches; at the limit only payload-adding uploads and pushes stop, except re-seeding, an erasure's bounded CLOSURE push with its uploads, and config and mailcfg pushes within §7.9's limits. *Why:* stateless evs has no counter to lock, and shared batches cannot be listed per repo.

**D-EVS-17 (proposed).** Owner devices mirror record-class repos and the config in full, slots included, and re-seed evs after a site loss, erasures first and slots last; a repo admin's EvsReseed lets readers accept a shorter history as a loss. *Why:* owner decisions [90](#od-90) and [94](#od-94) keep no operator copy; a slotless mirror cannot open unread entries.

**D-EVS-18 (proposed).** The write gate is the head CAS: a commit's authorization and generation pins pass §10.6's predicate against evs's newest authorization state, read within 5 s, and never fall below the head's. *Why:* [owner decision 5](#od-5) leaves no server transaction, and a separate gate object cannot fence the commit.

**D-EVS-19 (proposed).** Deletion is a `repo/` state machine that follows the access log: RepoDelete or RepoRestore is filed first and the route, or taskworker's reconciler, applies it; restore and shred contend for one CAS, the timer waiting out api's 7-day RepoRestore window; terminal `shredding` precedes any key destruction, and deletion ids fence jobs. *Why:* owner decisions [82](#od-82), [133](#od-133); no restore returns a keyless repo, and no re-seed trusts a log that shows a deleted repo live.

**D-EVS-20 (proposed).** A push over 1 MiB or 1,024 entry writes travels in up to 1,024 hashed parts that its signed statement binds and one head PUT commits; a git-mode one holds a seal lease of at most 2 min. *Why:* imports and large merges stay one atomic, verifiable git push.

**D-EVS-21 (proposed).** 11.13 budgets every metadata write in drive bytes, which bound its IOs too, with leases, the push sequence and gkm acks in Redis and a per-network fair share that sheds the heaviest network first. *Why:* every drive takes every write (owner decisions [21](#od-21), [116](#od-116), [140](#od-140)).

**D-EVS-22 (decided; [owner decision 141](#od-141)).** Refs have a mode fixed at creation: git-mode refs commit only on their tip and keep the original commits; file-mode refs use path-level CAS and export one deterministic commit per version; head mode writes file-mode refs only. *Why:* git commits bind tree and parents (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24), [81](#od-81)).

**D-EVS-23 (proposed).** A push id names one statement, whose retry returns its original version; an unknown outcome resolves from the head and at most two log pages, or stays unknown; a refusal the head does not settle for good follows a fence on its ref written after it arrived, its own or another's, at most one a second, which ends every attempt that arrived before it; no answer deletes anything, and evacuation deletes only a dead push's slots. *Why:* a store can apply a write and lose its response, and another attempt of the same push id, a client's retry or the lb's re-send, may still commit.

**D-EVS-24 (proposed).** Log pages hold the signed statements (at most 1 KiB each), and the head window names each recent one's place and hash; head readers verify every statement after their pin and the one behind each entry they read. *Why:* [owner decision 7](#od-7) for every reader (Q-EVS-6), at one block per head write.

**D-EVS-25 (proposed).** Orphans are found without the log: hourly evacuation resolves every batch record, which names every slot its push wrote, and an unadopted segment or path map, found by the nightly LIST, is deleted only after fencing each idle ref of its repo. *Why:* an upload that never reached the log is otherwise invisible, and a grace period cannot fence a late commit.

**D-EVS-26 (proposed).** Erasure is a committed ERASE push that destroys every key of every representation: each retained version, each derived-field chain (re-keyed first, by a CLOSURE push that only replaces committed file versions, each new chain within Padmé of the one it replaces, taken at the storage limit with size-bounded uploads within its eraser's own rate and daily allowance, which has a floor §21 cannot lower) and the deposit, which is slot-keyed. *Why:* owner decisions [61](#od-61), [133](#od-133), [146](#od-146); a shared index or live deposit would otherwise outlive the erasure, and no admin's closures spend another's.

**D-EVS-27 (proposed).** Segments are addressed only by content id, locators carry a kind with two reserved values, and `spidx/` is reserved, so packing needs no format change. *Why:* locators are signed and cannot be rewritten; Q-OPS-2.

**D-EVS-28 (proposed).** The local tier publishes through git's proc-receive hook with per-ref statuses, no atomic pushes and a durable journal resolved by push id. *Why:* a pre-receive hook cannot report per-ref outcomes or survive a crash between the remote and local updates.

**D-EVS-29 (proposed).** The head holds the commit point and a window of 64-byte entries (push id, statement hash prefix, place, path digest, flags), at most ~9 KiB: one block on each drive per commit. *Why:* every push rewrites the head on all 8 drives, plus a backup ([owner decision 140](#od-140)).

**D-EVS-30 (proposed).** evs group-commits push, part and seal records into immutable minute-bucketed batches of at most 256 KiB, written at once when load is light, within 20 ms under load, and evacuated whole after 25-26 h. *Why:* bursts, and a process's stream to a cluster past ~50 pushes/s, share one create and one delete per batch ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); at ~8 evs processes a set near capacity sees ~1-1.6 records a batch.

**D-EVS-31 (proposed).** `idx/` holds only committed versions, folded lazily (the oldest 64 at 96 unfolded, the rest after 10 min idle, always before a page-out and in a path epoch's own commit), a file's newest version per fold and every directory delta in order; a removal writes, If-Match and only over an older version, a marker that keeps the path's version, and markers go in head-announced collection windows once the horizon passes them by a base range; reads and the CAS read an entry only after a head and merge the window versions after that head's folded_through. *Why:* a busy path is written once per fold, nothing pending evicts a committed version ([owner decision 140](#od-140)), and a DELETE, which MinIO applies unconditionally, could remove an entry a later fold wrote ([owner decision 148](#od-148)).

**D-EVS-32 (proposed).** Hourly evacuation moves each repo's records and log pages older than 24 h into one HDD pack once they reach 256 KiB, else into NVMe parcels that pack within 7 d. *Why:* [owner decision 136](#od-136)'s residency, with whole-batch deletes and no tiny HDD objects.

**D-EVS-33 (proposed).** evs, gkm and taskworker share each metadata cluster's write budget (0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS on its busiest drive not under heal), a bucket only measured drive bytes drain, which bounds IOs too (at least 512 B each, ≤ 39% of rated), through two accounts: P1 work pays at admission for itself and the P2 work it causes, and P2 spends only that credit, topped up to 40% of the allowance while its backlog exceeds it, in deadline order; per-network fair queues refuse the heaviest network first, never authorization, deletion, shredding or erasure within its rate. *Why:* [owner decision 140](#od-140); charging P2 at admission and again when issued would admit ~27% fewer pushes, and a capped P2 would let evacuation outgrow 26 h.

**D-EVS-34 (proposed).** Segment uploads write nothing to the metadata cluster: evs returns a MAC'd receipt that the push presents, and GC deletes an unadopted segment only after 25 h and a fence on each idle ref of its repo. *Why:* markers cost three writes per segment.

### 11.17 Open questions

**Q-EVS-1.** [X2] Which header values may evs see, and how do head reads and subpath subscriptions work without plaintext paths? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 2](#od-2)):** keyed path tokens in an object index, token-prefix subscriptions, path-key rotation on member removal and all storage state as objects (11.5-11.8). *Residual:* Q-EVS-6, closed by peer review 2026-11-04.

**Q-EVS-2.** [X19] How does evs stay git-compatible? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 24](#od-24)):** a local git tier over authenticated http and ssh plus `git-remote-ur`; only the sidecar talks to evs; owner decisions [84](#od-84) and [130](#od-130) set the bind, with only TLS or ssh beyond loopback (11.11). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-3 (closed 2026-11-03).** Separate repos for path prefixes in v0; in v1, prefix rules in the encrypted repo config, enforced by sidecars with an alarm; applied in §8 (D-ACL-11) and 11.21. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-4.** How does PLAN.md:59's forced git identity apply to plaintext commits? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 81](#od-81)):** signed pushes authenticate commits, and the local git server refuses new commits whose committer is not the pushing sidecar, except signed imports (11.11). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-5.** Should repo deletion start as a soft delete? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 82](#od-82)):** yes: access ends at once, and keys are shredded after 7 days unless restored, or at once with `--now` (11.12). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-6.** Must a head reader that does not replay verify per-file freshness? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (c), made cheap: head readers replay signed statements, not payloads, from their pin, carried by the read response, and check the statement behind every entry they read (11.9), in D-EVS-24's format (statements of at most 1 KiB; for larger change lists, `changes_root` over sorted changes, so inclusion and adjacent-leaf proofs settle a path); phones keep durable pins and catch up by at most 4 MiB of statements and proofs, else re-pin and mark the gap. The sensitive classes (config, mailcfg, the mailbox's `vault/` and `i/`, approvals) are mirrored and replayed in full (11.13), and a head below a pin needs a verified EvsReseed. Disclosed limit (§2.8): for a path a head reader has never read, which writer-signed version is current as of its first pin, and, after a re-pin past that budget, for every path, rests on evs; HeadCheck confirms the pin, not those versions. (b), a Merkle root over the token tree, is rejected: a PUT per path level, root contention, d+1 GETs per read. *Residual:* that limit.

**Q-EVS-7.** Cross-cutting (§11, §21). Does a preservation hold pause user-initiated shredding (`--now`, the 7-day timer, slot erasure)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 133](#od-133)):** (a) no: holds pause only the server's TTL sweeps and GC for in-scope records, and user-initiated shredding always proceeds (11.12), if counsel confirms that deleting wrapped keys to ciphertext URnetwork cannot read is permitted (§21). A hold keeps only the ciphertext a shred leaves. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-8.** Cross-cutting (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24)). On a shared git ref, disjoint landing ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) leaves a tree no git commit has, so git compatibility and R-EVS-10's CAS cannot both hold. **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 141](#od-141)):** (a): git-mode refs commit only on their tip (D-EVS-22), and file-mode refs (vaults, mailboxes, records, the config) keep disjoint landing, so exact git oids and stock non-fast-forward errors hold; a loser pulls or merges, about 2% of merges in the twenty-agent test. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-9.** Cross-cutting (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [140](#od-140), [145](#od-145); §19, §22). Must the design meet the ~10-15 KiB of drive writes a push in [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s record, when [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s commit point, the head's If-Match overwrite, alone writes ~14 KiB a drive (~10.5 on 1 KiB blocks), since MinIO also rewrites the old xl.meta (11.3)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 140](#od-140), record corrected):** (a): the binding budget, gated at 43 KiB a push per drive (D-TEST-11). The ~10-15 KiB figure was the design team's first estimate, not the owner's requirement, which is the PM9A3 profile itself ("We have to make that iop profile work"): at most 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS at the design load. Not taken: (b) a head per version created If-None-Match, which departs from [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s If-Match commit point; (c) patching MinIO to skip the old xl.meta's copy on overwrite, which gives up its torn-write backup. *Residual:* none.

### 11.18 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:59**, second sentence (plaintext paths, the git-crypt model): superseded by owner directive 2026-11-03; paths are keyed tokens and names are sealed ([owner decision 2](#od-2)). Its first sentence stands (Q-EVS-4).
- **PLAN.md:57** is met at the sidecar's local git server; evs speaks an object API ([owner decision 24](#od-24)).
- **Not in PLAN.md:** cli/UI.md:94 requires an active remote to start the git server, but only the first sync needs one; cli/UI.md:11's 0.0.0.0 default stands ([owner decision 84](#od-84)), with TLS or ssh off loopback ([owner decision 130](#od-130); D-TRUST-8); cli/UI.md:87-89's quotas give way to PLAN's ([owner decision 27](#od-27)); git directories over 4,096 entries or 448 KiB of name table (3,584 entries whose names are under 64 B; 11.7) are refused in v0.

### 11.19 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `EvsClient` and `EvsRepo` (`evs_*.go`: `CreateRepo`, `ReadHead`, `List`, `History`, `Write`, `Deposit`, `Consume`, `Subscribe`, `Shred`, `Delete`, `Restore`, `Import`, `Export`, `Mount`), whose per-path version, signer and git oid answer §16.6's `Lookup(effect_key)` for an evs effect (D-MCP-11); ref modes (11.7); the sync engine, local git server and `git-remote-ur`; the `sidecar/evsservice` engine ([owner decision 104](#od-104)); the push sequence that versions §6.8's `evs:<repo_id>`; `place/` and storage for `proj/`, `projrows/`, `rev/`, `hold/` and `gkm/`; 11.13's write budget and fair share, shared with gkm and taskworker; §2.8's evs-1 to evs-25 (evs-10 is §19.6's; evs-20 withdrawn).
- **Consumes:** §5 `ServiceToken`, binding log, `git` hello; §6 hints, `Signed`, `HeadCheck` and `RefHead`, `PushReset`; §7 token exchange and its re-seed mode, `rev/`, the authorization log and its `{acl_}e` cache, `AuthPin`, bootstrap; §8 `RepoReaders`, writer sets, kind defaults, `consented`, `audit`, access logs (`RepoDelete`, `RepoRestore`), `EvsShare`, `OwnerConfirm`; §10 `GkmClient`, `DeriveKey`, `GenRotate`, the gate predicate; §12 `ResolveNetworkLabel`; §13 certificates; §18 wakes; §19 clusters, drive counters, `{nvb_<set>}`; §20 `ReportUsage`; §21.9 holds.
- **Subprotocol messages:** `EvsHeadChanged` (0x1401; server→client in §6 `PushHint`; a ref moved); `RefHead` inside §6's `HeadCheck` (compare ref pins); 0x1402-0x1403 stay reserved, never reused.
- **API routes:** Client class, authorized by a service token with aud `evs`, specified in connect/api/bringyour.yml.

  ```text
  PUT|GET|DELETE /evs/v1/repos/<id>[?now=1];  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/restore (409 SHREDDING past deleted), /reseed (admin);
       DELETE and restore answer 409 STATEMENT_MISSING without their projected RepoDelete or RepoRestore
  PUT  /evs/v1/repos/<id>/segments/<sid>?push=<push_id>[&closure=1] (rw, deposit; closure: admin): 200
       {EvsUploadReceipt}, or 409 SEGMENT_STALE; at the storage limit or while spent, §20.7's QuotaRefusal (402
       with x402 terms when a purchase lifts the limit, else RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; a closure upload past its
       eraser's 60 a minute or daily closure allowance 429 with retry_after_ms, 11.12, §20.7)
  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/push {statement, payload, receipts}, /push/<push_id>/<k> {part, receipts}: 200 {place}
       (rw; deposit only to the caller's deposit ref); the seal POSTs .../push {statement, the parts' places}
  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/push/<push_id>/lease, /path-epoch, /path-epoch/block (rw)
  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/read {..., fresh} (`base` {ref, version} for an overlay's path it holds no version of);
       GET /evs/v1/repos/<id>/refs, /log?ref=&since=
  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/slots/delete (admin);  POST|GET|DELETE /evs/v1/subscriptions
  push refusals, each with the push id: 409 REF_MODE, PUSH_ID_REUSED, SEGMENT_GONE, SEGMENT_STALE, PARTS_MISSING,
       DIRECTORY_FULL, NOTHING_TO_ERASE, SHREDDING, non-fast-forward; 412 GATE_CLOSED, PATH_EPOCH, PATH_EPOCH_DUE,
       EPOCH_SOURCES_FULL; QuotaRefusal at the storage limit or while spent, as for uploads, after a fence; 429
       BUSY, FOLD_BEHIND, the budget's RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, a CLOSURE past its eraser's daily closure allowance
       (§20.7) and lease and fence waits, with retry_after_ms, which refuse nothing; 503 outcome: unknown, or
       before step 4 while evs's clock is unsure
  ```
- **Tables:** none; evs keeps only 11.8's objects ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), plus Redis soft state: §6's hint keys, {evsl_} leases, the {evsq_} push sequence and the {evsh_} head cache ([owner decision 136](#od-136)).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/evs` (staged, stateless) with 11.13's `streamable_paths`; the segment bucket and one bucket per metadata cluster (owner decisions [94](#od-94), [145](#od-145)); limits in config/all/pro.yml (`<tier>.sidecar:` with `store_weight`, `sidecar_abuse:`); the receipt keys; the `{nvb_<set>}` allowance, which taskworker publishes from §19.6's drive counters; GC, evacuation, path-epoch copies, shredding and reconciliation in taskworker; the system git where the local tier runs.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §2.8's evs rows follow 11.8's families (evs-8 and evs-24 in Redis; evs-21 to evs-23 `spidx/`, `pb/`, `hp/`; evs-25 `place/`; evs-20 withdrawn), evs-1 listing the `secret` kind, evs-3 a mapper's creation-block end (block_until_ms), the time of the newest refusal, evacuation or GC fence (fence_ms) and a marker collection's done, through and window end, evs-4 whether an upload was a closure upload, evs-11 a carried row's epoch, each removal's marker (the removing push id and version, the path's version) until collected and, while sources stand, each entry's state (carried, fresh or removed), evs-12 the CLOSURE flag, an ERASE's or CLOSURE's erased-list hash (a CLOSURE's equals its ERASE's, linking the re-keyed paths to that erasure), a PATH_EPOCH's tail hash with its tail moves (old and new token paths, linking created paths across epochs as evs-15's maps do) and the source-paths hash with each change's source token paths, evs-24 each cached head's time, and the head-reader disclosure every path after a re-pin past 11.9's budget; §3.7's F2 follows 11.8's commit and 11.9's statement reads; §22.7's guard lists the families, `place/` included, and lets evs and gkm write their `{nvb_<set>}` reports.
  - §8.5's kind defaults take the `secret` kind (§13.8's account keys) as `vault`, deposits aside; §8.8's RepoDelete and RepoRestore precede 11.12's routes; §7.9's append limits bound 11.13's P0 log writes; §20.7 states 11.12's rekey bounds, its {sq_} counting each eraser's closure uploads against its own 60 a minute, not the network's, and its closure bytes against its own `evs_closure_bytes_per_day`, never below `evs_closure_bytes_floor`, with 11.13's wait ([owner decision 146](#od-146)).
  - §15 and §16 size directories by 11.7's 448 KiB of name table (EvsName rows of token, kind and sealed name with nonce and tag: 3,584 names under 64 B), not by the 4,096 count; evs sees each record entry's token, time and padded size; ingest ends in CONSUME, §16.8's taking only `read` entries from a receipt-only depositor (11.12); §15.7 re-keys an erased message's `i/` chains by CLOSURE pushes, and it and §8 make every device that erases a mailbox's or group repo's messages, the trash shred included, a repo admin, since ERASE, CLOSURE and closure uploads take `admin`; §16.8 holds a record entry's `erasure` entry while the network is at the storage limit or spent (11.12); §15.7 and §16.8 delete an erased entry's decrypted copies; §16.2's `evs_write` on a git-mode ref commits through the local tier at the tip.
  - §19.6 quotes 11.13's mix and drive writes (~670 and ~5,000 PUT/s; ~8.5 and ~69 MiB/s a drive; 3.7-4.0 DWPD at a near-capacity set's ~1-1.6 records a batch), sets the store's 10 s request deadline, which a request's own earlier cancel shortens, none applying after it (11.7's stale and collect rows), runs chrony on the evs, gkm, taskworker and Redis master hosts within 50 ms of UTC, alarmed past 25 ms, a taskworker whose offset is unknown or over 50 ms raising no fence and GC deleting nothing (§19.10's clock row), exports drive counters, publishes T, A1 and A2 by 11.13's accounts and provides the clusters and a conformance suite that refuses multi-pool metadata, and §19.9's triggers start each next cluster ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), §19.9 sizing year two at five to six sets by 11.13's per-cluster batches; §19.10 re-seeds slots last and places a repo re-seeded as deleted in that state first; §10.6 keeps gkm's objects on the repo's cluster, acks in Redis; §21.9's api writes `hold/`, and §21 tracks counsel's confirmation for [owner decision 133](#od-133).
  - §22's evs tests add a helper clone with no prior mount, a shred under a hold, and placement: two creates of one id racing at `place/`, a retried create, and a second cluster never receiving a placed repo's objects. Beyond the FS rows §22 already writes, they add: FS-1, every refusal fenced whether evs2 serves a retry or the lb's re-send of a first send, a paused attempt that arrived before a fence ending at its next read, evs1 slowed past the lb's 30 s read timeout while evs2 loses 8 races and answers 429 BUSY (the retry returning evs1's version), DIRECTORY_FULL and EPOCH_SOURCES_FULL only after a fence, an instance 150 ms fast answering 503 and committing nothing after a sibling's fenced refusal, and fenced refusals streamed beside honest pushes (one fence a second, the rest 429; leases and parts never ended by them, a seal only when it arrived before the fence, its retry then committing); FS-3, A's PUT timing out after the gate closes, not reissued past 5 s: A's rerun checks refuse, and A answers 412 GATE_CLOSED after its fence, or 200 if its first PUT applied first; FS-4, a child added to an unmoved directory in a paused copy and folded first, then, the copy still paused, a carried child removed and folded, its row dropped, the copy resuming to translate the rest, and a fold of that directory between the copy's GET and its If-Match PUT (a reread; no row lost or duplicated), the listing name-verified after the sources drop; a file and a directory removed after cut-over before the copy reaches them, and a directory removed then re-created with one new child, each read and listed once the removal leaves the window and again after the sources drop: nothing removed served or listed, no reader alarming; a move landing between one round's GETs, for a push creating the path, one modifying it and a listing; a directory carried from p1 into p2, then into p3 after a superseded copy, listed and name-verified before and after the p3 copy; no source-epoch token of a name created after cut-over reaching the server; and steady creation through a batched epoch, which commits with a tail, then under a block; FS-5, a push after a commitless PATH_EPOCH succeeding with no ng, and with a warm head cache a lease, parts and seal with no ng, a lease taken after another push's refusal fence, a git push after a refusal fence committing, one during another's lease getting 429; a git-mode agent branch from a main with unfolded changes whose first push changes one of those paths and commits; an overlay of a file-mode ref refused (409 REF_MODE), and a read of an overlay's unchanged path answering `base`; FS-6, a gkm commit held across a `--now` shred re-creating nothing, a held `--now` shred whose records in 25 h-old batches are packed, kept and deleted once the hold ends, and a re-seed of a soft-deleted repo, then a restore that opens every file; FS-9, the reverse order: D's removal first, then a push based before it creating D/n (409), the bound built from real sealed names (3,584 under 64 B), held through a paused copy with carried rows counted untagged, and a multi-part file-mode push in both orders and at the bound; FS-10, a refused push's entry served as current for a never-read path, accepted as §2.8 publishes, a path a 100,000-change push left alone verified by adjacent-leaf proofs with no change list fetched, and an unsorted change list refused; FS-30, a receipt-only depositor's other entry consumed, not ingested, with an alarm; FS-47, a mail erasure at the exact limit whose IndexEntry shares an `i/` segment, its merged record crossing a padding step: its CLOSURE push and upload pass; a CLOSURE growing a chain refused below the limit too; a non-admin one and a plain upload refused, and at the limit a closure upload over 1,088 KiB; a CLOSURE push past the network's erasure rate queuing as P1 and committing; an eraser's closure uploads past its own 60 a minute, and its uploads and CLOSURE pushes past its daily allowance, getting 429 while another eraser's pass; a record entry's `erasure` entry held at the limit and committed once under it; FS-58, a PATH_EPOCH on an idle ref whose folded_through trails v folding and committing, and a fold plus a horizon-raising commit between a push's step 4 and its 412 rerun, and between its head and entry reads: 409, never a commit over the change; a rerun after the window paged out versions past A's horizon, from a cluster head and from a cached head minutes old: A reads X's entry again after the reread head (409); a fold and a horizon-raising commit between an entry GET and a newer head's GET, then a listing; two folds of a range holding D's removal, the first queued in P2 or its marker PUT applying late, D and D/x re-created and folded between: nothing newer overwritten, D/x served and listed, a creation of D/x refused; a file removed and re-created, a push based on its old version refused before and after, its versions continuing; a collection window held at a barrier while a fold re-creates a covered path, deleting no live entry (I-EVS-8 as FI-15, read with 0 naming an absent path and a creation's version exceeding a standing removal's, checked in EvsCommit.tla with its fold thresholds and window bounds scaled, the minimum window above the base range, and a version bound fitting a page-out between a push's step 4 and its rerun; its head's lease field and the lease route reaching FI-9's 429 branch; its folder running a stale or late removal and its collector a window); FS-59, the stalled push ending 503 unknown and its retry getting 409 SEGMENT_GONE; FS-60, a run killed after its container and restarted once its material aged, nothing stored twice past the nightly pass; FS-61 and §22.8's `nvme` row, the budget refilled at 0.8 DWPD and refusing no push at 2× year one, then a full-rate path-epoch copy beside that load; FS-62, one ref's cached head past 10 min, another ref writing, not served; §22.8, the rotations, full checkpoints and copy operations a day of 1 h requested grants on large repos.

### 11.20 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A flaw in the format, token tree or commit protocol, unaudited and so disclosed (owner decisions [99](#od-99), [119](#od-119)) | Medium | High | Peer review before format 1 freezes; vectors, fuzzing, a model check of 11.8 (§22) |
| The final MinIO build loses conditional-write or listing consistency | Low | High | One-object commit point; §22's suite gates every build |
| A 1M-file ref's path epoch copies for ~17 h, while readers read both epochs | Medium | Medium | Epochs only on removal or compromise, else daily; up to three sources read in one round; the copy speeds to 150 operations a second with two sources |
| No writer able to map is online when an epoch is due, so creation stays blocked in a name-bearing repo, and dropped holders keep testing names past due elsewhere | Low | Medium | Writers alarm 1 h past due_by_ms, batched epochs included; `ur status` names the ref; any capable writer maps, a tail and a 2-min creation block landing it under steady creation |
| Fenced refusals on a busy ref end other pushes in flight (503 unknown, then a retry), which a writer could provoke | Medium | Low | Refusals coalesce on any fence after their arrival, at most one a ref a second, the rest 429; leases, blocks and source drops end nothing, parts never; FS-1 |
| Counsel does not confirm [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition (shredding under a hold) | Low | High | §21's counsel item, before holds ship (M5) |
| Site loss destroys repos no device mirrors | Low | High | Mirrors; coverage in `ur status`; re-seeding |
| Read and subscription patterns leak more than 11.5 states | Medium | Medium | Whole small reads; 64 KiB alignment; publish the leak |
| A client bug corrupts history, which the server cannot check | Low | High | Oid checks; replay; mirrors; export |
| An import, hostile tenant or reconnect storm saturates the NVMe set | Medium | High | 11.13's write budget and fair share, part bounds, leases in Redis; §22.8; §19.9's triggers ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) |
| Measured per-operation costs hold a set below ~400 pushes/s (~530 on 1 KiB blocks) at the ~1-1.6 records a batch of a set near capacity, or year two arrives early | Medium | High | §22.8's M2 gate and records per batch per cluster; 1 KiB blocks; the write budget sheds the heaviest network; §19.9's triggers order the next cluster ahead of its lead time, for new repos ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); a per-cluster batcher (Later) |
| Per-push drive writes cannot fall far below ~27 KiB: the head's If-Match overwrite alone is ~14 KiB ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) | Certain | Low | The binding DWPD and IOPS limits hold at ~27-43 KiB a push ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); D-TEST-11's §22.8 gate measures it |
| A shredded repo's statements and ciphertext stay up to 26 h in shared batches | Certain | Low | Keys go first (11.12); §2.8 states the bound |
| [Owner decision 148](#od-148)'s markers add ~12.5-14 KiB of drive writes a removed entry, and a collection window holds a fold re-creating a covered path for up to 30 s | Medium | Low | §22.8's fold row counts removals and markers a push before the 43 KiB gate; a window per ref at most nightly, and only re-creations over covered markers wait |

### 11.21 Phasing

- **v0a** (§23 M2): format 1 with 11.8's objects and protocols (parts, ref modes, the seal lease, batches, receipts, lazy folds with removal markers and their collection, placement); streams, deposits, slots and ERASE, and the owner-bound read-receipt budget, which an `EvsShare` reader needs before it reads (§16.8, D-MCP-18); subscriptions, Redis soft state, the verified head cache and reads of §7.9's `{acl_}e`; head mode; path epochs; the gate and HeadCheck's ref pins (§6.4); usage events, fair share and the write budget; GC and hourly evacuation; mirrors and re-seeding; soft deletion; export; `ur evs rekey`, re-checkpointing every file of a repo under the current generation (§10.16). Format 1's specification freezes at M2's entry review, after peer review of 11.5-11.8 and RECORD.md, and its bytes at M2's exit (D-PHASE-7), after §22.8's drive-write gate (owner decisions [25](#od-25), [99](#od-99), [140](#od-140)).
- **v0b** (§23 M2, with v0a; no format change): the local git server, `git-remote-ur`, the identity hook, the proc-receive journal and imports, the desktop sync engine, overlays and conflict branches, which M2's twenty-agent test uses (§3.15).
- **v1:** compaction and retention; working-tree sync; Q-EVS-3's prefix rules; cross-network and derived shares; agent-subkey provenance.
- **Later:** full sync on mobile; a state commitment if measurements show head readers need pre-pin freshness; directory-resident children for append-only record directories (the reserved `layout`), if §22.8 shows stream entries' index objects binding; a tool moving placed repos between clusters with one commit point ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); a per-cluster batcher, two evs processes batching each cluster's records near ~5 a batch, if §22.8 shows it saves a set; a segment placement that keeps the receipt check, before any added HDD set (§19.9).
- **Blocking:** §7's token exchange, `rev/`, authorization log and bootstrap, §8's projection, consent rule and access logs, and §10's objects block v0a; counsel's confirmation of [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition precedes holds (M5, §21); X13's clusters passing §22's suite and 11.13's benchmark block production storage.

## 12. DNS: the ur.network zone and per-network zones

### 12.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns public naming: the user root (X4), the network label (X5) and X17; the `dns` engine and dns edge; DNSSEC; zone content and reverse zones; the record API; DNS-01; custom domains; private names (with §17); takedown hooks (§21). §13 owns certificates and CAA, §14 and §15 mail record content, §19 the dns edge hosts, §20 quotas. Notation follows D-ARCH-1.

### 12.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-DNS-1 | `<root>` is its own zone; `*.<root>` reaches tlsedge; `mx.<net>.<root>` reaches the local mail server | PLAN.md:80-81,104; [owner decision 32](#od-32) |
| R-DNS-2 | A network owns the zone `<net>.<root>` and its entries | PLAN.md:25 |
| R-DNS-3 | DNS entries 5/200/2000; custom domains Team only | PLAN.md:357,364 |
| R-DNS-4 | DNS reveals as little as possible | CONVENTIONS §0 |
| R-DNS-5 | A released name routes nothing to a new owner | §2 I-14 |
| R-DNS-6 | Labels are issuable LDH labels; platform names are unclaimable | [R:server-identity](design-research/server-identity.md) §2.2 |
| R-DNS-7 | Challenge TXT served within 60 s (p99); negative TTL ≤ 60 s | [R:ext-edge](design-research/ext-edge.md) §3; §19 |
| R-DNS-8 | Nothing collides with WhoDis on public UDP 53 | vault/main/services.yml:345-347 |
| R-DNS-9 | Mail policy records per network; the sending addresses' PTRs under bringyour.com | RFC 8461 §3.4; [owner decision 124](#od-124) |
| R-DNS-10 | Self-hosted DNS, signed online from the first deploy, on two NS at the one site | owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [109](#od-109), [123](#od-123) |

### 12.3 What exists today

- ur.network: Route 53, expires 2027-07-02; signed by a KMS key shared with bringyour.com, no DS (RDAP 2026-11-03; mmm/lag.dev/ops/dnssec.md:25-27); MX at Google Workspace, `_dmarc` `p=none`, no SPF or CAA (dig 2026-11-03).
- The platform left ur.network on 2026-10-01: `api`, `connect` and `mcp` are NXDOMAIN, though warp and vault list them (apple/app/network/Shared/Config/NetworkConfig.swift:19-23; warp/services/services.go:396-438; vault/main/services.yml:3-35,641-739; config/main/tls.yml:2-6).
- Public UDP 53 on the lb interfaces is connect's WhoDis transport; no TCP 53 (vault/main/services.yml:345-347; server/connect/transport.go:2321).
- network_name: 5-50 of `[a-z0-9-]`, edge hyphens and `xn--` allowed, nothing reserved; one rename path holds the old name 24 h; deletion frees it (server/model/network_model.go:178-206; server/controller/account_controller.go:13,161-166; server/model/account_model.go:379).

### 12.4 Roots: the registrable domain (X4, X17)

A **root** is a user-content zone that `dns` signs and serves (`config/<env>/dns.yml`). v0's one root, `<root>` = ur.network, carries user content only (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [16](#od-16)): burners live in network zones ([owner decision 32](#od-32)), and recurd.dev only redirects to ur.io/recurd (§19; [owner decision 15](#od-15)). Platform names, the report, lb and HELO hosts included ([owner decision 124](#od-124)), live on bringyour.com; `<root>` keeps only `ns1`, `ns2` (glue), `_psl` (the PSL's proof), `canary` (12.6), `<token>.acme` (certs' challenge targets) and §14.6's `_spf`, keeping SPF checks in the signed zone.

Until `<root>` is on the Public Suffix List (PSL), its networks share one site (cookies, saved logins), one reputation (§21.6), one Let's Encrypt budget and one DMARC organization ([R:ext-edge](design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.5; mmm/lag.dev/ops/psl.md:51-56). Steps (D-DNS-1):
1. M0: renew to 2036 under registrar lock; the PSL wants over 2 years of term at listing.
2. Move platform names and company mail off ur.network, warp and tls.yml; the lb sends `*.<root>` to tlsedge (§13.4), and only the apex redirects to ur.io.
3. Serve the zone from the dns edge, switch NS (no DS exists) and delete the Route 53 zone.
4. Set `_dmarc.<root>` to `p=reject` once company mail has left.
5. Once eligible (~3,000 active users, `_psl`, an abuse contact), apply to the PSL and request recategorization (connect/EXTENDERUPDATE.md §10.1).

Until listed: no URnetwork cookies on the root, HSTS preload with `includeSubDomains`, exact-host autofill (§15, §18), and §13.7's rule for session cookies on same-site requests from other networks' pages.

### 12.5 The network label (X5)

**Label ([owner decision 14](#od-14)).** 10 characters `[a-z][a-z0-9]{9}` from crypto/rand (~51 bits), allocated on first need, immutable, never reassigned, and not derived from network_id, whose ULID exposes creation time ([R:server-identity](design-research/server-identity.md) §2.11). A draw that hits an existing row or fails `ScreenName`'s reserved or brand rules is redrawn ([owner decision 97](#od-97)).

**Alias** (opt-in, "public forever (CT)"): the network_name, one per network: a copy of the label's records except challenges, live once §13's certificates name it. Labels and aliases share `dns_label`'s primary key (root, label) across kinds and states, so alias claims and `RenameNetwork` (§7.12) refuse any name a row holds, live, retiring or tombstoned.

**Validation** (aliases and new names, §7.12; every new name through `ScreenName`, §21.6): `ValidateNetworkName`; no edge `-` (Boulder refuses it); no `--` at positions 3-4 (no `xn--` or IDNA homographs); not reserved; not brand-confusable after mapping 0→o, 1→l, 3→e, 5→s and rn→m per `-` token ([R:ext-edge](design-research/ext-edge.md) §5). Team scope labels (v1; owner decisions [40](#od-40), [58](#od-58)), from the signed projection (§8), also avoid reserved owners, hosts, client names (§7.7) and word-number labels. Reserved, versioned in the sidecar repo:

```text
www mail mx smtp imap pop dns ns ns1-ns9 edge acme canary rpt out mta-sts autoconfig autodiscover
  wpad isatap localhost
api app web connect mcp gossip grafana taskworker proxy alt monitor mmm lb auth login account admin
  status abuse postmaster security support billing evs gkm sockets tlsedge smtpedge mxedge certs
fuji cosmic fireside crisp gala snow jazz honey, plus every services.yml host label (a release check)
*-lb *-v4 *-v6 main-* beta-* canary-* community-* local-* by-*
ur urnetwork bringyour recurd burner, plus a curated list of the most-phished brands
```

**Census** (a read-only query in M0):

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name !~ '^[a-z0-9-]{5,50}$') AS pre_rule,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name ~ '(^-|-$)') AS edge_hyphen,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE substr(network_name, 3, 2) = '--') AS dash34,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name = ANY($1) OR network_name ~ $2) AS reserved
FROM network;
```

**Renames, deletion and restore (D-DNS-10).** Renaming network_name changes nothing. A changed or released alias serves 90 days as `retiring` (outlasting 5-day sender retries) under CAA `issue ";"`, its certificates revoked (§13), then is tombstoned forever; deleting a network withdraws its records at once and tombstones label and alias, whose certificates are revoked or expire within 45 days. After a Postgres restore and 12.6's restore step (§19.10), taskworker re-reads CT for `<root>` names logged since the restored dump's time minus 7 d and inserts each name `dns_label` lacks as `retiring` with no network; `label-reclaim` (12.8) re-binds it to its network, and the rest tombstone after the 90 days, so I-14 holds across the gap.

### 12.6 Hosting: the self-hosted dns edge

```text
write (api or dns route), one transaction: under a decision, §16.6's gate first (12.8): a stored result
  for the request's effect_key answers it with no write, else the spend check, then the approval_use claim;
  lock the dns_root row (503 while restoring), serial+1, records + dns_zone_journal diff (+ the use's
  result), commit; then raise {dns}serial:<root> to that serial (a script that never lowers it), which
  wakes the feed (PgBouncer's transaction pooling bars LISTEN/NOTIFY)
dns API blocks (dns.bringyour.com): GET /dns/journal?root=&after=<applied> (long-poll <= 25 s); /dns/snapshot
  (the rows at one serial); a poll the journal cannot continue (after < serial, no row after+1: a
  7-day gap, a restore) answers reload, with restore_serial
  rows and snapshots stay readable across releases N and N+1: N ignores fields N+1 adds, and writes
  N cannot read wait until N+1 serves 100% (§19.11)
dnsedge on ns1, ns2 (host-pinned; UDP and TCP 53; no proxy in front, so RRL sees resolver addresses):
  apply each diff atomically, in serial order --> zone in memory + local snapshot; a reload swaps in
    /dns/snapshot's; a replaced snapshot older than restore_serial is kept only until POST
    /dns/reload-diff takes its diff, at most 24 h, and any other is deleted at once
  serve a zone build or key set only once its self-check passes, else keep the previous one
  answer from memory, sign online, rate-limit; SOA serial = root serial
  probe each lb interface every 10 s (owner decision 34; server/services_lb_inventory.go:11-17,35):
    tlsedge's alert on 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 (§13.4; owner decision 121);
    the 25 banner on §19.5's router interfaces
    drop one after 3 failures, never all, and the one §19.5's W1 drains
      --> answered from the healthy set at answer time, with no journal write: the A, AAAA at *, @,
          each copy of *'s records and each mx host on router interfaces (12.7)
certs: GET /dns/ready?serial=s --> stale while restoring or for s <= restore_serial (certs writes again
  at a new serial, §13.8); else API blocks read each running NS's SOA over TCP --> ready when all >= s
restore (§19.10, after the dumps load and the abuse step, before api's replay; Postgres comes back at dump
  age with an empty journal, while ns1 and ns2 serve newer zones until they reload):
  §19.10 sets dns_root.restoring as the dumps load, before api or the dns blocks serve: every dns write
    gets 503, so the CT replay (12.5) and api's replay of revocations (§7.10), their DKIM and TLSA
    deletions (I-15) included, commit after this step; until the transaction below, 12.9's SuspendZone,
    SuspendHost and Restore set only their rows, taking no serial, so the suspensions and lifts
    §19.10's abuse step re-places (§21.10) are in its snapshot
  read each NS's SOA over TCP; an NS that does not answer is stopped, and serves again only from a
    reload, its local snapshot taken as the replaced one
  one transaction: serial := restore_serial := max(restored serial, the SOAs read, {dns}serial:<root>)
    + 2^24, above every serial the lost primary issued, since the key lacks only raises that failed or
    that a Redis failover lost (RFC 1982 allows a jump below 2^31); raise the key
  each edge reloads at restore_serial and posts its diff (POST /dns/reload-diff); once every running
    NS answers that SOA, restoring := false; the step lists, by network_id, owner and type, each RRset
    but challenges' and canaries' in a posted diff, and has W1 regenerate the custom-host map from the
    restored rows (§19.5), listing the hosts that adds or drops, in the incident and in each network's
    admin events (§7.11), both kept 400 d, flagging networks with an open §21 case
monitor, at the site and on 1 outside host: rewrite canary.<root> TXT each minute through the journal;
  validate it through each NS against the KSK as a configured trust anchor (Unbound trust-anchor);
  2 public resolvers check propagation only until the DS, then validate as well;
  DNSKEY window > 7 d; equal SOA serials
  --> incident alert (server/monitor/alert_classes.go:3-8); from M5, both NS failing or a canary
      signature failing pages §19.8's rota at any hour, 30 min to acknowledge (owner decision 143)
```

```yaml
# config/<env>/dns.yml (sketch)
roots: [ur.network]
reverse: from smtpedge.yml's sending addresses   # M9; HE's classless delegation; unsigned
delegated: Team customers' _domainkey.<domain> zones   # v1 (§14.6); not roots
ns: [ns1, ns2]                  # two hosts at the site; IPv4 and IPv6 from different gateway blocks
ttl: {challenge: 60, edge: 60, mx: 300, mx_host: 300, tlsa: 300, mail_policy: 3600, caa: 3600,
      user: 300, user_range: [60, 3600], soa_minimum: 60, ns: 86400, ptr: 3600}   # edge: A, AAAA at *, @
rrl: {ipv4_prefix: 24, ipv6_prefix: 56, slip: 2, classes: [answer, denial, error]}
signatures_per_second: <cap per host>   # cached answers first
edns_udp_size: 1232
any: minimal                    # RFC 8482
client_subnet: ignore           # RFC 7871; never echoed or stored
tcp: {connections_per_source: <cap>, idle_timeout_s: 10}
```

**Placement (D-DNS-3; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123)).** The `dns` engine (`sidecar/dnsservice`, miekg/dns) runs as server/cli/dns: API blocks serve §12.8's routes and the feed; the edge role, `dnsedge`, runs only on §19's dns edge hosts, whose own addresses leave the lb's UDP 53 to WhoDis (R-DNS-8), and deploys one host at a time (§19.11). Edges never query Postgres (I-12), so with the core down they keep serving and signing while writes and ACME wait. Both NS sit at the one site (12.15).

**Signing (D-DNS-5; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [109](#od-109))**, online from the first deploy:
- **Denial.** ECDSA P-256. Compact denial (RFC 9824; NXDOMAIN kept without DNSSEC) and wildcard answers signed as the queried name reveal neither which names exist nor which a wildcard covers.
- **Keys.** The KSK stays on an offline HSM, backed up in a second safe; a two-person quarterly ceremony pre-signs DNSKEY RRsets (current, next and standby ZSK) in 14-day windows, released one at a time. The current ZSK is a `secret_files` entry (warp/warpctl/run.go:172-204) mounted only on dns edges, rolled quarterly by pre-publication; the standby stays in vault.
- **DS.** Without one, validators treat the zone as insecure, so a fault harms no one and only the anchored monitors prove signing; the DS follows 30 clean canary days, before M7's TLSA, which §15.5's "validated" label checks ([owner decision 135](#od-135)).

**Runbook (§19.10).** NS down or flooded: resolvers retry the other; HE null-routes a flooded address. ZSK leak: mount the standby and hold a ceremony; forgery ends with the old windows (≤ 14 days). Both KSK HSMs lost: a new KSK's DS before the last window expires.
