```text
     H_sh   = Transcript-Hash(ClientHello .. ServerHello)       RFC 8446 §4.4.1, a HelloRetryRequest included
     H_sf   = Transcript-Hash(ClientHello .. server Finished)   the server's flight as E2 opened it
     Z1: SHA-256(HKDF-Expand-Label(HS, "s hs traffic", H_sh, 32)) = H_shts; MS from HS (RFC 8446 §7.1);
         each direction's key and IV (§7.3) from HKDF-Expand-Label(MS, "c ap traffic" | "s ap traffic", H_sf, 32)
1.2  r_c, r_s = the ClientHello and ServerHello randoms
     S_ckx  = the SHA-256 state (chaining value, unhashed tail, length) after ClientHello .. ClientKeyExchange,
              every handshake message before the client's Finished; the sidecar's client offers no SessionTicket,
              so the server's Finished is the next message after the client's; any other shape fails Z1
     SF     = the server Finished record as relayed: explicit nonce and ciphertext
     Z1: key_block = PRF(master_secret, "key expansion", r_s ‖ r_c), both directions' keys and IVs;
         cf = 14 00 00 0c ‖ PRF(master_secret, "client finished", SHA-256 finished from S_ckx)[0:12];
         SF opened under key_block's server key and IV = 14 00 00 0c ‖
           PRF(master_secret, "server finished", SHA-256 resumed from S_ckx over cf)[0:12]   RFC 5246 §6.3, §7.4.9
```

**Relation (D-SMTP-22).** Public inputs are values the edge holds anyway: Z1's handshake inputs (above), the client ciphertexts a part opens (`records`, which the stream must repeat, E3), the server records it covers, the preamble and issued values, and the part's ranges. Both directions' keys, IVs and plaintext are private witnesses, and no application key or commitment to one is public, so every part re-proves Z1. A part covers the client records `first_record` to `last_record` and the server records from the previous part's `server_record_count` up to its own, so prover and edge check the same records, and it can verify before its records are sent, so the sidecar paces them (14.4). An MX awaiting a command sends no reply, so a server record relayed past a part's count, such as a late NewSessionTicket, only holds the part's message records (E3) until the next part, or the same part proven again, covers it; once the MX closes, a 421 included, outstanding parts are moot. DATA opens every octet. BDAT's π3 opens the records through the header block and the final `QUIT`; the body between streams unopened once π3 verifies, and the edge counts each of its records as its length minus 17 octets, the most a 1.3 record carries (RFC 8446 §5.2; a 1.2 record, typed in clear by E1, carries exactly its length minus 24). So the MX never counts more chunk octets than the edge: it reaches octet n and the proven `QUIT` only if every body record is unpadded application data, and otherwise ends the chunk inside the `QUIT` record, or never. No client record reaches the MX after it (14.7), and 6 octets hold no transaction, so a malformed body alters only its own unproven content or fails the send. A part that cannot be proven, as after a refused MAIL or RCPT, ends the connection before any message octet, and the sidecar retries or returns a DSN per recipient; a part resent under its `send_id` and `index` is idempotent, and one proven again with a later `server_record_count` replaces it.

```text
sidecar                         smtpedge                           MX
 (EHLO is answered before MAIL, RFC 2920 §3.1; data waits for proven replies, E3)
 |--SmtpPreamble------------------>|--banner, EHLO, STARTTLS---------->|
 |==ClientHello .. Finished (spliced; 1.3 discloses SHTS, E2)=========>|
 |--pi1: Z1 + EHLO record; key and IV are private witnesses-->| verify
 |==EHLO record (forwarded once pi1 verifies)=========================>|
 |<=EHLO reply: the post-TLS keywords==================================|
 |--pi2: server records to that reply (Z7-Z9) + MAIL, RCPT x R-->| verify
 |==MAIL, RCPT x R (forwarded once pi2 verifies)======================>|
 |<=their replies======================================================|
 |--pi3, last: replies 2xx (Z8) + BDAT n LAST, header block, QUIT--->| verify
 |==BDAT n LAST, header block, body (unopened, to n), QUIT, once pi3 verifies>|
 DATA: pi2 also covers DATA; pi3 also proves the 354 and covers the header
 block and the first body part; each later part goes once its own proof
 verifies, and the last ends ". CRLF QUIT CRLF". Without PIPELINING each
 command, QUIT included, goes only after the previous reply.
```

**DATA mode (D-SMTP-20; [owner decision 125](#od-125)).** An MX without CHUNKING after TLS gets DATA, which ends at the first CRLF.CRLF, or on some receivers at bare-LF forms (SMTP smuggling, CVE-2023-51764), so Z6 checks every message octet, at minutes per 100 KiB on desktops. Parts carry the scan state across their boundaries, and the sidecar sizes them by its measured speed to prove within 2 min, inside the MX's 5-minute timeout (RFC 5321 §4.5.3.2.7). A 2 h connection therefore proves at most `smtp_data_proof_bytes`, measured on each host and recorded (≈1 MiB on the M1 reference, ≈600 KiB on an m5.large): a larger message to an MX without CHUNKING gets a DSN before MAIL, as does a body still unproven at 2 h, while other recipient domains and every CHUNKING MX are unaffected.

**The M9 gate (D-SMTP-16)** turns owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99) and [125](#od-125) into tests, in both modes:
- **Soundness.** `smtpproof/SPEC.md`, frozen at M9's entry review, states the relation (D-SMTP-22), public inputs, E1-E3, soundness against a malicious sidecar (a colluding MX gets only its own mail) and zero knowledge against a malicious edge that ran the setup, and names the sidecar's TLS client, whose TLS 1.3 handshake yields the HS that Go's `KeyLogWriter` never exports (14.3). Two engineers who did not write the circuits argue soundness in writing. Through that client, in both TLS versions and modes, §22's adversarial corpus must fail before any effect while honest controls pass: key substitution, record splits, replayed server replies, a pipelined second transaction, smuggled headers, an early or bare-LF DATA end, and scripted MXs with no CHUNKING, CHUNKING only before TLS, no PIPELINING, a refused MAIL or RCPT, mixed recipient outcomes, no 354, a late NewSessionTicket, or a second transaction in the alleged BDAT body; padded or KeyUpdate BDAT body records may fail the send but smuggle nothing.
- **Speed** (p95). BDAT, for a 4 KiB header block and 10 recipients: ≤ 10 s for π1 and ≤ 30 s for π1 to π3 on an Apple M1 MacBook Air (8 GB), ≤ 60 s on an AWS m5.large. DATA, for a 100 KiB message: ≤ 10 min and ≤ 20 min. For scale, ORIGO proves in 1.5 s (c5.4xlarge) to 9.8 s (m5.large) with a 112 MB proving key, and in-circuit AES-GCM takes over 1 s per 512 B on an M2 MacBook Air ([R:ext-email-zk](design-research/ext-email-zk.md) §2.12).
- **Coverage.** The M7 census (D-MAIL-9) probes the Tranco top 10,000's MXs (EHLO, STARTTLS, a handshake and the EHLO inside it, no mail); Gmail, Outlook.com, Exchange Online, Yahoo, AOL, iCloud and ≥ 95% of its MX domains offer a covered TLS version and suite.
- **Interop.** Through the same client, strict DMARC passes at those providers in both modes (DATA forced where CHUNKING is offered), TLS 1.2 to Exchange Online included.

### 14.6 Sending identity

§12.7 is the only record table; this subsection sets the rules for its rows marked §14.6 and lists the rest:

```text
_spf.<root>                    TXT  "v=spf1 ip4:<sending addresses> -all" ; b.<net>.<root>'s SPF includes it
o<k>.out.bringyour.com         A    <sending address>, whose PTR is this name ; warpctl (§19 W11); HELO, FCrDNS
rpt.bringyour.com              MX   itself; A the report address         ; warpctl (§19); RUA, ARF, TLS-RPT, role mail
*._report._dmarc.rpt.bringyour.com  TXT  "v=DMARC1"                      ; warpctl; authorizes every network's rua (RFC 7489 §7.1)

headers (D-SMTP-6):
Message-ID: <26 base32 random>@<net>.<root>        ; the sidecar's; <blabel>.<net>.<root> for burners
X-UR-Ref: 1.<base32(key_id ‖ send_id[12] ‖ HMAC-SHA256(key, send_id ‖ network_id ‖ day)[0:8])>   ; the edge's
Feedback-ID: <class>:<tier>:<nettoken>:urnetwork   ; the edge's; nettoken: a keyed hash of the network id,
                                                   ; constant for burners, and the <token> of its rua
```

- **Alignment (D-SMTP-5).** SPF never aligns (`-all` on the header domain `<net>.<root>`; the envelope domain `b.<net>.<root>` passes SPF), so on shared sending addresses only strict DKIM alignment stops network A passing DMARC as `From: x@B.<root>`. `_dmarc.<root>` is strict too, since burner domains have no `_dmarc` and receivers fall back to it (RFC 7489 §6.6.3).
- **DKIM ([owner decision 36](#od-36)).** Each sending sidecar generates RSA-2048, and URnetwork publishes only public keys through `POST /smtp/dkim-keys`, replying and forwarding burners' selectors included until the PSL listing ([owner decision 79](#od-79); §15.9). Opaque selectors rotate every 90 days, keeping the retired one 7 days; removal (§7.10, I-15) deletes the sidecar's selectors in the same write. Signing is relaxed/relaxed, no `l=`, oversigned From, `x=` 7 days, plus a second signature over only `from:date:message-id:x-ur-ref:feedback-id`, which survives reports that mask recipients.
- **Addresses ([owner decision 124](#od-124)).** smtpedge sends from its hosts' shared lb IPv4 addresses, each with one PTR name, `o<k>.out.bringyour.com`, that HELO repeats and whose A record names it (FCrDNS); no address sends before its FCrDNS holds. Every network and burner shares every address, with no IP pools or per-IP warm-up; reputation is per sending domain and per network, through selectors, halts and rate limits (14.7, 14.8). A listed address leaves the sending set, not ingress, within the feed refresh, its mail spreading over the remaining shared addresses, and rejoins after delisting and 3 clean days (§21.5).
- **Team custom domains (v1, D-SMTP-15).** A Team network's verified `network_domain` (§7.6) may be the header domain, its `_domainkey` delegated to §12 or CNAMEd per selector to `<net>.<root>`, its `_dmarc` at `adkim=s` (§2.8 EX2). The envelope stays `b.<net>.<root>`; strict mode (§15.4) moves it to `b.<domain>`, with the customer's MX and SPF include, as Z4 proves.

**PSL listing ([owner decision 79](#od-79)).** Once `<root>` is on the PSL (§12.4) and a test network's burner mail, signed only under its network selector, passes DMARC at Gmail, Outlook.com and Yahoo (D-SMTP-5), each `_dmarc.<net>.<root>` switches to `adkim=r` and burners sign with the network's selectors; 7 days later §12 deletes the per-burner selectors and records. `_dmarc.<root>` keeps `adkim=s`.

### 14.7 Quotas

The unit stays PLAN.md:89's outbound connections per UTC day ([owner decision 30](#od-30)), at PLAN.md:356's 5/200/20,000, hard ([owner decision 27](#od-27)); §20.4 holds the `smtp_*` keys and numbers. A connection carries one message to one recipient domain (14.4) and costs a unit once its MAIL record is forwarded, an earlier refusal only a burst token; retries, forwards and relayed replies are new connections (§15.10). The recipient cross-check is a daily cap (D-SMTP-14): each preamble reserves its recipient count, capped per message and proven exact by Z4, against `smtp_recipients_per_day`, or gets QUOTA.

**Abuse limits** (`sidecar_abuse:`, equal on every tier, D-QUOTA-7; §21 tightens them per network):
- **Send gate (D-SMTP-14).** Internet mail needs `network_abuse_state` standard or better and starts 24 h after `POST /mail/enable` (§15); restricted networks resume at Community caps after a halt, and probation and anonymous-only networks deliver only same-network deposits (§21.7; D-MAIL-8; [owner decision 96](#od-96)).
- **Breaker.** Community connections are capped per hour at the larger of 500 and 3× the trailing 7-day hourly median; a trip answers Community preambles TRY_LATER and alerts §19.
- **Destinations.** At most 200 Community connections per destination domain per hour; concurrency caps per (sending address, destination /24).
- **Records.** The edge forwards exactly the records E3 admits, within 14.4's time limits; a client record its part refuses (unequal ciphertext, or a body past octet n), or a failed part, cuts the connection (14.8). Once the MX has closed, an outstanding part is moot, and a client record after the final `QUIT`, such as a close_notify, only ends the connection unforwarded; neither is a cut.

**Enforcement.** Each preamble runs one Redis script on `{smq_<networkId>}` (halt, bucket, concurrency, the day's counters and reservations); MAIL debits a connection and its recipients, and close the observed bytes. Keys expire after 48 h; refusals return QUOTA with `retry_after_ms`.

### 14.8 Abuse attribution and the halt rule

Reports and role mail reach `rpt.bringyour.com` (D-SMTP-19). Aggregate reports carry no Message-ID (RFC 9990), so attribution keys on each network's domain.

| Source | Carries | Joined by |
|---|---|---|
| ARF loops: JMRP (IP-based; headers only since 2026), Yahoo CFL (by DKIM d=) | Original headers, sometimes the body | A signature under the network's selector; X-UR-Ref; the Message-ID hash; last-hop Received IP and time against the send log |
| Gmail loop | Rates per Feedback-ID | `nettoken` |
| DMARC RUA, XML (TLS-RPT likewise, JSON, for §15), often gzipped | report_id, source_ip, header_from, DKIM d= and s=, counts | header_from, `rua` token |

**Confidence (D-SMTP-8).** High: a network signature verifies over the reported headers, and the last-hop Received shows a sending IP within ±10 min of a send. Medium: the X-UR-Ref MAC verifies and matches that IP and time, and the report carries a verifying DKIM signature whose `d=` is the MAC's network; without that `d=` the join is dropped, not demoted, since a recipient on the shared addresses could paste another network's X-UR-Ref into a complaint. Low: a Received join only, never halting; §21 reviews it.

False reports fail: replays come from other IPs, forgeries lack signatures, each (network, Message-ID hash) counts once, only allowlisted operators with verifying DKIM count, and `not-spam` (RFC 6430) cancels.

**Halt rule ([owner decision 37](#od-37)).** Pro and Team halt on rates, since at 20,000/day Gmail's 0.1% target allows about 20 complaints.

| Trigger (high or medium confidence) | 24 h halt of |
|---|---|
| A complaint against one `<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, any tier | That label |
| Community: the first complaint against `<net>.<root>`, or a second halted label within 24 h | The network, burners included |
| Pro: complaints above 0.5% of 24 h recipients, at least 2 | The network |
| Team: above 0.1%, at least 5 | The network |
| Verified fraud, virus or phishing, any tier | The network, with §21 review |
| Two record cuts in 24 h (14.7) | The network |
| A network's RUA message counts from the sending addresses exceed its proven sends, per recipient (`smtp_send`), by >20% + 5 a day | No halt: §21 reviews it as an investigation signal |
| 3 halts in 30 days | Suspension until §21 reviews it |

- **Mechanics.** A Redis flag plus an `smtp_halt` row, for the network or one label, lasts 24 h from the report's arrival; edges reload every 60 s. New preambles in scope get HALTED, in-flight connections finish, and a §6 `mail` hint holds the sidecar's queue.
- **Appeals.** An admin, never a client token (AUTHZ1), appeals via `POST /smtp/appeal`; rechecks lift halts from duplicates, replays or contradicted medium joins, and §21 reviews the rest. smtpedge stores no session ciphertext (D-SMTP-10), so the only content evidence is the network's sealed report copy, which it may volunteer.
- **Reports (D-SMTP-12, D-SMTP-23; [owner decision 78](#od-78)).** ARF parsing is header-only: the `message/feedback-report` part and, to the first CRLFCRLF (≤ 64 KiB), an enclosed `message/rfc822` or `text/rfc822-headers` header block (DKIM-Signature, Message-ID, X-UR-Ref, Feedback-ID, From domain, Received); no enclosed message body or attachment is decoded. Aggregate reports' XML or JSON, machine data rather than user content, is parsed within 8 MiB inflated (`report_inflate_bytes`) and a 100:1 ratio, with DTDs and external entities refused and nesting ≤ 32; it counts only from a reporter whose DKIM verifies, at the network's `rua` token, once per (reporter, `report_id`). The raw bytes pass once, in memory, through the reporter's DKIM body hash and an HPKE seal to the network mail key (§15.8; burner reports included), kept in `smtp_complaint.sealed_report` for 30 days. The row keeps §2.8 smtp-5's fields; the last-hop Received IP and time serve the join only. Unattributable reports, role mail included, are dropped unread (§21.8).
- **Self-reports.** `SmtpOutcome` (reply codes, DSN counts, TLS level, refused downgrades) only tightens: over 10% hard bounces in 24 h halt.

### 14.9 The smtpedge service and the sidecar/server split

| Piece | sidecar repo | server, ops |
|---|---|---|
| `SmtpSender`: handoff, outbox, per-domain split, DKIM, preamble, proofs, TLS levels and pins, retries, DSNs; a `ReachReceipt` per send (recipients with BCC; §16.8, [owner decision 25](#od-25)) | `smtp_*.go` | — |
| DKIM keys | `smtp_dkim_*.go`, keychain (§5) | `POST /smtp/dkim-keys`; §12 publishes |
| Engine (gate, quota, MX, pre-TLS, proof checks, splice, send log) and reports (ARF and aggregate parsing, attribution, seal, halt, reconcile) | `smtpedgeservice` | `server/cli/smtpedge`, `SmtpEdgeStore`, vault `secret_files`; taskworker jobs |
| Prover and verifier (TLS 1.2 and 1.3; BDAT and DATA) | `smtpproof`, a nested module the root never requires; `cli/` injects its provers on desktop builds ([owner decision 104](#od-104); §4.4) | server injects the verifier into smtpedge |

```go
type SmtpEdgeStore interface { // server implements; batched, off the connection path
	InsertSends(ctx context.Context, sends []*SmtpSendRecord) error
	FindSends(ctx context.Context, key *SmtpJoinKey) ([]*SmtpSendRecord, error)
	InsertComplaint(ctx context.Context, complaint *SmtpComplaint) error
	InsertAggregate(ctx context.Context, report *SmtpAggregateReport) (inserted bool, err error) // once per (reporter, report_id)
	SetHalt(ctx context.Context, halt *SmtpHalt) error
	ActiveHalts(ctx context.Context) ([]*SmtpHalt, error)
}
func NewSmtpEdgeService(ctx context.Context, host *ServiceHost, store SmtpEdgeStore, verifier SmtpProofVerifier, settings *SmtpEdgeSettings) (*SmtpEdgeService, error)
func (self *SmtpSender) Send(ctx context.Context, message *SmtpOutboundMessage) (*SmtpSendResult, error)
```

- **Shape.** One connect client per process on a platform JWT in `urnetwork-edge`, on the two sending hosts (§19.4); each dial binds one of its host's lb addresses in the sending set by fwmark; no lb route or inbound port.
- **Prerequisites,** asked in M0, due at M9's entry review: HE's outbound TCP 25 and reverse delegation, with PTRs §12 serves from smtpedge.yml; the HELO names' A records and W7's rules (§19); SNDS, JMRP, Yahoo CFL and Postmaster Tools enrollment. No address sends until its PTR and its HELO name's A record agree (FCrDNS).
- **Failure.** An edge crash resets its streams, and the sidecar retries on the §9 backup ticket; mail waits in the sender's queue or outbox, never at the edge. Losing Redis reloads halts from Postgres and restarts counters, failing open by at most a day's quota; DNS or MX failure returns TRY_LATER without a debit.
- **Metrics** (`urnetwork_smtpedge_*`) carry results, modes, TLS levels and proof times, never network, domain or IP labels.

### 14.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edge-terminated submission, an edge-held DKIM key, an SES relay, audit by disclosing the ECDHE secret, parsing enclosed message bodies, vendor report intake, a shared VERP bounce domain | Filtering, exact counts, sound without ZK, richer joins, bounce rates | URnetwork or a vendor reads user mail | Ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| Prove client records only, trusting the sidecar's reading of MX replies | No server-record circuit, one part fewer | An MX without CHUNKING, or one that refused the envelope, runs commands smuggled in the alleged body | Rejected (D-SMTP-22) |
| BDAT only | No body-wide circuit | MXs without CHUNKING unreachable | Superseded ([owner decision 125](#od-125)) |
| DMARC `ruf` | Failure samples | Mail copies at URnetwork | Rejected: `rua` only |

### 14.11 Decisions proposed

**D-SMTP-1 (proposed).** The sidecar reaches `smtpedge` only by a §6 stream; the edge dials the MX, runs pre-TLS and splices from the ClientHello on (14.4). *Why:* TCP/25 stays off providers, and the proofs get no-MITM.

**D-SMTP-2 (proposed).** STARTTLS is mandatory, TL4 needs the user's consent per recipient domain, and no host is sent below its pin (14.4). *Why:* an active edge could read such mail.

**D-SMTP-3 (proposed).** The preamble is protobuf frames ahead of raw TLS (14.5). *Why:* PLAN's placement without PROXY v2's 2,048 B parser cap (server/connect/transport_pp.go:28), and versioned.

**D-SMTP-4 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 35](#od-35): no declared preamble ships, and D-SMTP-16 sets the proof gate.

**D-SMTP-5 (proposed).** 14.6's identity: header domain `<net>.<root>` with SPF `-all`, envelope `b.<net>.<root>`, strict DMARC with `rua` only, FCrDNS with HELO = PTR ([owner decision 124](#od-124)), relaxed alignment only after the PSL test. *Why:* only the network's key passes, bulk rules hold (https://support.google.com/a/answer/81126), and old PSL copies still apply the strict `_dmarc.<root>`; a listed address leaves the sending set (14.6), with no separate IP pool ([owner decision 124](#od-124)).

**D-SMTP-6 (proposed).** The sidecar declares the Message-ID; the edge issues a MAC'd X-UR-Ref and a per-network Feedback-ID (14.6). *Why:* unforgeable references with no recipient data.

**D-SMTP-7 (withdrawn).** Superseded by owner decisions [34](#od-34) and [124](#od-124): smtpedge sends from the shared lb addresses, with no IP pools.

**D-SMTP-8 (proposed).** Attribution has three confidence levels; only high and medium halt, and a medium join needs a verifying `d=` of the X-UR-Ref MAC's network (14.8). *Why:* resists replay, forgery and guessed Message-IDs, and a recipient on the shared addresses replaying another network's X-UR-Ref.

**D-SMTP-9 (proposed).** Halts are 24 h Redis flags with `smtp_halt` rows, per network or burner label (14.8). *Why:* PLAN.md:91 without per-packet work.

**D-SMTP-10 (proposed).** Retention follows §2.8 smtp-1 to smtp-6, plus 14 days of backups; send records keep the MX host, not its IP, and recipients, third-party IPs, subjects, bodies, report plaintext, session ciphertext and record lengths are never stored, nor the SHTS that sidecars disclose (E2); everything else a connection shows stays in memory. *Why:* joins need only a network and a time (§2.11).

**D-SMTP-11 (proposed).** The engine is `smtpedgeservice`, hosted by `server/cli/smtpedge`; the prover and verifier are the nested module `smtpproof`, which the root never requires ([owner decision 104](#od-104)). *Why:* owner rule 1; no client links the engine, and only desktops link the prover.

**D-SMTP-12 (proposed).** Reports are parsed header-only, aggregate attachments by D-SMTP-23's bounded parser, then sealed unparsed to the network mail key or dropped (14.8). *Why:* the directive; attribution needs only headers and aggregate counts, neither of them user content.

**D-SMTP-13 (proposed).** For a URnetwork MX, smtpedge splices to mxedge over the host LAN (14.4). *Why:* Q-ARCH-3 (a); TLS stays sidecar to sidecar.

**D-SMTP-14 (proposed).** 14.7's send gate, breaker and destination caps bound Community volume, and its daily recipient cap every tier. *Why:* free Sybils are the largest risk, and connections alone would allow a Team network 2,000,000 recipients a day.

**D-SMTP-15 (proposed).** In v1, Team networks send from verified custom domains (14.6). *Why:* PLAN.md:364.

**D-SMTP-16 (proposed).** M9's gate is 14.5's soundness, speed, coverage and interop tests, in both modes, through the sidecar's own TLS client. *Why:* owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99) and [125](#od-125) set the bar without a threshold or method.

**D-SMTP-17 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 125](#od-125): the DATA-mode proof is built beside BDAT, and DATA coverage is part of D-SMTP-16's gate (D-SMTP-20).

**D-SMTP-18 (proposed).** Phones do not prove: they write outbound mail, signed by their identity key, to the member's mailbox outbox (§15.7), which one of the member's consented prover hosts (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)) sends as in 14.4, burner replies and forwards included ([owner decision 53](#od-53)). *Why:* no phone proves yet, and plaintext stays on the member's devices.

**D-SMTP-19 (proposed).** Reports and role mail go to `rpt.bringyour.com`, whose TCP 25 reaches only §15.4's platform listener, terminating every session, SNI or not; `<root>`'s MX names it for `abuse@` and `postmaster@` (§21.8), from M5. *Why:* reporters without SNI must deliver; platform names stay off `<root>` (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [16](#od-16)).

**D-SMTP-20 (proposed).** 14.5's DATA mode: every message octet proven, in 2-minute parts, within a 2 h connection, up to the host's measured `smtp_data_proof_bytes` (≈1 MiB on an M1); a larger message to an MX without CHUNKING gets a DSN. *Why:* [owner decision 125](#od-125) keeps MXs without CHUNKING reachable; DATA ends by content, so an unchecked body could smuggle a second transaction; an idle MX closes after 5 min; and in-circuit AES-GCM bounds what 2 h proves.

**D-SMTP-21 (proposed).** Z1 proves TLS 1.2's server Finished in-circuit, so no 1.2 key is disclosed (14.5). *Why:* the server write key would open every MX reply, some of which echo recipients.

**D-SMTP-22 (proposed).** 14.5's relation also proves the MX's authenticated replies (post-TLS capabilities, envelope replies, the 354) under private server application keys (Z7-Z9); each part carries the client ciphertexts it opens and names the server records it covers, no message record leaves the edge before verified parts cover every server record relayed before it, and BDAT's body streams unopened under the relation's count bound; `smtpproof/SPEC.md` freezes it. *Why:* a malicious sidecar's control flow is no evidence of the MX's grammar (RFC 3030 §2, RFC 3207 §4.2); an implicit server range fails an honest part when a record arrives during proving; and a part that verifies before its records are sent lets the sidecar pace commands for an MX without PIPELINING and keeps message bodies out of edge memory.

**D-SMTP-23 (proposed).** DMARC and TLS-RPT aggregates are parsed within 14.8's bounds and counted once per (reporter, `report_id`), and the RUA check compares message counts with proven sends per recipient, not connections, as a §21 signal. *Why:* the counters live only in the XML or JSON, which header-only parsing skips, and one connection's message can count once per recipient (RFC 9990 §3.1.1.8).

### 14.12 Open questions

**Q-SMTP-1.** [X7] How is the preamble made trustworthy, and what ships before a sound proof? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99)):** nothing ships until 14.5's proofs pass D-SMTP-16's gate, with no external audit; burner email launches receive-only. **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 125](#od-125)):** always fund a DATA circuit, built beside BDAT and part of the gate (D-SMTP-20). DATA proves at most the host's `smtp_data_proof_bytes` in 2 h, so larger mail to an MX without CHUNKING gets a DSN, and both modes prove the MX's replies (D-SMTP-22). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SMTP-2.** What is the quota unit, given connects (PLAN.md:89) and emails/day (PLAN.md:356)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 30](#od-30)):** (a), outbound connections per day, with per-connection caps and a recipient cross-check, which D-SMTP-14 makes a daily cap (14.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SMTP-3.** Does any abuse report halt a network for a day on every tier (PLAN.md:91)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 37](#od-37)):** (d), tiered, domain-scoped halts (14.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SMTP-4.** [X7 residual] What happens to an unauthenticated MX (TL4)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 38](#od-38)):** (a), refused with a DSN unless the user allows the domain (14.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SMTP-5.** [X7 residual] Who holds DKIM keys? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 36](#od-36)):** (a), each sending sidecar, under an opaque selector, at most 64, revealing how many devices send (§2.8 smtp-6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SMTP-6.** Cross-cutting (§19.5, §21.5). Which IPv4 addresses send, under which PTR names? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 124](#od-124)):** (a), the shared lb addresses, PTR names under bringyour.com, HELO = PTR, and no IP pools or per-IP warm-up (14.6). A listed address leaves the sending set but stays in ingress, with nothing to drain to; a listing that also hits api and connect ingress is an accepted risk (14.15). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SMTP-7.** Cross-cutting (§15, §21). What happens to an attributed report's raw bytes? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 78](#od-78)):** (b), sealed unparsed to the network mail key for 30 days; URnetwork keeps only attribution fields (14.8). *Residual:* none.

### 14.13 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:90, :94.** The "first N bytes" proof is unsound as written; outbound mail waits for 14.5's BDAT and DATA proofs, which also prove the MX's replies (owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99), [125](#od-125); Q-SMTP-1). The "routing path" becomes the edge's trace (sending IP, HELO, MX, time).
- **PLAN.md:97.** DMARC aggregates carry neither Message-ID nor path, so joins use header_from, DKIM d= and IP; Message-ID and X-UR-Ref serve ARF (Q-SMTP-1).
- **PLAN.md:91.** A complaint halts its burner label, networks halt by 14.8's tiered ladder, and attribution is by DKIM, not Message-ID alone ([owner decision 37](#od-37); Q-SMTP-3).
- **PLAN.md:13.** The engine is a child package and the prover a nested module ([owner decision 104](#od-104); Q-REPO-5).

### 14.14 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `SmtpSender.Send` and the outbox sender (§15); send reach receipts (§16.8); `ur/smtpedge` and its LAN splice to mxedge; the report host, attribution and halts (§21); 14.6's record rules (§12, §19).
- **Consumes:** §4.4 module layout; §5 keychain; §6 streams, push, Service mode; §7.6 domains; §7.10 removal; §8 `mail_send`, consent; §9 Find; §10 drop keys in GenRotate (the network mail key, D-KEYS-17); §12 records, reverse zones; §15 handoff, header rules, outbox, forwarding, platform listener, mail key; §19 hosts, addresses, W7, W11; §20 tiers, leases; §21 standing, `ScreenName`, breakers; §22 corpus.
- **Subprotocol messages** (service 0x16, §6.11): `SmtpPreamble`, `SmtpPreambleResult` and `SmtpOutcome` on the stream to smtpedge; `SmtpProof`/`SmtpProofResult` (RPC to smtpedge; π1-π3 and DATA parts; M9); `SmtpStatus` (push `mail`; halt, quota).
- **API routes** (connect/api/bringyour.yml; server/api/route_authz.go classifies the Client routes sidecar, on §7.4's `strict_exp` allowlist): `POST /smtp/dkim-keys` (Client with `mail_send`; network and burner selectors); `GET /smtp/status` (Client; quota, halt); `GET /smtp/reports?since=` (Client with §8 read; fields, sealed copies); `POST /smtp/appeal` (admin scope, never a client token, so the allowlist still refuses it).
- **Tables** (smtpedge; migrations ≥926): `smtp_send` (daily partitions, PK (send_day, send_id), dropped after 30 days), `smtp_complaint` (13 months, with `sealed_report`, cleared at 30 days), `smtp_halt` (13 months), `smtp_dkim_key` (deleted 30 days after its selector leaves DNS), `smtp_dmarc_daily` (13 months; per network, day, reporter, header_from and `report_id`, so each report counts once); Redis `{smq_<networkId>}`.
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/smtpedge`; `config/<env>/smtpedge.yml` (sending addresses, HELO names, loop allowlist, report parser bounds); vault X-UR-Ref keys; `pro.yml` keys and `sidecar_abuse:`; taskworker jobs for reconciliation, retention, sealed reports and key expiry.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §12 runs 14.6's PSL steps, serves the reverse zones and Team `_domainkey` delegations, and writes a burner label's explicit MX and addresses with its first selector, removing them with its last (D-DNS-11); §19 W11 publishes the HELO names' A records; §21.5's breakers pull a listed address from the sending set; §2.8's smtp-2 lists proofs π1 to π3 and, in DATA mode, one per later body part, `helo_name`, the length and timing of every client and server record, and no key that opens application data (D-SMTP-21, D-SMTP-22), and smtp-5 the aggregate parser (D-SMTP-23); §22 runs FS-31's scripted MXs (no PIPELINING and a late NewSessionTicket included), padded and KeyUpdate BDAT body records, a mutated witness for each of E1-E3 and Z1-Z9, the X-UR-Ref replay, FS-39's report-intake cases at M5-out, halt scoping, and network A failing DMARC as B's burners too.

### 14.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| The BDAT or DATA proofs miss D-SMTP-16's bar, or unaudited circuits are unsound (owner decisions [99](#od-99), [125](#od-125)) | High | High | Started in M0; `SPEC.md`, non-author analysts, §22's corpus, the RUA check; disclosed as unaudited ([owner decision 119](#od-119)); burner email launches receive-only (owner decisions [9](#od-9), [35](#od-35)) |
| DATA proves minutes per 100 KiB, so a message above `smtp_data_proof_bytes` (≈1 MiB on an M1) to an MX without CHUNKING gets a DSN, and smaller ones are slow or hit the MX's session limit | Medium | Medium | 2-min parts; the cap reaches only the non-CHUNKING tail the M7 census sizes; retries; a designated-verifier prover (Later) |
| Sybil free networks send their caps | High | High | Send gate, breaker, halts |
| A mail listing of a shared lb address also blocks api and connect ingress there; with no separate IP pool to drain to and no warm-up ([owner decision 124](#od-124)), enough listings degrade sending and the shared ingress together (accepted) | Medium | High | The listed address leaves the sending set (14.6); per-domain and per-network reputation; halts; §21.5's breakers; delisting |
| HE refuses port 25 or reverse delegation | Unknown | Critical | Ask in M0 |
| MXs without a covered TLS version or suite, and phone-only members, get no outbound mail | Medium | Medium | Census, DSN, outbox (D-SMTP-18); designated-verifier prover (Later) |
| A refused or mixed RCPT ends the connection before data, so the resend costs a second unit | Medium | Low | Resends go only to accepted recipients; Z8 keeps the proven envelope exact |
| Weak signals: bounces after the envelope are self-reported, hiding some list-washing; Postmaster Tools or Yahoo CFL ignore subdomains | High | Medium | Self-reports; connections ending before π3 bound envelope refusals (Z8); IP-based loops, RUA; test first |
| A compelled edge reads TL4-override mail | Low | High | Off by default; pins; label (§2.8 EX4) |
| After the PSL switch, a receiver on an old PSL copy aligns one network's selector with another's From | Low | High | 14.6's test gate (D-SMTP-5) |

### 14.16 Phasing

- **Before M9:** the report host with header-only and aggregate parsing (M5), whose M5-out waits on FS-39's report-intake cases, with S7's SNI-less abuse@`<root>` case run at M5 (§22.17, §23.6); the outbound probe (M7).
- **v0 (M9; owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99), [124](#od-124), [125](#od-125)):** the relay with edge-driven pre-TLS; TL1-TL3, TL4 refusal and pins; TLS 1.2 and 1.3 circuits in BDAT and DATA modes, proving the MX's replies (D-SMTP-22), past D-SMTP-16; the LAN splice; per-sidecar DKIM, strict DMARC; the shared lb addresses with bringyour.com PTR and HELO names, none sending before its FCrDNS holds; quotas, send gate, breaker, record cuts; header-only reports, reconciliation, halts; the outbox, with §15's replies and forwarding. Blocked by D-SMTP-16, HE, C9 (M5), §12 and §15.
- **v1 (Team, from M9):** custom domains.
- **Later:** a designated-verifier (VOLE) prover for phones and faster DATA (megabytes per message); the PSL cut-over (14.6); DKIM2.

## 15. The local email server, inbound mail, and burner email

### 15.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns the sidecar's `mail` component (`mail_*.go`, §4) and the `mxedgeservice` engine that server hosts as `mxedge` (owner decisions [19](#od-19), [104](#od-104)): the local SMTP server for `mx.<net>.<root>`, inbound routing (X6), platform report mail, offline behavior, the mailbox, labels, addresses and burner email. mxedge sees ciphertext plus §2.8's mx-1 to mx-4. Sending, DKIM and abuse are §14's; records §12's; certificates §13's; keys §10's; deposits §11's; approvals §16's; phones §18's; hosts §19's; quotas §20's.

### 15.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-MAIL-1 | A local SMTP server "terminates a public `mail.<me>.ur.network`", stores mail encrypted and sends through the SMTP edge | PLAN.md:104 |
| R-MAIL-2 | Inbound TLS ends on customer devices; servers see ciphertext and small header values only, D-MAIL-10's report intake excepted (§2.8 mx-4) | CONVENTIONS §0; D-TRUST-4 |
| R-MAIL-3 | An admin address; unlimited aliases, each an id or a group, with members and a history | cli/UI.md:21-27, :68-71 |
| R-MAIL-4 | Each id or group has a title, password, one-time auth, URL and notes | cli/UI.md:72-73; MM:633-657 |
| R-MAIL-5 | Group addresses fan out to every member | RA:1584; [R:product](design-research/product.md) §2.2 N3 |
| R-MAIL-6 | Burners: generated addresses, "Used at", inbox, reply, compose, logins, notes, autofill | MM:467-657 |
| R-MAIL-7 | Burners show no network name without an alias, and a network's burners are linkable | [R:product](design-research/product.md) §2.3; [owner decision 32](#od-32) |
| R-MAIL-8 | Mail sent while devices are offline survives the sender's retry window | [R:product](design-research/product.md) §2.2 E6; [owner decision 12](#od-12) |
| R-MAIL-9 | Listeners use §9's `smtp/<port>/<host>` | PLAN.md:69 |
| R-MAIL-10 | Outside mail is untrusted and taints the run | sidecar/pitch5.html:707; I-9 |
| R-MAIL-11 | A released label routes no mail to a new owner while retries live | I-14; R-DNS-5 |
| R-MAIL-12 | Storage is 1/20/200 GB; sends are 5/200/20000 per day | PLAN.md:355-356; [owner decision 27](#od-27) |
| R-MAIL-13 | Works in the daemon, the apps and the extension worker | PLAN.md:28 |
| R-MAIL-14 | Approval by email reply: dropped ([owner decision 80](#od-80)) | P5:899 |
| R-MAIL-15 | Abuse and DMARC, TLS-RPT and feedback-loop reports reach URnetwork without SNI | PLAN.md:91, :97; RFC 2142 |
| R-MAIL-16 | Received mail is labeled "validated" or "opportunistic", checkably, from DNS as it stood at reception | owner decisions [98](#od-98), [135](#od-135); I-11; RFC 6376 §3.1 |

### 15.3 What exists today

- **No inbound mail.** Account mail is outbound-only SES (server/controller/aws_controller.go:638-705), whose bounces and complaints "never reach code" (server/EMAIL1.md:44). ur.network's MX is Google Workspace, with DMARC `p=none`, in a zone signed without a DS (§12.3).
- **lb and warp.** No port 25 exists. Stream ports send PROXY v1 with the sender's address (warp/warpctl/config.go:2508-2510), and an lb interface may send a TCP port to its own service (`tcp_stream_port_services`, warp/services/services.go:1001).
- **connect** keeps TCP/25 local (connect/ip_smtp_policy.go:16-19) and before TLS passes only EHLO, HELO, QUIT and STARTTLS, within 2,048 B and 510 B per line (:29-30). `DohCache.Forward` resolves over DoH (connect/net_http_doh.go:1111).
- **emersion/go-smtp v0.25.0 (MIT)** takes connections only through `Serve(net.Listener)`, whose `greet()` always writes a 220 (https://github.com/emersion/go-smtp, read 2026-11-03).
- **Senders** ([R:ext-email-zk](design-research/ext-email-zk.md) §2.2, §2.5). Postfix and Exim send SNI only under DANE (RFC 7672 §8.1); by anecdote Gmail does, Yahoo, AOL and Proton do not, and SES is unknown. Postfix at level `may` retries with TLS before plaintext (https://www.mail-archive.com/postfix-users@postfix.org/msg99840.html, 2023-08-15). Retry windows run 14 h (SES) to 5 d (Postfix).

### 15.4 Inbound architecture (X6)

**Roles.** mxedge's router serves TCP 25 on every lb interface but the platform listener's two ([owner decision 34](#od-34); §19.5 W4), as a `urnetwork-edge` platform client (§13.6) in Service mode (C9), holding no TLS key. A receiver is a sidecar with an approved `listen` on `sock:smtp/25/mx` (15.5): it holds its mail-host key and sees its hosts' mail in transit, but only deposits to the drop key (§10); readers decrypt (15.7).

```text
sender MTA --TCP/25--> lb stream port (PROXY v1: sender address) --> mxedge router (urnetwork-edge)
  router: 220; EHLO reply (STARTTLS, ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES); "220 2.0.0 Ready to start TLS"
  router: read ClientHello; route by SNI: mx.<net>.<root>, an alias's or scope's, or a custom MX host
  §9 Find <network_id>:smtp/25/mx (a scope's: mx.<scope>) with the edge's K client ids (§9.6)
  §6 StreamOpen{ticket, MailIngress, early_data=ClientHello's first 2,048 B} on a Required stream (D-PROTO-6)
receiver: tls.Server, no second 220; EHLO, MAIL, RCPT, BDAT/DATA; SPF, DKIM, DMARC and PTR as received
  --> deposit (§11.12): the body under its own key, that key in a slot to the drop key, a sealed header
      with MailIngress and MailAuthEvidence --> 250 once durable
reader: ingest; score and label from the sealed evidence (15.5); write the 15.7 layout

report sender --TCP/25--> rpt.bringyour.com (two other lb interfaces) --> platform listener
  TLS ends here, SNI or not; RCPT only <token>@rpt.bringyour.com, postmaster@<root>, abuse@<root>
```

**Routing (Q-MAIL-1).** RCPT arrives inside TLS, so the router routes on SNI alone, through `{mxr_}` (15.15), to the network, alias, Team scope ([owner decision 58](#od-58)) or strict-mode custom MX host (§12.8) it names. DANE TLSA, live from M7 after §12's soak ([owner decision 109](#od-109)), makes DANE senders send SNI.

**Team (v1; owner decisions [33](#od-33), [98](#od-98)).** A direct MX (`POST /mail/direct-mx`) names up to two always-on receivers answering public TCP 25 themselves; mxedge verifies each (a public unicast address, STARTTLS, its `mail_host_key` SPKI) before §12.8 points `mx.<net>.<root>` at it and `{mxr_}` drops the network, re-probes every 5 min and alerts with `MailHint{receiver_needed}` after 15 min of failures, reverting only on `DELETE`; a receiver's removal drops its address (I-15). Under the config's signed `mail.strict`, receivers refuse spliced sessions for URnetwork-zone MX hosts and accept direct-MX sessions and splices for custom MX hosts whose customer-signed zones carry their TLSA (§12.8 step 4), which they watch (D-TRUST-9). Only that custom-MX path, with every MX the recipient domain lists and its TLSA under customer authority, keeps URnetwork from redirecting a DANE sender, and only its mail carries `tls_basis.strict_custom_mx` (15.5). In URnetwork's zone, a direct MX included, an operator can replace the MX, A and TLSA records, and the sender then delivers where no receiver checks (RFC 7672 §2.2): ordinary mail with EX2's residual. Senders without DANE stay exposed (EX3).

**mxedge protocol (D-MAIL-2).** Before TLS, the router accepts only EHLO, HELO, STARTTLS and QUIT, within connect's limits; any byte between STARTTLS and its 220 resets the connection (the CVE-2011-0411 class). The banner names `mx.bringyour.com` ([owner decision 16](#od-16)).

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| SNI names a mail-enabled network, and a receiver accepts (§9.6) | splice |
| SNI names one with no receiver, or sockets is down (§9.8) | close in the handshake, from M8 after a wake hold of up to 30 s (15.6) |
| SNI missing or unknown | close in the handshake ([owner decision 34](#od-34)) |
| Plaintext MAIL, RCPT, DATA or BDAT | `451 4.7.0` within 1 h of a closed handshake from the sender's /24 or /48, fleet-wide; else `530 5.7.0`, linking the published deviation ([owner decision 33](#od-33), §21.11) |
| A botnet or exploit listing (below) | `554 5.7.1` at the banner ([owner decision 111](#od-111)) |
| Over a cap: per sender /64 or /32, with /48 and /24 aggregates; 2 sessions per sender /24 per network; per network | `421 4.7.0` |

**Listings.** The banner rejects only a commercial feed's botnet and exploit categories (for example Spamhaus XBL: https://www.spamhaus.com/data-access/rsync/, read 2026-11-04), from a licensed local mirror refreshed every 5 min, so no sender IP leaves for a lookup; other categories pass in `MailIngress.ip_listings`, and with the feed down nothing is rejected.

**Memory and limits.** A closed handshake writes Redis `{mxc_<HMAC_k(prefix)>}` for the sender's /24 or /48, for 1 h under a daily `k`, storing no address (§2.8 mx-1), so a Postfix plaintext retry from a sibling sending address or another lb host gets 451. Splices end after 10 min idle (RFC 5321 §4.5.3.2.6), 10 min with under 1 MiB passed, 30 min, or 2× the message cap plus 1 MiB. Each router session leaves one `mail_connection_record` row (receiving network, time, size, result; no sender address or burner label), written in 10 s batches and kept 24 h, a §21.9 hold's copy excepted (§2.8 mx-2; 15.15).

**Platform mail (D-MAIL-10; from M5).** `<root>`'s MX and §14.8's report addresses name `rpt.bringyour.com` (D-SMTP-19; §19.5 W4). Its listener terminates every session under a bringyour.com certificate, with the router's caps and plaintext refusal, refuses other recipients with `550 5.1.1` and passes the rest to §14.8's intake, which parses headers and aggregate report data only (D-SMTP-23), seals the raw bytes and persists no plaintext ([owner decision 78](#od-78); §2.8 mx-4, the statement's one exception). Session envelopes stay in memory.

### 15.5 The receiver: local SMTP server, listener, certificates

**Library (D-MAIL-3).** emersion/go-smtp with an upstreamable `ServeConn(conn, ServeConnOptions{AfterStartTls: true})` that skips `greet()` (RFC 3207 §4.2), pure Go for gomobile and wasm (sdk/js/Makefile:69). Receivers verify mail as it arrives with emersion/go-message and mox's `spf`, `dkim` and `dmarc` (MIT) over `DohCache.Forward` (D-MAIL-14).

**Listener.** Each receiver holds one §9 registration, `smtp/25/mx` (a scope's: `smtp/25/mx.<scope>`), protocol `smtp-starttls`, `max_streams` 16, `serving=false` until its key is published; burners share it, a Find samples at most 64 receivers (§9.7), and the `listen` grant needs an I-8 approval. In a member scope ([owner decision 58](#od-58)), `ValidateListen` (§9.4) and §12's `/dns/key-record` accept only that member's consented devices (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)), and readers alarm on a scope deposit from any other receiver.

```proto
message MailIngress {                // 0x1701 (§6.11), in StreamOpen.metadata, <= 1,024 B
  reserved 4, 6, 7;                  // destination_ip, route, burner_id: SNI-only routing
  uint32 version = 1;
  bytes sender_ip = 2;
  uint32 sender_port = 3;
  string sni = 5;
  string ehlo_name = 8;              // pre-TLS argument, <= 255 B
  string ptr_name = 9;               // mxedge's forward-confirmed PTR, or ""; labels use the receiver's own
  repeated string ip_listings = 10;  // categories from the local feed mirror, e.g. "pbl"
  uint64 receive_time_millis = 11;
}
```

**Session.** EHLO advertises SIZE (the tier cap), 8BITMIME, SMTPUTF8, PIPELINING, CHUNKING, ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES and REQUIRETLS (RFC 8689), without AUTH. MAIL must follow the handshake within 60 s. RCPT is checked against the signed `mailcfg` (15.8): unknown `550 5.1.1`, full `452 4.2.2`, at most 100. DATA and BDAT stream into the sealer in 64 KiB chunks. `250` follows evs's confirmation of the deposit, and `451 4.3.0` its failure, including a drop key still pending under D-KEYS-17's rule, §11.13's write-budget refusal and §11.8's closed write gate, or a reset (RFC 5321 §3.8). Accepted mail never bounces, and no authentication result refuses it.

**Reception-time evidence (D-MAIL-14).** Before the deposit commits, the receiver checks SPF, DMARC and every DKIM and ARC signature, resolves `sender_ip`'s forward-confirmed PTR itself, every lookup over DoH (§2.8 ext-3), and notes whether the SNI host's TLSA held its key and, under `mail.strict`, whether its zone watch holds the MX-to-TLSA chain customer-signed, sealing the verdicts and the records relied on, never a DNS transcript; a failed lookup records `temperror`.

```proto
message MailAuthEvidence {         // sealed in the deposit header beside MailIngress (15.7); <= 8 KiB,
  uint32 version = 1;              //   past which verdicts stay and records drop
  bytes message_sha256 = 2;        // the bytes as received, before ingest adds headers
  uint64 receive_time_millis = 3;
  bytes receiver_sidecar_id = 4;
  SpfResult spf = 5;               // pass|fail|softfail|neutral|none|temperror|permerror; domain, ip, records
  repeated DkimResult dkim = 6;    // per signature: d=, s=, pass|fail|temperror, the public key relied on
  DmarcResult dmarc = 7;           // the record (p, adkim, aspf), alignment, pass|fail|none
  string ptr_name = 8;             // the receiver's own forward-confirmed PTR of sender_ip, or ""
  bool sni_tlsa_live = 9;          // the SNI host's TLSA held this receiver's key
  ArcResult arc = 10;              // cv=, and each set's d=, s= and the key relied on
  bool strict_chain = 11;          // mail.strict: SNI named a custom MX host, and this receiver's zone watch
                                   //   (D-TRUST-9) holds every recipient domain's MX hosts and that host's
                                   //   TLSA, with this key, customer-signed, none in a URnetwork zone
}
```

**Certificates (D-MAIL-4).**
- **Mail host.** Each receiver presents its own §13 P-256 certificate for `{*.<net>.<root>, <net>.<root>}`, covering `mx.<net>.<root>` and so every burner; a scope's receivers hold only that scope's pair (§13.8; owner decisions [40](#od-40), [58](#od-58)). It is self-signed on the same key until §13 issues it, and no URnetwork component or evs repo holds a mail-host key.
- **TLSA** (from M7; [owner decision 109](#od-109)): §12 publishes `_25._tcp.mx.<net>.<root>` (a scope's under `mx.<scope>`) `3 1 1` per receiver key, TTL 300 s, via `/dns/key-record`. A key goes live 2 TTLs after publication (RFC 7671 §8.1), and a removed receiver's record is dropped (I-15).
- **MTA-STS** (M8; verified networks, [owner decision 96](#od-96)). Once every receiver holds a §13 certificate, receivers serve the `mode: enforce` policy at `mta-sts.<net>.<root>` as a system publish that `POST /mail/enable` turns on (`tls/443/mta-sts`, audience `public`, no `tls_endpoints` unit or expiry), and §12.7 publishes `_mta-sts`; later receivers serve only once certified. It needs no `tls/` listen or publish grant: each receiver's approved `smtp/25/mx` listen grant stands in for both at registration, Find and admission, and its expiry or revocation ends that receiver's publish (§9.10, §13.9). Burners rely on DANE: burner domains publish no policy, and senders never take a parent zone's (RFC 8461 §3.4), so a listed operator's MTA-STS enforcement never covers burner mail (Labels, below).

**Labels ([owner decision 135](#od-135); I-11).** Since opportunistic senders accept any certificate (§2.8 EX3), ingest labels a message "validated" only if MAIL carried REQUIRETLS (RFC 8689), or if the SNI host had live TLSA in our signed zone (in strict mode, the customer's) and the sender is a listed operator (D-MAIL-13), matched by the forward-confirmed PTR of `sender_ip` or a passing DKIM `d=` aligned with From; else "opportunistic". Every input is the receiver's sealed value (D-MAIL-14), and a receiver's deposit without evidence is "opportunistic", marked "evidence unavailable". Beside the label, the UI and API state its basis and never claim end-to-end path confidentiality: the list is an operator-reputation check, not proof of a DANE or MTA-STS path, and REQUIRETLS, the only exact mark, records the final hop's requirement, never that URnetwork did not read the message (RFC 8689 §8.3). `tls_basis` keeps the rule, operator and list version for rechecks. Burner mail from an operator listed only for MTA-STS enforcement is still "validated" ([owner decision 135](#od-135)), though it arrived opportunistically with no policy to apply; for any burner recipient the stated basis cites an entry's DANE enforcement where it publishes one, else the listing alone, never MTA-STS (15.16). Strict mode's exclusion claim (15.4) appears only where ingest set `tls_basis.strict_custom_mx` from a sealed `strict_chain`, never on direct-MX or URnetwork-zone mail, and says only that URnetwork could not redirect a DANE-validating sender, not that this sender validated; 15.16 states the residual.

### 15.6 When no receiver is online

The edge cannot queue: with no key holder online, no TLS session exists ([owner decision 12](#od-12)).
1. **Several receivers.** §9's scheduler picks one; the backup ticket covers one that died.
2. **Sender retries.** No-receiver cases fail temporarily, so mail waits out the sender's retry window (15.3).
3. **Always-on receivers.** With mail on, `ur daemon` never idles out (§5.8); the apps prompt for a desktop, NAS or VPS receiver; Android receives while its VPN runs (§18.5); Teams run two receivers, or two per scope ([owner decision 58](#od-58)).
4. **iOS.** The tunnel stays keyless (§18.4), and the app listens only while open, so it mostly resyncs mail a receiver took and catches only a retry that lands in that window: iOS alone cannot reliably receive, and iOS-only users may miss time-sensitive codes, as `GetReceiverCoverage` says ([owner decision 12](#od-12)).
5. **Wake (M8; [owner decision 88](#od-88)).** On a miss, the router sets a forced `mail` hint (§6.8, §18.7) and holds the ClientHello up to 30 s (Postfix waits 300 s), at most 1,000 per process and 4 per network, while §18.7's trigger and §19's push sender wake a lapsed Android or desktop receiver; an iOS wake only resyncs.

### 15.7 The mailbox in evs

**Repos (D-MAIL-5, D-MAIL-6)** in plaintext view: §11 replaces names with keyed path tokens (X2), so the server sees only shape, padded sizes and change times (§2.8).

```text
mailcfg             one per network and one per Team scope (kind mailcfg); members write signed
                    records (I-4); tag:mail receivers read, by ReaderWrap (owner decision 114); a
                    scope's is read only by its member's consented devices (§8.5) and receivers;
                    member devices hold at most 1,000 leaves, as in any data repo, and an unseated
                    one waits keyless, creating no address until seated (§8.12; owner decision 144)
  addr/<h>/<address>    MailAddress{kind: admin|id|group|agent|burner|bounce, mailbox, members, creator,
                        effect_key}, created only if absent (15.8)
  burner/<h>/<blabel>   mailbox, state (live, paused, burned), replying, created, effect_key; created only
                        if absent; burned labels kept forever
mailbox:<member>    kind mailbox, owner-bound (§8.5): one member's ids, agents and burners
group:<group>       a general repo on a file-mode ref, whose readers are the group's members (§8)
  vault/<h>/<entry_id>  VaultEntry, one key slot each (15.8); mailboxes only
  m/<yyyymm>/<h>/<id>   raw RFC 5322 bytes plus ingest headers, one deletable slot/ object each (§11.6);
                        yyyymm from the sealed receive time, so racing readers write one path
  r/<yyyymm>/<h>/<id>   reference to (group repo_id, message id); mailboxes only
  i/<yyyymm>/<n>        append-only index segment, <= 1 MiB or 4,096 entries of
                        IndexEntry{id, address, time, from, subject, snippet (200 B), message_id,
                        thread_key, size, attachments[{name, type, size}], auth_results, tls_label,
                        tls_basis{rule: requiretls|operator, operator_id, list_version,
                        strict_custom_mx},
                        spam_score, one_time_code}; auth_results and tls_basis from the
                        deposit's MailAuthEvidence (15.5)
  f/<yyyymm>/<n>        flag-op segments of <= 4,096 ops (seen, flagged, label, trash); last writer
                        wins by hybrid logical clock
  o/<h>/<effect_key>    outbox: internet mail queued for a desktop sender, created only if absent
                        (15.10; §16 D-MCP-11), a forward's key derived from its message id; removed
                        once sent and past its approval's retry window; mailboxes only
  forward               the verified forwarding address and the opted-in burners (15.10); mailboxes only
  ra/<h>/<token>        reverse alias: original sender and burner address (15.10); mailboxes only
  s/model               spam model trained by user verdicts
  deposit refs          MailDeposit records from receivers (§11)
  shards                <h> = hex of SHA-256(the last name)[0]: 256 directories a family (a month, where
                        dated); each child is one EvsName row of §11.7's 448 KiB name table (token, kind, the
                        name sealed with its 24 B nonce and 16 B tag): 128 B for a name under 64 B, 194 B for
                        an addr/ address of 64-127 B, 2-3 B more while a path-epoch copy carries its epoch;
                        bytes bind before the 4,096 count, at §11.7's bound, which no copy moves: at least
                        3,500 children a directory (about 900,000 names a family), and 2,340 (600,000) for
                        addr/ addresses under 128 B
```

**Readers** are the owner's consented devices (§8.5), as MLS leaves, their `EvsShare` subjects (agents by ReaderWrap, [owner decision 114](#od-114)) and [owner decision 63](#od-63)'s visible audit reader ([owner decision 126](#od-126); D-ACL-13). A device an admin admitted under the owner stays parked until a consented device signs `OwnerConfirm`; it, the tagged sidecars the owner sponsors and `tag:mail` receivers only deposit. **Admins.** ERASE and CLOSURE pushes take `repo:<id>:admin` (§11.8, §11.12), so each consented device that is not read-only files `RepoAdmin{add}` for itself once seated (§8.8), and any of them erases, shreds trash or deletes a vault entry, whether or not the mailbox's creating device survives; `EvsShare` subjects, the audit reader and deposit-only sidecars never erase.

**Group mail** is deposited once, into the group repo, and members' devices add `r/` references to their own mailboxes, so storage counts once (§20); a group has at most 100 members (§20.4). Only the group repo's admins (§8.8: its creating device and those a repo admin or config writer adds) erase its messages and shred its trash; members' devices then drop their `r/` references.

**Deposit** (§11.12): a body under a random key, HPKE-wrapped (X-Wing) in a slot to the drop key of the repo's newest signed GenRotate, which the receiver accepts only under D-KEYS-17's depositor rule. A sealed header holds `MailIngress`, `MailAuthEvidence` (15.5), MAIL FROM and its REQUIRETLS flag, this repo's recipients, the TLS version and suite, and the receiver's `sidecar_id`; evs sees the repo id, size, time, depositor and slot.

**Ingest.** On a §11 hint, any reader takes the deposits in order; checks that `MailAuthEvidence` names the message's hash and the signing receiver; scores and labels the message from it (15.5), never from later DNS, showing any re-check apart (D-MAIL-14); adds `Authentication-Results` and `Received`; writes `m/` and `i/` in one push on the repo's file-mode ref, which lands by path ([owner decision 141](#od-141)); records §16.8's reach receipt ([owner decision 25](#od-25)); and consumes the deposit ref. The deposit id is the message id, so racing readers converge; slot ids are 16 random bytes drawn per statement, never derived from a deposit, message or entry id (§11.6): a deposit rebuilt for a newer drop key after 412 GATE_CLOSED, or an ingest re-sealed under a newer generation, draws new ones, and only a retry of the same statement keeps them. An admin's erasure, of one message or a batch such as the trash shred, also re-checkpoints each `i/` segment holding them once, without them, into one record under a fresh key, by a CLOSURE push bound to the ERASE, one pair per part (Limits), which evs takes even at the storage limit (§11.13), since §11.12's closure bound admits a merged record that padding rounds up a step past the replaced records' sum; the ERASE then destroys the old chains' keys and any unconsumed deposit's slot (§11.12); on its hint, every reader and mirror deletes its cached keys, slot copies and every decrypted copy (local store, index and search caches) and refuses those keys, and a daemon serving IMAP expunges the messages; copies an IMAP client or agent already took stay beyond recall (§2.18). Attachments stay inside messages, as content-addressed extraction would leak equality.

**Limits** (`config/all/pro.yml`, §20.4): `mail_inbound_message_bytes` 25 MiB on Community, else 50 MiB; 100 recipients; all mail counts as evs storage (PLAN.md:355), and erasing it frees no stored bytes in v0 (§20.7), so at the storage limit RCPT gets `452 4.2.2`. Admins shred trash after 30 days, a per-entry erasure that preservation holds never block ([owner decision 133](#od-133)) and the storage limit only paces: there, and while spent, §20.7 counts each erasing sidecar's closure uploads against its own 60 a minute and its closure bytes against its own `evs_closure_bytes_per_day` a UTC day, which §21 may tighten but never below `evs_closure_bytes_floor` (§11.12, §20.4; [owner decision 146](#od-146)), so no other admin's closures spend either; ERASE and CLOSURE pushes past the network's 60 a minute queue as P1 and commit. An erasure therefore runs in parts, each one CLOSURE and its ERASE for the messages of whole `i/` segments, sized to what remains of the allowance, since a CLOSURE adopts only uploads under 24 h old (§11.13); a part refused 429 past its eraser's rate or allowance resumes at its `retry_after_ms`. An allowance re-keys 60 full segments a day by default and 3 at the floor, so at the floor one message's erasure waits at most until the next 00:00 UTC, and a backlog of n full segments under ⌈n/3⌉ days (§11.13, §20.7), the waiting messages' bodies and IndexEntries staying openable until their part's ERASE commits.

**Reads.** Apps head-read `i/` and messages through §11 (PLAN.md:63), learning of mail by hints or §18 pushes. The daemon serves §16's `mail_list`, `mail_read` and `ur://mail/{alias}`, and IMAP (emersion/go-imap v2; M8) under D-MAIL-11 and 15.10's AUTH. Outside mail is `untrusted` and taints the run (I-9), whose outward actions, sends included, then each need a fresh second-device or presence-key decision; harness evidence counts only where the matching `requests` rule names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)).

### 15.8 Addresses, groups, vault entries

| Address | Form | Mailbox |
|---|---|---|
| Admin (`@` in the CLI) | `admin@<net>.<root>`, aliased by `postmaster@` and `abuse@` (RFC 5321 §4.5.1, RFC 2142) | the owner's; on Team, an `autogroup:admin` group repo |
| Id | `ur id create <name>` gives `<name>@<net>.<root>` | the creator's |
| Group | `ur id group-create`, `group-add` | the group repo |
| Agent | `<agent>@<net>.<root>`, at registration ([R:product](design-research/product.md) §2.2 N2) | the sponsor's |
| Scoped (Team) | `<name>@<scope>.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 58](#od-58)) | the scope member's |
| Bounce | `bounces+<token>@b.<net>.<root>` (§14.6) | the sender's |
| Burner | `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` (15.9) | the owner's |

- **Local parts** match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; `admin`, `postmaster`, `abuse`, `mailer-daemon`, `bounces` and `r-*` are reserved. No device can terminate cli/UI.md:21's shared `you@ur.network`, so cli/UI.md:68's form holds.
- **Directory.** A receiver honors a creator-signed `mailcfg` record only if §8's policy grants the creator `mail:<alias>#listen` (D-ACL-12). Policy and `mailcfg` are encrypted, and the projection carries only `mail_send` (§8.8), so alias names never reach the server. Creating an alias or a burner is an I-8 outward action: the `mail` component writes the record only once `Authorize` passes (§5.4), for `ur id`, the apps and §16's `mail_alias_*` alike. The record is created only if absent and, under a decision, carries the use's `effect_key`, which also seeds the DRBG a burner draws its candidate labels from, so a retry or a restart's `Lookup` finds its own record (§16 D-MCP-11). MCP's evs tools never write `mailcfg` (D-MCP-17).
- **Same-network mail** is deposited to the recipient's drop key and signed with the sender's identity key (§6.9), without smtpedge, send quota or DKIM; that signature replaces the TLS label (D-MAIL-8).
- **Network mail key:** the admin mailbox's drop key, carried in each of that repo's GenRotates (a scope's: its member's mailbox; D-KEYS-17); §14.8 seals reports to it, burners' included.
- **Vault entries** (MM:594-605) each have their own slot, so deleting one shreds every version of it ([owner decision 61](#od-61)); only the owner's consented devices (§8.5) read them or write "Used at".

```text
VaultEntry{entry_id, address, title, username, password, password_history,
           totp{secret, algorithm, digits, period} (RFC 6238), urls, notes,
           used_at[{registrable_domain, first, last}], created, updated, state}
```

### 15.9 Burner email

**Format.** Burners sit in the network's own zone ([owner decision 32](#od-32)): `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, with `<blabel>` a generated word-number label such as `otter-4821` (`^[a-z]+-[0-9]{4}$`) and `<name>` any local part (D-MAIL-7). They are linkable through `<net>`, and an alias, which shared receiver keys in TLSA and CT tie to the label, names the network (Q-MAIL-10). The sidecar picks unused labels, and §12.7 and §7.7 refuse word-number DNS owners and client names, so nothing shadows the wildcard; labels live only in `mailcfg`.

**Records** are §12.7's rows marked §15, outside the user's quota: the wildcard MX `*.<net>.<root>` → `mx.<net>.<root>` covers every burner label, with 15.5's TLSA, and alias zones and Team scopes repeat both with their own `mx` host. Until the PSL listing, a replying burner's selector (§14's `POST /smtp/dkim-keys`) gives its label its own records, guessable but not walkable under §12.6's compact denial ([owner decision 79](#od-79); §2.8 dns-1). Since a child name makes `<blabel>` an empty non-terminal the wildcard no longer answers (RFC 4592 §2.2.1), dns writes `<blabel>` MX and A/AAAA equal to the wildcard's in the journal write of its first `_domainkey` child and deletes them with its last selector, at §14.6's cut-over or a burn (D-DNS-11).

**Replies** come with sending (M9, [owner decision 35](#od-35)), through §14 with `header_from_domain = <blabel>.<net>.<root>` and flag BURNER. They pass strict DMARC under the burner's own selector ([owner decision 79](#od-79)), send from the shared lb addresses, sharing the domain's reputation (owner decisions [32](#od-32), [124](#od-124)), and count against the daily connection quota ([owner decision 30](#od-30)).

**Spam.** The edge applies only IP listings and rate limits (15.4); readers apply the sealed SPF, DKIM and DMARC results (a DMARC reject files it as spam), rules, a per-mailbox naive Bayes model (mox `junk` is a candidate) and user verdicts, never greylisting, since one-time codes cannot wait.

**Burn** is local ([owner decision 32](#od-32)): receivers answer `550 5.1.1` for the label from then on, the label is never reissued, and devices mark the vault entry burned and may shred its mail; pause answers the same, reversibly. DNS and the server change only when a replying burner's selector retires (§14.6).

**App seams (§18).** `SidecarMail` gains `CreateBurner(site)`, `Burn(id)`, `GetVaultEntries`, `GetUsedAt(entry)`, `GetOneTimeCodes(since)` (from vault TOTP and mail) and `GetReceiverCoverage()` (§18.5). Its `foreground-only` copy reads "iOS alone cannot reliably receive mail: an always-on receiver (a desktop `ur daemon`, a NAS or VPS, or Android with the VPN on) is needed; time-sensitive codes may not arrive", and its copy adds that large attachments may not reach a minority of destinations, those without CHUNKING, until the designated-verifier prover ships (Later; §14.5). Before the first burner, `CreateBurner` shows the `foreground-only` copy whenever coverage is `foreground-only` or `none`, and it never refuses for coverage ([owner decision 12](#od-12)). Autofill is app work (§18.15). With no server burner state, the sidecar applies `mail_burners_active` and `mail_burner_creates_per_day` locally (§20.4).

### 15.10 Sending

The local server is the MTA (PLAN.md:104), on §5.8's submission port under D-MAIL-11 and D-TRUST-8's certificate rule (owner decisions [84](#od-84), [130](#od-130)). AUTH uses a per-instance keychain credential granting only what the daemon grants its OS user ([owner decision 47](#od-47)). Agents use §16's `mail_send`; both paths pass §5.4's outward-action gate (I-8). For each message the server:
1. checks From against `mail:<alias>#send` (D-ACL-12) and holds mail to unapproved recipients until an I-8 channel approves it (`ur approve <id>`, §16.6);
2. stores a copy in `sent`, and deposits same-network mail directly;
3. for BURNER sends, applies the header rules: removes every Received header and adds none, rewrites Date to UTC at minute precision, strips User-Agent, X-Mailer and client `X-*` headers, and regenerates the MIME boundaries and the Message-ID under `<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, so replies reveal no device, client or timezone (§14.4 step 3);
4. queues the rest at `o/<h>/<effect_key>`, created only if absent (§16 D-MCP-11), for §14's `SmtpSender.Send`, which holds it on HALTED, QUOTA or TRY_LATER (§14.7-14.8); probation and anonymous-only networks deliver only same-network deposits (§21.7, D-SMTP-14).

Internet sending waits for smtpedge's BDAT and DATA proofs (M9, owner decisions [35](#od-35), [125](#od-125)), which only desktop-class hosts run, so the owner's consented daemon, NAS or VPS sidecars send what a phone queues (D-SMTP-18).

**Forwarding ([owner decision 53](#od-53); M9).** (1) One external address per mailbox, confirmed by a 6-digit code sent through §14, is kept with the opted-in burners in the mailbox's signed `forward` entry. (2) Readers forward opted-in burner mail only if it scores below the spam threshold with no DMARC fail as received. (3) The forward is a new message From `r-<token>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, `<token>` being a MAC of the original sender under a vault key (`ra/`), with step 3's header rules and `X-UR-Forwarded`, DKIM-signed like a reply (15.9) and queued in `o/` for a prover host. (4) Mail to `r-<token>` from the verified address, passing DMARC as received, is relayed From the burner to the original sender. (5) Each code, forward or relay costs one connection ([owner decision 30](#od-30)). (6) Forwards never go to `<root>` addresses or repeat a message carrying `X-UR-Forwarded`, which stops loops.

DSNs arrive at `b.<net>.<root>`, and receivers deposit them to the sending mailbox.

### 15.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| SNI splice with DANE | end to end for senders that send SNI | senders without SNI defer | chosen (owner decisions [31](#od-31), [34](#od-34)) |
| Encrypt-on-receipt (Proton, Tuta) or plaintext SMTP at the edge | every sender; filtering; a queue | plaintext at URnetwork | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| Hosted or TEE receiver, delegated credentials (RFC 9345), or an iOS tunnel receiver | always on; phone-only users | keys on our hardware, or in the keyless 1 MiB role (§18.4) | ruled out ([owner decision 12](#od-12)) |
| Per-network IPv6 or IPv4 | senders without SNI reach receivers | no dedicated addresses (§19.5, D-OPS-15) | not now ([owner decision 34](#od-34)) |
| Shared burner domain (mock), or labels on a burner root | short; or unlinkable | routable only on RCPT; a new domain and per-burner DNS | ruled out ([owner decision 32](#od-32)) |
| Verify SPF, DKIM and DMARC at ingest | one verifier, on the reader | judges DNS days after reception, past selector rotation (RFC 6376 §3.1) | rejected (D-MAIL-14) |
| An MTA-STS policy per burner | MTA-STS-only senders enforce for burners | a policy host, certificate and CT entry per burner | rejected ([owner decision 32](#od-32)) |

### 15.12 Decisions proposed

**D-MAIL-1 (proposed).** Inbound TLS ends only at customer receivers, except at D-MAIL-10's platform listener for URnetwork's own report and role addresses (§2.8's statement, mx-4); mxedge's router routes by SNI alone, and every unroutable or offline case gets a temporary failure. *Why:* the directive, with D-TRUST-4's one exception; senders retry.

**D-MAIL-2 (proposed).** mxedge's router speaks only 15.4's pre-TLS dialog, refuses plaintext transactions and splices from the ClientHello on. *Why:* RFC 3207, CVE-2011-0411 and Postfix's retry with TLS.

**D-MAIL-3 (proposed).** Receivers run emersion/go-smtp with 15.5's upstreamable `ServeConn`, forked if declined, and verify with mox over DoH as mail arrives. *Why:* pure Go everywhere.

**D-MAIL-4 (proposed).** Each receiver presents its own §13 certificate and TLSA record for `mx.<net>.<root>`, which serves every burner, and serves MTA-STS as a system publish (15.5). *Why:* URnetwork holds no key, removal deletes one record (I-15), and user-publish rules would break policy fetches.

**D-MAIL-5 (proposed).** Receivers deposit each message under its own key, slotted to the drop key in the repo's newest GenRotate (D-KEYS-17), and answer 250 only once it is durable; readers ingest with per-message slots, and an erasure also takes the deposit slot, the index copy and every reader's decrypted copies. *Why:* receivers never read archives, no stale drop key reaches a removed reader, and erasure covers every copy (§11.12).

**D-MAIL-6 (proposed).** Each member has one owner-bound `mailbox` repo, which each of the member's consented devices that is not read-only joins as a repo admin, each group one general repo storing its mail once, which only its repo admins erase, and each network one signed `mailcfg`. *Why:* few MLS groups; one upload per message, not ~5 GB per 50 MiB message to 100 members; and erasure, which takes `admin` (§11.12), never waits on the device that created a mailbox, nor lets every group member destroy the group's mail.

**D-MAIL-7 (proposed).** Burners are `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` under the wildcard MX; receive-only burners have no records, keys or server state of their own, and burning is local (owner decisions [32](#od-32), [79](#od-79)). *Why:* nothing can be enumerated, and URnetwork stores nothing.

**D-MAIL-8 (proposed).** Same-network mail is delivered by deposit and never crosses the internet. *Why:* "end to end between members" (sidecar/pitch5.html:708).

**D-MAIL-9 (proposed).** Burners launch once the owner accepts the SNI loss the M7 census measures ([owner decision 34](#od-34)): per sending ASN, SNI, DANE, TLS version and plaintext fallback, from provider, ESP, top-100 sign-up and report senders, plus §14's destination-MX probe. Proposed bar: under 5% of sign-up and code mail, by volume, lacks SNI. *Why:* SES and Yahoo coverage is unknown ([R:ext-email-zk](design-research/ext-email-zk.md) §5 item 3).

**D-MAIL-10 (proposed).** Reports and role mail reach `rpt.bringyour.com`'s platform listener, which terminates every session and accepts only platform recipients (D-SMTP-19), for §14.8's intake, which parses headers and aggregate report data only (D-SMTP-23) and persists no plaintext. *Why:* reporters without SNI must deliver, the router holds no key, and no third party stores reports.

**D-MAIL-11 (proposed).** Submission and IMAP bind every interface unless `--listen` narrows them ([owner decision 84](#od-84)); off loopback they speak implicit TLS (RFC 8314 §3), chosen per connection by local address, and plaintext stays on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 ([owner decision 130](#od-130); D-TRUST-8, I-17). *Why:* no credential or mail crosses a LAN in cleartext, and one port serves both.

**D-MAIL-12 (proposed).** A Team direct MX names at most two receivers, verified before §12 publishes them; strict mode refuses spliced URnetwork-zone hosts and accepts direct-MX sessions, and only an MX selection and TLSA both in customer-signed zones carry the claim that URnetwork cannot redirect mail, surfaced only as `tls_basis.strict_custom_mx`, so a URnetwork-zone direct MX keeps EX2's residual; a member scope's receivers are that member's consented devices (15.4, 15.5). *Why:* owner decisions [33](#od-33), [58](#od-58) and [98](#od-98), trusting neither URnetwork's zone, which a DANE sender follows wherever it points (RFC 7672 §2.2), nor a lone admin.

**D-MAIL-13 (proposed).** [Owner decision 135](#od-135)'s operator list is `mail_operators.yml` in the public sidecar repo ([owner decision 118](#od-118)), embedded in each release with a list version; each entry names an operator's PTR suffixes, DKIM domains and published DANE or MTA-STS enforcement, which a label's basis cites, never MTA-STS for burner mail (15.5). *Why:* anyone can recheck a label against it, with no new server or key; the list is an operator-reputation check, and REQUIRETLS records only the final hop's requirement (15.5).

**D-MAIL-14 (proposed).** Receivers capture 15.5's reception-time authentication evidence and seal it in the deposit, bound to the message hash, time and receiver (`MailAuthEvidence`); readers label, score, receipt and forward from it and never rewrite a label from later DNS. *Why:* DKIM selectors have a lifecycle (RFC 6376 §3.1), and SPF, DMARC and PTR records change, so a later check would judge other DNS.

### 15.13 Open questions

**Q-MAIL-1.** [X6] How does mxedge route without terminating TLS? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [31](#od-31), [34](#od-34)):** by SNI alone, with DANE TLSA; senders without SNI defer (15.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-2.** [X6 residual] Which devices receive mail? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 12](#od-12)):** always-on receivers, and the iOS app in the foreground, which listens only while open and so is no reliable receiver (15.6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-3.** [X6 residual] What are the burner format and domain? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 32](#od-32), superseding [owner decision 29](#od-29)):** `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` under the wildcard MX (15.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-4.** Should burners forward to external inboxes (MM:583)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 53](#od-53)):** opt-in, to one verified address, with sending (15.10). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-5.** Who receives a Team network's mail? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 58](#od-58), superseding [owner decision 54](#od-54)):** disclosed designated receivers, or member scopes with their own `mx` host (15.6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-6.** Should mxedge reject at the banner on IP reputation? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 111](#od-111)):** only on botnet and exploit listings, never greylisting (15.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-7 (withdrawn).** Withdrawn with Q-ARCH-4; §2.8 lists mx-1 to mx-4.
