- **v1 (M6):** the team record and coordination log, with admin mirrors (Team; [owner decision 102](#od-102)); reach receipts; agent subkeys; filesystem events; model calls (Codex PostModelRequest, harness OpenTelemetry); retention policies; the `audit` reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63)), with its receipts; RECORD.md's verifiable log and client disclosure packets, RS2's (sidecar/pitch5.html:898), over 16.8's leaf hashes, order and commitments.
- **Later:** a team's own legal holds (§23's assurance stage).
- **Blocked by:** D-CORE-9, §5.4's gate and §5.8's `.ur`; §7.8's receipt scope; §7.9's config repo, authorization log and `read_only` admissions; §6.11's `SignedType`; §8.5's consent (M2; [owner decision 126](#od-126)); §11's streams, multi-part pushes, deposits, slots, ERASE pushes and mirrors; D-ACL-7; RECORD.md.

## 17. IP addresses, subnet routing, and port forwarding

### 17.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns PLAN.md's bridge (PLAN.md:113-119): the overlay address plan (X18, owner decisions [28](#od-28), [132](#od-132)), subnet routing, provider port mapping, bridge rules, their engine and states, native IP principals (`WindowDelegation`), cross-network shares ([owner decision 86](#od-86), C18), the connect changes, `BridgeHost`, `ur tun` and `ur bridge`. §7.9 owns the config repo and authorization log; §8 policy, grants, shares and gates; §12 names; §13 `public-tls`; §18 the sdk seam, device-role channel and app work; §20 billing.

### 17.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-BRIDGE-1 | A destination in a client's subnet goes to that client, not the default route | PLAN.md:115 |
| R-BRIDGE-2 | Providers rewrite destination ip:port by port mappings for same-network packets | PLAN.md:117 |
| R-BRIDGE-3 | Rules stored on the server, pushed in real time, decided locally | PLAN.md:119; owner decisions [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6) |
| R-BRIDGE-4 | The sdk device gains "ip addr, port forward" through Sidecar-implemented abstractions | PLAN.md:31 |
| R-BRIDGE-5 | A permanent private address per agent and service, plus routed subnets; Linux and WSL2 first | sidecar/pitch5.html:687, :894 |
| R-BRIDGE-6 | A forward is a grant (one agent, port and window, approved), encrypted between sidecars | sidecar/pitch5.html:680-681 |
| R-BRIDGE-7 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges and exit only through customer exits | sidecar/pitch5.html:689; [owner decision 120](#od-120) |
| R-BRIDGE-8 | `ur tun`, `ur bridge` and the BRIDGE notes; listeners bind 0.0.0.0/:: unless `--listen` narrows them | cli/UI.md:11, :42-52, :104-122; [owner decision 84](#od-84) |
| R-BRIDGE-9 | No locks, I/O or PostgreSQL per packet; every delivery path carries the decision; fail closed | connect/CODESTYLE.md:98, :106 |
| R-BRIDGE-10 | With an ACL document, only rules open a provider's loopback, LAN, link-local or overlay addresses; its own daemon listeners never open, and unverified policy state opens nothing private | §2 I-10; owner decisions [50](#od-50), [105](#od-105), [120](#od-120) |
| R-BRIDGE-11 | Forwarding unlimited on every tier: no count caps; bytes count | PLAN.md:353, :359; owner decisions [10](#od-10), [66](#od-66) |
| R-BRIDGE-12 | Bridge flows are Required at both ends and come from principals the customer signed; outward bridge actions need an I-8 approval | owner directive; [owner decision 3](#od-3); §2 I-3, I-4, I-8 |
| R-BRIDGE-13 | A /16 per network that admins cycle or choose; private names in v0; cross-network forwards on the IP path, aliased and isolated | owner decisions [28](#od-28), [85](#od-85), [86](#od-86), [132](#od-132) |

### 17.3 What exists today

| Piece | Fact | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Sender | One lock-free `sendRoute` load per packet or burst, sdk sockets included, then the mux, a multi client or the local NAT; a destination change rebuilds the multi client, dropping every flow; `NetworkPeer` sends everything to one peer. Window clients (a multi client's per-provider children) show providers their own ids, form no session without `PostQuantumEncryption`, force P2P in Network mode unless overridden, and keep TCP/25 local | sdk/device_local.go:5666-5683, :4984-4995, :5286-5302; sdk/socket.go:141; connect/ip_remote_multi_client_api.go:1033-1038; connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:1643-1649, :3205-3220, :6718-6725 |
| Provider | Flows open at three points (17.6). The sdk provider is Opportunistic: plaintext until a session forms, or forever. Network sources reach anything, LAN and loopback included; every other mode, FriendsAndFamily included, is Public at both ends: public unicast only, else an Incident calling `ReportAbuse`; RFC 1918 is not public, but 100.64/10 is | connect/ip.go:10416-10421, :10449-10451; sdk/device_local_provider.go:258; connect/transfer_encrypt.go:477-483; connect/ip_security.go:385-390, :567-576, :892-908; connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:6704 |
| Apps | All four capture 0/0 and exclude RFC 1918 and fc00::/7 | apple/app/extension/PacketTunnelProvider.swift:1797-1806; android/.../MainService.kt:755-758; windows/app/src/Service/NetPolicy.h:79-83; linux/app/src/Tunnel.hpp:508-510 |

Missing: overlay addresses, destination routing, port mapping, per-port provider checks, private egress for shares, and a customer-vouched principal: contracts are HMACed under a provider secret the platform holds (connect/protocol/transfer.proto:375-379, :563-567).

### 17.4 Address plan (X18)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Block | One IPv4 /16 per network, at random from 100.64.0.0/10 ([owner decision 28](#od-28)) except 100.64.0.0/16 (likeliest in use) and 100.100.0.0/16 (Tailscale's 100.100.100.100); no IPv6 overlay |
| Cycle or choose | An admin re-rolls it or picks a /16 in 100.64.0.0/10 or RFC 1918 only ([owner decision 132](#od-132); D-BRIDGE-16); hosts keep their host bits while the old block drains (17.8) |
| Uniqueness | None across networks; a device whose networks share a block ([owner decision 23](#od-23)) routes it only to the first-joined one, warning in `ur status` and a `SidecarEvent` until an admin cycles one |
| Host address | A random free /32 of the lower /17 outside `<block>.0.0/24`, which holds services (the resolver at `<block>.0.53`); once that is full, the highest free /32 of the upper /17, whose bottom aliases fill first-fit (17.9); never x.y.z.0 or x.y.z.255; a chosen address (`ur tun ip <ip>`) must lie in the lower /17 |
| Binding | The §5 `sidecar_id` (an agent's own only under its own OS user, container or VM, §5.5); it survives re-enrollment and the reaper |
| Assignment | On demand (`ur tun ip`, the host's first map, an admin); the first claim in log order wins (17.8) |
| Release | On revocation or removal, then a 30-day tombstone (I-14) |

Addresses avoid connect's tun ranges, 10.a.b.0/24 and 169.254/16 (sdk/device_local.go:1851-1861; connect/tun.go:387-399, :533-551). Where a local route overlaps the block, as a CGNAT carrier address can, the device routes overlay peers by their /32s and carves out of the router's table and every exported route each local /32 its physical path needs: interface addresses, gateways and system resolvers, from the platform's routes and DNS settings (§18.6's `SetBridgeLocalAddresses`), since `connect.LocalIpv4Networks` sees only interface subnets, or nil where enumeration is restricted (connect/tun.go:490-495). The block is never dropped wholesale; until those /32s are known, the export holds per-peer /32s instead of the block. If a carved /32 is an assigned overlay address, `ur status` warns and an admin cycles the block (D-BRIDGE-16).

### 17.5 Data path and the router

The bridge adds a sender lookup (PLAN.md:115) and a provider decision (PLAN.md:117) to connect's client-to-provider NAT path (D-BRIDGE-1).

```text
sender (app tun | ur tun | userspace connect.Tun)      target (sidecar-owned, Required)
  sendPacket / sendPacketsWithPolicy                     ClientReceive -> principal -> policy
    deviceBridge.Route --link--> multi client(target) ==> LocalUserNat flow -> EgressHook (C5, C18)
      | default | reject: RST or ICMP into the tun          pass | map | deny -> real socket
    UpgradeMux -> default multi client
```

- **Insertion.** After `route := self.sendRoute.Load()` (sdk/device_local.go:5707, :5800), before the mux, so bridged :53 and :80 are never claimed. `deviceLocalSendRoute` gains §18.6's `deviceBridge` (`device.Bridge`, 17.10): nil costs one check, `Route` one atomic load plus `BridgeTable.Classify` and, where an entry offers a choice, one pin probe, two for TCP while it holds 5-tuple pins. Every send path passes here (connect/CODESTYLE.md:98); the CLI runs the same table over `ur tun` or a userspace `connect.Tun`.
- **Batches.** A burst splits in place (a 64-entry stack array) into per-link batches, keeping flow order; an all-default burst passes unchanged.
- **Classify.** A fixed-offset destination read, then an immutable longest-prefix lookup (bart v0.30.0, MIT, 2026-09-21, https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gaissmai/bart, at 0 allocs/op, else in-repo): ≤50 ns at 1,000 prefixes (§22 gate). Unassigned block addresses answer unreachable; carved local /32s (17.4) take the default route.
- **HA and pins** (D-BRIDGE-7, D-BRIDGE-9). A weighted rendezvous hash of (source, destination, protocol), fragment-safe, picks among an entry's advertisers, and pins keep a live pair on its link across edits, since TCP cannot change exit mid-flow (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:6593-6597):

```text
pins     the sender's lock-free table: 8,192 slots on desktop, 1,024 on mobile
key      the pair (source, destination, protocol), in every fragment's header, so a pair's flows and
         fragments share one pin and one link; only a TCP connection under a 5-tuple pin (syn) leaves its
         pair's link, and connect's multi clients forward only reassembled UDP, dropping fragmented TCP,
         since TCP uses MSS (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:6679, :6848-6850, :6875)
record   only where an entry offers a choice, two or more advertisers or links with draining ones
         included; overlay /32s and one-advertiser routes otherwise have one link and need none; one
         atomic store per pair per second
lookup   a TCP segment's 5-tuple pin, then its pair's pin, while its link still serves the entry; else
         the window; else the hash, pinned where the entry offers a choice and a slot is free
full     no free slot: the pair routes by the hash unpinned; nothing is refused (owner decision 66)
window   an entry that offered no choice (one advertiser and one link, so no pins) and now offers one pins
         a pinless pair at first sight to the pre-change link for 600 s after the change, 5 min for UDP and
         ICMP, while that link remains in the entry, draining included: live flows stay while it serves
         them, and new UDP and ICMP pairs, which cannot be told from live ones, follow it
syn      a TCP SYN of a pair the window would pin, or pinned to a draining link, takes the hash over the
         entry's undrained links under a 5-tuple pin instead, so new connections take the new rule at once
         (with no such link or free slot, it follows its pair)
idle     a pin ends when its pair or connection idles out on its link: 600 s for TCP, 5 min otherwise,
         the link's idles (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:210-213); hosts hold bridge flows as long
         through C5's per-flow IdleTimeout (17.6), raising for them alone connect's NAT idles: TCP 300 s
         (connect/ip.go:510), UDP 60 s (:446) or, in the targetless provider profile, 300 s (:578, :711),
         ICMP 60 s (connect/ip_icmp.go:157); a NAT at its flow caps still evicts an approximately least
         recently active flow (connect/ip.go:11682)
kept     an edit that leaves a pair's link serving it (an advertiser joining, a weight change, another
         link's health) keeps its pin until it idles out
removed  a withdraw, retarget, address or block change, or a link rebuild, leaves the old advertiser or
         link in the entry, draining: it serves its pinned pairs, and every pair while nothing else
         remains, TCP pins for max(drain_seconds, 600 s) and others for max(drain_seconds, 5 min), a
         rebuilt link's until its strict_exp, then leaves
health   a refusal or 3 s connect timeout marks a link down for 30 s; a down link takes no new pairs
         while another advertiser of the entry is up, and keeps its pins
```

- **Links** (Q-BRIDGE-2). One multi client per target, built by `BridgeHost` (17.10): fixed `ProviderSpec{ClientId}`, `FixedWindowSize: 1`, `PostQuantumEncryption` (Required), `OverrideAllowDirect=false` until C3 (D-PROTO-10), `EnableIcmp`, never `DefaultMultiClientSettings`' six-client window; each window client carries the subject's `WindowDelegation` (17.9). Window clients are the subject's children, so a sidecar's expire unrefreshed at §7.4's 7-day `strict_exp`, and links rebuild after 6 days, draining under the pins above. Same-network links run Network mode, share links FriendsAndFamily, carrying private destinations only inside their aliases (17.9). Relayed bytes are debited (§20.6). Links idle-close after 600 s, as long as a TCP pin, survive default-route rebuilds, and send TCP/25 to the local NAT, so bridged TCP/25 is refused. Until C16 only sidecar-owned Required clients are targets (D-BRIDGE-5), so replies are sealed too.
- **Memory.** A window client carries a full client graph (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:217-222), so a device short of its §18.4 budget closes its least recently used idle link; the iOS tunnel runs none until §22.9 measures one ([owner decision 100](#od-100)).
- **Rejects.** A TCP RST or ICMP administratively prohibited (v4 3/13, v6 1/1) enters the tun through a per-source token bucket (20/s, burst 40), since connect writes policy resets unthrottled (connect/ip_smtp_policy.go:847-864).

### 17.6 Provider hook and port mapping

C5 (§4) gives `LocalUserNatSettings` an `EgressHook`, called once per flow before the dial: at the TCP dial (connect/ip.go:5671-5676), the UDP open (:3597-3599) and ICMP egress (connect/ip_icmp.go:786), which every lane uses (connect/ip_provider_reliable_ingress.go:158-191). Replies are rebuilt from the flow (connect/ip.go:4075-4077, :7289-7291), so a map is DNAT with no checksum or return-path rewrite.

```go
// connect (C5, with C13's seals, C15's key and C18's switch); a nil hook keeps today's behavior
type EgressFlow struct {
	Source        TransferPath
	ProvideMode   protocol.ProvideMode
	SourceSubject Id               // C13: the sealed source subject, a consistency check only
	SourceNetwork Id               // C13: the sealed source network, in every mode (D-PROTO-19)
	Principal     *BridgePrincipal // the verified WindowDelegation's subject and network (17.9); nil: none
	                               // (not Peer.Principal, the contract signer's string)
	Sealed        bool             // the source peer had a sealed session (EncryptionEventSealed,
	                               // connect/transfer_encrypt.go:520) when the flow opened
	Protocol      IpProtocol
	From, To      netip.AddrPort
}
type BridgePrincipal struct {
	Subject, Network, ShareId Id // ShareId is zero on a same-network link
	NotAfter                  time.Time
}
type EgressDecision struct {
	Verdict          EgressVerdict  // Pass | Map | Deny (RST or unreachable; never an Incident)
	Target           netip.AddrPort // Map; port 0 keeps the port
	RuleTag          uint64         // names a (subject, rule) pair, so CloseFlows can end a subject's flows
	PolicyGeneration uint64         // the published policy the decision used
	IdleTimeout      time.Duration  // this flow's NAT idle in place of the NAT-wide one; 0 keeps the NAT's
}
type EgressHook interface {
	// once per contract a source presents, in its first flow's sequence before the dial, from the peer's
	// C13 seals and C15 key; connect keeps the answer on that source's flows until the contract ends
	VerifyPrincipal(source TransferPath, peer Peer) *BridgePrincipal
	ResolveEgress(flow *EgressFlow) EgressDecision // inline, non-blocking
	PolicyGeneration() uint64                       // the published generation, one atomic load
	// C18: true hands FriendsAndFamily flows to private destinations to ResolveEgress
	// instead of the public-only rules (connect/ip_security.go:574-576)
	FriendsAndFamilyEgress() bool
}
// RST to the source and close the socket of every flow registered with ruleTag below the published
// generation, dials in progress included
func (self *LocalUserNat) CloseFlows(ruleTag uint64) int
// C18's source half: MultiClientSettings (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:578) gains
// SharePrivateDestinations []netip.Prefix, which egressRelationship's caller (:6704) admits
```

```text
C5's contract (D-BRIDGE-21; TCP, UDP and ICMP)
register  ResolveEgress returns {verdict, target, rule tag, policy generation, idle}; LocalUserNat records
          them on the flow's sequence before it starts the dial (TCP), opens the socket (UDP) or sends
          (ICMP), each under the sequence's context (connect/ip.go:5671, :3597)
publish   a revocation first swaps in the new policy (an atomic pointer swap, generation g+1), then calls
          CloseFlows(rule tag), which cancels every flow registered with that tag at a generation <= g, a flow
          whose dial is in progress included (its sequence context ends)
recheck   a flow whose dial completes re-reads the published generation before it sends the SYN-ACK or
          forwards a first byte; a newer one re-resolves the flow, and a Deny closes it with an RST or
          unreachable; one atomic load per flow, no lock on the packet path
```

`device.BridgeEgressPolicy` implements the hook from the host's verified state (17.8):

```text
Public, or FriendsAndFamily at an sdk provider -> Pass   // today's public-only rules follow
Service                                    -> Deny   // no IP (§6.10.1)
no verified principal (17.9), or its       -> Deny   // D-BRIDGE-17; sdk providers skip it until C16
  subject or share revoked or suspended here
not Sealed                                 -> Deny   // hosts are Required (D-PROTO-6)
FriendsAndFamily at a host (17.9)          -> C18 on and To in an alias A_i of the principal's share ? To = T_i,
                                              then rules 0-3 (3 by grant only) and 6 under the share grant : Deny
0 one of this device's daemon listeners    -> Deny   // D-BRIDGE-19, document or not
1 map(To, protocol, port)                  -> AllowDial(subject, host, port) ? Map(target) : Deny
2 a block address not hosted here          -> Deny   // one hop; never dial another host's address
3 a hosted address                         -> (no document and untagged) or AllowDial(subject, host, port)
                                              ? Map(127.0.0.1:port), never a daemon listener : Deny
4 no ACL document, untagged source         -> Pass   // today's allow-all, disclosed (owner decisions 50, 105, 120)
5 loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified -> Deny
6 a served prefix                          -> AllowRoute(subject, prefix, port) ? Pass or Map(remap) : Deny
7 public unicast                           -> AllowExit(subject, host) ? Pass : Deny
8                                          -> Deny   // LAN without a route rule
subject: the principal's (at an sdk provider before C16, C13's sealed subject); "no document" means a
verified enforcing{nodoc} state (17.8); idle: a Pass or Map of a flow with a principal sets IdleTimeout to
600 s for TCP and 5 min otherwise (17.5), and every other flow keeps its NAT's
```

- **Maps** match the destination as sent: `:5432` → `127.0.0.1:5432` on a hosted address, or `:8000` → `192.168.1.20:8000` ("client:port → ip:port"); ranges map by offset; ICMP echo follows rule 3. A map never targets another client's overlay address, the daemon's own listeners or a §13.7 control panel.
- **Own listeners** (D-BRIDGE-19). Rule 0 matches the daemon's local API, MCP, git, IMAP and submission listeners on loopback and every local address, since they bind all interfaces by default ([owner decision 84](#od-84)); the state lists them (17.8), and the control channel is a socket or pipe, never a port (I-17).
- **No document.** Rules 3-4 apply owner decisions [50](#od-50), [105](#od-105) and [120](#od-120): untagged sources keep today's reach, minus rule 0, the hosted address standing for loopback, and tagged ones get §8.5's implicit rules, so R-BRIDGE-7 holds for tagged agents, and for all once a policy exists; product copy and §2.18 disclose this (I-10).
- **sdk exit NAT** (sdk/device_local.go:6351-6364). Until C16 the sdk installs the policy without the principal and Sealed rows and rules 1-3 and 6, since an Opportunistic provider's sources may be plaintext: Network sources keep the public exit their rules allow and, with a document, lose LAN, loopback and overlay reach.
- **C6a.** 100.64/10 becomes non-public, as IANA lists it (RFC 6598; https://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv4-special-registry/, updated 2025-10-09), so public exits refuse overlay traffic. Providers shadow-count it for a release, then drop it as `SecurityPolicyReasonSharedAddressSpace`, not as an Incident.

### 17.7 Subnets: advertisement, conflicts, HA

- **Advertising.** `ur bridge expose <ranges>` files a `BridgeRoute` delta (17.8). As in Tailscale, approval is separate from access ([R:connect-ip](design-research/connect-ip.md) §2.10): a standing grant in a config head or an I-8 approval (§16.6) activates it; §8 `route` grants decide who uses it.
- **Overlap** (D-BRIDGE-8). The longest prefix wins. An identical prefix is an HA replica (same `site_id`) or a remap, an exposed prefix from the block that the advertiser maps back keeping host bits.
- **Sender conflicts.** The sdk drops and reports exposed subnet-route prefixes overlapping `connect.LocalIpv4Networks()` (connect/tun.go:490-531), so the local LAN wins until a remap or block change; where it returns nil, only 17.4's carve keeps the physical path's /32s. The overlay block follows that carve rule instead. The block and approved prefixes join `RandomLocalIpv4`'s avoid list.
- **HA.** When no link to an advertiser of the most specific prefix can carry a packet (17.5), the router answers unreachable, never falling back to a broader prefix or the default route, which could reach another network reusing the addresses.

### 17.8 Rules in the config repo, delivery, engine, disposition

```text
statement (sidecar/protocol/bridge/bridge.proto; §6.9 Signed,             signer; carried in
  purpose bridge, SignedType 0x1901-0x1907 in row order; a delta
  begins with auth.proto's StatementHeader, §7.9; §4.4)
BridgeBlock{ipv4_prefix, previous_prefix, drain_until}                    an admin; a head (owner decisions 28, 132)
BridgeAddress{sidecar_id, ipv4}                                           the sidecar or an admin; a delta
BridgeRoute{route_id, advertiser, prefixes, exposed_prefix, site_id,      the advertiser; a delta, active once
            weight, kind subnet|exit, drain_seconds, approval}              approved (17.7)
BridgeMap{map_id, host, match_prefix, protocol, ports, target,            the host; a delta, active once
          target_port, expires, drain_seconds, approval}                    approved (17.7)
BridgeEgress{subject, mode auto|exits|none, exit sidecar_ids or tag_id}   an admin, owner or sponsor; a delta
BridgeAlias{share_id, target_index, alias_prefix, host sidecar_id}        the accepting sidecar; a delta (17.9)
BridgeWithdraw{rule_id, reset|drain}                                      the rule's signer or an admin; ids only
approval  none under a standing grant (17.7), or the I-8 decisions and this use's CanonicalAction (§16.8),
          which readers verify as §8.8 does a GrantActivate's, the signer being every decision's requester
rule id   route_id or map_id: under a decision, SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/bridge-rule" || effect_key),
          the use's §16.6 ledger key, which readers recompute, so a retry or restart files one id; under a
          standing grant, 32 random bytes; a filing of a held id may change only weight, site_id and
          drain_seconds and activates nothing; readers refuse an id a BridgeWithdraw named and a decision's
          ids past its uses (§7.9); a fold keeps a withdrawn id, with its approval_id, until its decision's
          not_after
```

- **Placement** ([owner decision 5](#od-5)). Admin-signed heads carry the block, standing rules and 17.9's `BridgeShareSigner` files; sidecars file statements about themselves, and owners or sponsors about their subjects, as deltas entering §7.9's authorization log, verified at their position until a writer folds them in. Rule bodies are sealed to the config's current key generation (§10), so §8.12's invariant and D-TRUST-10's witness stop can delay them; a bodiless `BridgeWithdraw` never waits. Only ids show (kind, signer, subject, rule id, expiry and, for an approved route, the advertiser and the `route` rules it serves), which readers check. Gates see only §8's reach rules between sidecar ids and `BridgeRows`' egress modes (§8.10), never prefixes, addresses, ports, maps or aliases (§2.8, api-12).
- **Engine.** The sidecar role (`bridge_*.go`, §5) reads the config ([owner decision 6](#od-6)), verifies statements against §7.9's admissions and §8's grants within §8.9's latency targets, and compiles a `BridgeState` off the packet path; `device.Bridge` (17.10) applies it and later verified log entries, manages links, and swaps table and hook atomically. Before its first verified state it is pending and denies every private destination and exit; it persists its last verified state and never lowers it on unsigned input:

```text
states (D-BRIDGE-18), per network; §18.6's device role runs the same machine as its posture
legacy                no sidecar role has enrolled for the network on this device: no hook, today's behavior
pending               an anchor and no verified state: Network-source flows to loopback, LAN, link-local,
                      overlay and served prefixes, and every exit, are denied; the block deny stands; maps and
                      hosted addresses refuse
enforcing{doc}        a verified state whose rows have has_document = true: 17.6's rules
enforcing{nodoc}      a verified state with has_document = false: owner decisions 50, 105 and 120's allow-all
persist               the anchor, the newest verified AuthPin, the signed base header and rows, the entries
                      since, the latch document_seen_at (the newest pin with has_document = true) and each
                      served share's newest verified ShareCert (17.9); on restart they re-verify offline
                      against the anchor and the pinned ShareKeys, and the state applies before the first
                      packet
legacy -> pending     the sidecar role enrolls and sends Pending{network_id, genesis_sha256}
pending -> enforcing  the first state verified against the anchor
doc -> nodoc          only a verified base above document_seen_at whose rows say has_document = false
any -> legacy         only this sidecar's own sign-out (its SidecarRevoke), which wipes the stored state
never                 an unsigned has_document, a projection that does not chain, or a lower pin changes the
                      state; one that fails to verify leaves it and alarms
```

- **Device roles** ([owner decision 87](#od-87)). A keyless device role gets `BridgeState` and `Pending` from its sidecar role (§18.6), its `Names` feeding C14's zone (§12.9), and between states applies the log's `SidecarRevoke`, `MemberRevoke`, `Suspend`, `Unsuspend`, `GrantRevoke` and `BridgeWithdraw` entries, verified against the anchor (§7.9) with `protocol/bridge`'s types alone, so revocations apply while the sidecar role sleeps.
- **Limits.** None per network ([owner decision 66](#od-66)); the block bounds addresses at 64,770.

```proto
message BridgeRows {                      // bridge.proto; acl.proto's AclRows.bridge (§8)
  repeated BridgeEgressRow egress = 1;    // subject (sidecar_id or keyed atom), mode; ids only
}
```

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/bridge/bridge.proto (§4.4; std and protobuf only), importing auth.proto (§7.9) and
// signed.proto (§6.9): a sidecar role's compiled view for its device role (§18.6), in process or as
// DeviceLocalRpc.SetBridgeState; auth only rises, and verified entries apply on top
message BridgeState {
  AuthPin auth = 1;                        // auth.proto's (n, A_n), the newest verified state; ApplyDeltas chains from it
  bytes genesis_sha256 = 2;                // the anchor (§7.9)
  bool has_document = 3;                   // that state's rows: enforcing{doc} or enforcing{nodoc}
  bytes rules = 4;                         // this device's compiled block, routes, maps and hook rules
  map<string, fixed32> names = 5;          // client name -> overlay IPv4 (§7.7, 17.4), versioned with rules
  repeated string name_zones = 6;          // <net>.<root>, and the alias zone where one is chosen (§12.9)
  repeated BridgeIdentity identities = 7;  // the subjects its rules let reach this host (17.9), ~64 B each
  repeated BridgeShareKey share_keys = 8;  // the shares this host serves (17.9)
  repeated string daemon_listeners = 9;    // rule 0 (17.6): the daemon's listener binds, host:port
}
message BridgeIdentity { bytes sidecar_id = 1; bytes identity_public_key = 2; uint64 admitted_at = 3;
                         bool revoked = 4; bool suspended = 5; }
message BridgeShareKey { bytes share_id = 1; bytes public_key = 2; }   // the pinned ShareKey, Ed25519
message Pending { bytes network_id = 1; bytes genesis_sha256 = 2; }  // legacy -> pending
```

**Disposition** (D-BRIDGE-7):

| Change | Sender | Provider |
|---|---|---|
| Revocation (revoked or expired grant, the subject's `SidecarRevoke` or suspension, rejected route, `--reset`) | Reset at once: pins to a revoked advertiser drop, and an entry left with no advertiser answers its packets with an RST or prohibited reply for 600 s, then leaves | `CloseFlows` after the policy swap, dials in progress included (17.6) |
| Edit (withdraw, retarget, advertiser or health change, new address or block) | Drain under 17.5's pins: while the table has room no live pair leaves a link that still serves it, and a removed advertiser or old address drains as 17.5's `removed` row sets (`drain_seconds` 300 s by default, 3,600 s at most); new pairs take the new rule, as do new TCP connections of pairs pinned to a draining link, but new UDP and ICMP pairs follow the pre-change link through 17.5's window; a full table refuses nothing | A removed route or old address stays compiled, draining and admitting flows, for max(`drain_seconds`, 600 s), and a retargeted map keeps only the flows it opened; then the engine drops it, swaps the policy and runs `CloseFlows` on its tags |

### 17.9 ACL, identity, egress, cross-network shares (C18)

- **Permissions** (§8.4): `route` on `ip:<cidr>`, `dial` on the subject for hosted addresses and maps, `autogroup:internet` via the exit, and per forward a requested grant (port, `expires`, 1 h by default; [owner decision 74](#od-74)). §8's contract gate checks pairs, and the hook each flow by the principal a verified `WindowDelegation` names, checked against C13's seal (D-PROTO-19). `forward`, `expose`, `egress` and `invite` are outward actions under `Sidecar.Authorize` (§5, I-8) at every entry point, whose deltas carry the approval (§8.6), in a tainted run only by I-9's evidence ([owner decision 142](#od-142)). Own-resource filings sign from any mode, MCP included (§5.8, §16.6): `bridge_forward` files a `GrantActivate` from its decision and returns its grant_id; `bridge_expose` a `BridgeRoute` or `BridgeMap` under a standing grant or its decision, a map preceded by this host's own `BridgeAddress` where the log holds none for it (17.4), and returns 17.8's rule id; `bridge_close(grant_id | rule_id)` a `GrantRevoke` of a forward's grant whose subject it is, or a `BridgeWithdraw` of this sidecar's own rule; `block`, `egress`, `invite` and `accept-invite` sign only for a `ur` command confirmed on /dev/tty or in an app's UI.
- **Principals** (D-BRIDGE-17). C13's seal is the operator's statement, so a host admits a native flow only from a window client a customer key vouches for:

```proto
// bridge.proto; §6.9 Signed, purpose window-delegation, SignedType 0x1908; by the subject's
// identity key or, on a share link, the ShareSigner its share_cert names (share signers, below)
message WindowDelegation {
  bytes network_id = 1;                // the source network
  bytes subject_sidecar_id = 2;
  bytes window_client_id = 3;
  bytes window_client_public_key = 4;  // the window client's ClientKey public key
  bytes target_sidecar_id = 5;         // the host this link reaches
  int64 not_after_ms = 6;              // at most the window client's strict_exp (§7.4)
  bytes share_id = 7;                  // set for a cross-network share
  bytes share_cert = 8;                // with share_id: the Signed ShareCert below
}
message ShareCert {                    // §6.9 Signed, purpose window-delegation, SignedType 0x1909, by the ShareKey
  bytes share_id = 1;
  uint64 config_generation = 2;        // g, the source network's config generation (§10.5)
  bytes signer_public_key = 3;         // g's ShareSigner, Ed25519
  int64 not_after_ms = 4;              // at most 7 days after signing
}
message BridgeShareSigner {            // Y's config file per accepted share; sidecar roles only, not in BridgeState
  bytes share_id = 1;
  uint64 config_generation = 2;        // g, as in share_cert
  bytes signer_seed = 3;               // g's ShareSigner: a fresh 32-byte Ed25519 seed
  bytes share_cert = 4;                // its Signed ShareCert
}
```

```text
sign     BridgeHost gets one per window client it builds from the subject's sidecar role (over §18.6's
         channel when the builder is a keyless device role), signed by its identity key or, on a share
         link, by a ShareSigner (share signers, below), and passes it in CreateContract; the contract signer
         copies it unchanged into StoredContract (C13)
verify   once per contract, before the first flow's dial: the signature, by the subject's identity key
         pinned through its SidecarAdmit and neither revoked nor suspended at this state, or by a ShareSigner
         that share signers admit; window_client_id = the contract's source; window_client_public_key = the
         sealed session's peer key (C15); target_sidecar_id = this host; not_after_ms ahead; network_id =
         C13's sealed network; C13's sealed subject resolves through §5's binding log to subject_sidecar_id,
         else deny and alarm
use      the principal {subject, network, share, not_after} rides that source's flows; the hook rechecks the
         subject, or a share's grant, against the state per flow (one lookup), so a SidecarRevoke, Suspend
         or share revocation denies it and CloseFlows ends its flows, and not_after_ms lapses it; a source
         without one is never passed by rule 4
target   the sender's link admits a contract only if destination_client_public_key is the target's current
         SidecarIdentityBinding client key, verified against its pinned identity key
         (GET /sidecar/identity/<sidecar_id>, cached per link)
cost     ~200 B (~350 B with a ShareCert) and one Ed25519 verification (~50 µs) per contract per link, and
         one per new ShareCert
```

- **Egress spec.** A subject's default route goes to an approved exit, or nowhere (app devices: `NetworkPeer` with `PostQuantumEncryption`, v1, §18); §8.10's gate refuses Public contracts under `exits` or `none`.
- **Shares** ([owner decision 86](#od-86)). X's `ur bridge invite` files §8.11's admin-approved share (a `route` or `dial` grant to `network:Y`) with a 256-bit code and seals its targets T_i (index, host `sidecar_id`, ports or prefix) under K = HKDF-SHA256(code, "urnetwork-sidecar-v1/bridge-share"), which the server, holding the code's hash, cannot derive. Y's `accept-invite`, approved by a Y admin, runs the preflight below, aliases each target with an equal-length A_i in Y's block (`BridgeAlias` deltas) and returns the aliases sealed under K. Y routes A_i over a share link to T_i's host (resolved through §5's binding log), whose hook maps A_i to T_i, keeping host bits. Y's approving admin device also generates the share's Ed25519 ShareKey, which certifies a ShareSigner per generation of Y's config (share signers, below); its public key, sealed under K, enters X's share grant at X's activating approval, and X's host verifies the `WindowDelegation`s those signers sign, while Y's routers enforce Y's grants: §8.11's intersection is these two points.

```text
preflight  (D-BRIDGE-20) on Y's approving device before any BridgeAlias, since the server sees no prefix
size       aliases live in the upper /17 (17.4), so a target wider than /17 is refused_too_large
space      each A_i is a free aligned block of its target's length in the upper /17, overlapping no alias
           and no host /32 spilled there, a /32 alias avoiding x.y.z.0 and x.y.z.255; none free:
           refused_no_space, the shortfall sealed under K
allocate   first fit from the upper /17's bottom, aligned, while spilled hosts take its top; overlapping /24
           requests get disjoint blocks; a draining alias keeps its block until its drain ends
status     network_bridge_share.accept_status: active | refused_too_large | refused_no_space
```

```text
X: targets T_i, sealed under K --> server (§8.11 share; network_bridge_share) <-- Y: aliases A_i, ShareKey, sealed under K
X's host hook: FriendsAndFamily from Y, To in A_i -> T_i      Y's routers: A_i -> share link to T_i's host
```

```text
share signers (D-BRIDGE-17)
ShareKey     an owner-bound `secret` of Y's approving admin (§11.12), as §13.8 keeps an account key, never in
             the config, so it reaches only §8.5's readers of that secret; it signs only ShareCerts
ShareSigner  at accept, and whenever a ShareKey holder that writes the config sees a newer generation g of
             Y's config (§10.5), the holder replaces the share's BridgeShareSigner {share_id, g, a fresh seed,
             its ShareCert} in a config head at g, unless it already names g, and re-certifies g when the cert
             has under 3 days left, unprompted as §7.9's folds are; §10.6's write gate takes a write at g only
             while g covers the config's holders_shrunk_at, so a sidecar that has stopped reading Y's config
             gets no later signer or cert; a ShareSigner signs only share-link WindowDelegations
file         a BridgeShareSigner is a config file, not a statement, with no Signed or SignedType of its own:
             only config writers' heads change it, as with K_sock (§8.8), and their signatures cover it; a writer
             without the ShareKey cannot certify, so X refuses its signer; a Y sidecar signs with one only
             while its share_id, g and seed's public key match its cert
keys         the ShareKey and ShareSigners, Ed25519, sign §6.9 Signeds in the sidecar role's bridge_*.go,
             beside §5.4's identity-key Sign: signer_id = share_id, key_id = SHA-256 of the signing public key;
             verifiers require signer_id = the body's share_id and resolve key_id, a ShareCert's to the
             share's pinned BridgeShareKey and a share delegation's to its ShareCert's signer_public_key
sign         a Y subject signs with the share's current BridgeShareSigner while its cert is unexpired; when
             that file changes, its sidecar role has BridgeHost re-sign each share link's delegations (§18.6's
             ResignShares for a keyless builder), which their next contracts carry
admit        X's host requires the ShareCert to verify under the pinned ShareKey with the delegation's
             share_id, not_after_ms ahead and at most 7 days away (§8.6's 60 s skew), and g at least the
             share's newest verified generation, which it raises and keeps in 17.8's persisted state, then the
             delegation under signer_public_key; the principal's not_after is the earlier not_after_ms
bound        a sidecar Y removed is admitted on new contracts until a later generation's ShareCert reaches the
             host in any Y delegation, at most 7 days after its removal reaches evs, and those it opened run
             to their end (at most 60 min, server/model/subscription_contract_expiration.go:14); with no
             renewal for 7 days the share lapses for everyone; a reaped Delegation-admitted agent signs while
             it reads Y's config (§10.5); a removed holder device, or a holder member leaving the AdminSet, can
             certify until X revokes the share, so Y's devices raise a SidecarEvent naming it, and X re-invites
```

- **Isolation.** Only sidecar-owned Required hosts holding a share grant turn `FriendsAndFamilyEgress()` on; sdk providers never do. The principal's verified share and network, never an address, select the aliases, which resolve only to that share's targets through maps, dialable hosted addresses and served prefixes: never rule 4, rule 0's listeners, unmapped loopback, another host's address or an exit ([owner decision 11](#od-11)). NAT state is per source path and 5-tuple (connect/ip.go:2072-2098), so foreign flows share no entry with local ones; replies carry the alias back unrewritten. Foreign flows are shed first under NAT pressure. Reach events name the source network (§16).

### 17.10 Placement, sdk seams, apps, hosts

| Repo | Change |
|---|---|
| connect (X9) | §4.6's C5, C6a, C13 and C14 (M4), C15's key (M1), C16 before app devices host, C18 for shares (M6); not C6b, since providers terminate flows without a tun |
| sidecar | Root `bridge_*.go` (the sidecar role): statements, the compiler that builds `BridgeState`, forwards. `device/` (`device.Bridge`, D-SDK-20): table, pins, links, `BridgeEgressPolicy`, principals, aliases, routes, the per-link resolver and zone, and 17.8's states, importing connect and `protocol/bridge` only. `cli/` wires `device.Bridge` to the root's state producer for `ur tun` and `ur bridge` and holds `ur tun`'s OS tun (`golang.zx2c4.com/wireguard/tun`, MIT) and the userspace stack, out of every sdk binding (Q-SDK-5) |
| sdk | Both insertion points and the exit-NAT hook through §18.6's `deviceBridge`; `DeviceLocal` implements `BridgeHost`; route export (§18) |
| server | No rule tables; `network_bridge_share`; gates read `BridgeRows` |
| apps | Out of scope (owner rule 6): applying exported routes, a chosen block included, is §18's app work |

```go
// device (sidecar/device); implemented by sdk DeviceLocal and the CLI host, which own the client generators
type BridgeHost interface {
	// one link per target (Q-BRIDGE-2); shareAliases is nil for a same-network link (ProvideMode_Network),
	// and for a share link (FriendsAndFamily) lists the aliases C18's source half may carry; sign returns
	// the Signed WindowDelegation for each window client the link builds, not_after_ms at most notAfter, the
	// client's strict_exp (§7.4), and on a share link the host calls it again for each live one when the
	// sidecar role signals a new BridgeShareSigner (§18.6's ResignShares, or in process), for its later
	// contracts (17.9)
	NewBridgeLink(ctx context.Context, target connect.Id, subject connect.Id, shareAliases []netip.Prefix,
		sign func(windowClientId connect.Id, windowClientPublicKey []byte, notAfter time.Time) ([]byte, error),
	) (connect.UserNatClient, error)
}
```

**Device abstractions (PLAN.md:31).** `device.Bridge` satisfies §18.6's `deviceBridge`, `BridgeEgressPolicy` being its hook; on iOS and desktop apps the keyless device role runs it ([owner decision 87](#od-87)), and on Linux and WSL2 the daemon does, through `cli/`.

### 17.11 cli/UI.md mapping

| Command or UI note | Meaning (v0 unless noted) |
|---|---|
| `ur tun` | OS tun `ur-<instance>` with the block and granted prefixes; the default route only under `exits`; yields to an app bridge |
| `ur tun ip [<ip>\|auto]`; "client assign local ip" | Show or claim the address |
| `ur bridge`; "show all ips", "show all hostname:port" | Run the bridge; list addresses, private names, rules, forwards |
| `ur bridge expose <ranges>`; "client forward ip subnet" | Advertise subnets (a route) |
| `ur bridge expose :<port>[=<ip>:<port>]` (added); "client:port → ip:port" | Map this client's port |
| `ur bridge forward client:port[:local ip]:local port`; "client:port → client:port" | Listen on all interfaces unless `--listen` narrows it ([owner decision 84](#od-84)); dial over the userspace stack under a §8 grant |
| `ur bridge egress auto\|<exit>\|tag:<t>\|none` (added); "client egress spec" | The default route |
| `ur bridge block [cycle\|<cidr>]` (added; admins) | Re-roll or choose the block (17.4; owner decisions [28](#od-28), [132](#od-132)) |
| `ur bridge invite`, `accept-invite` | Cross-network port and subnet shares (17.9), v1 |

Without an active grant, these commands print the approval prompt and wait (§16.6); `forward` warns that it serves every host reaching the listener. `ur bridge public-tls` is §13's.

### 17.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routing inside the multi client (a `RouteOverride`) | One place | After the mux; per-packet evaluation; reaches the IpAssoc cluster (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:7384-7395) | Rejected |
| Per-packet rewrite: in `clientReceiveAdmitted`, or of aliases at the sender | Any protocol; no alias table at hosts | Port-aware rewrite both ways, a copy per packet (connect/ip.go:10316-10335) | Rejected: the hook maps once per flow |
| Cross-network forwards over §9 streams | No foreign packets in provider NATs | No subnet invites; a second data plane | Not chosen ([owner decision 86](#od-86)) |
| App devices as targets now (Opportunistic) | Phones and app desktops host at once | Replies can cross relays in plaintext (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:477-483) | Ruled out by the owner directive until C16 |
| Trust C13's sealed subject at hosts | No signature per contract | The platform holds the HMAC key: a breached server mints any subject | Rejected (D-BRIDGE-17) |
| One ShareKey every Y reader holds, rotated on removals and re-pinned at X from Y's update | No admin key or renewal | A removed sidecar holds the old key, so it signs a successor of its own, which the operator can deliver first | Rejected: an admin's ShareKey certifies per-generation signers (17.9) |
| Bootstrap from the unverified projection's `has_document` | Opens at once after a restart | A forged `has_document = false` reopens a LAN | Rejected (D-BRIDGE-18) |
| A pin per 5-tuple flow, a full table refusing; or the pre-edit table for TCP non-SYN segments through a drain | Exact per flow; no pair state | 1,024 slots holding UDP 5 min cap a phone near 3.4 new flows/s; a new connection's SYN and later segments split across links, and a provider drops a non-SYN segment it has no flow for (connect/ip.go:4659-4687) | Rejected: pair pins where an entry offers a choice (17.5) |

### 17.13 Decisions proposed

**D-BRIDGE-1 (proposed).** The bridge reuses connect's client-to-provider NAT path: sender routing, a per-flow provider decision, one hop. *Why:* PLAN.md:115-117; targets need no tun or root.

**D-BRIDGE-2 (proposed).** The router sits before the mux behind `deviceBridge` (17.5); the CLI shares it. *Why:* all device egress passes there.

**D-BRIDGE-3 (proposed).** Fail closed: the block is a deny backstop; providers serve only sealed flows, never dial another host's address and, with an ACL document, open private destinations only by rule. *Why:* R-BRIDGE-10, R-BRIDGE-12.

**D-BRIDGE-4 (proposed).** The C5 hook applies 17.6's order, relying on C6a, C13, C15 and, for shares, C18 (17.10). *Why:* once per flow; a nil hook changes nothing.

**D-BRIDGE-5 (proposed).** Links run Required to a fixed target with one window client, relay-only until C3, never count-capped; targets are sidecar-owned until C16. *Why:* D-PROTO-6, D-PROTO-10; [owner decision 66](#od-66).

**D-BRIDGE-6 (proposed).** Bridge rules are signed config-repo statements, sidecars' own as sealed deltas in the authorization log; gates see only reach rules and `BridgeRows`. *Why:* [owner decision 5](#od-5); no prefixes, addresses or ports reach the server (I-4).

**D-BRIDGE-7 (proposed).** Revocations reset both ends at once. Edits move no live pair off a link that still serves it while the pin table has room, and drain a removed advertiser or address for max(`drain_seconds`, 600 s) for TCP and max(`drain_seconds`, 5 min) otherwise. New pairs take the new rule, as do new TCP connections of pairs pinned to a draining link, but for 5 min after an entry first offers a choice new UDP and ICMP pairs, which cannot be told from live ones, follow the pre-change link. Pins key on the rendezvous pair, exist only where an entry offers a choice, and a full table leaves a pair unpinned, refusing nothing (17.5). *Why:* revocation is a security event; an edit should not break live TCP; [owner decision 66](#od-66) allows overload protection, not count caps.

**D-BRIDGE-8 (proposed).** An identical advertisement is an approved HA replica or remap; nesting is allowed; other overlaps are refused. *Why:* LAN prefixes repeat across sites.

**D-BRIDGE-9 (proposed).** HA is active-active by weighted rendezvous over healthy advertisers; a down mark removes a link from the hash only while another advertiser is up, and moves no pin. *Why:* NAT keeps flows symmetric; nothing waits on the server; one timed-out connect must not cut a route's live flows.

**D-BRIDGE-10 (proposed).** A forward listens on 0.0.0.0/:: unless `--listen` narrows it, under a requested grant, disclosed as LAN-exposed. *Why:* [owner decision 84](#od-84); D-TRUST-8.

**D-BRIDGE-11 (proposed).** Hosted devices (sdk/device_local.go:893-910), URnetwork-run WireGuard proxy clients, the extension worker and isolated clients (server/connect/resident.go:4790-4793) never route, host or serve. *Why:* I-10; js has no raw sockets.

**D-BRIDGE-12 (proposed).** The sdk exports hosted addresses, granted prefixes, aliases and an RFC 1918 block, minus every local /32 the physical path needs (interfaces, gateways, system resolvers), and per-peer /32s instead of the block while those are unknown, for apps to capture. *Why:* apps exclude RFC 1918, Apple's overlap semantics are undocumented ([R:connect-ip](design-research/connect-ip.md) §2.6), and a captured carrier resolver black-holes DNS.

**D-BRIDGE-13 (proposed).** 17.9's egress spec sets a subject's default route, enforced at §8.10's gate. *Why:* R-BRIDGE-7 must survive a compromised agent sidecar.

**D-BRIDGE-14 (proposed).** C18 reaches the hook only on sidecar-owned Required hosts holding a share grant, which map foreign flows by the principal's verified share and network to that share's targets only (17.9). *Why:* [owner decision 86](#od-86); isolation must not rest on addresses.

**D-BRIDGE-15 (proposed).** The accepting network aliases shared hosts and prefixes in its own block; both tables travel sealed under the invite code's key. *Why:* blocks and LANs repeat across networks; the server learns no addresses.

**D-BRIDGE-16 (proposed).** `ur bridge block` refuses a block outside 100.64/10 and RFC 1918, readers keep the previous block and alarm on a head carrying one, and renumbering keeps host bits; an overlap no carve resolves (17.4) is fixed by cycling, readers keeping the previous block until a head carries a valid one. *Why:* [owner decision 132](#od-132); a CLI check binds no other signing tool.

**D-BRIDGE-17 (proposed).** A host admits a native IP flow only from a window client whose customer-signed `WindowDelegation` it verified against the subject's pinned identity key or, on a share link, a ShareSigner of the source network's newest certified config generation, which the share's pinned ShareKey, kept in the approving admin's `secret`, certifies for at most 7 days; C13's seal serves only as a consistency check (17.9). *Why:* C13's seal is the operator's statement, and a sidecar its network removes must stop signing within a bound, which no key every reader keeps allows.

**D-BRIDGE-18 (proposed).** Only a verified state opens a private destination: the engine and the device role run 17.8's legacy, pending and enforcing states, persisted, never lowered by unsigned input (§18.6). *Why:* a restart plus a forged `has_document = false` must not reopen a LAN.

**D-BRIDGE-19 (proposed).** A provider never dials its own daemon listeners, document or not (17.6's rule 0). *Why:* [owner decision 120](#od-120) opens LAN and loopback destinations, not the sidecar's own control and content plane.

**D-BRIDGE-20 (proposed).** Hosts draw from the lower /17 and aliases fill the upper /17 first-fit (17.4), so a share is refused, before any flow and with its reason in `accept_status`, only when it is wider than /17 or the upper /17 has no aligned room for it (17.9). *Why:* a /16 cannot alias a /8 or itself, and random host /32s across the whole block leave few free aligned blocks (about 5 free /24s among 1,000 hosts).

**D-BRIDGE-21 (proposed).** A revocation swaps the provider's policy before `CloseFlows`, and a flow registers its rule and policy generation before its dial and re-checks it before its first byte (17.6). *Why:* a dial can outlast the reset that should have ended it.

### 17.14 Open questions

**Q-BRIDGE-1.** [X18] Which range carries overlay addresses? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 28](#od-28)):** IPv4 only, a random /16 per network from 100.64.0.0/10 after C6a, which admins may cycle or replace (17.4). *Residual:* none; Q-BRIDGE-7 bounds the choice.

**Q-BRIDGE-2.** How do links reach targets? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (c). One `BridgeHost` link per target, as a fixed `ProviderSpec{ClientId}` multi client with window size 1 (`FixedWindowSize: 1`), `PostQuantumEncryption` Required, `OverrideAllowDirect=false` until C3, and `EnableIcmp`; not `DefaultMultiClientSettings`, whose six-client quality window (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:217-234) is the wrong default and six times the memory. Each window client carries the subject's customer-signed `WindowDelegation` into C13's seal, which the provider verifies (D-BRIDGE-17). Option (b), a link on the subject's own client, is adopted only where §22.9 measures per-target memory over §18.4's iOS budget and the new framing passes fragment, reply-filter and lifecycle tests; the iOS tunnel is the first candidate and runs no link until measured ([owner decision 100](#od-100)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-3.** Should upgraded providers refuse private destinations to Network sources unless a rule allows them? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 50](#od-50)):** only with an ACL document; without one, untagged sidecars keep today's reach (17.6 rules 3-4; [owner decision 105](#od-105)), which [owner decision 120](#od-120) keeps and discloses (Q-TRUST-7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-4.** Do overlay addresses get private names? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 85](#od-85)):** yes, in v0: `<client-name>.<net>.<root>` from the config repo, answered on the device by C14 or `ur tun`'s resolver, never forwarded or published (§12.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-5.** Which bind do forwards and local listeners use? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 84](#od-84)):** 0.0.0.0/:: unless `--listen` narrows it (cli/UI.md:11), forwards disclosed as LAN-exposed (D-TRUST-8). **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 130](#od-130)):** off loopback, git over http, IMAP and SMTP submission serve only TLS, git also ssh, and plaintext stays on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (I-17); port forwards, which carry the user's own protocol, are unaffected. *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-6.** Cross-cutting (§8, §9). Which data plane carries forwards and invites? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 86](#od-86)):** the IP path for all, cross-network included, with C18 (17.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-7.** Cross-cutting (§18). May a chosen block lie outside 100.64/10 and RFC 1918? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 132](#od-132)):** (b), no: only 100.64.0.0/10, 10/8, 172.16/12 or 192.168/16, narrowing [owner decision 28](#od-28)'s "any /16" (D-BRIDGE-16). Public exits refuse RFC 1918 today (connect/ip_security.go:897) and 100.64/10 after C6a, so overlay traffic never reaches the internet; any /16, or adding 198.18.0.0/15, was not chosen. *Residual:* none.

### 17.15 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:117** ("from same network"): [owner decision 86](#od-86) extends maps to cross-network shares (Q-BRIDGE-6).
- **PLAN.md:353 with :359.** Relayed bridge bytes count ([owner decision 10](#od-10)); P2P bytes after C3 do not (§20, Q-QUOTA-6).
- **PLAN.md:31.** `device.Bridge`, not the whole `Sidecar`, implements the device abstractions (17.10; Q-SDK-2).
- **cli/UI.md, not PLAN.md:** the added `expose :<port>`, `egress` and `block` forms (17.11).

### 17.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `device.Bridge`, `device.BridgeEgressPolicy`, `device.BridgeHost`, `BridgeStatus`; `protocol/bridge/bridge.proto`'s `BridgeState`, `BridgeIdentity`, `BridgeShareKey`, `Pending`, `BridgeRows`, `WindowDelegation`, `ShareCert`, `BridgeShareSigner` and 17.8's statements; 17.8's states, route export, reach events (§16), the `ur tun` resolver (§12.9).
- **Consumes:** §7.9's config repo, authorization log (`AuthPin`, entries, `StatementHeader`), deltas and `team` hints; §7.4's `strict_exp`; §8 grant chains, `AclEngine`, approvals, suspension, contract gate, shares; §10's generations; §11.12's `secret` kind; §6 `Signed` and §6.11's `SignedType`, Required, §6.10.1; §5 identities, the binding log, `GET /sidecar/identity/<sidecar_id>`, `Sidecar.Authorize`, `SidecarEvent`; §16.6's decisions and `effect_key`; §12.9; §18 `deviceBridge`, device-role channel; §20.6 debits; §4 C5, C6a, C13, C14, C15, C16, C18.
- **Subprotocol messages:** none; rules ride the config repo (§6.11 leaves MessageType 0x19 unused). `Signed` types 0x1901-0x1909 are 17.8's statements, `WindowDelegation` and `ShareCert`; `BridgeShareSigner`, a config file, takes none (17.9).
- **API routes:** statements through §7's `POST /network/config/delta`; shares through §8's `POST /acl/invite` and `POST /acl/accept-invite`, which carry the sealed tables, the accept status included; `GET|PUT /network/bridge/share/<share_id>` (Client, a sidecar of either network: read both tables, or replace its own at a higher version).
- **Tables:** `network_bridge_share` (api): share_id, both network ids, sealed target and alias tables, versions, `accept_status enum{active, refused_too_large, refused_no_space}`; kept until revoked.
- **Services and config:** no new service and no `sidecar_abuse:` caps; sdk flag `EnableBridge`; `ur tun` needs CAP_NET_ADMIN or root.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §7.9 carries 17.8's statements as log entries, its type rule bounding a decision's bridge rules by 17.8's rule ids; §16.6's step 5 has a bridge component whose Lookup finds that id in the authorization log, AU1 counts those rules, `bridge_expose` returns the id, and `bridge_close` takes it or a forward's grant_id (§16.5); a device role parses only `protocol/bridge`'s auth.proto (§7.9: `AuthPin`, `AuthEntry`, `ProjectionHeader`, `StatementHeader`, `Genesis`, `SidecarRevoke`, `MemberRevoke`, and §8.8's `Suspend`, `Unsuspend` and `GrantRevoke`) and signed.proto (§6.9: `Signed`, `WebAuthnEvidence`, `SignedType`), which `config.proto` and `acl.proto` import (§4.4); §5.8 and §16.6 sign 17.9's own-resource filings, a host's own `BridgeAddress` among them, from any mode, and other bridge statements only for a /dev/tty-confirmed `ur` command or in an app's UI; §18.6's channel carries `BridgeState` and `Pending`, has the sidecar role sign a keyless device role's delegations by `SignWindowDelegation` (with the identity key, or a share's ShareSigner and its ShareCert) and, by `ResignShares`, have it re-sign a share's links when its `BridgeShareSigner` changes, persists 17.8's states as the device role's posture, and takes the physical path's /32s; §2.8 lists `network_bridge_share` with its accept status and C13's delegation with a share's ShareCert, §2.10 17.9's share-signer bound, and §2.6 and §7.9 the ShareKey's custody and the `BridgeShareSigner` seeds every Y config reader, agents included, holds; §6.9's Signers and §5.5's identity-key rule (D-CORE-6) admit 17.9's two share keys; §22 states the dial fence as an invariant (no byte reaches a target after its flow's revocation; D-BRIDGE-21), which FS-56 tests, and tests D-BRIDGE-16 to D-BRIDGE-21, aliases, the no-document rules, the CGNAT carve, private names, MCP's own-resource bridge filings (a host's first map with its `BridgeAddress`) and the refusal of any other (§16.6), a `BridgeAddress` naming another sidecar_id or a second one for an addressed host included, share signers in FS-38's M6-out run with C18 (a ShareSigner-signed delegation passes; a ShareCert below the host's newest verified generation, expired, over 7 days out or not signed by the pinned ShareKey is refused, after a host restart from 17.8's persisted state too; a sidecar Y removed is refused new contracts once a later generation's ShareCert reaches the host, at most 7 days after its removal; with no renewal for 7 days the share lapses), and 17.5's pins: a TCP flow idle 300-600 s keeps its link across a withdraw, a long-lived flow across an advertiser join, and a one-advertiser retarget's live flows through the drain, while a new pair's TCP connection takes the new rule at once and new UDP and ICMP pairs follow the pre-change link for 5 min; a fragmented UDP datagram stays on one link; mobile churn past a full table (§22.9); and §22.9's link cell holds an app-device host's NAT at C5's per-flow idles.

### 17.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Without an ACL document, untagged sidecars reach every provider's LAN and loopback (owner decisions [50](#od-50), [105](#od-105)) | High | High | Accepted and disclosed ([owner decision 120](#od-120); §2.18); never the provider's own daemon listeners (D-BRIDGE-19); every tier may write a document ([owner decision 73](#od-73)) |
| Providers not yet on C5 let Network sources reach everything | High | High | D-ACL-5's legacy rule; only enforcing clients advertise or host |
| Before C16, sdk providers apply rules 4 and 7 to C13's operator-asserted subject | Low | Medium | With a document, private destinations stay denied whatever the subject; D-BRIDGE-17 there from C16 |
| Foreign flows probe or exhaust a host's NAT (C18) | Medium | High | 17.9's isolation; per-source NAT state; foreign-first shedding; §22 tests |
| A sidecar the source network removed keeps signing share delegations that operator-made contracts carry: a ShareSigner until a later ShareCert reaches the host (at most 7 days), a reaped Delegation-admitted agent while it reads that config, a removed ShareKey holder until the share is revoked | Low | Medium | 17.9's per-generation ShareSigners under 7-day ShareCerts; the ShareKey only in the approving admin's `secret`; a `SidecarEvent` on a holder's removal, then a new invite |
| A forward on all interfaces serves the LAN and every local user ([owner decision 84](#od-84)) | High | Medium | Disclosure; `--listen`; grant expiry; the Host check |
| The block clashes with Tailscale, CGNAT or, if chosen in RFC 1918, a LAN | Medium | Medium | Cycling or choosing the block; /32 peer routes and carved interface, gateway and resolver /32s, or per-peer /32s while those are unknown (17.4); the local LAN wins (17.7); §22.9's CGNAT fixture |
| A full pin table leaves pairs unpinned, so an edit can move their live flows | Low | Medium | One pin per pair, only where an entry offers a choice; nothing refused ([owner decision 66](#od-66)); `ur bridge` counts unpinned pairs; §22.9's mobile churn case |
| After an uncovered agent's reap, new bridge deltas wait for a config rotation (§8.12) by a config writer or the agent's admitting device, a wrapped one by rotation alone (§7.10; owner decisions [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144)) | Medium | Medium | No admin needed ([owner decision 128](#od-128)); covered agents' reaps need none (§10.5); withdrawals never wait; `ur bridge` shows the wait |
| A tun's overlay address leaks in WebRTC (libwebrtc's 100.64/10 handling is unverified) | Unknown | Low | A §22 test before `auto` assigns one |
| Links do not fit the iOS tunnel; a keyless sender's new link waits for its sidecar role | High | Medium | No iOS bridge until §22 measures; Q-BRIDGE-2's own-client links; links fail closed meanwhile |

### 17.18 Phasing

- **v0, M4 (same network; Linux and WSL2 first):** C5 with its dial fence, C6a, C13 with `WindowDelegation`s, C14; statements in the config repo and 17.8's states; router, hook (rule 0 included), userspace stack; `ur tun` on Linux; private names via `ur tun`'s resolver and C14's seam, dark on app paths; forwards, expose and egress under I-8 approvals; HA, pins, dispositions, block changes and the CGNAT carve; sidecar-owned hosts; the sdk insertion behind `EnableBridge`. Blocked by §7.9's config repo and authorization log (M2), §8's grant chains and gates, and C13.
- **v0, M8** (with §18's app hosts): Apple platforms, app-device hosts after C16, iOS links after §22.9's measurement, private names on app paths, keyless senders' delegations over §18.6's channel.
- **v1:** cross-network shares through C18, with ShareKeys, per-generation ShareSigners and the preflight, and `ur tun` on macOS and Windows (M6); P2P after C3 (§6).
- **Later:** L3 delivery, multi-hop maps, IPv6 subnet routes.

## 18. SDK, apps, and extension integration

### 18.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns `sdk/sidecar.go` and its binding gates, host services, wakes, the device seam `deviceBridge` and the device role's posture, per-platform placement (with §5, X10), the browser sidecar and its key origin (X14), cloud hosts and their allow-list, and size budgets. §17 owns the bridge engine, §7.9 and §8 admissions and the projection, §5 the gate, pairing and alarms, §16 approvals, §19 the push sender; app UI is out of scope (owner rule 6).

### 18.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-SDK-1 | An sdk `Sidecar` struct exposes the key controls | PLAN.md:28 |
| R-SDK-2 | Apps use it directly; the extension runs it as a background web worker | PLAN.md:28 |
| R-SDK-3 | Device integration (ip addr, port forward) via abstractions the Sidecar implements | PLAN.md:31 |
| R-SDK-4 | Bindings link only the sidecar core, never `mcp/` or `cli/` | PLAN.md:7 |
| R-SDK-5 | gobind types only; exports pass mobileexports, the C ABI and js | x/mobile bind/gen.go:480-512 |
| R-SDK-6 | iOS extension within 52,428,800 B and a 32 MiB Go soft limit | sdk/build/check_apple_size.sh:9; apple/app/extension/TunnelMemoryBounds.swift:139,143 |
| R-SDK-7 | No server holds keys or plaintext | CONVENTIONS §0 |
| R-SDK-8 | Quick burner: "Must log in, runs a new DeviceRemote in browser" | cli/UI.md:160-164 |
| R-SDK-9 | With no connected remote, "start a local device that listens" | cli/UI.md:67 |

| R-SDK-11 | The sdk Api owns the JWT and its refresh | sdk/device_token_manager.go:20-27 |
| R-SDK-12 | Apps approve outward actions, admit devices, act on admission alarms, veto recovery windows | §2 I-4, I-8; owner decisions [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126), [127](#od-127), [149](#od-149) |

### 18.3 What exists today

- **Bindings.** gomobile binds only `github.com/urnetwork/sdk` (sdk/build/Makefile:101, :150, :160), plus an `ios_extension` binding (:155); Android output passes `mobileexports` (:118; sdk/build/cmd/mobileexports/main.go:128-137). The signed extension had 4,690,096 B of headroom on 2026-11-02 (sdk/build/APPLE_EXTENSION_MEMORY_BUDGET.md); sdk.wasm is 74,965,628 B (2026-10-31).
- **Auth.** The Api owns the token, its refresh (sdk/device_token_manager.go:20-27; sdk/api.go:364, :3672) and the network credential (:203-207), which `.auth_state` keeps beside the device client token in a 0600 file (sdk/local_state_auth.go:31-35; sdk/local_state.go:22). A confirmed 401 reaches `AddAuthLogoutEventListener` with its generation, which `IsAuthLogoutCurrent` checks (sdk/api_auth_logout_event.go:11-39), and cause `session_revoked` only for a session the server confirms revoked (sdk/api_auth_logout_cause.go:31).
- **Extension.** Its background script (extension/manifest.config.ts:35-43) keeps a network `by_jwt` in `chrome.storage.local`, written on SSO login, an external `SET_JWT` and the ur.io bridge's `SETUP` and `REFRESH_JWT` (src/background/index.ts:134, :201-206; src/bridge/background.ts:502-508, :560-565); its sdk.wasm serves only the popup (src/utils/sdk-wasm.ts:1-10).
- **connect.** In-band auth exists (connect/transport.go:2556-2600; server/connect/transport.go:1507-1552), but without `CheckOrigin` (:1597-1601) cross-origin browser upgrades fail (gorilla/websocket@v1.5.3/server.go:89-99). Proxies are SOCKS5 only (connect/net.go:333-363). `Client.Send` takes a per-frame ack callback (connect/transfer.go:4228-4235).
- **Apps, hosted devices.** The iOS app has `aps-environment` (apple/app/network/network.entitlements:5-6); no server code sends APNs or FCM. ur.io's hosted DeviceLocal (server/proxy/proxy_device.go:1268) sets `HostedIncompatible` (:1435; sdk/device_local.go:893-910); the server knows it by its `proxy_device_config` row (server/db_migrations.go:2777) or as that client's child (server/model/network_client_retired_hosted.go:2-6).

### 18.4 Roles, placement, identity

The device role is the leaf package `sidecar/device` (D-SDK-20) in `DeviceLocal`'s process: §17's bridge hooks, keyless and without sidecar-subprotocol peers, enforcing what its sidecar role sends (18.6). The sidecar role is the full `sidecar.Sidecar` (§5) on its own Required client: a child in the device client's network (server/model/network_client_model.go:359-379), top-level in any other ([owner decision 23](#od-23)).

| Host | Device role | Sidecar role | Client (X10) | Secrets | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iOS | tunnel, ≤1 MiB growth | app | child | keychain group `network.ur.sidecar` | 32 MiB |
| Android | app process | same | child | AndroidKeyStore; `noBackupFilesDir` | 16 MiB, added |
| Desktop apps | tunnel, `urnetworkd`, service | `ur daemon`; app in remote mode | child after §5.8's pairing | §5.9 | 128 MiB |
| CLI, cloud VM | none | `ur daemon` | top-level, §20.8 (cloud: tagged, ephemeral, by ReaderWraps) | §5.9 | 128 MiB |
| Extension, ur.io pages | none | Worker (18.8) | top-level, declared no-egress (§20.8) | non-extractable WebCrypto key and IndexedDB, in 18.8's key origin (quick burner: memory) | 64 MiB heap above wasm data |

Phones mirror `mailcfg`, `vault/` and `i/` in full and head-read `m/` (§11.13), and keep MLS trees on disk, one loaded at a time (≤2.83 MB at 1,000 leaves; D-KEYS-14). Of §7.9's authorization log, every sidecar, phones, page Workers and agents included, keeps the digests A_k, its newest entries' bytes up to a `HeadCheckProof`'s 64 KiB (bases as headers) and, while it sends `proven`, the proof it verified, so any witness answers §6.4's `HeadCheckProofRequest`; member devices running `ur daemon` (desktop and CLI hosts) also keep every entry from api's retention point, which a site loss resumes from (§19.10). A config writer folds once the unfolded tail spans 1,024 entries or 24 h, at its next start if it was offline (§7.9's fold), so while one runs, kept tails stay within about 2,048 entries and a new device, a page Worker included, re-applies at most about 1,024. Marks: fg, foreground; VPN, Android VPN on; awake, Firefox event page alive; outbox, D-SMTP-18; C4, §4's browser carrier.

| Feature | iOS app | Android | Desktop daemon | Extension: Chrome / Firefox |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| evs, mail read, burner logins | fg | fg, VPN | yes | yes / awake |
| Mail send | fg, outbox | fg, VPN, outbox | yes (§14) | outbox |
| Socket dial | fg | fg, VPN | yes | C4 |
| Listen: mail, sockets, TLS | fg | fg, VPN | yes | no |
| Approvals, admissions, alarms (18.5) | fg | fg | app or `ur approve` (for other sidecars); presence key | alarms only |
| Bridge routes / hosting (§17) | after §22.9 / after C16 | VPN / after C16 | `ur tun` / `ur bridge` | no |

iOS suspends backgrounded apps (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/backgroundtasks); without the VPN, Android 15 caps `dataSync` at 6 h a day [R:sdk-clients](design-research/sdk-clients.md).

### 18.5 `sdk/sidecar.go`

```go
// sdk/sidecar*.go: bound types only; no sidecar-package value crosses.
type SidecarKeyStore interface { // app-implemented, gobind-safe: a host never throws across it (D-SDK-15)
	PutSecret(name string, valueBase64 string) int32 // SidecarKeyStoreOk | SidecarKeyStoreLocked | SidecarKeyStoreFailed
	GetSecret(name string) *SidecarSecret            // never nil
	DeleteSecret(name string) int32                  // Ok (deleted or absent) | Locked | Failed
}
type SidecarSecret struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Status      int32  // SidecarSecretPresent | SidecarSecretAbsent | SidecarSecretLocked | SidecarSecretFailed
	ValueBase64 string // set only when Present
}
type SidecarPresenceSigner interface { // app-implemented: a Secure Enclave or platform FIDO key, per §16.6's profiles; nil: another device approves
	GetAttestation() string                       // public key and attestation, registered per §16.6
	SignWithPresence(messageBase64 string) string // §6 signature after a presence check; "" if refused
}

	Instance, StateDir    string      // StateDir "" on js: IndexedDB
	Components            *StringList // "evs", "mail", "sockets", "bridge", "tls" (§5.4)
	MemoryBudgetByteCount int64
}
```
