| D-REPO-5 | Connect (X9) changes are generic, additive, off by default, wire-compatible, and merged to connect main first. | [§4](#413-decisions-proposed) |
| D-REPO-6 | Consumers get replaces, a lock entry, a release step and a rollout class per service; branches follow §4.8. | [§4](#413-decisions-proposed) |
| D-REPO-7 | License, style and commit hook per §4.9; distribution per §4.10 with offline-signed checksums. | [§4](#413-decisions-proposed) |
| D-REPO-8 | **Withdrawn.** Superseded by [owner decision 117](#od-117): no scrub, archive, filtered clone or path allowlist; the repo keeps its documents and history. | [§4](#413-decisions-proposed) |
| D-REPO-9 | **Withdrawn.** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): no private mirrors; each `sidecar` branch uses its normal remote, merging to `main` each Gn-out. | [§4](#413-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-1 | PLAN.md:14's fields: its own client JWT, a connect client per generation (none under `sidecar_http`), the APIs, its network's root key. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-2 | `NewSidecar` returns a running Sidecar with its constructor components attached; there is no Start. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-3 | Envelopes go to bounded zero-wait component queues; stream bytes go to credit-bounded buffers. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-4 | One client per sidecar, a child of the device client where available, else top-level; agents are labels on it. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-5 | Durable identity is sidecar_id plus identity key, admitted by a config-repo SidecarAdmit from v0, bound by dual-signed bindings. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-6 | The identity key signs every statement; agent subkeys sign only sealed provenance. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-7 | Enrollment uses one-time or scoped credentials only; the daemon declares no egress by default and fails closed without admin_refused. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-8 | The core reimplements sdk's refresh schedule; a refused refresh ends the client generation; only a verified SidecarRevoke revokes. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-9 | One daemon per instance hosts a Sidecar per network behind uid-checked sockets or pipes that return no secrets. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-10 | A random root key per network seals local files, wrapped by the instance unlock key and that network's recovery key. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-11 | Every outward action passes Sidecar.Authorize and runs only under an approved grant or a §16.6 decision labeled by evidence. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-12 | macOS wraps the unlock key in the data protection keychain via purego, from a bundled `ur`. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-13 | Members' devices alarm on unsigned admissions and sign `OwnerConfirm` only via `ur approve` or the app, never MCP. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-14 | Local roots are per network under one instance unlock key, so one network's recovery code opens no other's keys. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-CORE-15 | Only store state `Absent`, with no recorded sidecar_id, creates a root key; a lost item asks before a new identity. | [§5](#512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-1 | One public subprotocol id, 21842, carries §6.5's envelope. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-2 | Envelopes are capped at 4,080 B; larger bodies are chunked. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-3 | Peer RPC follows §6.6; sidecar-to-server calls use HTTPS. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-4 | Streams share one sequence per peer from M5, revisited if p99 shared-sequence stalls exceed 500 ms. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-5 | Push follows §6.8: ControlId hints, a long-poll answering 200 `PollResponse`, and wakes for unacked wake-class hints. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-6 | Sidecar clients run Required, providing Network, plus Service or FriendsAndFamily as §6.10.1 allows, never Public; edge clients are relay-only. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-7 | Statements others act on carry a typed Signed envelope whose signed bytes name the message type. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-8 | Push types are accepted only from ControlId on platform carriers, and nothing else from ControlId. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-9 | Cross-network grants and edge relationships are never minted as ProvideMode Network. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-10 | Sidecar clients never request P2P, staying relay-only until connect change C3 lands and P2P is tested. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-11 | Protobuf package urnetwork.sidecar, protoc-gen-go v1.36.11, and connect.ProtoCodec until a pooled codec is justified. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-12 | Hint writes and triggers follow §6.8, since HSET and XADD emit nothing in production and concurrent writers would lower versions. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-13 | Peer sessions pass §6.4's identity check before streams or RPC ([owner decision 3](#od-3)). | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-14 | Sidecars compare pins by scheduled HeadCheck, any admitted reader witnessing, reconcile, and refuse lower or conflicting values ([owner decision 129](#od-129)). | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-15 | Edges use Service and shares FriendsAndFamily ([owner decision 11](#od-11)); private destinations are reachable only through C18. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-16 | Tunables are §6.6's settings with process-wide caps; no security property is feature-gated. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-17 | HeadCheck compares auth pins, generations, ref heads, shared MLS epochs and vetoes, reconciles, and counts only same-pin peers as witnesses. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-18 | Any two admitted sidecars of a network get a `control` contract carrying only Hello, Ping, HeadCheck and HeadCheckProof. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-19 | C13 seals the server-authenticated subject, source network, contract class and WindowDelegation on every contract; only the dialer's network escrows. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PROTO-20 | §6's codes are frozen enums with 0 UNSPECIFIED, a protocol error; polls return `PollResponse`; partial resets advance nothing. | [§6](#613-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-1 | P0 stage 1, before any sidecar, refuses child and admin-refused tokens on 37 routes, confining `strict_exp` bearers to an allowlist. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-2 | admin_user_id stays immutable under a synthetic owner-of-record. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-3 | Seven roles, signed in the config repo; routes without a role mapping are owner-only. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-4 | Team SSO is OIDC only, with identities keyed (idp_id, sub) to block IdP-asserted and pre-registration takeover. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-5 | Auth keys replace urn_ keys for `ur connect --token`; a pre-approved key's Delegation secrets ride a client-only bundle. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-6 | OAuth clients mint auth keys valid at most 1 h; a CI-held Delegation admits their sidecars. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-7 | ur-cli tokens last 1 h, need code-matched consent, and are DPoP-bound to one command's method, path and body. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-8 | Token exchange trades a client JWT plus ClientKey proof for a 15-minute, single-audience, projection-scoped token, voided by rev/ objects. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-9 | Tags, groups, device names and sponsors live in the config repo, not on the server. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-10 | Removal denies at the server at once; evs refuses writes until a generation covering it is claimed. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-11 | Server audit log network_admin_event: hash-chained, no IPs, kept 400 days, with a webhook. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-12 | Records freeze as Signed statements; k of n for authority, a recovery key counting as one after its vetoable window. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-13 | One rename function; creation reads tombstones; deletion writes one. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-14 | Sidecar-held child and admin-refused tokens expire after 7 days under `strict_exp`, renewing only with the ClientKey proof. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-15 | Edge login issues a 60 s, nonce-bound ID token for one origin, only to members; sessions count only same-origin. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-16 | Consented devices admit their member's devices unless `self_admit` is off, recovery keys too; admins alone add no owner-bound reader. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-17 | One authorization log per network; positions rise, entries chain by hash; HeadCheck compares (n, A_n); unwitnessed writers stop at `witness_bound_hours`. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-18 | The first 1,000 live member devices are config leaves; later ones and agents hold wraps; a change's signer commits it. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-19 | One hash-chained authorization log per network orders bases and statements; its position is the projection version, (n, A_n) the pin. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-20 | Every log statement carries a StatementHeader; off-chain, stale beyond 4,096 positions, expired or repeated statements are refused. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-21 | k-of-n and recovery-signed statements are an AuthorityProposal plus AuthorityCosigns; recovery-signed ones wait 72 h without a RecoveryVeto. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-22 | A pre-approved auth key carries its Delegation's seeds only in a client-only `#<bundle>`; api refuses an `auth_key` containing `#`. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-23 | JIT links an IdP identity to an existing user only after that user logs in with its existing credential. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-24 | `SidecarAdmit.capabilities.read_only` limits a device to reading, sign-out, MLS maintenance, receipts and HeadCheck; never one of k. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-25 | SCIM removals deny at once and turn cryptographic only when an admin device or `scim_signer` daemon signs the MemberRevoke. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEAM-26 | A compromise `SidecarRevoke` parks every admission and OwnerConfirm the device signed since `since_ms` until reconfirmed. | [§7](#714-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-1 | One HuJSON source in the config repo and one compiler, run by every sidecar and by each base's writer. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-2 | Deny by default; grants form a union; hard denies win; tier defaults are starting documents. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-3 | network_client.acl_subject_client_id is written once at creation, nullable until a backfill and validated CHECK. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-4 | The in-memory gate checks non-companion contracts forward, companions reversed, and skips networks without a head row. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-5 | Legacy clients are reached only through unrestricted grants, otherwise source-only ([owner decision 106](#od-106)). | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-6 | **Withdrawn.** Server-compiled slices; superseded by owner decisions [5](#od-5) and [6](#od-6) (config repo, local evaluation). | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-7 | Requested grants activate within `maxExpiry` only on approvals over the rule's `evidence`, harness evidence in tainted runs only if named. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-8 | One Suspend statement per subject acts at once at gates and clients and closes its contracts. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-9 | Failing policy tests block a config head; rollbacks are new heads. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-10 | Shares need two-sided consent and resolve to FriendsAndFamily toward marked sidecars; the dialing network pays. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-11 | evs grants are per repo (read, write, admin, deposit), from policy or the repo's access log; prefix writes follow Q-EVS-3. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-12 | Mail authorization per Q-MAIL-8 (a): edges check listen and send grants; aliases are checked on devices. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-13 | Kind defaults precede every document; owner-bound repos take readers only from the owner's consent, shares and the visible audit reader. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-14 | Sidecars are subjects in autogroup:sidecar, named durably as `sidecar:<id>`; RepoReaders returns sidecar ids. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-15 | Policy reaches servers only as AclRows in §7.9's ProjectionRows, compiled at each base; grant chains ride the authorization log. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-16 | Server gates evaluate the newest verified base and later entries, cached per (network, n), refreshed by INCR and polling. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-17 | Member devices are leaves (config by §7.9's rank, data repos up to 1,000); everyone else reads through ReaderWraps. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-18 | Clients never encrypt to a non-reader (§8.12); the evs write gate is D-EVS-18. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-19 | Subjects are classed before expansion; an ephemeral sidecar's evs access is only grants naming it, deposits and EvsShares to it. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-20 | `autogroup:untagged` is untagged non-sidecars; writers compile the implicit document into the projection whenever `has_document` is false. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-21 | evs and gkm honor `r`, `rw` or `admin` only while the subject holds that access in their newest verified state. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ACL-22 | One consent predicate, §8.5's `consented(d, M)`; a JIT member's first device enrolls from the admitting admin device's invite. | [§8](#814-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-1 | Key sockets on (network_id, name), resolving `<net>` per call. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-2 | Use 9.4's namespaces and host forms, refusing deeper names; [owner decision 40](#od-40)'s scopes add one label. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-3 | Registrations are 45 s leases, renewed every 15 s by the full set in pages of ≤1,024 entries carrying load. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-4 | Find returns single-use 30 s Ed25519 tickets (primary, backup) carrying the grant expiry; sockets never contacts listeners. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-5 | Schedule by weighted P2C on (est + 1) / weight, with listener caps, opt-in affinity, per-dialer share caps, 64-listener samples. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-6 | Dial with a 5 s accept timeout, the backup ticket, then up to 3 Finds; ejection needs two networks' reports. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-7 | Keep socket state in Redis Cluster with per-group hash tags and field TTLs. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-8 | Provide net.Listener and net.Conn adapters with syscall-compatible errors. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-9 | Delete registrations on client removal; keep no per-dial record beyond sock-2 fields (≤300 s) and sock-3 pairs (≤24 h). | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-10 | Host the engine as server/cli/sockets with Client-class routes, keeping registration load off api. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-11 | Platform services listen as `ur/<service>` in urnetwork-edge, authorized by the service. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-12 | Edge tickets bind one of the caller's K clients; edge Finds write {svc_} pairs authorizing C9 until grants end. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-13 | Names outside tls/, smtp/ and ur/ reach the server only as HMAC token paths under `K_sock`, rotated on §11.6's triggers. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-14 | Registrations and Finds are gated on the signed id-only projection; listener and dialer re-derive grants from the config repo. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-15 | Per-client token buckets bound Find and registration-page work, never name counts or established use; spend checks precede signing. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SOCK-16 | `ur share` is a live sharer: a blinded `share/<token>` socket, a fragment secret and a durable use count. | [§9](#912-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-1 | MLS distributes key-encryption keys under 10.5's hierarchy from v0, built in house (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [43](#od-43)). | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-2 | One MLS group per repo, a leaf per reading member device up to 1,000; others, config overflow included, hold ReaderWraps. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-3 | Member commits are PrivateMessage, adding only the generation and auth pin in clear; only external commits are PublicMessage. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-4 | Credential 0xF552 binds sidecar_id and identity key under a SidecarAdmit; only genesis is TOFU; owner-bound repos add only consented readers. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-5 | GKM keeps no state of its own; it orders, claims, delivers and retains through conditional writes on its repo's cluster. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-6 | Commit before write: a log entry shrinking a repo's key holders closes evs's gate until a covering generation is claimed. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-7 | **Withdrawn.** Superseded by owner decisions [113](#od-113) and [128](#od-128): the signed statement, not an admin committer, authorizes each membership change. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-8 | Drop keys in each signed GenRotate give write-only deposits to covering generations; each key domain is its own repo. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-9 | Rotating devices wrap each generation to every reading member's RecoveryBind key; Team's only escrow is a visible audit reader. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-10 | M2's entry fixes MLS wire fields, its exit freezes them on §22.10's interop artifact; the security page discloses unaudited MLS. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-11 | Tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars read and write through ReaderWraps; live Delegations get DelegationWraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-12 | MLS is 10.4's subset on ciphersuite 0x0010 from v0, migrating through GroupForm if IANA assigns another value. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-13 | After a site loss, repo admins' or owners' consented devices re-seed each group from their keychains under a ladder-linked GroupForm. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-14 | Groups scale by 10.6's sizes: self-update interval, KF5 resync, GroupInfo on demand above 16 leaves, daily acks, trees on disk. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-15 | `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match by the rotator, alone holds a generation; MLS commits never raise it. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-16 | KeyHolders: leaves, uncovered agents, live Delegations, recovery keys; a Delegation's key drops at revocation, `not_after` or an agent's non-reap revocation. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-17 | Drop keys ride each signed GenRotate for deposit kinds; depositors seal only to generations covering every known shrink and expiry. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-18 | At most 16 leaves, the epoch object carries sealed GroupInfo; above 16, recovery and resync need one leaf online. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-19 | `gkm:<group_id>` is versioned epoch × 2^24 + generation; work hints go on the acting sidecars' per-client `gkm` topic. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-20 | Retention keeps a group's newest epoch, moves `group-info` before deleting the epoch it names, and keeps gen/ for life. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-KEYS-21 | gkm acks are Redis soft state; the reconciler deletes only once acks span 30 days; big GroupInfos only on request. | [§10](#1011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-1 | Plaintext git lives only on reading sidecars; evs holds segments, index entries and signed pushes. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-2 | **Withdrawn.** Option (c)'s sealed client index; superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s token tree (D-EVS-12). | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-3 | Blobs are git-delta chains under 11.7's checkpoint rules, capping reconstruction at 17 records and 1.5× file size. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-4 | **Withdrawn.** Ref CAS in Postgres; superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s head/ objects (D-EVS-13). | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-5 | Only the §5 identity key signs pushes, which name sidecar_id and client_id and are pinned; agent attribution is sealed. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-6 | **Withdrawn.** No server path index; superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s object path index (D-EVS-12). | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-7 | **Withdrawn.** A helper-only git tier; superseded by [owner decision 24](#od-24)'s local git tier with git-remote-ur (D-EVS-15). | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-8 | Owned refs sync in real time; shared git-mode refs serialize by tip CAS, file-mode refs by path-level CAS; nothing auto-resolves. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-9 | **Withdrawn.** Usage counted in Postgres; superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s usage events (D-EVS-16). | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-10 | In record-class repos, owned refs are append-only streams; deposits end in a reader's CONSUME. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-11 | Kinds are fixed at creation; vault, mailbox and secret readers are only consented owner devices, EvsShares and the audit reader. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-12 | 11.6-11.7's token tree; a signed, head-bound map re-keys it at once on removal or compromise, else within 24 h. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-13 | Stateless evs: objects on each repo's placed cluster; only the head If-Match commits; everything else is immutable or rebuildable. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-14 | Subscriptions are token-prefix leases per path epoch in Redis soft state; hints carry server-held fields, versioned by the push sequence. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-15 | Local tier: system git behind authenticating fronts plus git-remote-ur; plaintext only on loopback, TLS or ssh beyond; committer hook. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-16 | Stored bytes: object sizes plus batch-resident records, counted nightly, moved by usage batches; at the limit, payload-adding pushes stop. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-17 | Owner devices mirror record-class repos and the config in full, slots included, and re-seed evs after site loss, slots last. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-18 | The write gate is the head CAS: a commit's authorization and generation pins pass §10.6's predicate against evs's newest state. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-19 | Deletion is a `repo/` state machine following the access log; restore and shred share one CAS; `shredding` precedes key destruction. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-20 | Pushes over 1 MiB or 1,024 entry writes split into at most 1,024 hashed parts; one head PUT commits them. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-21 | 11.13 budgets metadata writes in drive bytes and IOs; leases, push sequence and acks live in Redis; per-network fair share. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-22 | Refs have a mode fixed at creation: git-mode refs commit only on their tip; file-mode refs use path-level CAS. *(decided; [owner decision 141](#od-141))* | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-23 | A push id names one statement; retries return its version; the head resolves unknown outcomes; unsettled refusals fence the ref. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-24 | Log pages hold ≤1 KiB signed statements; head readers verify every one after their pin and each read entry's. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-25 | Orphans are found without the log: hourly evacuation resolves batch records; unadopted segments or maps die only after ref fences. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-26 | Erasure is a committed ERASE push destroying every key of every representation: retained versions, derived-field chains and the deposit. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-27 | Segments are addressed by content id; locators reserve two kinds and `spidx/` is reserved, so packing needs no format change. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-28 | The local tier publishes through git's proc-receive hook with per-ref statuses, no atomic pushes and a durable push-id journal. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-29 | The head holds the commit point and a window of 64-byte entries, ~9 KiB at most: one block a drive. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-30 | evs group-commits push, part and seal records into immutable minute batches of ≤256 KiB, evacuated whole after 25-26 h. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-31 | `idx/` holds only committed versions, folded lazily; reads and the CAS merge the unfolded window. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-32 | Hourly, history older than 24 h packs onto HDD once 256 KiB, else into NVMe parcels packed within 7 d. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-33 | One write budget per metadata cluster (0.8 DWPD, 50% IOPS); admissions prepay their background work; heaviest networks refused first. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-EVS-34 | Segment uploads write nothing to the metadata cluster: a MAC'd receipt rides the push; GC fences idle refs first. | [§11](#1116-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-1 | Roots are configuration; v0's only root is ur.network, for user content (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [32](#od-32)). | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-2 | Labels are random, lazy, immutable and never reused; aliases are copies; `<net>` resolves label, then alias. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-3 | Only 12.6's self-hosted dns edge serves `<root>`, from two NS at the site (owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123)). | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-4 | TTLs follow 12.6, short enough for ACME, failover and takedown. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-5 | Online DNSSEC signing from the first deploy, with compact denial, an offline KSK, 14-day DNSKEY windows, DS after 30 days. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-6 | System records follow 12.7, with no wildcard CNAME; an entry is one user RRset; replying burner labels copy the wildcard. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-7 | 12.7 refuses non-public addresses and listed types and owners, and caps RRsets; SRV and `*.<host>` extend own records. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-8 | certs is the only DNS-01 writer, after checking the caller's grant; writes are rate-limited and expire after 1 h. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-9 | Custom domains: a verified TXT, a one-time `_acme-challenge` CNAME, a CAA accounturi pin; CNAME hosts are weak mode. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-10 | Labels and aliases are tombstoned forever; a changed alias retires over 90 days. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-DNS-11 | A `<blabel>` with a child owner carries an atomic copy of the wildcard's MX, A and AAAA, served from `*`. | [§12](#1211-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-1 | Passthrough only: tlsedge holds no user key or user-name certificate, and no URnetwork-run client listens on tls/. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-2 | Ingress is 13.4's gated, probed SNI split on shared lb addresses, custom hosts by a generated map; port 80 redirects. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-3 | tlsedge is a layer-4 router that sees only SNI, ALPN and bytes. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-4 | tlsedge runs K platform clients per process on Service contracts, never a client per network. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-5 | The sidecar's TLS front enforces 13.7, dispatching on the registration's mode, never ALPN's absence; 421 and origin rules are mandatory. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-6 | Every device holds its own P-256 key and certificate for its set; member scopes only on that member's consented devices. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-7 | certs proxies CSRs, queues orders, puts ephemeral sidecars on GTS or ZeroSSL first, and alone writes DNS-01 in URnetwork zones. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-8 | Sidecars watch CT through two sources and check attestations against pinned identity keys. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-9 | Endpoint counting, caps, the kill switch, publish time boxes and 24 h records follow 13.9. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-10 | TCP 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 (owner decisions [68](#od-68), [121](#od-121)); no HTTP/3 or published ECH configs; tlsedge routes on SNI. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-11 | A Team custom domain's customer ACME account serves its ordering desktops; the CAA pin excludes URnetwork only in strong mode. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-12 | Active custom hosts reach tlsedge via the split's generated map, reloaded at most every 15 min. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TLS-13 | Dispatch binds the registration's mode: `http` through the HTTP front, `raw` only for `public` or pinned `link`; ALPN never decides. | [§13](#1312-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-1 | The sidecar reaches smtpedge only by a §6 stream; the edge dials the MX, runs pre-TLS SMTP, and splices TLS. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-2 | STARTTLS is mandatory; an unauthenticated MX needs the user's per-domain consent; pinned hosts are never downgraded. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-3 | The preamble is versioned protobuf frames ahead of the raw TLS stream. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-4 | **Withdrawn.** A declared v0 preamble; superseded by [owner decision 35](#od-35), with D-SMTP-16 setting the proof gate. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-5 | Header domain `<net>.<root>` with SPF -all, envelope `b.<net>.<root>`, strict DMARC, FCrDNS with HELO = PTR ([owner decision 124](#od-124)). | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-6 | The sidecar declares the Message-ID; the edge issues a MAC'd X-UR-Ref and a per-network Feedback-ID. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-7 | **Withdrawn.** Superseded by owner decisions [34](#od-34) and [124](#od-124): smtpedge sends from the shared lb addresses, with no IP pools. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-8 | Abuse attribution has three confidence levels; only high and medium halt, a medium join needing the MAC network's verifying `d=`. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-9 | Halts are 24 h Redis flags with smtp_halt rows, per network or burner label. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-10 | Retention follows §2.8 smtp-1 to smtp-6 plus 14 days of backups; recipients, plaintext and session ciphertext are never stored. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-11 | The engine is smtpedgeservice, hosted by server/cli/smtpedge; the prover and verifier are the nested module smtpproof. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-12 | Abuse reports are parsed header-only, aggregates by D-SMTP-23's bounded parser, then sealed unparsed to the network mail key or dropped. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-13 | For a URnetwork MX, smtpedge splices to mxedge over the host LAN. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-14 | 14.7's send gate, breaker and destination caps bound Community volume; its daily recipient cap bounds every tier. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-15 | In v1, Team networks send from verified custom domains. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-16 | M9's gate is 14.5's soundness, speed, coverage and interop tests, in both modes, with no external audit. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-17 | **Withdrawn.** Superseded by [owner decision 125](#od-125): the DATA-mode proof is built beside BDAT, and DATA coverage joins D-SMTP-16's gate. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-18 | Phones do not prove: they write signed outbound mail to the mailbox outbox, which a consented prover host sends. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-19 | Reports and role mail go to `rpt.bringyour.com`, whose platform listener terminates every session, SNI or not, from M5. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-20 | DATA mode proves every message octet in 2-minute parts within 2 h, up to `smtp_data_proof_bytes`; larger mail gets a DSN. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-21 | Z1 proves TLS 1.2's server Finished in-circuit, so no TLS 1.2 key is disclosed. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-22 | 14.5's relation also proves the MX's authenticated replies; parts name the records they cover, and BDAT bodies stream unopened. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SMTP-23 | DMARC and TLS-RPT aggregates are parsed within bounds, counted once per report, and compared with proven sends per recipient. | [§14](#1411-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-1 | Inbound TLS ends only at customer receivers, except D-MAIL-10's report listener; mxedge routes by SNI; failures are temporary. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-2 | mxedge's router speaks only 15.4's pre-TLS dialog, refuses plaintext transactions and splices from the ClientHello. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-3 | Receivers run emersion/go-smtp with 15.5's upstreamable ServeConn, forked if declined, and verify with mox over DoH on arrival. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-4 | Each receiver presents its own certificate and TLSA record for `mx.<net>.<root>`, serving every burner, and MTA-STS as a system publish. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-5 | Receivers deposit each message to the newest GenRotate's drop key and answer 250 once durable; erasure takes every copy. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-6 | Each member has one owner-bound mailbox repo, each group one general repo storing mail once, each network one signed mailcfg. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-7 | Burners are `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` under the wildcard MX; receive-only burners have no records, keys or server state. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-8 | Same-network mail is delivered by deposit and never crosses the internet. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-9 | Owner accepts the M7 census's loss before burners launch; proposed bar: under 5% of sign-up and code mail lacks SNI. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-10 | Reports and role mail reach rpt.bringyour.com's terminating platform listener, which accepts only platform recipients and persists no plaintext. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-11 | Submission and IMAP bind all interfaces unless narrowed; off loopback they speak implicit TLS only ([owner decision 130](#od-130)). | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-12 | A Team direct MX names at most two mxedge-verified receivers; strict mode refuses spliced hosts; scopes receive on consented devices. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-13 | [Owner decision 135](#od-135)'s operator list is `mail_operators.yml` in the public sidecar repo, versioned and embedded in each release. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MAIL-14 | Receivers seal reception-time authentication evidence in the deposit; readers label, score and forward from it, never from later DNS. | [§15](#1512-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-1 | sidecar/mcp uses server's pinned go-sdk (v1.7.0), bumped in lockstep; only `ur` links it, never sdk, gomobile or wasm. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-2 | MCP runs in the §5 daemon, one session per relay connection, not in each `ur` process. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-3 | The 16.5 catalog: outward tools behind §5's gate, no admin tools, subscribable ur:// resources. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-4 | Outside content returns only as tagged data; taint, including lapsed hooks, lasts the run; O actions need run-bound, evidence-labeled decisions. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-5 | Ingest via hooks, transcript tails and scans into a sealed, pre-redacted spool; hooks fail open, but lapses taint the run. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-6 | Freeze 16.8's record envelope at M3's entry review, after RECORD.md's review, gated by §22's vectors and peer review. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-7 | No URnetwork-hosted MCP serves sidecar tools; cloud agents run `ur` in their VM ([owner decision 49](#od-49)). | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-8 | Restore is the run_restore tool, writing only the run's attributed edits, rechecked against its preview, recorded, approved when tainted. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-9 | A harness prompt counts as a daemon-signed `harness` decision under harness_ok, never for authority, in tainted runs only if named. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-10 | Every record repo keeps a reader-daemon mirror; depositors spool until consumed; a re-seed re-uploads signed entries verbatim. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-11 | Each approval use is reserved durably before its effect; components are idempotent per `effect_key`; an uncertain use stays consumed. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-12 | Decisions bind spender and projection pin; spenders run 16.6's check; approvals activate one grant or up to `uses` bridge rules. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-13 | Results are version-aware, so every promised MCP version reads the same tagged data. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-14 | Only approval-capable devices give `device` evidence or disable `harness_ok`. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-15 | Restore points are local and exact; changes carry edit, shell or foreign attribution; restore writes only attributed edits. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-16 | Run taint is a monotone, fsynced bit written before untrusted data leaves the daemon; a missing file means tainted. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-17 | MCP's evs tools never write config or `mailcfg`; MCP signs no authority statement; `CanonicalAction` carries every field approvers render. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-18 | Read receipts are budgeted deposits made before decryption; a first read that cannot deposit fails closed. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-MCP-19 | Presence evidence follows 16.6's profiles: WebAuthn with UP and UV per use; Secure Enclave keys labeled asserted. | [§16](#1611-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-1 | The bridge reuses connect's client-to-provider NAT path: routing at the sender, a per-flow decision at the provider, one hop. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-2 | The router sits in DeviceLocal's send path before the mux, behind deviceBridge; the CLI shares it. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-3 | Fail closed: providers serve only sealed flows and, with an ACL document, open private destinations only by rule. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-4 | The C5 egress hook applies 17.6's order, relying on C6a, C13, C15 and, for shares, C18. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-5 | Links run Required to a fixed target with one window client, relay-only until C3, never count-capped; targets sidecar-owned until C16. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-6 | Bridge rules are signed config-repo statements; gates see only reach rules and BridgeRows, never prefixes, addresses or ports. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-7 | Revocations reset both ends at once; edits keep live pairs on serving links and drain removed advertisers for minutes. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-8 | An identical advertisement is approved as an HA replica or a remap; nesting is allowed; other overlaps are refused. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-9 | HA is active-active by weighted rendezvous over healthy advertisers; a down mark moves no pin and keeps the last advertiser. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-10 | A forward listens on 0.0.0.0/:: unless --listen narrows it, under a requested grant, disclosed as LAN-exposed. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-11 | Hosted, proxy, extension and isolated clients never route, host or serve. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-12 | The sdk exports hosted addresses, granted prefixes, aliases and an RFC 1918 block minus the physical path's local /32s. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-13 | 17.9's egress spec sets each subject's default route, enforced at §8.10's gate. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-14 | C18 reaches the hook only on sidecar-owned share hosts, mapping foreign flows by verified share and network to its targets. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-15 | The accepting network aliases shared hosts and prefixes in its own block; both tables travel sealed under the invite key. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-16 | `ur bridge block` refuses blocks outside 100.64/10 and RFC 1918; readers alarm on such a head; renumbering keeps host bits. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-17 | A host admits native IP flows only from window clients whose customer-signed `WindowDelegation` it verified, or a pinned ShareKey's. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-18 | Only a verified state opens a private destination: legacy, pending and enforcing states persist, never lowered by unsigned input. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-19 | A provider never dials its own daemon listeners, with or without a document (17.6's rule 0). | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-20 | Hosts use the lower /17, aliases the upper /17 first-fit; a share too wide or without room is refused. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-BRIDGE-21 | A revocation swaps policy before `CloseFlows`; flows register rule and policy generation before dialing and recheck before the first byte. | [§17](#1713-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-1 | Two roles: the sidecar role on its own Required client; only the keyless device role in network processes. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-2 | sdk.Sidecar is one struct with local and remote backends, 18.5's API and its gates. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-3 | Use 18.6's seam and mirror; app devices host, serve and map nothing before C16 (M4). | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-4 | The sdk Api session owns the token; the sdk injects 18.7's host services. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-5 | 18.4's memory budgets are carved from each process limit. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-6 | Browser sidecars phase per 18.8: Workers are member devices, the page Worker read-only, the quick burner a wrapped reader. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-7 | Cloud hosts climb 18.9's carrier rungs against its published host list ([owner decision 49](#od-49)). | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-8 | Adopt 18.10's size gates, set by 18.3's iOS headroom and 18.10's wasm sizes. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-9 | Apps decide approvals, admissions, alarms and vetoes through `SidecarApprovals`; control mode signs only confirmed `device` evidence for others. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-10 | Wake pushes carry only a topic class and version, from M8 ([owner decision 88](#od-88)). | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-11 | Desktop sdk hosts adopt 18.7's credential rules before §7.4's stage 2 (I-6; [owner decision 45](#od-45)). | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-12 | ur.io's hosted DeviceLocal runs no sidecar or bridge, and 18.3's hosted check marks it for §8.10's gate. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-13 | The device role takes rules only from its BridgeState and anchored deltas, restoring its persisted posture before the first packet. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-14 | Transport rejections are generation-bound and map to Unenrolled with a reason; only a verified `SidecarRevoke` maps to Revoked. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-15 | `SidecarKeyStore` returns status codes and a `SidecarSecret` struct, since gobind carries no error type. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-16 | Wakes follow 18.7: a slot-local script, a separate token-holder enqueue, client acks from connect's frame ack, a deferred live check. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-17 | Ephemeral clients are reaped with no open connection once their poll lease and newest disconnect pass 35 min. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-18 | Browser keys, tokens and the Worker live in a key origin that ur.io pages frame and message by exact origin. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-19 | The page Worker builds the root with `-tags sidecar_http`, excluding connect-facing and `host_*.go` files, so it links no connect package. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-SDK-20 | The device role lives in `sidecar/device`, importing only connect and `sidecar/protocol/bridge`. | [§18](#1812-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-1 | Host engines and jobs per 19.4, the push sender in taskworker; only api's OAuth issuer mounts signing keys. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-2 | gkm is its own service, server/cli/gkm, from v0; its reconciler runs in taskworker. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-3 | Build warp changes W1, W2 and W4-W11; keep the 16 MiB lb body limit. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-4 | The file clusters are LAN-only, unshared and without presigned URLs. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-5 | **Withdrawn.** Off-site copy of the file clusters; superseded by [owner decision 94](#od-94); D-OPS-18 covers Postgres-held sidecar rows. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-6 | Migrations follow 19.7: a group stays pending under `sidecar_pending` until its own Gn-out registers it. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-7 | Redis holds only rebuildable state; switches go to Postgres first; the clusters stay the only commit point. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-8 | Metrics and logs carry no identifying labels, names or query strings. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-9 | Adopt 19.8's SLOs and page classes, paging out of hours from M3; error-budget burn stops rollout steps. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-10 | Gates and the placement target live in `config/<env>/sidecar.yml`. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-11 | Classify and order releases per 19.11. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-12 | A builder job renews platform certificates at two thirds of lifetime (lego v5, ARI); W5 reloads them. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-13 | **Withdrawn.** Dedicated mail and tlsedge addresses; superseded by [owner decision 34](#od-34). | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-14 | Durability is 19.6's quorum writes, protection states, cold spare and daily off-site sidecar dump; site loss takes 19.10's restore. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-15 | Addresses and dns edges follow 19.4 and 19.5 (owner decisions [34](#od-34), [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123), [124](#od-124)). | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-16 | Redis backup bundles leave out sidecar key families, filtered from each node's rdb before sealing. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-17 | Size the metadata tier by measured drive writes, objects and bytes; [owner decision 136](#od-136)'s triggers order the next metadata cluster. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-18 | The tables 19.7's groups create get a daily off-site dump from MG0's Gn-out, excluded from the main dumps. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-19 | Metadata sets run 19.6's XFS and MinIO settings; storage hosts export drive write counters and SMART wear to the budget. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-OPS-20 | Both clusters run an in-house MinIO build whose cancels reach every drive and hold locks until drive operations answer. | [§19](#1913-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-1 | Tiers free (Community), pro and team resolve only in pro_model.go from in-window balances. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-2 | Limits and prices come only from pro.yml, with `network_sidecar_limit` overrides; limits ship dark; a missing price withholds overage. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-3 | Capacity except storage counts exactly; storage nightly from stored sizes, moved by usage batches; rates in one atomic Lua script. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-4 | Service contracts escrow nothing; edges bill by lease, relayed contracts by reservation and close report, evs by usage batches. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-5 | Refusals are 20.7's QuotaRefusal; agents spend only under I-8 approval. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-6 | Downgrade deletes nothing, breaks no inbound address, and freezes growth. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-7 | Abuse limits (`sidecar_abuse:`) are separate from quotas, never sold, equal on every tier, and tightened per network by §21. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-8 | Taskworker rolls usage into daily network_service_usage rows, each sent to a pre-aggregated daily Stripe meter, so re-sends replace. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-QUOTA-9 | One comparator, `escrowDrawLess`, orders every draw and return of transfer balances, with `team_credit` last. | [§20](#2011-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-1 | Abuse controls act only on names, metadata, rates and reports, never content. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-2 | 21.5's breakers guard `<root>` and the shared addresses, with thresholds in pro.yml `sidecar_abuse:`. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-3 | Takedown follows 21.6 and 21.8: within 1 h for confirmed public phishing, malware and paged notices; `<root>` in Search Console. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-4 | Screening, standing and verification follow 21.6 and 21.7. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-5 | Intake and appeals follow 21.8, report mail never touching the SNI router. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-6 | Legal process and holds follow 21.9 (owner decisions [93](#od-93), [133](#od-133)), each hold with its statutory kind and deadline. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-ABUSE-7 | Retention, access and transparency follow §2.8, 21.10 and 21.11. | [§21](#2113-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-1 | T1-T4 gate merges; sidecar/test.sh runs in RUN-ALL after connect; server engine tests fail fast. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-2 | sidecartest rebuilds connect's helpers from exported API and ships fakes whose store suites server also runs on real stores. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-3 | 22.5's gates and 22.9's budgets fail the build; raising one needs a reviewed change. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-4 | Every fuzz target ships seeds, plus a differential oracle where a second implementation exists. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-5 | Every scenario runs 22.7's privacy harness and guard; later, a synthetic main network repeats S2 and S5-S7 hourly. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-6 | The revocation suite runs with evs's write gate off, since server refusal is only defense in depth. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-7 | 22.8's load tests run per milestone, its soak before each release; conformance peers are pinned and rerun per pin change. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-8 | **Withdrawn.** External reviews gating freezes and the claim; superseded by [owner decision 99](#od-99). | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-9 | Freezes pass 22.10's gates in D-PHASE-7's two steps; nothing is audited ([owner decision 99](#od-99)). | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-10 | Every state machine of §7-§21 is tested by deterministic fault schedules against FI-1 to FI-14, beside TLA+ and Porcupine checks. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-TEST-11 | §22.8's `nvme` run gates M2's exit and format 1: no push refused, ≤43 KiB a push per drive, ≤50% IOPS. | [§22](#2212-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-1 | Build 23.4's milestones in dependency order, staffed as 23.5 proposes, releasing each recURd stage once its last item lands. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-2 | No code before G0; an unsettled blocker defers what it blocks; implementation findings return as Q- items. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-3 | P0 stage 1 and D-TEAM-14 reach production log-only at M0's Gn-out; stage 2 and sdk credential rules precede M3's pilot. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-4 | 23.7's M0 lead-time items and §10.4's MLS subset with its X-Wing KAT start in M0. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-5 | **Withdrawn.** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): every touched repo merges `sidecar` into `main` at each Gn-out. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-6 | The design-partner pilot starts at M3's exit; its measures feed M6's entry review. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |
| D-PHASE-7 | Each frozen format freezes twice: its specification at its milestone's Gn-in, its final bytes at its Gn-out, on 22.10's evidence. | [§23](#2311-decisions-proposed) |

## Appendix B. Open-questions register

Every Q- item, in section order: 175 items. 148 were decided by the owner (32 of them by the 2026-11-04 entries), 11 were closed by peer review on 2026-11-04, 12 were closed by the 2026-11-03 design-review round, not by human peer review, so reviewers may reopen them (§3.11), and 4 were withdrawn; none is open. The question is a summary of 25 words or fewer. The status of a decided item gives the owner decisions that settled it, as its section cites them, with the date for a 2026-11-04 entry. The recommendation column, 15 words or fewer, gives each item's outcome. The decider of a closed item is peer review, which may reopen one the design-review round closed.
